children.translated_text: Homage to that supreme one, the foremost physician of the world, by whose bliss-born, auspiciously potent, flashing radiance, by the nectar of perfected rasa and the ocean of nectar that is his compassionate glance,

children.text: bhaktānāṃ prabhavaprasaṃhṛtijarārāgādirogāḥ kṣaṇācchāntiṃ yānti jagatpradhānabhiṣaje tasmai parasmai namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the diseases of devotees, such as creation, dissolution, old age, passion, and the like, quickly come to peace.
<s>Ādima</s>, <s>Candrasena</s>, and the learned lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>,
<s>Kapālī</s>, the two <s>Mattamāṇḍavyas</s>, <s>Bhāskara</s>, and <s>Śūrasenaka</s>,
<s>Ratnakośa</s>, <s>Śambhu</s>, <s>Sāttvika</s>, and <s>Naravāhana</s>,
<s>Indrada</s>, <s>Gomukha</s>, <s>Kambali</s>, and <s>Vyāḍi</s> too,
<s>Nāgārjuna</s>, <s>Surānanda</s>, <s>Nāgabodhi</s>, and <s>Yaśodhana</s>,

children.text: khaṇḍaḥ kāpāliko brahmā govindo lampako hariḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Khaṇḍa</s>, the <s>Kāpālika</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Govinda</s>, <s>Lampaka</s>, and <s>Hari</s>,
these, twenty-seven in number, are givers of success in rasa.
<s>Rasāṅkuśa</s>, <s>Bhairava</s>, <s>Nandī</s>, and <s>Svacchandabhairava</s>,
<s>Manthānabhairava</s> and also <s>Kākacaṇḍīśvara</s>,
<s>Vāsudeva</s>, the sage <s>Śṛṅga</s>, and the compendium called <s>Kriyātantrasamuccaya</s>,
<s>Rasendratilaka</s>, the yogin, <s>Bhālukī</s>, and the one called <s>Maithila</s>,
<s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Narendra</s>, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, and <s>Harīśvara</s>:
having examined the tantras of these and of others, a compendium is made
of rasas and perfected substances that are useful for the purpose of treatment.
This <s>Rasaratnasamuccaya</s> is composed by the son of <s>Siṃhagupta</s>.
Rasas, secondary rasas, metals, apparatus, and procedures,
as well as the procedures from the tantras for the purification of metals,
purification, extraction of essence, liquefaction, and the making of ash will be explained.
There is a great mountain, the abode of snow, facing the northern quarter,
whose mass of lofty peaks rises beyond the clouds.
It is as though a host of autumn clouds, exhausted by the great toil of crossing the path of the sky,
had descended to the earth for rest.
With the rays from the jewels on the hoods of the lords of serpents, mass upon mass,
it shines as if it had burst through the earth and risen up, exceedingly high.
The jewel-grounds on its slopes, with their blazing herbs,
imitate at night the wild lightning of clouds.
For the kinnara women wandering on its ridges,
the red mineral dye on their feet performs the office of lac.
Adorned with the cool-rayed moon and clothed with the quarters as his garment,
he who dwells in its caves is sung by people as <s>Girīśa</s>, lord of the mountain.
On its ridges sages, their eyes always closed,
directly behold <s>Giriśa</s>, who is beyond the range of speech and mind.
Because of the spray of its waterfalls, struck against the stone surfaces,
the yakṣas see, even by day, a sky marked with stars.
There men, unable to endure the excess of mist and wind,
constantly enjoy the warmth of their own wives' breasts.
When the sun moves on its ridges even in summer,
his heat is checked by the fierce snowy wind and he is not distinguished from the moon.
In its cave-houses, fragrant with the musk from musk-deer navels,
kinnara women sing of the festival of <s>Gaurī</s>'s marriage.
There shines <s>Maheśvara</s>, the primal god of the worlds,
from whom the great rasa was born, in the form of rasa, to protect the world.
The merit that men would gain by performing a hundred horse-sacrifices, by giving ten million cows and a thousand measures of gold,
and by bathing at all sacred fords, that merit comes from the sight of sūtaka.
Whoever, full of devotion, makes a rasa-liṅga and worships it
obtains the fruit of worshipping the liṅgas of the three worlds.

children.text: bhakṣaṇaṃ sparśanaṃ dānaṃ dhyānaṃ ca paripūjanam
children.translated_text: Eating, touching, giving, meditation, and complete worship:
the worship of rasa is said to be fivefold and to destroy the great sins.
Merely by being eaten it destroys for men the whole mass of diseases
arising from sins of previous births; there is no doubt about this.
The sin committed in previous births by embodied beings is destroyed at once
if <s>Śambhu</s> is anointed with fragrant ground sūta.
Whoever causes even a truṭi-measure of mica to be digested by rasa
will have the fruit of a hundred sacrifices; so <s>Śiva</s> declared.
And whoever reviles the lord of sūta, the supreme radiance of <s>Śambhu</s>,
falls into a terrible hell for as long as kalpas are counted.
Whoever gives rasa to the sick, furnished with purification and cooking,
obtains forever the fruit of the tulā-gift and horse-sacrifices.
When rasa is perfected, I shall make the world free from poverty and disease.
This meditation on rasa has been taught as removing sins such as the killing of a brahmin.
A mouthful of mica for sūta is proclaimed to be the offering of food.
Having thus performed the worship of rasa, one obtains the fruit born of sacrifice.
If a man's life departs while sūta is situated in his belly,
he is freed from terrible wrongdoing and goes to the supreme state.

children.text: mūrchitvā harati rujaṃ bandhanamanubhūya muktido bhavati
children.translated_text: When made swoon, it removes disease; after undergoing bondage, it becomes a giver of liberation.

children.text: amarīkaroti hi mṛtaḥ ko 'nyaḥ karuṇākaraḥ sūtāt ||
children.translated_text: When dead, it makes one immortal; what other source of compassion is there besides sūta?
Even leukoderma, said to be incurable and born from the accumulation of sins such as harming gods, teachers, cows, and twice-borns,

children.text: śvitraṃ tadapi ca śamayati yastasmātkaḥ pavitrataraḥ sūtāt ||
children.translated_text: is calmed by it; therefore who is purer than sūta?

children.text: rasabandha eva dhanyaḥ prārambhe yasya satatamitikaraṇā
children.translated_text: Only the binding of rasa is blessed, for at its beginning there is always the resolve:
When rasa is accomplished, I shall make the earth free from old age and death.

children.text: sukṛtaphalaṃ tāvadidaṃ sukule yajjanma dhīśca tatrāpi
children.translated_text: This much is the fruit of good deeds: birth in a good family, and intelligence even there.

children.text: sāpi ca sakalamahītalatulanaphalā bhūtalaṃ ca suvidheyam ||
children.translated_text: And that intelligence has the fruit of weighing the whole surface of the earth in gift, while the earth itself becomes easy to command.
The fruits of bringing the earth under one's control are riches, and those riches have many kinds of enjoyment as their fruit.

children.text: bhogāśca santi śarīre tadanityamato vṛthā sakalam ||
children.translated_text: And enjoyments exist in the body; but that body is impermanent, and therefore everything is vain.
Thus, knowing wealth, the body, and enjoyments to be always impermanent, one should make effort

children.text: muktau sā ca jñānāt taccābhyāsāt sa ca sthire dehe ||
children.translated_text: toward liberation; and that comes from knowledge, that from practice, and that practice from a stable body.

children.text: tatsthairye na samarthaṃ rasāyanaṃ kimapi mūlalohādi
children.translated_text: No <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenating elixir) made of roots, metals, and the like is capable of making that body stable,

children.text: svayamasthirasvabhāvaṃ dāhyaṃ kledyaṃ ca śoṣyaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: for it is itself unstable by nature, liable to be burned, moistened, and dried out.

children.text: kāṣṭhauṣadhyo nāge nāgo vaṅge 'tha vaṅgamapi śulbe
children.translated_text: Woody herbs merge into lead, lead into tin, and then tin too into copper;

children.text: śulbaṃ tāre tāraṃ kanake kanakaṃ ca līyate sūte ||
children.translated_text: copper merges into silver, silver into gold, and gold into mercury.

children.text: amṛtatvaṃ hi bhajante haramūrtau yogino yathā līnāḥ
children.translated_text: For just as yogins, merged in the form of <s>Hara</s>, partake of immortality,
so too, when <s>gagana</s> (mica) has been swallowed by the king of <s>rasa</s> (mercury), gold and the other metals do so.

children.text: paramātmanīva satataṃ bhavati layo yatra sarvasattvānām
children.translated_text: As in the supreme Self, where there is constantly the dissolution of all beings,
that one king of <s>rasa</s> makes the body free from old age and death.
In a stable body, through the force of practice, one obtains knowledge endowed with the eight powers,
and reaches the state of <s>Brahman</s>, no longer the sorrows of dwelling in repeated birth.
The supreme light stands supporting the world all at once with one part of itself;
its immortality in the other three quarters is not easily gained by mere detachment.
For with a body in any way afflicted by the suffering of disease, old age, and death,
and perishing moment by moment, it is not possible to worship that subtle <s>Brahman</s>.
When bodily perfection is in question, who would even take up the name without a body
of that stainless reality, accessible through yoga and not even within the range of the mind?
From sacrifice, gift-giving, austerity, Vedic study, self-restraint, and good conduct,
self-realization through the power of yoga is said to be far greater than all of them.
The supreme light, situated between the two eyebrows and shining upon the world like fire, lightning, and the sun,
opens for some whose vision is meritorious, a light made of consciousness.
It should be known as the supreme light, of the single savor of supreme bliss, by nature radiant and undivided,
free from all afflictions, peaceful, and known through itself.
Fixing the mind on that, seeing the whole flickering universe as made of consciousness,
one whose bonds of action have been destroyed attains <s>Brahman</s>-hood here itself.
Freed from passion and hatred, truthful in conduct, and without falsehood,
they become without distinction everywhere through contact with consciousness-<s>Brahman</s>.
They remain endowed with powers such as <s>aṇimā</s>, with shining bodies and ever-arisen bliss,
and, having attained the immortal nature of <s>Brahman</s>, they are indeed fulfilled.
The body is the abode of the sciences and the root of <s>dharma</s>, wealth, desire, and liberation;
what higher good is there apart from the one body made free from old age and death?

children.text: pratyakṣeṇa pramāṇena yo na jānāti sūtakam
children.translated_text: He who does not know mercury by the direct means of knowledge,
how will he know the god without visible form, made of consciousness?
That which is worn out by old age and helpless from the suffering of cough, breathlessness, and the like
is not fit for <s>samādhi</s>, since the operation of intellect and senses is obstructed.
A child, then a sixteen-year-old, then one greedy for the taste of sense objects,
and finally an old mortal whose discrimination has passed away: how could such a person attain liberation?

children.text: asminn eva śarīre yeṣāṃ paramātmano na saṃvedaḥ
children.translated_text: Those who do not perceive the supreme Self in this very body,
for them, after abandoning the body, that <s>Brahman</s> is still farther away.
<s>Brahmā</s> and the others strive for it, taking refuge in a divine body,
as do other living-liberated sages who endure until the end of an aeon.
Therefore a yogin who seeks liberation while living should first
make a divine body through the union produced by <s>Hara</s> and <s>Gaurī</s>.
On this mountain, through the delight of the two, <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Gaurī</s>, and their desire to conquer one another,
intercourse began, shaking the three worlds.
To prevent that intercourse, Fire was sent by the gods,
who desired a son of those two, a slayer of the demon <s>Tāraka</s>.
<s>Agni</s>, having arrived in the form of a pigeon in a cave of <s>Himavat</s>,
was agitated in that improper bird-form while looking upon the sport of love.
Seeing him, <s>Śambhu</s> was ashamed and then ceased from lovemaking;
the final generative fluid slipped out and was taken by the trident-bearer.
It was cast into the mouth of Fire, and from there it also fell into the <s>Gaṅgā</s>;
as she was being burned by it, she too cast it outside.
From bearing its residue, metals arose as causes of accomplishment,
as that seed fell from the mouth of Fire with abundant essence.
Having made five wells a hundred yojanas deep,
from then onward that seed, situated in the wells, became fivefold.
It became <s>rasa</s>, <s>rasendra</s>, <s>sūta</s>, <s>pārada</s>, and <s>miśraka</s>;
thus, according to the difference of place, the substance born from <s>Śambhu</s> became fivefold.
<s>Rasa</s> is red, free from all defects, and a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenating elixir);
through it the gods became free from disease, old age, and death.
<s>Rasendra</s>, free from defects, is dark, dry, and very mobile;
through it the <s>Nāgas</s> became users of <s>rasāyana</s>, rid of death and old age.

children.text: devairnāgaiś ca tau kūpau pūritau mṛdbhir aśmabhiḥ
children.translated_text: Those two wells were filled by the gods and <s>Nāgas</s> with earth and stones;
from then onward they became exceedingly hard for people to obtain.
<s>Sūtaka</s> is slightly yellow, dry-bodied, and possessed of defects;

children.text: daśāṣṭasaṃskṛtaiḥ siddho dehaṃ lohaṃ karoti saḥ ||
children.translated_text: when perfected by eighteen processes, it transforms the body and metal.
Then another kind, born from a different well, is mobile and white in color;
that is <s>pārada</s>, for through various applications it removes all diseases.
The <s>rasa</s> that has the hue of a peacock's tail-eye is regarded as <s>miśraka</s>.
That too, when endowed with the eighteen <s>saṃskāras</s> (processes), is exceedingly productive of accomplishment.
The three substances beginning with <s>sūta</s> are all forms of <s>sūta</s> and are capable of producing every accomplishment,
being endowed with extraordinary power through the performance of their own specific operations.

children.text: etāṃ rasasamutpattiṃ yo jānāti sa dhārmikaḥ
children.translated_text: He who knows this origin of <s>rasa</s> is a righteous man;
he obtains long life, health, offspring, and success with <s>rasa</s>.
Because it assimilates all the metals, it is called <s>rasa</s>;
or <s>rasa</s> is so regarded because it is employed for the destruction of old age, disease, and death.
Because it is king over <s>rasa</s> and <s>uparasa</s> substances, it is celebrated as <s>rasendra</s>;
and because it produces accomplishment in the body and in metals, it is remembered as <s>sūta</s>.
Because it grants deliverance to those sunk in the muddy ocean of disease, it is also <s>pārada</s>.
Where the fiery essence present in all metals remains mixed together,
therefore it is called <s>miśraka</s>, the giver of results of many forms.
By the power of such <s>sūta</s>, which cuts off disease and death among mortals,
human beings became equal to gods in strength and length of life.
Seeing them, <s>Rudra</s> was thereafter petitioned by <s>Śakra</s>;
and the king of <s>rasa</s> was constrained by defects and coverings.
From that time onward this <s>sūta</s> does not become effective at all when unprocessed.
When it goes into water it has the form of water; when swift, it may have the swan-like motion.
When it goes into impurity it has the form of impurity; when smoky, it has the smoke-like motion.
Another, divine movement is the life-movement: the living principle comes forth as from an egg.

children.text: sa tāṃś ca jīvayejjīvāṃstena jīvo rasaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: It revives those living beings; therefore <s>rasa</s> is remembered as <s>jīva</s> (life).

children.text: catasro gatayo dṛśyā adṛśyā pañcamī gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Four movements are visible, and the fifth movement is invisible.
By mantra, meditation, and the like, its fifth movement is restrained.
Thus, because the royal <s>sūta</s> has different movements, its processing is difficult to obtain;
therefore a skilful physician should carefully guard its <s>saṃskāra</s>.
Having seen a bride who has bathed after her first menstruation, mounted on a horse, well adorned,

children.text: vīkṣamāṇāṃ vadhūṃ dṛṣṭvā jighṛkṣuḥ kūpago rasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and looking about, the <s>rasa</s> in a well, wishing to seize her,

children.text: udgacchati javātsāpi taṃ dṛṣṭvā yāti vegataḥ
children.translated_text: rises up swiftly; she too, seeing it, goes away quickly.
The <s>sūta</s> follows her as far as a boundary measuring a yojana.
Then the <s>Śivasambhava</s> (that which is born from Śiva) swiftly returns to the well.
People collect the <s>pārada</s> that has remained in pits made along the path.
When that <s>rasa</s>, through its heaviness, has fallen from the fire-mouth in the land of <s>Darada</s>,
it becomes absorbed into the surface of the earth; the inhabitants of those regions

children.text: tāṃ mṛdaṃ pātanayantre kṣiptvā sūtaṃ haranti ca ||
children.translated_text: put that soil into a distillation apparatus and extract <s>sūta</s>.
<s>Abhra</s>, <s>vaikrānta</s>, <s>mākṣīka</s>, <s>vimala</s>, <s>adrija</s>, and <s>sasyaka</s>,
together with <s>capala</s> and <s>rasaka</s>: knowing these eight, one should collect the <s>rasa</s>-minerals.

children.text: devyā rajo bhavedgandho dhātuḥ śukraṃ tathābhrakam iti kṣepakaḥ
children.translated_text: As an interpolation: sulfur is the menstrual blood of the Goddess, and <s>abhraka</s> is likewise the semen of the metal.

children.text: gaurītejaḥ paramamamṛtaṃ vātapittakṣayaghnam prajñābodhi praśamitarujaṃ vṛṣyamāyuṣyamagryam
children.translated_text: <s>Vyoma</s> (abhraka), the energy of <s>Gaurī</s>, is supreme nectar, destructive of wind, bile, and wasting, awakening intelligence, pacifying pain, aphrodisiac, and foremost for longevity;

children.text: balyaṃ snigdhaṃ rucidam akaphaṃ dīpanaṃ śītavīryaṃ tattadyogaiḥ sakalagadahṛd vyoma sūtendrabandhi ||
children.translated_text: it is strengthening, unctuous, taste-giving, not productive of phlegm, digestive, cooling in potency, remover of all diseases in its various preparations, and a binder of the lordly <s>sūta</s>.
The dense mineral that is brought from a mine from below the royal hand
will give the stated result; if it lacks essence, it is completely fruitless.
<s>Abhraka</s> is regarded as <s>pināka</s>, <s>nāga</s>, <s>maṇḍūka</s>, and <s>vajra</s>;
by distinctions of white and the other colors, each of these is fourfold.
The <s>pināka</s> variety, when strongly heated by fire, releases a mass of flakes.
When used, that variety binds the feces and indeed kills a person.
<s>Nāga</s>-abhraka, when placed in fire, makes a sound like a serpent.

children.text: tadbhuktaṃ kurute kuṣṭhaṃ maṇḍalākhyaṃ na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When eaten, it certainly produces the skin disease called <s>maṇḍala</s>.
The <s>maṇḍūka</s> variety of abhraka, when blown upon, leaps up repeatedly and falls down.
That produces stone disease, curable only by surgery and otherwise incurable.
<s>Vajra</s>-abhraka, heated in fire, is freed from all defects.
It produces accomplishment in the body and metals and is supreme in removing all diseases.

children.text: śvetaṃ raktaṃ ca pītaṃ ca kṛṣṇamevaṃ caturvidham
children.translated_text: White, red, yellow, and black: thus it is fourfold.
The white is prescribed for white operations, and the red-colored for red operations.
The abhraka that is yellowish is best for yellow operations.
Although four kinds of excellent <s>vyoma</s> are taught in <s>rasāyana</s>,
nevertheless black abhraka is many millions of times superior.
Oily, with broad layers, possessing good color, and especially heavy by weight,
with sheets that can be peeled apart easily: such abhraka is declared excellent.

children.text: sacandrikaṃ ca kiṭṭābhaṃ vyoma na grāsayedrasaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rasa</s> should not be made to consume <s>vyoma</s> that is lustrous and slag-like.
But once it has consumed it, that <s>rasa</s> is to be employed in metals and in <s>rasāyana</s>.

children.text: niścandrikaṃ mṛtaṃ vyoma sevyaṃ sarvagadeṣu ca
children.translated_text: Dead <s>vyoma</s>, without moonlike luster, is to be used in all diseases.
If used while still having that luster, it causes urinary disease and weak digestion.
Those who, devoid of proper method, have prescribed a rasāyana of sheet-abhraka
have thereby regarded the poison called <s>Kālakūṭa</s> as a cause of life.
One should use purified abhraka for the sake of extracting its essence and for internal use.

children.text: anyathā tv aguṇaṃ kṛtvā vikarotyeva niścitam ||
children.translated_text: Otherwise, having become devoid of virtue, it certainly causes disorder.
Abhraka heated intensely seven times and cast into sour gruel

children.text: nirdoṣaṃ jāyate nūnaṃ prakṣiptaṃ vāpi gojale ||
children.translated_text: surely becomes faultless, or also when cast into cow urine,
and into a decoction of <s>triphala</s>, and especially into cow's milk.
Then, after making it into <s>dhānyābhraka</s>, one should grind it with the juices of <s>matsyākṣikā</s>.

children.text: cakrīṃ kṛtvā viśoṣyātha puṭed ardhebhake puṭe
children.translated_text: Having made disks and then dried them, one should calcine them in a half-bhaka <s>puṭa</s>.
In this way one should calcine it six times together with the juices of <s>punarnava</s>.
It should also be triturated with one-sixteenth part of <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> and made into disks.
In the same way, with the so-called half-bhāka <s>puṭa</s> firings, one should indeed calcine it seven times.
So also with the juice of <s>vāsā</s>, and with the juice of <s>taṇḍulīya</s>,
one should give it seven repeated <s>puṭa</s> firings according to the method stated before.
The mica thus perfected should be employed in all formulations.
Powdered mica, mixed with śāli rice and tied in cloth, when placed in sour gruel,
and passed out through the cloth by rubbing, is called <s>dhānyābhra</s>.
<s>Dhānyābhra</s>, thoroughly rubbed with the juice of <s>kāsamarda</s>,
and calcined with ten <s>puṭa</s> firings, is killed; there is no doubt about this.
The same is done with the juice of <s>mustā</s> and also with the juice of <s>taṇḍulīya</s>.
Mica made into pellets after being ground with yellow āmalaka and saubhāgya,
when calcined sixty times, becomes like vermilion.
According to the disease and the vehicle, it becomes a destroyer of consumption and all other disorders.
With decoctions of the root-bark of the banyan, or with the essence of betel leaves,
or with <s>vāsā</s> and <s>matsyākṣikā</s>, or with <s>mīnākṣī</s> together with <s>kaṭhillā</s>,
mica rubbed with the milk of the banyan tree and calcined
becomes, after twenty repetitions, brilliant like vermilion.
Mixed with one quarter part borax and rubbed with the juice of <s>musalī</s>,

children.text: rundhyātkoṣṭhyāṃ dṛḍhaṃ dhmātaṃ sattvarūpaṃ bhaved ghanam ||
children.translated_text: it should be sealed firmly in a furnace and blown; the mica becomes a form of <s>sattva</s>.
Of <s>kāsamarda</s>, <s>ghanā</s>, <s>dhānyā</s>, <s>vāsā</s>, and <s>punarbhū</s>,
and of <s>matsyākṣī</s>, <s>kāṇḍavallī</s>, and <s>haṃsapādī</s>, with each juice separately,
having ground it again and again with care, one should dry it by applying heat.
One pala of wheat flour, small fish, and borax,
each in an eighth part, should be added again and again and thoroughly rubbed in.
At each rubbing it should be well dried by the rays of the sun.
Either the five products of the goat, the five products of the cow, or the five products of the buffalo
should be poured in, and balls should be made, somewhat larger than a tinduka fruit.

children.text: payo dadhi ghṛtaṃ mūtraṃ saviṭkaṃ cājam ucyate
children.translated_text: Milk, curds, ghee, urine, and dung are called the five goat-products.
In a downward-passing furnace one should blow it and cause the <s>sattva</s> to fall down.

children.text: koṣṭhyāṃ kiṭṭaṃ samāhṛtya vicūrṇya ravakān haret
children.translated_text: Having collected the slag in the furnace, one should pulverize it and remove the small grains.
That slag should be rubbed with a little borax and cow dung,
made into balls, dried in the heat, and again treated as before.
Again the slag should be collected, rubbed, and the <s>sattva</s> extracted.
Then those grains of <s>sattva</s> should be boiled with sour gruels,
combined with the group of purifying substances, and enclosed within a crucible.
When it is fully melted, it should be collected, and the mica should be blown twice.
Thus the <s>sattva</s> becomes purified and fit to be used in mercury preparations and <s>rasāyana</s>.
Melted in honey, oil, fat, and ghee, and repeatedly quenched in them,
hard metallic and other <s>sattva</s> becomes soft after ten repetitions.
Then, having made it into sheet-powder and soaked it with cow ghee,
one should fry it seven times in an earthen pan set on the hearth.
Until it becomes the color of fire, it should be powdered each time, again and again.
Or one should continue frying until a blade of grass thrown upon it burns up.
Thereafter, having ground it with sulfur and with decoction of banyan root,
one should calcine it twenty times, indeed with a boar-type <s>puṭa</s>.
Again, twenty times, with a decoction arising from <s>triphalā</s>,
and with <s>triphalā</s>, <s>muṇḍikā</s>, <s>bhṛṅga</s> leaves, <s>pathyā</s>, and <s>akṣa</s> roots,
it should be impregnated and then administered in proper dose for all diseases.
There is something a little different from mica-<s>sattva</s>: unaltered and greater in virtues.
If it is prepared in this way by <s>puṭa</s>-cooking a hundred times,
it becomes extremely endowed with virtues, supreme for digestion and kindling appetite.
Impregnated with the water of <s>gandharvapattra</s> and with jaggery,
with banyan leaves placed below and above, mica free from glitter is obtained by three <s>puṭa</s> firings.
It greatly produces hunger when taken in a dose of half a guñjā.
With formulations that remove each particular disease, it is supreme in removing all diseases.
A ball of <s>sattva</s>, heated by blowing, in sour gruel mixed with grain,
should be quenched, and immediately pounded with an iron pestle.
Having heated the large grains of mica and then thrown them into sour gruel,
one should collect them at once, pound them, and make them into powder.

children.text: goghṛtena ca taccūrṇaṃ bharjayet pūrvavat tridhā
children.translated_text: That powder should also be fried with cow ghee three times, as before.
The same should be done with the juices of āmalaka fruits, or with the juice of āmalaka leaves.
At each frying, grinding should be done on a stone slab.
Then, with the juices of <s>punarnavā</s> and <s>vāsā</s>, mixed with sour gruel,
one should give it ten repeated <s>puṭa</s> firings, and ten more with sulfur.
Thus purified, mica-<s>sattva</s> is superior in every virtue.
It should be used as desired in digestion of metals and in <s>rasāyana</s>.

children.text: drutayo naiva nirdiṣṭāḥ śāstre dṛṣṭā api dṛḍham
children.translated_text: <s>Drutis</s> are not described here, although they are firmly seen in the treatise.

children.text: vinā śaṃbhoḥ prasādena na sidhyanti kadācana ||
children.translated_text: Without the favor of <s>Śambhu</s>, they never succeed at any time.

children.text: vellavyoṣasamanvitaṃ ghṛtayutaṃ vallonmitaṃ sevitaṃ divyābhraṃ kṣayapāṇḍuruggrahaṇikāśūlāmakuṣṭhāmayam
children.translated_text: Divine mica, taken with ghee, together with <s>vellā</s> and <s>vyoṣa</s>, in a dose of one vallā, conquers consumption, pallor, disorders of <s>grahaṇī</s>, colic, illness from <s>āma</s>, and skin disease,

children.text: jūrtiṃ śvāsagadaṃ pramehamaruciṃ kāsāmayaṃ durdharaṃ mandāgniṃ jaṭharavyathāṃ vijayate yogairaśeṣāmayān ||
children.translated_text: as well as wasting, breathing disease, urinary disease, anorexia, severe cough, weak digestion, abdominal pain, and, through its formulations, all diseases without remainder.
Having eight edges, eight facets, six angles, smooth, and heavy,
and furnished with pure and mixed colors, it is called <s>vaikrānta</s>.
White, red, yellow, blue, pigeon-colored,
dark, black, and variegated: it is indeed of eight kinds.
It grants longevity, produces strength and complexion, is highly aphrodisiac, gives intelligence, and removes all diseases caused by the doṣas.
It kindles the digestive fire, has qualities equal to the thunderbolt, is powerful; <s>vaikrāntaka</s> indeed makes the body, strength, and metals firm.
Among all <s>rasāyana</s>s it is foremost, possessed of power;
<s>vaikrānta</s>, remover of every defect, should be employed in place of diamond.
The lord of the daityas, <s>Māhiṣa</s>, perfected and arisen together with the gods,

children.text: durgā bhagavatī devī taṃ śūlena vyamardayat ||
children.translated_text: was crushed with her spear by the blessed goddess <s>Durgā</s>.

children.text: tasya raktaṃ tu patitaṃ yatra yatra sthitaṃ bhuvi
children.translated_text: Wherever his blood fell and remained upon the earth,

children.text: tatra tatra tu vaikrāntaṃ vajrākāraṃ mahārasam ||
children.translated_text: there in each place arose <s>vaikrānta</s>, the great rasa, shaped like diamond.

children.text: vindhyasya dakṣiṇe bhāge hy uttare vāsti sarvataḥ
children.translated_text: It exists everywhere, both in the southern region of the <s>Vindhya</s> and in the north.
Because it cuts metals, it is remembered as <s>vaikrāntaka</s>.
It is white, yellow, red, blue, and of the lustre of a dove;
another is like a peacock's neck, and another has the lustre of emerald.

children.text: dehasiddhikaraṃ kṛṣṇaṃ pīte pītaṃ site sitam
children.translated_text: The black one brings perfection of the body; for a yellow operation the yellow is used, and for a white operation the white.
The red, and likewise the emerald-like one, grants accomplishment of all aims;

children.text: śeṣe dve niṣphale varjye vaikrāntamiti saptadhā ||
children.translated_text: the remaining two are fruitless and should be rejected. Thus <s>vaikrānta</s> is sevenfold.

children.text: yatra kṣetre sthitaṃ caiva vaikrāntaṃ tatra bhairavam
children.translated_text: In whatever field <s>vaikrānta</s> is found, there one should worship <s>Bhairava</s>
and <s>Vināyaka</s>, and then, with a purified mind, take it up.
<s>Vaikrānta</s>, resembling diamond, is considered to effect the body and metals.
It destroys poison, is a king among rasas, and drives away fever, skin disease, and wasting disease.

children.text: vaikrāntakāḥ syustridinaṃ viśuddhāḥ saṃsveditāḥ kṣārapaṭūni dattvā
children.translated_text: Pieces of <s>vaikrānta</s> become purified in three days when steamed after alkalis and salts have been added,
cooked in sour liquids, urines, kulattha decoction, plantain water, or else kodrava water.
<s>Vaikrānta</s> steamed in a decoction of kulattha becomes purified.
It is incinerated with eight <s>puṭa</s>s when combined with sulfur and citron juice.
When the pieces of <s>vaikrānta</s> are heated, one should pour horse urine upon them;

children.text: paunaḥpunyena vā kuryāddravaṃ dattvā puṭaṃ tvanu
children.translated_text: or one should do this again and again, then apply a liquid and afterward give a <s>puṭa</s>.
When <s>vaikrānta</s> has become ash, it should be employed in place of diamond.
It is impregnated with the alkalis of mocā, moraṭa, and palāśa, and with cow urine,
and combined with paste of vajrakanda and niśā and with fruit powder.
That paste, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, lac powder, and material produced from <s>vaikrānta</s>,
mixed with <s>navasāra</s> and furnished with the juice of meṣaśṛṅgī,
is made into a lump, placed in a sealed crucible, and blown with intense fire.

children.text: tatraiva patate sattvaṃ vaikrāntasya na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There the <s>sattva</s> of <s>vaikrānta</s> settles out; there is no doubt.
By the procedure for precipitating <s>sattva</s>, when it has been ground and made into pills,
<s>vaikrānta</s>, placed in a crucible and blown for a ghaṭikā, releases its <s>sattva</s>.

children.text: bhasmatvaṃ samupāgato vikṛtako hemnā mṛtenānvitaḥ pādāṃśena kaṇājyavellasahito guñjāmitaḥ sevitaḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>vaikrānta</s> has reached the state of ash, is combined with incinerated gold, mixed with a quarter part of kaṇā, ghee, and vella, and taken in a guñjā measure,

children.text: yakṣmāṇaṃ jaraṇaṃ ca pāṇḍugudajaṃ śvāsaṃ ca kāsāmayaṃ duṣṭāṃ ca grahaṇīm uraḥkṣatamukhān rogāñjayed dehakṛt ||
children.translated_text: it conquers consumption, wasting, anemia, hemorrhoids, asthma, cough disorders, bad grahaṇī, chest wounds, and other such diseases, and it builds up the body.
Blue <s>vaikrānta</s> ash, mixed with half as much ash of sūta,
and incinerated mica-sattva, weighed equal to the two and thoroughly ground,
combined with honey and ghee and consumed in the morning in a guñjā measure,
destroys all diseases that are hard to conquer by other medicines,
within three times seven days, as <s>Gaṅgā</s> water destroys sin among men.
The golden rasa, produced from the golden mountain by <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
is made in Tāpī, among the <s>Kirāta</s>s, the <s>Cīna</s>s, and the <s>Yavana</s>s.
<s>Tāpya</s>, heated by the rays of the sun, is seen in the month of <s>Mādhava</s>.
It is sweet and has the appearance of gold; another is slightly sour and resembles silver.
It is somewhat astringent and sweet, cooling, pungent in digestion, and light.
By using it, one is not overcome by old age, disease, or poisons.
<s>Mākṣika</s> is of two kinds: gold <s>mākṣika</s> and silver <s>mākṣika</s>.
Of these, the first <s>mākṣika</s>, produced in <s>Kānyakubja</s>, resembles gold.
That which arises on the bank of the <s>Tapatī</s> is like five-colored gold;
the one called silver, full of stone, is said to have little virtue.

children.text: mākṣīkadhātuḥ sakalāmayaghnaḥ prāṇo rasendrasya paraṃ hi vṛṣyaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣika</s> ore destroys every disease; it is the very life of rasendra and is supremely aphrodisiac.
It joins two metals that are difficult to combine, is superior in virtues, and is foremost among all <s>rasāyana</s>s.
<s>Mākṣika</s> is purified when cooked with castor oil and citron water,
or when cooked for two ghaṭikās with water from the plantain bulb.
When heated and thrown into a decoction of varā, <s>mākṣika</s> attains purification.
Ground with citron water and sulfur and placed inside a crucible,
burned with five kroḍa-<s>puṭa</s>s, <s>mākṣika</s> is indeed incinerated.
With castor oil, cow's ghee, or citron juice,
cooked firmly in a potsherd, it becomes like metal.

children.text: evaṃ mṛtaṃ rase yojyaṃ rasāyanavidhāv api ||
children.translated_text: Thus incinerated, it should be applied in rasa and also in the rasāyana procedure.
Combined with one thirtieth part of <s>nāga</s>, and treated with alkalis and acids,
when blown in an open crucible, <s>mākṣika</s> releases its <s>sattva</s>.
After being liquefied seven times and cast into the juice of nirguṇḍikā,
<s>nāga</s> mixed with <s>mākṣika</s>-sattva certainly disappears.
With honey and castor oil, with cow urine and ghee,
<s>mākṣika</s>, repeatedly impregnated with the essence of plantain bulb,

children.text: mūṣāyāṃ muñcati dhmātaṃ sattvaṃ śulbanibhaṃ mṛdu ||
children.translated_text: when blown in a crucible, releases a soft <s>sattva</s> resembling copper.
It has the color of a guñjā seed, melts quickly, and is cooling.
That purified <s>tāpya</s>-sattva is supreme for effecting the body and metals.

children.text: mākṣīkasattvena rasendrapiṣṭaṃ kṛtvā vilīne ca baliṃ nidhāya
children.translated_text: Having made rasendra ground with <s>mākṣika</s>-sattva, and, when it is melted, placing the bali...

children.text: saṃmiśrya saṃmardya ca khalvamadhye nikṣipya sattvaṃ drutimabhrakasya ||
children.translated_text: Having mixed and ground them together, one should place the essence and the liquefied <s>abhraka</s> in the mortar.

children.text: vidhāya golaṃ lavaṇākhyayantre paceddinārdhaṃ mṛduvahninā ca
children.translated_text: After making a ball, one should cook it in the apparatus called the salt-apparatus for half a day with a gentle fire.
When it has become quite cool by itself, one should powder it properly; measured by the <s>valla</s>, it is combined with <s>vyoṣa</s> and <s>viḍaṅga</s>.

children.text: saṃsevitaṃ kṣaudrayutaṃ nihanti jarāṃ sarogāṃ tvapamṛtyumeva
children.translated_text: Taken with honey, it destroys old age accompanied by disease and indeed untimely death.
It destroys even diseases hard to cure in seven days; not even the nectar-elixir is equal to this.
With oil produced from castor, together with <s>guñjā</s>, honey, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>,

children.text: marditaṃ tasya vāpena sattvaṃ mākṣīkajaṃ dravet ||
children.translated_text: when it has been triturated, by its vapor the essence born from <s>mākṣīka</s> melts.
<s>Vimala</s> is said to be of three kinds: the first is golden, the next is silvery,
and the third is bronze-<s>vimala</s>; it is recognized by each corresponding luster.
It is round, furnished with angles, smooth, and provided with plates.
<s>Vimala</s> alleviates <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>, is aphrodisiac, and is an excellent <s>rasāyana</s>.
The first is said to be suitable for work with gold; the second is regarded as producing silver.
The third is for medicines; among these, each preceding one is superior in qualities.
<s>Vimala</s> steamed in water of <s>āṭarūṣa</s> becomes pure <s>vimala</s>.
Steamed in the juice of <s>jambīra</s>, or else in the juice of <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s>,

children.text: āyāti śuddhiṃ vimalo dhātavaśca yathā pare ||
children.translated_text: <s>vimala</s> attains purification, as do the other metals.
It is incinerated with sulphur, stone, and the acids of <s>lakuca</s> by ten <s>puṭa</s> firings.
With liquids of <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> and <s>lakuca</s>, and with the ash of <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s>,

children.text: piṣṭo mūṣodare liptaḥ saṃśoṣya ca nirudhya ca ||
children.translated_text: it is ground, smeared inside a crucible, dried, and sealed.
Blown with six <s>prastha</s>s of <s>kokila</s> charcoal, <s>vimala</s>, resembling lead,

children.text: sattvaṃ muñcati tadyukto rasaḥ syātsa rasāyanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: releases its essence; mercury joined with that becomes a <s>rasāyana</s>.
<s>Vimala</s> with water of <s>śigru</s>, <s>kāṅkṣī</s>, <s>kāsīsa</s>, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>,
combined with <s>vajrakanda</s> and imbued with the juices of banana,
mixed with the alkali of <s>mokṣaka</s> and heated by blowing in a blind crucible,
yields an essence with the appearance of moon and sun; there is no doubt about this.
That essence, mixed with mercury, should be made into a paste and very thoroughly triturated.
Having cast it into melted sulphur, one should digest three times as much <s>alaka</s>.
And also five times as much <s>śilā</s> in a sand apparatus,
with one-tenth part ash of silver and the same amount of incinerated <s>vaikrāntaka</s>.
One should powder everything together and filter it through cloth.
Then, placing it inside a bottle, one should fill it carefully.

children.text: līḍho vyoṣavarānvito vimalako yukto ghṛtaiḥ sevito hanyāddurbhagakṛjjvarāñśvayathukaṃ pāṇḍupramehārucīḥ
children.translated_text: This <s>vimala</s> preparation, licked with <s>vyoṣa</s> and <s>varā</s>, combined with ghee and taken, destroys fevers that cause misfortune, swelling, anemia, urinary disorders, and lack of appetite.

children.text: mūlārtiṃ grahaṇīṃ ca śūlamatulaṃ yakṣmāmayaṃ kāmalāṃ sarvānpittamarudgadānkimaparairyogairaśeṣāmayān ||
children.translated_text: It destroys pain at the root, <s>grahaṇī</s>, unequalled colic, consumption, jaundice, and all disorders of <s>pitta</s> and <s>vāta</s>; what need is there of other formulations? It removes every disease.
<s>Śilādhātu</s> is said to be of two kinds: the first, beginning with cow's urine, is a <s>rasāyana</s>.
Another begins with camphor; of these, the first again is twofold:
with essence and without essence; of the two, the former is superior in qualities.
In summer, from the feet of the snowy mountains heated by the fierce sun,
<s>śilādhātu</s> flows out from deposits containing gold, silver, and copper.
That born from a gold-bearing mountain resembles a hibiscus flower, is heavy,
slightly bitter and very sweet; it is the supreme <s>rasāyana</s>.
That born from a silver-bearing mountain is sweet, pale, and heavy.
This rock-born substance destroys <s>pitta</s> disorders and especially removes anemia.
That born from a copper-bearing mountain is blue in color, compact, and heavy.
This rock-born substance alleviates <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>, is bitter and hot, and removes wasting disease.
When it is thrown into fire, if it becomes shaped like a <s>liṅga</s> and produces no smoke,

children.text: salile 'tha vilīnaṃ ca tacchuddhaṃ hi śilājatu ||
children.translated_text: and then dissolves in water, that indeed is pure <s>śilājatu</s>.

children.text: nūnaṃ sajvarapāṇḍuśophaśamanaṃ mehāgnimāndyāpahaṃ medaśchedakaraṃ ca yakṣmaśamanaṃ śūlāmayonmūlanam
children.translated_text: Surely it pacifies fever, anemia, and swelling, removes urinary disorders and weak digestion, cuts away fat, pacifies consumption, and uproots colic diseases.

children.text: gulmaplīhavināśanaṃ jaṭharahṛcchūlaghnamāmāpahaṃ sarvatvaggadanāśanaṃ kimaparaṃ dehe ca lohe hitam ||
children.translated_text: It destroys abdominal tumors and spleen disease, removes abdominal ailments, cures colic, removes undigested matter, and destroys every disease of the skin; what more? It is beneficial for the body and for metal.
Whatever qualities there are in <s>rasa</s>, subsidiary minerals, mercury, jewels, and metals,
they dwell in <s>śilādhātu</s>, for the sake of conquering old age and death.
<s>Śilājatu</s> is certainly purified when washed with alkalis, acids, and cow's water.
Putting <s>śilādhātu</s> in an iron vessel with milk and with liquids such as <s>triphala</s> and <s>arka</s>,
one should purify it with the greatest care.
When placed in a steaming apparatus with alkalis, acids, and <s>guggulu</s>,
and steamed for the measure of a <s>ghaṭikā</s>, <s>śilādhātu</s> becomes thoroughly purified.
With <s>śilā</s>, sulphur, <s>tāla</s>, and the juice of citron,
<s>śilādhātu</s>, when fired in a <s>puṭa</s>, is incinerated by eight <s>giriṇḍaka</s>s.

children.text: bhasmībhūtaśilodbhavaṃ samatulaṃ kāntaṃ ca vaikrāntakaṃ yuktaṃ ca triphalākaṭutrikaghṛtairvallena tulyaṃ bhajet
children.translated_text: One should take, in a quantity equal to a <s>valla</s>, the ash of the mountain-born substance, an equal amount of <s>kānta</s> and <s>vaikrāntaka</s>, together with <s>triphala</s>, the three pungents, and ghee.

children.text: pāṇḍau yakṣmagade tathāgnisadane meheṣu mūlāmaye gulmaplīhamahodare bahuvidhe śūle ca yonyāmaye ||
children.translated_text: It is to be used for anemia, wasting disease, weakness of digestion, urinary disorders, disease at the root, abdominal tumors, spleen disease, great abdominal enlargement, many kinds of colic, and diseases of the womb.
If one should take it for six months according to the <s>rasāyana</s> regimen,
free from wrinkles and gray hair, one would live happily for a hundred years.
The mountain-born substance is ground with the acidic substances of the dissolving class.

children.text: kṣiptvā mūṣodare ruddhvā gāḍhairdhmātaṃ hi kokilaiḥ
children.translated_text: After placing it inside a crucible and sealing it, it is strongly blown with <s>kokila</s> coals.
<s>Śilādhātu</s> releases an essence, resembling iron, through the blasts.
The camphor-type <s>śilājatu</s> is pale and sand-like.
It destroys dysuria, urinary stone, urinary disorders, jaundice, and anemia.
When broken up with cardamom water and cooked, it attains purification.
The wise have not prescribed calcination or extraction of <s>sattva</s> for this.
After drinking the hālāhala poison, <s>Garutmat</s>, who had drunk nectar, vomited it out.
On the mountain called <s>Marakata</s>, that poison was joined with nectar.

children.text: tadvāntaṃ hi ghanībhūtaṃ saṃjātaṃ sasyakaṃ khalu ||
children.translated_text: That vomited substance, having solidified, indeed became sasyaka.
It is especially praised when it has the true luster of a peacock's neck and is heavy in weight.
Whatever substance is joined with poison becomes greater in virtue than that substance itself.
So too hālāhala joined with nectar becomes greater in virtue than nectar.
It removes every fault and poison, disease, colic, piles, skin disease, sour bilious disorders, and constipation, and is supreme.

children.text: rasāyanaṃ vamanarekakaraṃ garaghnaṃ śvitrāpahaṃ gaditamatra mayūratuttham ||
children.translated_text: Here mayūratuttha is declared to be a <s>rasāyana</s>, to cause vomiting and purging, to destroy artificial poison, and to remove white leprosy.
Sasyaka obtains purification when it has been impregnated with the group of red substances.
Sprinkled with the group of unctuous substances seven times, it becomes uncontaminated.
Sasyaka, well steamed in a swing-apparatus for three watches of the day,
is purified in cow, buffalo, and goat urine, as is pañcakharpara.
Combined with the juice of lakuca, gandhāśma, and borax,
and sealed inside a crucible, it is calcined by cock-type <s>puṭa</s> firings.
The powder of sasyaka should be combined with one quarter part of saubhāgya.
It should be kept for one day within karañja oil.
Placed inside a blind crucible-mouth, it should be blown for three kokilas.
Then an excellent <s>sattva</s>, with the appearance of indragopa insects, is produced.
Having sealed it inside a crucible with lemon juice and a little borax,
when strongly blown, sasyaka releases <s>sattva</s> resembling copper.
Purified sasyaka, covered with śilā and combined with the previously mentioned medicines,
surely releases its <s>sattva</s> by various procedures.
Having taken this <s>sattva</s>, which consumes the <s>sattva</s> of khara and bhūnāga,
a ring made from it, by mere contact, becomes a remover of colic at once.
It conquers poison from moving and unmoving sources, and poison caused by beings, ḍākinīs, or the evil eye.
This ring should be made; it produces results that have been directly observed.
The syllables, such as 'rāmavat somasenānīḥ,' are also to be sealed in the ring.
On the northern side of the <s>Himālaya</s> there is a great tree called aśvakarṇa.

children.text: tatra śūlaṃ samutpannaṃ tatraiva vilayaṃ gatam ||
children.translated_text: There colic arose, and there itself it disappeared.
Water from the ring, enchanted seven times with this mantra and drunk,
is said to remove colic immediately; so <s>Bhāluki</s> has stated.
Oil thoroughly heated by means of this ring in the fire,

children.text: lepitaṃ hanti vegena śūlaṃ yatra kvacidbhavet
children.translated_text: when smeared on, swiftly destroys colic wherever it may be.
It immediately causes delivery for a woman and immediately removes pain of the eyes.
Capala is fourfold: pale, white, red, and black.
It also has a golden sheen or a silvery sheen, and is especially a binder of mercury.

children.text: śeṣau tu madhyau lākṣāvacchīghradrāvau tu niṣphalau
children.translated_text: The remaining two middle kinds, like lac, are quick to melt but fruitless.
Since capala melts in fire like tin, it is so called.
Capala is held to be scraping and unctuous, and to make body and metals fit for transformation.
It is an aid to the king of metals, mercury, and is considered bitter, hot, and sweet.
Capala has the luster of crystal, is six-angled, unctuous, and heavy.
It removes the three doṣas, is highly virilizing, and brings about the binding of mercury.
Some authorities have counted capala among the great minerals.
Capala is purified through impregnations with <s>jambīra</s>, karkoṭaka, and ginger.

children.text: śailaṃ tu cūrṇayitvā tu dhānyāmlopaviṣair viṣaiḥ
children.translated_text: Having pulverized the mineral, with sour grain-gruel, lesser poisons, and poisons,
one should bind it into a lump in the prescribed manner and likewise cause the capala to fall.
Rasaka is declared to be of two kinds: durdura and kāravellaka.
Durdura is said to be furnished with layers, while kāravellaka is without layers.
The first is good for extraction of <s>sattva</s>; the second is good in medicines and the like.
Rasaka removes all urinary disorders and destroys kapha and pitta.
It removes eye disease and wasting, and it colors iron and mercury.
Both mercury and rasaka were taught by <s>Nāgārjuna</s>.
The two are known as excellent perfected rasas, supreme for transforming body and metals.
For the one by whom both mercury and rasaka have been made able to endure fire,
perfection in body and metals is his servant; of this there is no doubt.
One should stir rasaka in the sap of bitter bottle-gourd and cook it.
Purified and freed from faults, it becomes yellow in color.
Kharpara, thoroughly heated and immersed seven times
in the juice of bījapūra, attains purity.

children.text: nṛmūtre vāśvamūtre vā takre vā kāñjike 'thavā
children.translated_text: Or, heated and immersed properly in human urine, horse urine, buttermilk,
or else sour gruel, kharpara is purified.
Rasaka kept for a month in human urine will certainly color
purified copper, mercury, and silver so that they shine like purified gold.
With turmeric, <s>triphalā</s>, ārālā, salt fumes, and borax,
with marking-nut in quarter portions and with sour substances, one should rub kharpara.
Smeared on an eggplant crucible, dried, and sealed,
one should place kharpara over the mouth of the crucible and then blow upon it.

children.text: kharpare prahṛte jvālā bhavennīlā sitā yadi
children.translated_text: When the kharpara is struck, if a blue and white flame appears,

children.text: tadā saṃdaṃśato mūṣāṃ dhṛtvā kṛtvā tvadhomukhīm ||
children.translated_text: then, holding the crucible with tongs and turning it face downward,
one should strike it gently on the ground so that the tube is not broken.
One should collect the fallen <s>sattva</s>, which resembles tin, and apply it.
Thus, in three or four repetitions, all the <s>sattva</s> will issue forth.
With myrobalan, lac, bhūnāga, turmeric fumes, and borax,
when blown inside a dumb crucible, it releases pure <s>sattva</s>.
With lac, jaggery, <s>asurī</s>, <s>pathyā</s>, turmeric, resin, and borax,
having thoroughly powdered them, one should cook that with cow's milk and ghee.
Enclosing it in pill form inside a brinjal-shaped crucible,
one should blow it again and again, draw it out, and cast it on a stone slab;
one should take the beautiful <s>sattva</s> (essence) of <s>rasaka</s>, having the form of tin.
Or one should bury a pot filled with water in the belly of the furnace,
place a perforated vessel at its mouth, and put an inverted crucible at that opening.
Above the crucible one should place fuel and blow strongly.
The <s>sattva</s> that has fallen into the water of the pot should be taken and employed.
Putting that <s>sattva</s>, together with <s>tālaka</s>, into a potsherd,
one should grind it with an iron rod; it certainly becomes ash.
That ash should be combined with an equal amount of incinerated <s>kānta</s> iron,
and an eight-<s>guñjā</s> measure of the powder should be joined with a decoction of <s>triphalā</s>.
Kept at night in a <s>kānta</s> vessel, with sesame-born oil as an admixture,
when used, it quickly and certainly destroys even <s>madhumeha</s> (diabetes).

children.text: pittaṃ kṣayaṃ ca pāṇḍuṃ ca śvayathuṃ gulmameva ca
children.translated_text: It also removes bilious disorder, wasting, anemia, swelling, and <s>gulma</s>,
as well as bloody <s>gulma</s> in women, vaginal discharge, and <s>somaroga</s>.
It removes all diseases of the womb and vagina, and irregular fevers too,

children.text: rajaḥśūlaṃ ca nārīṇāṃ kāsaṃ śvāsaṃ ca hidhmikām ||
children.translated_text: menstrual pain in women, cough, dyspnea, and hiccup.
<s>Gandhāśma</s>, red chalk, <s>āsīsaka</s>, <s>kāṅkṣī</s>, <s>tāla</s>, and <s>śilāñjana</s>,
and <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>: these are the eight <s>uparasas</s> (secondary minerals) in the work of mercury.
<s>Pārvatī</s> said:

children.text: gandhakasya tu māhātmyaṃ tadguhyaṃ vada me prabho ||
children.translated_text: Tell me, lord, the greatness of sulfur, that secret matter.
<s>Īśvara</s> said:
Long ago, goddess, on <s>Śvetadvīpa</s>, adorned with every jewel,
on the lovely shore of the Milk Ocean, which grants every desire,
with foremost women beginning with the <s>Vidyādharas</s>, and with women of the yogins,
with excellent perfected women and likewise with hosts of apsarases,
with charming divine women, in delightful play,
with songs, varied dances, and many kinds of instruments,
as you were thus sporting, menstrual fluid flowed forth.
That menstrual fluid, O fair-hipped one, was exceedingly fragrant and very beautiful.
Because of the great abundance of that blood, your garment became red;

children.text: tatra tyaktvā tu tadvastraṃ susnātā kṣīrasāgare ||
children.translated_text: leaving that garment there, you bathed well in the Milk Ocean.
Surrounded by divine women, you returned again to <s>Kailāsa</s>;
by the waves, that blood-stained garment was carried into the middle of the ocean.

children.text: evaṃ te śoṇitaṃ bhadre praviṣṭaṃ kṣīrasāgare
children.translated_text: Thus your blood, auspicious one, entered the Milk Ocean,
and at the churning of the Milk Ocean it arose together with the nectar.
By its own fragrance it delighted all those <s>Dānavas</s>,
and then the hosts of gods said, 'Let this be called <s>gandhaka</s>.'
Let it serve for the binding of mercury and for its digestion;

children.text: ye guṇāḥ pārade proktāste caivātra bhavantviti ||
children.translated_text: let the very qualities declared for <s>pārada</s> be present here also.

children.text: iti devagaṇaiḥ prītaiḥ purā proktaṃ sureśvari
children.translated_text: Thus, O queen of the gods, it was formerly declared by the delighted hosts of gods;
therefore this is renowned on the surface of the earth by the name <s>gandhaka</s>.

children.text: sa cāpi trividho devi śukacañcunibho varaḥ
children.translated_text: And it is threefold, goddess: the best resembles a parrot's beak;
the middling kind is yellow in color, and the inferior is white, dear one.

children.text: caturdhā gandhako jñeyo varṇaiḥ śvetādibhiḥ khalu
children.translated_text: Sulfur should indeed be known as fourfold by colors such as white and the rest.
Here the white is called <s>khaṭikā</s>, used for smearing and for incinerating metals.
Likewise there is <s>amalasāra</s>, which is yellow in color;
that very one is <s>śukapiccha</s>, best in mercurial <s>rasāyana</s>.
The red kind, called <s>śukatuṇḍa</s>, is excellent in the procedure of metal transmutation;
the black-colored kind is rare and destroys old age and death.

children.text: gandhāśmātirasāyanaḥ sumadhuraḥ pāke kaṭūṣṇo mataḥ kaṇḍūkuṣṭhavisarpadadrudalano dīptānalaḥ pācanaḥ
children.translated_text: Sulfur is an excellent <s>rasāyana</s>, very sweet, considered pungent and hot after digestion; it breaks itching, skin disease, erysipelas, and ringworm, kindles the digestive fire, and promotes digestion.

children.text: āmonmocanaśoṣaṇo viṣaharaḥ sūtendravīryaprado gaurīpuṣpabhavastathā kṛmiharaḥ satyātmakaḥ sūtajit ||
children.translated_text: It removes <s>āma</s>, dries, counteracts poison, gives potency to lordly mercury, is born from <s>Gaurī</s>'s flower, kills worms, is true in nature, and conquers mercury.
Formerly it was consumed by <s>Bali</s> as a cause of abundant strength.
As he dragged <s>Vāsuki</s>, melted by the flame from his mouth,
fat rich with the odor of sulfur flowed out everywhere from his body.
It attained the state of sulfur, and the odor was remembered as poisonous;
therefore the exceedingly beautiful sulfur is called <s>Bali</s>'s fat.
Sulfur steamed in milk for one <s>ghaṭī</s> and washed with water,
melted in cow's ghee and filtered through cloth, attains purification.

children.text: evaṃ saṃśodhitaḥ so 'yaṃ pāṣāṇān ambare tyajet
children.translated_text: When purified in this way, it should leave stones behind in the cloth;

children.text: ghṛte viṣaṃ tuṣākāraṃ svayaṃ piṇḍatvameva ca ||
children.translated_text: in the ghee it leaves poison, husk-like matter, and its own lumpiness.

children.text: iti śuddho hi gandhāśmā nāpathyairvikṛtiṃ vrajet
children.translated_text: Thus purified, <s>gandhāśma</s> does not become altered through unsuitable foods;
otherwise, because of unsuitable foods, when drunk it kills like <s>hālāhala</s> poison.
Sulfur, melted and thrown into the juice of <s>bhṛṅga</s>, is purified;
when split seven times with those juices, sulfur becomes fully purified.

children.text: sthālyāṃ dugdhaṃ vinikṣipya mukhe vastraṃ nibadhya ca
children.translated_text: Having placed milk in a pot and tied cloth over its mouth,
one should place there sulfur powdered like sand.
One should cover the sulfur with a broad and long potsherd,
and kindle fire above the potsherd with forest dung-cakes and likewise with dried dung fuel.
The sulfur, melted and fallen into the milk, becomes purified;

children.text: śatavāraṃ kṛtaṃ caiva nirgandho jāyate dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: when this is done a hundred times, it surely becomes odorless.
Thus, when thoroughly purified and mixed with <s>triphalā</s>, ghee, <s>bhṛṅga</s>, and honey, it is licked in a <s>śāṇa</s> measure.
It makes the pair of eyes like those of a vulture and grants a long life free from disease.
Sulfur, mixed with a kalā portion of <s>vyosha</s> and ground to a fine powder,

children.text: aratnimātre vastre tad viprakīrya viveṣṭya tat ||
children.translated_text: should be scattered over a cloth measuring an <s>aratni</s>, and that should be wrapped up.
After wrapping it with thread, one should immerse it in oil for a <s>yāma</s>.
Then, holding the middle of the wick with tongs, one should light it.
The sulfur, when melted, falls drop by drop into a glass vessel.

children.text: tāṃ drutiṃ prakṣipet pattre nāgavallyās tribindukām
children.translated_text: One should put three drops of that melt onto a leaf of <s>nāgavallī</s>,

children.text: vallena pramitaṃ svacchaṃ sūtendraṃ ca vimardayet ||
children.translated_text: and triturate it with clear king-mercury measured by a <s>valla</s>.

children.text: aṅgulyātha sapattrāṃ tāṃ drutiṃ sūtaṃ ca bhakṣayet
children.translated_text: Then one should eat that melt, together with the leaf and the mercury, with the finger.

children.text: karoti dīpanaṃ tīvraṃ kṣayaṃ pāṇḍuṃ ca nāśayet ||
children.translated_text: It produces a powerful stimulation of digestion and destroys consumption and anemia.
It also destroys cough, dyspnea, colic pain, and very hard-to-subdue <s>grahaṇī</s>,
and it quickly destroys <s>āma</s> and produces lightness.
Purified sulfur, melted in an iron vessel smeared with ghee,
and poured with a ghee-smeared ladle, should be consumed in a measure of two <s>niṣka</s>s.
It destroys diseases headed by consumption, and especially the disease of <s>kuṣṭha</s>.
During the use of purified sulfur one should avoid alkalis, sour foods, oils, <s>sauvīra</s>, heating foods,
and also pulses, while following the proper regimen.
Sulfur equal in amount to black pepper and combined with six times as much <s>triphala</s>,
ground with the root of <s>śamyāka</s> and drunk, destroys every kind of <s>kuṣṭha</s>.
The same root, ground in water, should be applied every day to the body.
This is a tested formula, effective everywhere with counteracting potency,
and it has been properly proclaimed here by the illustrious <s>Somadeva</s>.
Having ground sulfur measured at two <s>niṣka</s>s and mixed it with oil,
then with water of <s>apāmārga</s>, and likewise with oil and pepper,

children.text: vilipya sakalaṃ dehaṃ tiṣṭhedgharme tataḥ param
children.translated_text: one should smear the whole body and then stand in the sun.

children.text: takrabhaktaṃ ca bhuñjīta tṛtīye prahare khalu ||
children.translated_text: In the third watch one should eat rice with buttermilk.

children.text: bhajedrātrau tathā vahniṃ samutthāya tathā prage
children.translated_text: At night one should tend the fire, and then, rising early in the morning,
one should smear oneself with buffalo dung and bathe with cold water.
Then, after anointing the body with ghee, one should bathe with suitably warm water.
By this ordered procedure there is destroyed with great speed,
certainly, stubborn, long-standing <s>pāmā</s> and itching.
The hundred applications of sulfur have not been set forth
by king <s>Somadeva</s>, because he feared an expansion of the treatise.
Alternatively, a cloth should be smeared seven times with the milks of <s>arka</s> and <s>snuhī</s>.
After grinding sulfur with fresh butter, one should smear the cloth thickly.

children.text: tadvartiṃ jvalitāṃ daṃśe dhṛtāṃ kuryād adhomukhīm
children.translated_text: One should make that burning wick, held in tongs, face downward.
The oil falls into the vessel below; it should be collected and employed in preparations.
Purified sulfur removes diseases such as <s>kuṣṭha</s>, death, and old age.
It kindles digestion, is very hot, and increases virility.
There are two kinds: stone <s>gairika</s> and, secondly, golden <s>gairika</s>.
Stone <s>gairika</s> is said to be hard and copper-colored.
Golden <s>gairika</s> is extremely red, unctuous, and smooth.

children.text: svādu snigdhaṃ himaṃ netryaṃ kaṣāyaṃ raktapittanut
children.translated_text: Golden <s>gairika</s> is sweet, unctuous, cooling, beneficial to the eyes, astringent, and removes <s>raktapitta</s>.
It destroys hiccup, vomiting, and poison, and it checks bleeding.
The other, stone <s>gairika</s>, has qualities inferior to the former.

children.text: gairikaṃ tu gavāṃ dugdhairbhāvitaṃ śuddhim ṛcchati ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gairika</s>, when impregnated with cow's milk, attains purification.
<s>Gairika</s> in the form of <s>sattva</s> has been described by <s>Nandin</s>.
Some say that the <s>sattva</s> falls from <s>gairika</s> moistened with alkalis and acids,
and that, serving king-mercury, it reaches a more excellent union and quality.
<s>Kāsīsa</s> is one kind as <s>vālukā</s>, and another as that beginning with <s>puṣpa</s>.
<s>Vālukā-puṣpa-kāsīsa</s>, resembling the smoke of alkali, acid, and agaru, has hot potency and removes poison.
It destroys leukoderma and colors the hair.
The <s>kāsīsa</s> beginning with <s>puṣpa</s> is very excellent, hot, astringent and sour, and highly beneficial to the eyes.
It destroys poison, diseases of wind and phlegm, wounds, leukoderma, and consumption, and it colors the hair.
<s>Kāsīsa</s> becomes stainless when moistened once with juice of <s>bhṛṅga</s>.
Its <s>sattva</s> too should be extracted just as in the case of <s>tuvarī-sattva</s>.
<s>Kāsīsa</s> attains purification also through bile and a woman's menstrual blood.
Strong incinerated <s>kāsīsa</s> and penetrated, killed <s>kāsīsa</s>,
both in equal parts and combined with <s>triphala</s> and <s>vella</s>,
soaked in unequal portions of ghee and honey, should be taken in the morning in a <s>śāṇa</s> measure.
Used in this way, it quickly destroys leukoderma, anemia, and wasting disease.
It destroys abdominal tumors, spleen disease, colic, and especially disease of the rectum,
when used for a full year according to the <s>rasāyana</s> procedure.
It is excellent for drying up <s>āma</s> and for kindling weak digestion.
It certainly destroys grey hair together with wrinkles.
That <s>tuvarī</s> is regarded as born from stone in <s>Saurāṣṭra</s>.
It is applied to cloth, where it fixes the color of madder dye.
A second kind is called <s>phaṭakī</s> and <s>phullikā</s>.
The yellowish kind is heavy and unctuous; <s>pītikā</s> destroys poison.
It removes wounds and <s>kuṣṭha</s>, and especially destroys all kinds of <s>kuṣṭha</s>.

children.text: nirbhārā śubhravarṇā ca snigdhā sāmlāparā matā
children.translated_text: Another is considered light, white in color, unctuous, and slightly sour.
That is called <s>phulla-tuvarī</s>; by application it makes copper, and also iron, act.

children.text: kāṅkṣī kaṣāyā kaṭukāmlakaṇṭhyā keśyā vraṇaghnī viṣanāśanī ca
children.translated_text: <s>Kāṅkṣī</s> is astringent, pungent, sour, beneficial to the throat, good for the hair, wound-healing, and poison-destroying.
It removes leukoderma, is beneficial to the eyes, brings pacification of the three doṣas, and digests mercury.
Tuvarī, when put into sour gruel, obtains purification after three days.

children.text: kṣārāmlair marditā dhmātā sattvaṃ muñcati niścitam ||
children.translated_text: Rubbed with alkaline and sour substances and blown upon, it certainly releases <s>sattva</s> (extractable essence).
Then one should impregnate saurāṣṭrā a hundred times with cow bile.
After blowing it, one should cause the <s>sattva</s> to fall; the krāmaṇa procedure is extremely secret.
Haritāla is declared to be of two kinds: the first is leafy, and the other is called lump-like.

children.text: svarṇavarṇaṃ guru snigdhaṃ tanupattraṃ ca bhāsuram
children.translated_text: Golden in color, heavy, unctuous, thin-leaved, and shining,
that is called leaf-haritāla, having many leaves and useful as a rasāyana.
The leafless kind, resembling a lump, has little <s>sattva</s> and is likewise heavy.
It removes women's menstrual flow; that lump-haritāla has few virtues.
It removes phlegm, blood disorders, poison, wind, and afflictions by beings, and indeed it stops women's menstrual flow.
Haritāla is said to be unctuous, hot, pungent, digestive-kindling, and a remover of skin disease.

children.text: snigdhaṃ kūṣmāṇḍatoye vā tilakṣārajale api vā
children.translated_text: Being unctuous, it is purified in the water of kūṣmāṇḍa, or in water with sesame alkali,
or in water mixed with powders, by means of a dolāyantra.
Unpurified tāla destroys life and causes kapha, vāta, and urinary disorders.
It produces burning, eruptions, and contraction of the limbs; therefore one should purify it.

children.text: tālakaṃ kaṇaśaḥ kṛtvā daśāṃśena ca ṭaṅkaṇam
children.translated_text: Having made tālaka into small particles, and adding borax as a tenth part,
one should wash it with liquids produced from jambīra and then wash it with sour gruels.

children.text: vastre caturguṇe baddhvā dolāyantre dinaṃ pacet
children.translated_text: Having tied it in cloth folded four times, one should cook it for a day in a dolāyantra.
With sour gruel mixed with powders for a day, and in the juice produced from kūṣmāṇḍa,
or it should be steamed with waters of śālmalī; tālaka obtains purification.
When a decoction made from brahmamūla has become thick like honey,

children.text: trivāraṃ tālakaṃ bhāvyaṃ piṣṭvā mūtre 'tha māhiṣe ||
children.translated_text: the tālaka should be impregnated three times with it, after being ground in buffalo urine.
A sealed heating should be given with ten cow-dung cakes, and then it should be ground.

children.text: evaṃ dvādaśadhā pācyaṃ śuddhaṃ yogeṣu yojayet ||
children.translated_text: Cooked in this way twelve times, it is purified and should be used in preparations.
With a decoction of kulattha, saubhāgya, buffalo ghee, and honey poured over it,

children.text: sthālyāṃ kṣiptvā vidadhyācca tv amlena chidrayoginā ||
children.translated_text: one should place it in a pot and then fit it with a perforated device using a sour liquid.
Having sealed it properly, one should kindle the fire, gradually increased,
for the measure of one prahara, covering the hole with cow dung.

children.text: yāmānte chidramudghāṭya dṛṣṭe dhūme ca pāṇḍure
children.translated_text: At the end of a yāma, having opened the hole and seen pale smoke,
one should remove the cooled pot, draw out the <s>sattva</s>, and take it.
There are countless methods for all mineral <s>sattvas</s>.
From fear of expanding the book, I have not written them down.
One should rub palālaka for one day with the milks of the sun-plant.
Having put it into one-sixteenth measure of oil and mixed it, one should then cook it.
Certainly in an uncovered place for the duration of seven yāmas,
when it has cooled by itself, one should collect the white <s>sattva</s> below.
Then, with the hair of a strong young goat
one should rub tālaka for two days with the utmost care.
Combined with the group of melting substances, one should put it into a glass bottle.

children.text: tridhā tāṃ ca mṛdā liptvā pariśoṣya kharātape ||
children.translated_text: Having smeared that bottle three times with clay and dried it in fierce sunlight,
then one should insert half of that bottle into a hole in a potsherd
and kindle the fire for twelve praharas.
One should collect the cool, pure <s>sattva</s> situated in the neck of the bottle.

children.text: palārdhapramitaṃ tālaṃ baddhvā vastre site dṛḍhe
children.translated_text: Having tied half a pala measure of tāla in a strong white cloth,
one should carefully smear it with goat hair and dry it three times.
When three palas of copper have been melted, one should throw in the bundle of tālaka.
One should quickly cover it with ash; white <s>sattva</s>, enveloped by the copper,
soft, should be taken out. This is taught in rasarasāyana.
Manaḥśilā is said to be of three kinds: śyāmāṅgī, kaṇavīrakā,
and the one called khaṇḍā. Their forms are distinguished and described.

children.text: śyāmā raktā sagaurā ca bhārāḍhyā śyāmikā matā
children.translated_text: Dark, red, slightly pale, and heavy, it is considered śyāmikā.
Bright, without paleness, and coppery in appearance is kaṇavīrakā.
Powdered, very red-bodied, and heavy is the one formerly called khaṇḍā.
With the qualities stated later, it is proclaimed excellent and rich in <s>sattva</s>.
Manaḥśilā is foremost among all rasāyanas, bitter, pungent, hot, and destructive of kapha and vāta.
It is possessed of <s>sattva</s> and removes afflictions by beings, poison, weak digestive fire, itching, skin eruption, cough, and wasting.

children.text: aśmarīṃ mūtrakṛcchraṃ ca aśuddhā kurute śilā
children.translated_text: Unpurified śilā causes stone disease and painful urination,
as well as weak digestion and constipation; purified, it removes all diseases.
Impregnated seven times with water from agastya leaves,
or with juices of ginger, manaḥśilā is purified.
One should cook śilā with juices produced from jayantī, bhṛṅgarāja, red agastya,
in a dolāyantra for a yāma, and for a yāma with goat urine.
One should wash it with sour gruel and use it in all diseases.
With an eighth part of slag, with jaggery, guggulu, and ghee,

children.text: koṣṭhyāṃ ruddhvā dṛḍhaṃ dhmātā sattvaṃ muñcenmanaḥśilā ||
children.translated_text: when firmly sealed in a furnace and blown upon, manaḥśilā releases <s>sattva</s>.
With bhūnāga, washed saubhāgya, and madana, rubbed together,
one should make a crucible with the water of kāravallī leaves and place it there.
Then one should blow upon the śilā, ground with alkaline and sour substances.
After blowing for merely the measure of two kokilas, it gives up its <s>sattva</s>.
Sauvīrāñjana has been described; after that comes rasāñjana.
Srotoñjana is another, and there is also puṣpāñjana,

children.text: nīlāñjanaṃ ca teṣāṃ hi svarūpamiha varṇyate ||
children.translated_text: and nīlāñjana; their forms are described here.
Sauvīrāñjana is smoky, removes disorders of blood and pitta, and is cooling.
It destroys poison, hiccup, and eye diseases, and cleanses and heals wounds.
Rasāñjana is yellowish and removes poison and diseases of the mouth.
It removes dyspnea and hiccup, improves complexion, and destroys vāta, pitta, and disorders of the blood.

children.text: srotoñjanaṃ himaṃ snigdhaṃ kaṣāyaṃ svādu lekhanam
children.translated_text: <s>Srotoñjana</s> is cooling, unctuous, astringent, sweet, and scraping.
It is beneficial for the eyes and removes hiccup, poison, vomiting, kapha, pitta, and diseases of the blood.
<s>Puṣpāñjana</s> is white, unctuous, cooling, and removes all diseases of the eyes.
It destroys even extremely difficult hiccup and removes poisoning, fever, and disease.
<s>Nīlāñjana</s> is heavy and unctuous, beneficial for the eyes, and removes the three doṣas.
It is a rasāyana, destroys gold, and makes iron soft.
Collyriums are purified with the native juices of <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>.
One should extract the <s>sattva</s> (essence) of collyriums in the same way as the <s>sattva</s> of manohvā.
The wise should identify <s>srotoja</s> as shaped like the peak of an anthill, blue-lotus-like in luster when broken,
and, when rubbed, having the color of red ochre.
When it has been repeatedly impregnated with the juice of cow dung, with urine,
and with ghee, honey, and fat, it quickly binds mercury.
<s>Rasāñjana</s> attains purification by the procedure beginning with <s>sūryāvartā</s>.
From <s>srotoñjana</s> too one should take a <s>sattva</s> like that of <s>rājāvartaka</s>.
<s>Kaṅkuṣṭha</s> is produced on the foot-slopes and summits of the <s>Himālaya</s>.
Of it, one kind is called nālikā, and another is regarded as reṇuka.
The first <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, yellow in appearance, heavy, and unctuous, is the best.

children.text: śyāmapītaṃ laghu tyaktasattvaṃ neṣṭaṃ hi reṇukam ||
children.translated_text: The reṇuka, dark-yellow, light, and devoid of <s>sattva</s>, is not desired.
Some say that <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> is the dung of a newly born elephant,
dark-yellow in appearance and described as purgative.
Some say that the stalk of fast-moving mounts is what is called <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>,
white-yellow in appearance and exceedingly purgative.
In mercury work it is an excellent rasāyana; lacking <s>sattva</s>, it has many altered forms.
<s>Kaṅkuṣṭha</s> is bitter and pungent, hot in potency, and strongly purgative.
It removes wounds, upward movement of wind, colic pain, gulma swellings, spleen disorders, and rectal pain.
<s>Sūryāvartaka</s>, plantain, vandhyā, kośātakī, and suradālī,
together with śigru, vajrakanda, niraṅkaṇā, and kākamācī:
when rasas and uparasas are repeatedly impregnated with the juice of any one of these, along with salt, alkali, and acid,
they are purified and, when smelted, release their <s>sattvas</s>.
<s>Kaṅkuṣṭha</s> attains purification when it has been impregnated three times with ginger water.

children.text: sattvākarṣo 'sya na prokto yasmātsattvamayaṃ hi tat ||
children.translated_text: Extraction of its <s>sattva</s> is not taught, because it is itself composed of <s>sattva</s>.
For purgation one should take it with astringent substances in a dose the size of a barley grain.
After purging, it destroys the accumulation of undigested matter in just a moment.
If eaten together with betel leaves, after causing purgation it may destroy life.
Decoction of barburī root, cumin, and saubhāgyaka are to be taken in equal measure.
For neutralizing poison, a man should drink <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> with these again and again.
<s>Kampilla</s>, capala, gaurīpāṣāṇa, navasāraka,
kaparda, agnijāra, and the two, girisindūra and hiṅgula,
these eight, with modāraśṛṅga, are remembered as the ordinary rasas.
They have been declared by authorities beginning with <s>Nāgārjuna</s> to bring about mastery of mercury.
Resembling powdered brick, rich in sheen, and strongly purgative,

children.text: saurāṣṭradeśe cotpannaḥ sa hi kampillakaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that which arises in the land of <s>Saurāṣṭra</s> is remembered as <s>kampillaka</s>.
<s>Kampillaka</s> destroys pitta disorders, wounds, distension, and obstruction; it is hostile to phlegm, abdominal disease, worms, and gulma swellings.
It removes root hemorrhoidal swelling, fever, and pain; it is a purgative and remover of disease.
<s>Gaurīpāṣāṇaka</s> is yellow, formidable, and reduced to powder by striking.
Three kinds are remembered: crystal-like, conch-like, and turmeric-like.

children.text: pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ guṇaiḥ śreṣṭhaḥ kāravallīphale kṣipet
children.translated_text: Each preceding kind is superior in qualities; one should put it into a bitter gourd fruit,
and steam it inside a pot. When purified, it becomes fit for the crucible.
One should extract its <s>sattva</s> like that of tāla; when purified and white, it should be used.
It binds mercury, is unctuous, removes doṣas, and strengthens the potency of mercury.
The alkali produced when the wood of karīra and pīlu is being cooked
is <s>navasāra</s>, also called cūlikā-lavaṇa.
The pale, light salt produced in brick-burning
is said to be named <s>navasāra</s>; it is also cūlikā-lavaṇa.
It digests mercury, liquefies metals, and kindles the digestive fire.
It removes gulma swellings, spleen disease, and dryness of the mouth, and digests eaten meat and the like.
Cūlikā-lavaṇa, known as viḍa, is considered to remove the three doṣas.
A yellowish cowrie with a knot on its back, long and round,
is designated by mercury physicians as <s>varāṭikā</s>, called carācara.
One weighing one and a half niṣkas is best; one weighing a niṣka is middling.
One weighing a quarter less than a niṣka is declared inferior.
It removes colic beginning with that caused by digestion and destroys grahaṇī disease and wasting.
It is pungent, hot, digestive, aphrodisiac, beneficial for the eyes, and removes vāta and kapha.
It is prescribed for the digestion of mercury and is praised among viḍa substances.

children.text: tadanye tu varāṭāḥ syur guravaḥ śleṣmapittalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Other cowries are heavy and increase phlegm and pitta.
Cowries boiled in sour gruel for three hours attain purification.
What has been cast out by the ocean as the outer afterbirth of the fire-crocodile,
and dried by the heat of the sun, is remembered as <s>agnijāra</s>.
<s>Agnijāra</s> removes the three doṣas and removes vāta disorders such as tetanus.
It increases the potency of mercury, kindles digestion, and also serves for digestion in alchemical processing.
It is purified by oceanic alkali; because of that, further purification is not desired.
The resinous substance situated inside small stones in the great mountains,
dry and red, is designated by the name <s>girisindūra</s>.
<s>Girisindūra</s> pacifies the three doṣas, is purgative, and is foremost for binding mercury.
It is said to make the body and metals fit for transformation and to be beneficial for the eyes.
Hiṅgula is of the kind called śukatuṇḍa, and another kind is haṃsapāka.
Among these, the first has few good qualities; it is called carmāra.
That which has white streaks and resembles coral is declared to be haṃsapāka.
Hiṅgula removes all doṣas, stimulates digestion, and is an excellent rasāyana.
It removes every disease, is virilizing, and is highly praised for jāraṇa.
The mercury obtained from it is equal in qualities to mercury that has assimilated sulfur.
Seven times with the juices of ginger, or else with the liquid of lakuca,

children.text: śoṣito bhāvayitvā ca nirdoṣo jāyate khalu ||
children.translated_text: after being impregnated and dried, it indeed becomes free from faults.

children.text: kimatra citraṃ daradaḥ subhāvitaḥ kṣīreṇa meṣyā bahuśo 'mlavargaiḥ
children.translated_text: What is surprising here? Darada, well processed many times with ewe's milk and sour substances,
when thus heated with intense heat, makes gold directly take on the luster of fine saffron.
Darada, placed in a pātana apparatus and made to descend into a water receptacle,
should yield its <s>sattva</s>, resembling mercury; there is no doubt about this.
In the region of <s>Gurjara</s>, it is layered and yellow in color;
mṛddāraśṛṅgaka is produced on the side of Mount <s>Arbuda</s>.
Its <s>sattva</s> is lead-like, heavy, pacifies kapha, and removes disorders of men.
It is excellent for binding mercury and supreme for dyeing the hair.
