All ordinary rasas, with the juices of citron and ginger,
when impregnated for three nights and dried, become free from faults.

children.text: yāni kāni ca sattvāni tāni śudhyantyaśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever <s>sattva</s>s there are, they are purified completely,
and, when smelted with the purification group, they unite with one another.
Thus says <s>Karavālabhairava</s>.
Rājāvarta whose luster is slightly red and mixed with deep blue,
being heavy and smooth, is the best; another kind is considered middling.
Rājāvarta removes urinary disorders, wasting, hemorrhoids, anemia, kapha, and vāta.
It stimulates digestion, digests food, is virilizing, and is a rasāyana.
With lemon juices, cow urine, and alkalis, when they are duly steamed,
rājāvarta and other minerals are purified in two or three repetitions.
One should purify rājāvarta with the fresh juices of śirīṣa flowers.
Rājāvarta, powdered together with citron-water and sulfur,
becomes killed by calcination seven times.
The powder of rājāvarta, mixed with kunaṭī and ghee,
one should cook in an iron vessel together with buffalo's milk.
Bound into a lump with saubhāgya-pañcagavya, it should be subjected to jāraṇa;
when blown with khadira charcoal, it releases a splendid <s>sattva</s>.
By this sequence of procedure, gairika becomes stainless;

children.text: kramāt pītaṃ ca raktaṃ ca sattvaṃ patati śobhanam ||
children.translated_text: in due order, both the yellow and the red yield a fine <s>sattva</s>.
Gemstones too should be understood as agents for binding mercury.
Vaikrānta, sūryakānta, diamond, pearl, and maṇi,
and likewise candrakānta and rājāvarta as the seventh,
and garuḍodgāraka too: these should be known as gemstones.
Puṣparāga, mahānīla, padmarāga, coral,

children.text: vaiḍūryaṃ ca tathā nīlamete ca maṇayo matāḥ
children.translated_text: vaiḍūrya, and likewise nīla: these also are considered gemstones.
They should be collected carefully for the sake of binding mercury.
Padmarāga, indranīla, and likewise excellent emerald,
puṣparāga together with diamond: these five are remembered as the best jewels.

children.text: māṇikyamuktāphalavidrumāṇi tārkṣyaṃ ca puṣpaṃ bhiduraṃ ca nīlam
children.translated_text: Ruby, pearl, coral, tārkṣya, puṣpa, bhidura, and nīla,

children.text: gomedakaṃ cātha vidūrakaṃ ca krameṇa ratnāni navagrahāṇām ||
children.translated_text: gomedaka and then vidūraka are, in order, the jewels of the nine planets.
According to the friendship of the planets, kuruvinda, puṣpa, coral, pearl, tārkṣya, and diamond,
nīla, gomedaka, and vidūraka are worn in rings, in sequence, for the attainment of desired success.
In rasa, rasāyana, gifting, wearing, and worship of deities,
well-born gemstones are said to be carefully protected for success.
Ruby is called padmarāga; the second kind is nīlagandhi.
Having the shade of a lotus petal, clear, unctuous, large, and sparkling,
round-oblong, with an even body, a ruby is said to be the best.
Blue, born from the waters of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, with a blue interior and reddish luster,
excellent like the previous ruby: that ruby is nīlagandhi.
With holes, roughness, dirtiness, dryness, and lack of clarity,

children.text: cipiṭaṃ laghu vakraṃ ca māṇikyaṃ duṣṭamaṣṭadhā ||
children.translated_text: flat, light, and crooked: ruby is defective in eight ways.
Ruby stimulates digestion, is virilizing, and removes kapha, vāta, and the pains of wasting.
It destroys beings, vetālas, sin, and diseases born of karma.

children.text: hlādi śvetaṃ laghu snigdhaṃ raśmivannirmalaṃ mahat
children.translated_text: Pleasing, white, light, unctuous, ray-bearing, spotless, and large,

children.text: khyātaṃ toyaprabhaṃ vṛttaṃ mauktikaṃ navadhā śubham ||
children.translated_text: famed for a watery luster and round: pearl is auspicious in nine ways.

children.text: muktāphalaṃ laghu himaṃ madhuraṃ ca kāntidṛṣṭyagnipuṣṭikaraṇaṃ viṣahāri bhedi
children.translated_text: Pearl is light, cooling, and sweet; it promotes complexion, eyesight, digestive fire, and nourishment, removes poison, and is laxative.

children.text: vīryapradaṃ jalanidherjanitā ca śuktirdīptā ca paktirujamāśu haredavaśyam ||
children.translated_text: It gives vigor; and ocean-born shell, when bright, surely and quickly removes disorders of digestion.
A pearl with a rough body, dry, dark, coppery, resembling salt,

children.text: ardhaśubhraṃ ca vikaṭaṃ granthilaṃ mauktikaṃ tyajet ||
children.translated_text: half-white, misshapen, and knotty should be rejected.
Pearl is held to destroy kapha, pitta, and wasting, and to remove cough, dyspnea, and weak digestion.
It gives nourishment, is virilizing and life-promoting, and removes burning sensation.
Coral with the color of a ripe bimba fruit, round-oblong and not crooked,
unctuous, without wounds, and thick is auspicious in seven ways.
Coral that is pale, gray, minute, wounded, or furnished with cavities,
weightless and copper-colored is undesirable in eight ways.
It removes wasting, pitta, blood disorders, and cough; it stimulates digestion, digests food, and is light.
<s>Vidruma</s> (coral) calms poison, beings, and the like, and removes eye diseases.
Green-yellow in color, heavy, unctuous, auspicious, with a cluster of flashing rays,

children.text: masṛṇaṃ bhāsuraṃ tārkṣyaṃ gātraṃ saptaguṇaṃ matam ||
children.translated_text: smooth and radiant: the body of <s>tārkṣya</s> (emerald) is considered to have seven qualities.

children.text: kapilaṃ karkaśaṃ nīlaṃ pāṇḍu kṛṣṇaṃ ca lāghavam
children.translated_text: A tawny, rough, blue, pale, black, or light one,

children.text: cipiṭaṃ vikaṭaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ rūkṣaṃ tārkṣyaṃ na śasyate ||
children.translated_text: flat, misshapen, black, or dry: such a <s>tārkṣya</s> is not recommended.
<s>Tārkṣya</s> removes fever, vomiting, poison, difficult breathing, saṃnipāta, and weak digestive fire,
destroys piles, pāṇḍu disease, and swelling, and increases vital vigor.

children.text: puṣparāgaṃ guru svacchaṃ snigdhaṃ sthūlaṃ samaṃ mṛdu
children.translated_text: <s>Puṣparāga</s> (yellow sapphire) should be heavy, clear, unctuous, large, even, and soft,
resembling a karṇikāra blossom and smooth; it is auspicious in eight ways.

children.text: niṣprabhaṃ karkaśaṃ rūkṣaṃ pītaṃ śyāmaṃ natonnatam
children.translated_text: A dull, rough, dry, yellow, dark, unevenly raised and depressed,
brownish, tawny, or pale <s>puṣparāga</s> should be rejected.
<s>Puṣparāga</s> removes poison, vomiting, kapha, vāta, and weak digestive fire,
calms burning, skin disease, and blood disorders, stimulates appetite, digests, and is light.

children.text: vajraṃ ca trividhaṃ proktaṃ naro nārī napuṃsakam
children.translated_text: Diamond is said to be of three kinds: male, female, and neuter.
Here each preceding kind is superior to the following in taste, potency, and post-digestive effect.
Eight-cornered or eight-faced, six-angled, and extremely brilliant,
cloud-colored or rainbow-colored and floating on water: this is called a male diamond.
That same stone, when flat in shape, round and elongated, is a female diamond.
Round, with a blunt angular point and somewhat heavy, it is neuter.
A female, male, and neuter diamond should be used respectively for female, male, and neuter cases.
When used in reverse it gives no result, and without a male diamond it succeeds nowhere.
By the distinction of colors such as white, each of those is fourfold:
brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya, vaiśya, and śūdra, each giving the fruit proper to its own color class.
A most excellent higher color also gives the fruit of a lower color.
This rule was stated by <s>Bhairava</s> for all substances without exception.

children.text: āyuḥpradaṃ jhaṭiti sadguṇadaṃ ca vṛṣyaṃ doṣatrayapraśamanam sakalāmayaghnam
children.translated_text: Diamond grants life, quickly gives good qualities, is aphrodisiac, pacifies the three doṣas, and destroys every disease.
It produces the binding, killing, and good qualities of mercury, kindles digestion, conquers death, and is indeed like nectar.
Grāsa, trāsa, bindu, rekhā, and having water inside:
these five are regarded as common defects in all gems.

children.text: kṣetratoyabhavā doṣā ratneṣu na laganti te ||
children.translated_text: Defects born of the field or of water do not adhere to gems.
Diamond boiled in a decoction of kulattha, or in water boiled with kodrava,
boiled for the duration of one yāma, is certainly purified.
A diamond impregnated four times with the blood of bedbugs
should be rubbed with pellets made from fragrant mouse flesh and wrapped up.
After that, one should heat it thirty times with the puṭas called varāha.
Having blown on it again and again, one should throw it a hundred times into a decoction of kulattha.
According to others, this prescribed procedure should be done a hundred times.
With śilā ground in lakuca juice mixed with kulattha decoction,

children.text: śilayā liptamūṣāyāṃ vajraṃ kṣiptvā nirudhya ca ||
children.translated_text: one should place the diamond in a crucible smeared with it and seal it.
One should heat it properly eight times with dried forest cow-dung cakes.
Then, after blowing it a hundred times, when it has been cast into purified mercury,

children.text: niścitaṃ mriyate vajraṃ bhasma vāritaraṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: the diamond is certainly killed, and its ash becomes able to float on water.
The truthful <s>Somasenānī</s>, delighting in rasa,
declared this killing of diamond, furnished with observed proof.
Smeared with bedbug blood and dried seven times,
it is placed in an iron vessel filled with kāsamarda juice.
Heated all around seven times, it indeed becomes diamond ash.
This procedure was proclaimed by the great sage <s>Brahmajyotir</s>.
Ground with the root of the nīlajyotir creeper and dried in sunlight,
diamond comes to the state of ash through the fire of knowledge, just as action does.
With juice produced from the fruit of madana and with earth-nāgas,
one should smear it with a prepared paste and heat it twenty times.
Excellent diamond powder is produced, and one should apply it in mercury preparations and the like.
Having powdered that diamond, then mixed with a little ṭaṅkaṇa,
it is surely melted with one-twentieth part of kharabhūnāga-sattva.
Blown together with an equal amount of gold, it should be applied in mercury preparations and the like.
Ground with three times as much mercury and made into a pill,
when held in the mouth it quickly brings about the fastening of loose teeth.

children.text: triṃśadbhāgamitaṃ hi vajrabhasitaṃ svarṇaṃ kalābhāgikaṃ tāraṃ cāṣṭaguṇaṃ sitāmṛtavaraṃ rudrāṃśakaṃ cābhrakam
children.translated_text: Diamond ash measuring thirty parts, gold in a kalā portion, silver eightfold, excellent white nectar, and mica in an eleventh part,

children.text: pādāṃśaṃ khalu tāpyakaṃ vasuguṇaṃ vaikrāntakaṃ ṣaḍguṇaṃ bhāgo 'pyuktarasai raso 'yamuditaḥ ṣāḍguṇyasaṃsiddhaye ||
children.translated_text: with tāpyaka in a quarter part, vaikrānta eightfold, and mercury also in a sixfold portion: this rasa, with the stated juices, is taught for accomplishing sixfold efficacy.
There are <s>jalanīla</s> and <s>śakranīla</s>; of the two, <s>śakranīla</s> is the better.
Light, blue in appearance with whiteness inside: that is <s>jalanīla</s>.
Blue in appearance with blackness inside and weighty: that is <s>śakranīla</s>.
Of a single hue, heavy, unctuous, clear, and compact in form,
soft, with light shining in the middle: the best <s>nīla</s> (sapphire) is sevenfold in quality.

children.text: komalaṃ vihitaṃ rūkṣaṃ nirbhāraṃ raktagandhi ca
children.translated_text: Too soft, fissured, dry, without weight, and with a reddish trace,

children.text: cipiṭābhaṃ sasūkṣmaṃ ca jalanīlaṃ ca saptadhā ||
children.translated_text: flat-looking and with minute specks: <s>jalanīla</s> too is sevenfold in defect.
<s>Nīla</s> is said to remove asthma and cough, to be aphrodisiac, to destroy the three doṣas, and to kindle digestion well.
It destroys intermittent fever, piles, and evil.
Because it has a color like cow's fat, the gem is called <s>gomeda</s> (hessonite).
Very clear, with the color of cow-water, clear, unctuous, even, and heavy,
without splits, smooth, and bright: <s>gomeda</s> is auspicious in eight ways.
A <s>gomeda</s> that is without color, light, rough-bodied, flattened, and covered with layers,
without brilliance and resembling yellow glass, does not bring good fortune.
<s>Gomeda</s> destroys kapha and pitta, and cures wasting and pallor.
It kindles digestion, cooks what has been eaten, is appetizing, benefits the skin, and awakens the intellect.

children.text: vaidūryaṃ śyāmaśubhrābhaṃ samaṃ svacchaṃ guru sphuṭam
children.translated_text: <s>Vaidūrya</s>, dark and pale in appearance, even, clear, heavy, and distinct,
containing a moving white band within it, is declared auspicious.
<s>Vaidūrya</s> that is dark, water-like in color, flattened, light, and rough,
and also one containing a red band, is not praised.
<s>Vaidūrya</s> destroys disorders of blood and pitta and increases wisdom, lifespan, and strength.
It removes diseases chiefly caused by pitta, kindles digestion, and releases the stools.
Ruby is purified with a sour liquid, and pearl likewise with <s>jayantī</s>.
Coral is purified by the alkaline group, and <s>tārkṣya</s> likewise with cow's milk.
<s>Puṣparāga</s> is purified with fermented liquids, in packets of horse-gram decoction;
diamond with waters of <s>taṇḍulīya</s>, and sapphire with the juice of indigo,
<s>gomeda</s> with <s>rocanā</s>, and <s>vaidūrya</s> with water of <s>triphalā</s>.
With <s>śilā</s>, sulfur, and <s>tālaka</s>, ground in the juice of <s>lakuca</s>,
all gems except diamond are indeed killed by eight <s>puṭas</s> (heatings).
<s>Rāmaṭha</s>, the five salts, and also the three alkalis,
meat juice, sour <s>vetasa</s>, and <s>cūlikā</s> salt,

children.text: sthūlaṃ kumbhīphalaṃ pakvaṃ tathā jvālāmukhī śubhā
children.translated_text: a large ripe <s>kumbhī</s> fruit, and likewise good <s>jvālāmukhī</s>,

children.text: dravantī ca rudantī ca payasyā citramūlakam ||
children.translated_text: <s>dravantī</s>, <s>rudantī</s>, <s>payasyā</s>, and <s>citramūlaka</s>,
and the milk of <s>snuhī</s> and of <s>arka</s>: one should grind all this carefully,
make a ball, and thereafter place them in its middle.
The nine gems, possessing good qualities, genuine and auspicious,

children.text: bhūrje taṃ golakaṃ kṛtvā sūtreṇāveṣṭya yatnataḥ ||
children.translated_text: one should place in that ball in birch bark and carefully wind it with thread.
Again wrapping it in cloth and placing it in a <s>dolāyantra</s>,
inside a pot filled with a fermented preparation mixed with all sour substances,
one should heat it with a strong fire for three days and nights.
Removing it from that and washing it, one should obtain the <s>druti</s> (liquefied essence) born from the gems.
It is shining like the gems, light, auspicious, and effective for the body and metals.
Pearl powder, rubbed for seven days with sour <s>vetasa</s>,
one should place inside a citron and in a heap of grain.
When it has been taken out after seven days and put in a <s>puṭa</s>, a <s>druti</s> arises.
Having placed diamond within <s>vajravallī</s>, one should confine the diamond.
It should be heated in a sour vessel; after seven days it passes into liquidity.
White <s>vaikrānta</s>, impregnated with sour <s>vetasa</s>,
without doubt liquefies after seven days in intense heat from the sun.
One should take the fresh juice of <s>ketakī</s>, rock salt, <s>svarṇapuṣpikā</s>,
and <s>indragopaka</s>; one should place everything together in a vessel.
One should heat <s>vaikrānta</s> in it for seven days; it passes into liquidity.
So too, in the eight metals, by the casting in of diamond and by heating, a <s>druti</s>
is produced; there is no doubt of this, through the power of this formula.
This king of formulas produces the supreme liquefaction of gems.
The <s>drutis</s> should each be kept separately in safflower oil.

children.text: tiṣṭhanti cirakālaṃ tu prāpte kārye niyojayet ||
children.translated_text: They remain for a long time, and one should employ them when the occasion for use has come.
The wearing of gems is said to remove the seizures and influences of the Sun and other planets and to give long life and health;
it grants fortune, the rise of good luck, controllable prosperity, vigor, and steadfastness.
It always removes misfortune arising from bad complexion, instability, dust, and contact,
and destroys beings and the like.

children.text: śuddhaṃ lohaṃ kanakarajataṃ bhānulohāśmasāraṃ pūtīlohaṃ dvitayamuditaṃ nāgavaṃgābhidhānam
children.translated_text: Pure metal is stated to be gold, silver, copper, iron, and the two base metals called lead and tin.

children.text: miśraṃ lohaṃ tritayamuditaṃ pittalaṃ kāṃsyavartaṃ dhātur lohe luha iti mataḥ so'pyanekārthavācī ||
children.translated_text: Mixed metal is stated to be threefold: brass, bronze, and <s>varta</s>; <s>dhātu</s>, <s>loha</s>, and <s>luha</s> are considered terms for metal, and that word too has many meanings.
Gold is remembered as fivefold: natural, innate, fire-born, mine-born,
and that produced by the transmuting action of <s>rasendra</s>.

<s>Gāṅgeya</s> gold brings lifespan, prosperity, radiance, intelligence, and memory, destroys every disease, is meritorious, pacifies possession by beings, gives the happiness of strong desire, and makes well-being and nourishment manifest.

children.text: gāṅgeyaṃ cātha rūpyaṃ gadaharamajarākāri mehāpahāri kṣīṇānāṃ puṣṭikāri sphuṭamatikaraṇaṃ vīryavṛddhiprakāri ||
children.translated_text: And silver removes disease, prevents old age, removes urinary disorders, nourishes the emaciated, produces clear intelligence, and increases virility.
That by which the cosmic egg was enveloped, born indeed from the quality of passion,
is called natural gold, difficult to obtain even for the gods.
The gold membrane by which <s>Brahmā</s> was covered when born,

children.text: tanmerurūpatāṃ yātaṃ suvarṇaṃ sahajaṃ hi tat ||
children.translated_text: and which assumed the form of <s>Meru</s>: that gold is indeed innate.
The yellow and very unbearable <s>Śaiva</s> radiance emitted by fire
became, all of it, what is designated fire-born gold.
This triad of gold is divine and endowed with sixteen grades of color.
By merely wearing it, it would make the body free from old age and death.

children.text: tatra tatra girīṇāṃ hi jātaṃ khaniṣu yadbhavet
children.translated_text: What is produced here and there in the mines of mountains
is rich in fourteen grades of color and, when eaten, removes all diseases.
That which is produced from the transmutation effected by <s>rasendra</s> is called transmutation-born.

children.text: rasāyanaṃ mahāśreṣṭhaṃ pavitraṃ vedhajaṃ hi tat ||
children.translated_text: That transmutation-born gold is the very best <s>rasāyana</s>, pure and sacred.

children.text: snigdhaṃ medhyaṃ viṣagadaharaṃ bṛṃhaṇaṃ vṛṣyamagryaṃ yakṣmonmādapraśamanaparaṃ deharogapramāthi
children.translated_text: It is unctuous, good for intellect, removes poison and disease, is nourishing, aphrodisiac, foremost, chiefly pacifies consumption and madness, and crushes bodily disease.

children.text: medhābuddhismṛtisukhakaraṃ sarvadoṣāmayaghnaṃ rucyaṃ dīpi praśamitarujaṃ svādupākaṃ suvarṇam ||
children.translated_text: Gold produces intelligence, understanding, memory, and happiness; it removes all <s>doṣas</s> (humoral faults) and diseases, is pleasing to the taste, kindles digestion, pacifies pain, and has a sweet postdigestive effect.

children.text: saukhyaṃ vīryaṃ balaṃ hanti rogavargaṃ karoti ca
children.translated_text: Unpurified and uncalcined gold destroys happiness, virility, and strength, and produces a whole class of diseases;
therefore gold that is impure and not subjected to <s>māraṇa</s> (calcination) should be purified and calcined.
A gold leaf of one <s>karṣa</s> measure, enclosed in a shallow dish and combined with <s>paṭu</s> and <s>dhātu</s>,
when set among coals for half a <s>prahara</s>, becomes, by blowing, truly of full color.
For all metals, <s>māraṇa</s> (calcination) with <s>rasa-bhasma</s> is the best form of calcination;
they call the method with roots middling, and the inferior one is with sulphur and the like.
Calcination of a metal by means of its enemy-metal produces bad qualities.
Having made the gold leaves pierceable by thorns, one should smear them
with ash-mercury and citron juice; the gold is killed by ten <s>puṭas</s> (heating cycles).
Into molten gold one should cast calcined mercury equal to the measure of the metal;
having powdered it with citron water and combined it with <s>darada</s> (cinnabar),
the gold becomes saffron-colored through twelve <s>puṭas</s>.

children.text: hemnaḥ pādaṃ mṛtaṃ sūtaṃ piṣṭamamlena kenacit
children.translated_text: Calcined mercury equal to one quarter of the gold, ground with some sour liquid,
should be smeared on the leaf and cooked by <s>puṭas</s>; with eight it is certainly killed.
With frog bone, fat, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), horse saliva, and <s>indragopa</s> insects,
through repeated additions, gold remains molten for a very long time.
Powder of <s>surendragopa</s> insects, impregnated with the juices of <s>devadālī</s> fruits,
makes gold of the same sort melt like water.

children.text: etadbhasma suvarṇajaṃ kaṭughṛtopetaṃ dviguṃjonmitaṃ līḍhaṃ hanti nṛṇāṃ kṣayāgnisadanaṃ śvāsaṃ ca kāsārucim
children.translated_text: This ash produced from gold, mixed with pungent drugs and ghee, two <s>guñjās</s> in measure, when licked, removes in people wasting disease, loss of digestive fire, dyspnea, cough, and anorexia.

children.text: ojodhātuvivardhanaṃ balakaraṃ pāṇḍvāmayadhvaṃsanaṃ pathyaṃ sarvaviṣāpahaṃ garaharaṃ duṣṭagrahaṇyādinut ||
children.translated_text: It increases <s>ojas</s> and the bodily tissues, gives strength, destroys pallor disease, is wholesome, removes every poison, counters toxins, and relieves diseased <s>grahaṇī</s> and the like.

children.text: balaṃ ca vīryaṃ harate narāṇāṃ rogavrajaṃ kopayatīva kāye
children.translated_text: Unprepared gold takes away men's strength and virility and seems to provoke a mass of diseases in the body;

children.text: asaukhyakāraṃ ca sadaiva hemāpakvaṃ sadoṣaṃ maraṇaṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: it always causes discomfort, and, being immature and faulty, brings about death.
Silver is held to be of three kinds: natural, mine-born, and artificial.
Each earlier type, in order, is superior to the following one in its own qualities.
Natural silver is that which is produced in mountains such as <s>Kailāsa</s>;
if merely touched, it becomes a destroyer of diseases for embodied beings.
The silver that is produced on peaks such as the Himalaya

children.text: khanijaṃ kathyate tajjñaiḥ paramaṃ hi rasāyanam ||
children.translated_text: is called mineral by experts; it is indeed the supreme <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenant).
Tin placed upon the sandals of <s>Śrī Rāma</s>, which became silver,
is called <s>pādarūpya</s>; it is artificial and removes all diseases.

children.text: ghanaṃ svacchaṃ guru snigdhaṃ dāhe chede sitaṃ mṛdu
children.translated_text: Dense, clear, heavy, unctuous, white when heated and cut, and soft,
smooth, conch-like, and free from fissures: such silver is good.

children.text: dāhe raktaṃ ca pītaṃ ca kṛṣṇaṃ rūkṣaṃ sphuṭaṃ laghu
children.translated_text: Silver that is red, yellow, or black when heated, dry, cracked, light,
coarse-bodied and rough-bodied is to be rejected in eight ways.

children.text: rūpyaṃ vipākamadhuraṃ tuvarāmlasāraṃ śītaṃ saraṃ paramalekhanakaṃ ca rūpyam
children.translated_text: Silver has a sweet <s>vipāka</s> (postdigestive effect), is astringent and sour in essence, cooling, fluid, and a supreme scraping agent.

children.text: snigdhaṃ ca vātakaphajijjaṭharāgnidīpi balyaṃ paraṃ sthiravayaskaraṇaṃ ca medhyam ||
children.translated_text: It is unctuous, overcomes <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>, kindles the digestive fire in the belly, gives strength, greatly stabilizes age, and promotes intelligence.

children.text: raupyaṃ śītaṃ kaṣāyāmlaṃ snigdhaṃ vātaharaṃ guru
children.translated_text: Silver is cooling, astringent-sour, unctuous, removes <s>vāta</s>, and is heavy.
Prepared according to the <s>rasāyana</s> procedure, it takes away all diseases.

children.text: taile takre gavāṃ mūtre hyāranāle kulatthaje
children.translated_text: In oil, buttermilk, cow urine, sour gruel, and a liquid made from horse gram,
one should successively quench the heated metal seven times in each molten state;
this purification of leaves of gold and the other metals is praised.
Silver that is impure and not calcined destroys life span, semen, and strength, and causes burning, constipation, and disease;

children.text: aśuddhaṃ na mṛtaṃ tāraṃ śuddhaṃ māryamato budhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore purified <s>tāra</s> (silver) should be subjected to <s>māraṇa</s> by the wise.
When cast together with lead and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), it attains purification,
silver being thrown three times into oil made from <s>jyotiṣmatī</s>.
In a potsherd one should make a surrounding rim with ash and powder;
there, having placed silver together with an equal amount of lead,
one should blow on it again and again until the produced lead is exhausted.
Silver purified in this way should be used in preparations with mercury and the like.
One should smear silver leaf with <s>lakuca</s> juice and mercury paste;

children.text: ūrdhvādho gandhakaṃ dattvā mūṣāmadhye nirudhya ca ||
children.translated_text: having placed sulphur above and below, and having sealed it inside a crucible,
one should heat it in a sand apparatus for one day with a strong fire.

children.text: svāṃgaśītāṃ ca tāṃ piṣṭiṃ sāmlatālena marditām
children.translated_text: When that paste has cooled by itself, it should be ground with sour <s>tāla</s>;
one should heat it twelve times by <s>puṭa</s>; the silver becomes ash.
Silver rubbed with powder of <s>mākṣīka</s> and sour citron and heated gradually
becomes completely reduced to ash by thirty operations.
<s>Tāpya</s> should be impregnated with the latex of <s>snuhī</s>, and one should smear the silver leaves with it.
One should kill them by the <s>puṭa</s> method; they certainly become <s>niruttha</s> (not revivable as metal).
Four parts of silver leaf and one part of purified <s>tālaka</s>
should be rubbed with citron juice, and the silver leaves should be smeared with it.
One should purify it in an <s>andha-yantra</s> and cook it with thirty <s>utpalas</s> of fuel.
In this way, with fourteen <s>puṭas</s>, it certainly becomes <s>niruttha</s>.
One should impregnate <s>devadālī</s> seven times with human urine;
by the mere addition of that powder, gold and silver become molten.

children.text: bhasmībhūtaṃ rajatamamalaṃ tatsamau vyomabhānū sarvaistulyaṃ trikaṭu savaraṃ sāraghājyena yuktam
children.translated_text: Pure silver reduced to ash, with equal parts of <s>vyoma</s> and <s>bhānu</s>, with <s>trikaṭu</s> and <s>vara</s> equal to all of them, and joined with <s>sāraghājya</s>,

children.text: līḍhaṃ prātaḥ kṣapayatitarāṃ yakṣmapāṇḍūdarārśaḥ śvāsaṃ kāsaṃ nayanajarujaḥ pittarogānaśeṣān ||
children.translated_text: when licked in the morning, thoroughly eliminates wasting disease, pallor, abdominal enlargement, piles, dyspnea, cough, eye disorders, and all pitta diseases.
Copper is of two kinds, mleccha and <s>Nepālaka</s>; of the two, <s>Nepālaka</s> is superior.
That which is produced from mines other than those of <s>Nepāla</s> is called mleccha.
Having a whitish, black, or reddish hue, very dull and hard,
and becoming black again after it is washed: this is mleccha copper.
Very unctuous, soft, red, able to withstand heavy hammering, and weighty,
unchanged and excellent in qualities: such copper is called <s>Nepāla</s> copper.
Copper that is pale, black-red, light, and marked by cracks,
with a rough body and lamination, is not desired for rasa work.

children.text: tāmraṃ tiktakaṣāyakaṃ ca madhuraṃ pāke'tha vīryoṣṇakaṃ sāmlaṃ pittakaphāpahaṃ jaṭhararukkuṣṭhāmajantvantakṛt
children.translated_text: Copper is bitter and astringent, sweet in digestion, hot in potency, and slightly sour; it removes pitta and kapha, and destroys abdominal pain, skin disease, undigested matter, and worms.

children.text: ūrdhvādhaḥ pariśodhanaṃ viṣayakṛt sthaulyāpahaṃ kṣutkaraṃ durnāmakṣayapāṇḍurogaśamanaṃ netryaṃ paraṃ lekhanam ||
children.translated_text: It purifies both upward and downward, causes toxic effects if improperly used, removes obesity, stimulates appetite, pacifies hemorrhoids, wasting, and anemia, benefits the eyes, and is supremely scraping.
Unpurified copper destroys life and takes away luster, virility, and strength.
It causes vomiting, fainting, dizziness, nausea, skin disease, and colic.
Nausea, splitting pain, dizziness, burning, and stupor are indeed the faults of copper, hard to bear.
Through purification, when it is freed from its own faults, it becomes like nectar in taste, potency, and post-digestive effect.
Copper, combined with alkali and sour substances, melted, and supplied with gairika,
should be placed seven times in buffalo buttermilk and goat dung.
It then becomes free from the five faults and fit for making bhasma.
Clean sheets of copper should be smeared with lemon-water and salt;
after heating, by the addition of sauvīraka, it is purified in eight repetitions.
Sheets smeared with lemon-water and salt and heated eight times
are purified by immersion in the juice of nirguṇḍī.
One should cook a copper sheet in cow urine for a yāma with a strong fire.
It is purified; there is no doubt here. Now its killing by calcination is also stated.
A copper sheet smeared with mercury and sulfur ground with the juice of citron,
placed inside covered earthen dishes, comes to destruction by three puṭas.
Or else, calcined copper should be rubbed with a single sour liquid.
Having enclosed that ball inside a sūraṇa tuber, one should seal it and smear it all around.
When dry, it should be cooked in a gajapuṭa; it will remove all faults.

children.text: vāntiṃ bhrāntiṃ virekaṃ ca na karoti kadācana ||
children.translated_text: It never causes vomiting, delusion, or purgation.
Fine copper sheets should be placed in cow urine for five yāmas.

children.text: kṣiptvā rasena bhāṇḍe taddviguṇaṃ dehi gandhakam ||
children.translated_text: Having put them in a vessel with mercury, add twice that amount of sulfur.
Then, after grinding amlaparṇī, place the copper all around it.

children.text: samyaṅ nirudhya bhāṇḍe tamagniṃ jvālaya yāmakam
children.translated_text: Seal it properly in the vessel and kindle the fire for a yāma.
That copper becomes ash; one may employ it as desired.
Copper leaf in twice the amount of mercury, soaked with the juices of kumārī,
should be ground with an equal amount of bali and placed inside a vessel.
Cover it with a small earthen dish; above that, put salt.
After placing a small earthen dish over the mouth, apply fire for four yāmas.
Powder that copper and administer it in a dose of one valla.
It should be used together with long pepper and honey in all diseases.
It is excellent for the treatment of dyspnea, cough, wasting, anemia, weak digestion, loss of appetite,
abdominal tumors, diseases of the spleen and liver, fainting, colic, and digestion.
It surely conquers diseases arising from the three doṣas.
Together with the proper anupāna, it conquers fever lodged in the bodily tissues.
In rasa work and in rasāyana, copper should be used in the proper dose.
With mercury equal to the copper, with bali equal to that,
with tāla in half that amount, and with śilā in half of that again,
one should make a smooth kajjalī, resembling split collyrium.
Inside the cavity of the garbhayantra described in the chapter on apparatus,
one should place the kajjalī and copper sheets in alternating layers.
It should be cooked for a full yāma; when cooled by itself, it should be powdered.

children.text: tattadrogaharānupānasahitatāmraṃ dvivallonmitaṃ saṃlīḍhaṃ pariṇāmaśūlamudaraṃ śūlaṃ ca pāṇḍujvaram
children.translated_text: This copper, in a measure of two vallas and licked together with the anupāna that removes each particular disease, removes post-digestive colic, abdominal disease, colic, anemia, and fever,

children.text: gulmaplīhayakṛtkṣayāgnisadanaṃ mehaṃ ca mūlāmayaṃ duṣṭāṃ ca grahaṇīṃ hared dhruvam idaṃ śrīsomanāthābhidham ||
children.translated_text: abdominal tumors, spleen and liver disorders, wasting, weakness of digestion, urinary disease, hemorrhoids, and severe grahaṇī disease; this is surely the preparation called <s>Śrī-Somanātha</s>.

children.text: muṃḍaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ ca kāṃtaṃ ca triprakāramayaḥ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Iron is remembered as threefold: muṇḍa, tīkṣṇa, and kānta.

children.text: mṛdu kuṇṭhaṃ kaḍāraṃ ca trividhaṃ muṇḍamucyate ||
children.translated_text: Muṇḍa is said to be threefold: soft, kuṇṭha, and kaḍāra.
That which melts quickly, does not burst, and is smooth and soft is auspicious.
That which, when beaten, spreads out only with difficulty is called kuṇṭha, the middling kind.
That which, when beaten, breaks, and is black at the break, is kaḍāra.
The best muṇḍa, being very soft, removes kapha and vāta, colic, hemorrhoids, urinary disease, jaundice, and anemia.
It removes abdominal tumors, rheumatism from undigested matter, and abdominal pain; it kindles digestion, removes swelling, produces blood, and cleanses the bowel.

children.text: aśuddhalohaṃ na hitaṃ niṣevaṇād āyurbalaṃ kāntivināśi niścitam
children.translated_text: Unpurified iron is not wholesome when consumed; it certainly destroys life, strength, and luster.

children.text: hṛdi prapīḍāṃ tanute hyapāṭavaṃ rujaṃ karotyeva viśodhya mārayet ||
children.translated_text: It produces oppression in the heart, incapacity, and pain; therefore one should purify it and kill it by calcination.

children.text: kharaṃ sāraṃ ca hṛnnālaṃ tārāvaṭṭaṃ ca vājiram
children.translated_text: Khara, sāra, hṛnnāla, tārāvaṭṭa, vājira,
and that called kālaloha: tīkṣṇa iron is said to be sixfold.
That which is rough, free from pogara, and has at its fracture a luster like mercury,
and which breaks when bent, is called khara iron.
That whose edge breaks quickly is called sāra iron.
Sāra is said to have the appearance of pogara, to be pale, and to be born from the earth.
With a black-and-white body and with large pogara marks like cañcu seeds,
and very rough when cut, it is called hṛnnāla.
Aṅgakṣaya, vaṅga, and pogara are the three designations of pogara.

children.text: cikuraṃ bhaṅguraṃ lohāt pogaraṃ tatparaṃ matam ||
children.translated_text: Cikura, bhaṅgura, and that which comes from iron are considered to be pogara beyond that.
Covered with diamond-like pogaras, with fine lines and dense texture,
and having a dark body, that is proclaimed to be vājīra.
Blue-black in luster, compact, smooth, heavy, and shining,
with an edge whose nature is not broken even by a blow of iron, it is regarded as kālāyasa.

children.text: rūkṣaṃ syāt kharalohakaṃ samadhuraṃ pāke'tha vīrye himaṃ tiktoṣṇaṃ kaphapittakuṣṭhajaṭharaplīhāmapāṃḍvartinut
children.translated_text: Kharalohaka is dry and rough, sweet in digestion, cooling in potency, bitter and hot; it removes kapha, pitta, skin disease, abdominal disease, spleen disease, āma, anemia, and pain,

children.text: sadyaḥ śūlayakṛdgadakṣayajarāmehāmavātāpahaṃ dīptaṃ cātirasāyanaṃ balakaraṃ durnāmadāhāpaham ||
children.translated_text: and quickly removes colic, liver disease, wasting, old age, urinary disease, āma, and vāta; it is fiery, an excellent rasāyana, strength-giving, and removes hemorrhoids and burning.
Everything beyond kharaloha is superior by a hundredfold, each one after the previous one.

children.text: bhrāmakaṃ cumbakaṃ caiva karṣakaṃ drāvakaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Bhrāmaka, cumbaka, karṣaka, and drāvaka:

children.text: evaṃ caturvidhaṃ kāntaṃ romakāntaṃ ca pañcamam ||
children.translated_text: thus kānta is fourfold, and romakānta is the fifth.
It has one, two, three, four, five, or faces on every side.

children.text: pītaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ tathā raktaṃ trivarṇaṃ syātpṛthak pṛthak
children.translated_text: It is yellow, black, and also red; the three colors are separate in each case.
In order, the deities there are <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Maheśvara</s>.
The yellow is effective by touch; the black is best for rasāyana.
The red color too is praised for binding mercury.

children.text: bhrāmakaṃ tu kaniṣṭhaṃ syāccumbakaṃ madhyamaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Bhrāmaka is inferior, and cumbaka is middling;
karṣaka is excellent, and drāvaka is the very best.
That which makes a mass of iron turn is regarded as bhrāmaka kānta.
That which attracts is cumbaka kānta, and that which draws in is karṣaka.
That kānta which directly melts iron is drāvaka.
It is romakānta when, from a split in it, a hair-like growth appears.
One-faced is inferior; two- and three-faced are middling.
Four- and five-faced are superior; facing every direction is excellent.
Bhrāmaka and cumbaka are praised for destroying diseases.

children.text: rase rasāyane caiva karṣakaṃ drāvakaṃ hitam ||
children.translated_text: Karṣaka and drāvaka are beneficial in mercury and in rasāyana.
Mercury is an elephant maddened with rut; kānta is called its goad.
Having recognized the deposit, the wise person should collect it carefully.
One should reject what has been scattered by wind and sun; there is no doubt about this.

children.text: pātre yasya prasarati jale tailabindurna lipto gandhaṃ hiṅgustyajati ca tathā tiktatāṃ nimbakalkaḥ
children.translated_text: When, in its vessel, a drop of oil spreads on water without smearing it, and when asafoetida loses its smell and neem paste its bitterness,

children.text: pāke dugdhaṃ bhavati śikharākārakaṃ naiti bhūmau kāntaṃ lauhaṃ tadidamuditaṃ lakṣaṇoktaṃ ca nānyat ||
children.translated_text: and when, on cooking, milk becomes peak-shaped and does not fall to the ground, this is declared to be kānta iron, possessing the stated marks, and no other.

children.text: kāntāyo 'tirasāyanottarataraṃ svasthe cirāyuḥpradaṃ snigdhaṃ mehaharaṃ tridoṣaśamanaṃ śūlāmamūlāpaham
children.translated_text: Kānta-iron is still better than the highest rasāyana; for the healthy it gives long life, is unctuous, removes urinary disease, pacifies the three doṣas, and removes colic, āma, and piles.

children.text: gulmaplīhayakṛtkṣayāmayaharaṃ pāṇḍūdaravyādhinut tiktoṣṇaṃ himavīryakaṃ kimaparaṃ yogena sarvārtinut ||
children.translated_text: It removes abdominal tumors, spleen disease, liver disease, wasting disorders, anemia, and abdominal disease; it is bitter and hot, cooling in potency, and, what more, when properly combined it removes every ailment.
Among properly prepared medicinal formulations, the iron preparation is praised.
Therefore, with every effort, one should purify iron and calcine it.
One should not cook iron in a quantity below five palas or above thirteen.

children.text: ādau mantrastataḥ karma kartavyaṃ mantra ucyate ||
children.translated_text: First the mantra, then the procedure, should be performed; the mantra is now stated.

children.text: oṃ amṛtodbhavāya svāhā anena mantreṇa lohamāraṇam
children.translated_text: "Oṃ, svāhā to the one born of nectar"; with this mantra, the calcination of iron is performed.
All iron becomes successively better in qualities by a hundred thousandfold, one after another.
Among them kānta is ten-millionfold in quality; and that too is progressively superior.
Smeared with hare's blood and heated all around three times,
all iron beginning with muṇḍa gives up every defect.
Sixteen palas of triphalā should be decocted in eight times as much water.
When one quarter remains of that decoction, five palas of iron
should be made into leaves, heated, and quenched seven times.
In this way the mountain-born defect arising in iron is dissolved.
Heated together with sea salt and then quenched,
iron certainly gives up its mountain defect in a decoction of triphalā.
Decoctions made from tamarind-fruit water and the like remove the defect.
Or, combined with the three fruits and boiled briefly in cow urine,
purged and mixed with ghee, the iron should be put into a potsherd and cooked.
One should stir it with an iron rod until a blade of grass thrown in burns.
Grinding and cooking it in this way, one should continue for five repetitions thereafter.
Or, with juices of dhātrī fruit or with waters boiled with triphalā,
one should subject the iron to four puṭas; indeed it becomes vāritara, able to float on water.
Iron filings, smeared with oil, should be treated in urine and also in the fresh juice of night-soaked dhātrī fruits.
Roasted separately seven times in this way, it is to be used in all diseases.
The leaves of sharp iron, stripped of their layers, in a strong fire,
should be heated by blowing and immediately thrown into water inside a stone mortar.
One should pound them with heavy blows by means of a large iron pestle.
From among them, the coarse pieces should be enclosed between two crucibles.
After heating them by blowing and throwing them into water, one should pound them well as before.
That powder should be calcined twenty times with mercury and sulfur.
At each puṭa, grinding should be carried out more and more firmly.
Iron made into bhasma in this way should be applied in the respective diseases.
Kānta-iron produces desirable beauty and eradicates anemia.
It destroys the disease consumption, removes poison, and uproots the three doṣas.
It destroys many kinds of skin disease, gives strength, is aphrodisiac, and arrests aging.
It removes every disease; it is the best rasāyana, an earthly nectar, and there is no other like it.
One should grind five palas of hiṅgula with woman's breast milk.
With that one should smear five palas of iron sheets.
Having sealed them, one should cook them in a gajapuṭa; again, with triphalā decoctions,
or with citrons or sour gruel, with hiṅgula in the proportion of one twentieth,
one should grind it, seal it, and cook the iron; again one should cook it with those liquids.
With forty puṭas in this way, kānta iron, tīkṣṇa iron, and muṇḍaka iron

children.text: mriyate nātra saṃdeho dattvā dattvaiva hiṅgulam ||
children.translated_text: are killed by calcination; there is no doubt here, when hiṅgula is added again and again.
Now the tīkṣṇa iron previously described, in the fats of vasu and bhallaka,
when puṭa-cooked with patra-water thirty times carefully,
becomes a red ash, bearing the appearance of prepared vermilion.
Or else the powder produced from leaves of tīkṣṇa iron should be ground with triphalā-water,
with a little cooked rice added, and made into a small cake.
After drying it with great care, one should cook it with five puṭas.
That ash is red in color and should be employed as appropriate.
With matsyākṣī, gandha, and bāhlīka ground in the juice of lakuca,
one should smear the whole iron, coated with a paste of matsyākṣī.
Blowing it very strongly with two bellows until the trident-like sparks come forth,
then, having taken it out, one should throw it into a decoction made of triphalā and cow-water.
Taking it from that, beating it, and taking the killed iron,
one should again blow it as before and kill all the iron by calcination.
Then, having broken it into pieces, together with gandha, jaggery, and triphalā,
one should puṭa-cook it thirty times; an ash that does not rise again is produced.
Iron powder with an equal amount of gandha, impregnated with the water of kumārī,
when made into a puṭa preparation for some time, surely the iron is killed by calcination.
Heated iron repeatedly thrown into darada mixed with lemon juice
is killed by calcination; there is no doubt here.
Triphalā should be decocted with cow urine; with that decoction one should impregnate it.
For three times seven days, carefully, one should grind it again for one day.
Having sealed it, one should cook it in a gajapuṭa and grind it for a day with the decoction.
It should be ground by day and puṭa-cooked at night, up to twenty-one days.
With twenty-one puṭas in this way, the threefold iron is killed by calcination.
That in whose vessel-steeped water a drop of oil does not spread,
and that which is turned with silver: that is thinly drawn kānta iron.
The best among irons should be sprinkled while very hot with the juice of varā.
Thus purified irons, ground with some sour liquid,
smeared with one fourth part of killed mercury, should be cooked in a puṭa-fire,
or with an equal amount of tāpya, gandhāśman, and haratejas.
Kānta iron, heated, smeared with alkali and sour liquid, and placed in hare's blood,
becomes ash, free from all faults.

children.text: śuddhaṃ sūtaṃ dvidhā gandhaṃ khallena kṛtakajjalam
children.translated_text: Purified mercury and twice as much gandha should be made into kajjalī in a mortar.
Iron powder equal to the two should be ground with the juices of kanyakā.
After two yāmas, the ball that is taken up should be placed in a copper vessel,
and covered with castor leaves; in half a yāma it becomes very hot.
Afterwards one should place it in a heap of grain and, at the end of three days, take it out.
Having ground it, one should strain it through cloth; truly, it will float on water.

children.text: kāntaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ ca muṃḍaṃ ca nirutthaṃ jāyate mṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Kānta, tīkṣṇa, and muṇḍa iron become killed and unable to rise again.
Gold and the other metals should be killed by calcination in this same way, after making them into powder, like iron.
This is the renowned perfected procedure, come from the mouths of adepts.
I have experienced it; it is true, and it removes all disease and old age.
Joined with triphalā and honey, it should be used in all diseases.

children.text: etasmād apunarbhavaṃ hi bhasitaṃ lohasya divyāmṛtaṃ samyak siddharasāyanaṃ trikaṭukīvellājyamadhvanvitam
children.translated_text: From this comes apunarbhava ash of iron, a divine nectar and a properly perfected rasāyana, accompanied by trikaṭukī, vellā, ghee, and honey.

children.text: hanyānniṣkamitaṃ jarāmaraṇajavyādhīṃśca satputradaṃ diṣṭe śrīgiriśena kālayavanodbhūtyai purā tatpituḥ ||
children.translated_text: A niṣka measure would destroy old age and diseases born of death, and gives good sons; formerly it was prescribed by glorious <s>Giriśa</s> for the arising of <s>Kālayavana</s> for his father.
Iron conquers disorders of worms, anemia, vāta, wasting, pitta diseases, obesity, hemorrhoids, grahaṇī disease, fever pains, kapha, swelling, and urinary disease.

children.text: gulmaplīhaviṣāpahaṃ balakaraṃ kuṣṭhāgnimāndyapraṇut saukhyālambirasāyanaṃ mṛtiharaṃ kiṭṭaṃ ca kāntādivat ||
children.translated_text: It removes abdominal tumors, spleen disease, and poison, gives strength, and removes skin disease and weak digestion; it is a rasāyana that supports well-being, removes death, and even its slag is like kānta and the others.

children.text: mṛtāni lohāni rasībhavanti nighnanti yuktāni mahāmayāṃśca
children.translated_text: Metals killed by calcination become rasa-like, and, when properly joined, destroy great diseases.
Through repeated practice they produce the accomplishment of a firm body and the destruction of disease, birth, and old age.
The best kānta iron has the hue of a ripe rose-apple fruit.
Impregnated twenty-one times in cow urine with jālinī ash,
one should dry it; by blowing with that, tīkṣṇa iron placed in a crucible melts.
Or suradālī ash, melted and dried twenty-one times in cow-water,
by blowing makes tīkṣṇa iron placed in a crucible like water.
Ash produced from suradālī, melted with human urine,
after twenty-one repetitions, through blowing with that alkali, brings about the liquefaction of kānta iron.
Sulfur and kānta-stone should be powdered in equal amounts.

children.text: drute lohe pratīvāpo deyo lohāṣṭakaṃ dravet ||
children.translated_text: A counter-blowing should be given to the melted iron; the eight metals will melt.
Sulfur should be impregnated with the juices of devadālī for seven days.
By the mere blowing of that, iron remains like mercury.

children.text: aśuddhalohaṃ na hitaṃ niṣevaṇād āyurbalaṃ kāntivināśi niścitam
children.translated_text: Impure metal, when used, is certainly not beneficial; it destroys lifespan, strength, and complexion.

children.text: hṛdi prapīḍāṃ tanute hyapāṭavaṃ rujaṃ karotyeva viśodhya mārayet ||
children.translated_text: It produces severe pain in the heart, weakness, and disease; therefore one should purify and calcine it.
<s>Muṇḍa</s> iron is ten times better than slag, and sharp iron is said to be a hundred times better than <s>muṇḍa</s>.
<s>Kānta</s> is a hundred thousand times better than sharp iron, and through ingestion it produces excellent qualities.

children.text: tasmāt kāntaṃ sadā sevyaṃ jarāmṛtyuharaṃ nṛṇām ||
children.translated_text: Therefore <s>kānta</s> should always be used by men, for it removes old age and death.
It grants lifespan, produces strength and virility, destroys disease, and acts as an aphrodisiac.

children.text: ayaḥsamānaṃ na hi kiṃcid anyadrasāyanaṃ śreṣṭhatamaṃ hi jantoḥ ||
children.translated_text: There is no <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative) equal to iron; it is indeed the very best for a living being.
One should heat iron slag with charcoal made from <s>akṣa</s> wood and quench it with cow urine.
One should pour it repeatedly inside an <s>akṣa</s> vessel seven times.
This is called <s>maṇḍūra</s>; one should apply it as a very fine powder.
Having decocted <s>triphala</s> with cow urine, one should slowly quench it in that decoction.
The iron slag should be thoroughly heated until it disintegrates of itself.
That becomes a powder suitable for grinding; this <s>maṇḍūra</s> should be used.

children.text: ye guṇā mārite muṇḍe te guṇā muṇḍakiṭṭake
children.translated_text: The qualities that exist in calcined <s>muṇḍa</s> iron also exist in the slag of <s>muṇḍa</s>.
Therefore <s>maṇḍūra</s> should be used in every case for the pacification of disease.
<s>Vaṅga</s> is said to be of two kinds: <s>khuraka</s> and <s>miśraka</s>.

children.text: khuraṃ tatra guṇaiḥ śreṣṭhaṃ miśrakaṃ na hitaṃ matam ||
children.translated_text: Among these, <s>khura</s> is superior in qualities, while <s>miśraka</s> is considered not beneficial.
When dead, white, unctuous, quickly melting, and heavy,
and silent, it is <s>khuravaṅga</s>; <s>miśraka</s> is blackish-white.
<s>Vaṅga</s> is bitter, hot, dry, and slightly aggravates <s>vāta</s>.
It destroys urinary disorders, diseases of phlegm, fat, and worms.
After melting it, with turmeric added, it should be placed in the juice of <s>nirguṇḍikā</s>.
<s>Khuravaṅga</s> is purified by three repetitions; there is no doubt.
Placed in sour buttermilk with <s>varṣābhū</s>, <s>viṣa</s>, and <s>tinduka</s>,
and then put in water of <s>kaṭphala</s>, the second kind of <s>vaṅga</s> is purified.

children.text: śudhyati nāgo vaṃgo ghoṣo ravirātape'pi munisaṃkhyaiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Nāga</s>, <s>vaṅga</s>, <s>ghoṣa</s>, and <s>ravi</s> are purified even in sunlight in seven applications
by sprinklings with the juice of <s>nirguṇḍī</s> and by additions of the powder of its root.
Having smeared leaves of <s>vaṅga</s> with <s>satāla</s> and the milk of <s>arka</s>,
one should give light <s>puṭas</s> with alkalis from the bark of <s>bodhiciñcā</s>.
After grinding, one should make it into <s>bhasma</s>; it is praised in mercurial and similar preparations.

children.text: pradrāvya kharpare vaṃgaṃ ṣoḍaśāṃśaṃ rasaṃ kṣipet
children.translated_text: After melting <s>vaṅga</s> in a potsherd, one should add mercury in a sixteenth part.
Adding small pieces little by little, by means of <s>Bhāradvāja</s> wood,
one should grind it and make it into <s>bhasma</s>; it is praised in mercurial and similar preparations.
One should coat a sheet of <s>vaṅga</s> with the liquid of <s>palāśa</s>.
After it has been subjected to a <s>puṭa</s> with <s>tāla</s>, it is killed; there is no doubt here.
<s>Vaṅga</s>, smeared with <s>bhallāta</s> oil and wrapped in cloth,
meets destruction in a fire of tamarind, pippala, and <s>palāśa</s> wood.
To an equal amount of <s>vaṅga-bhasma</s>, add <s>kānta</s> and the same amount of mica <s>bhasma</s>.
One should grind them with golden water and also with the juice of neem leaves.

children.text: dāḍimasya mayūrasya rasena ca pṛthak pṛthak
children.translated_text: Separately with the juice of pomegranate and of peacock,
then adding an equal part of <s>bhūpālāvarta-bhasma</s>,
one should grind it thoroughly with waters of <s>gomūlaka</s> and <s>śilādhātu</s>.
Then, with water of <s>guggulu</s>, one should grind it for eight days.
After drying and pulverizing it, one should combine it in equal proportion
with the exudates of <s>bandhūka</s> and powders of <s>nākulī</s> seed, well rubbed together.
Then one should place it in a box, after straining it through cloth.
It should be given to drink together with the essence of turmeric ground in cow buttermilk.
In a dose equal to four <s>vallakas</s>, this pleasant <s>vaṅga-rasāyana</s> is used.
By it, certainly, the twenty varieties of urinary disorder are destroyed.
Rice, mung-bean soup, fresh butter, sesame oil,
<s>paṭola</s>, bitter <s>tuṇḍīra</s>, and buttermilk are recommended as wholesome regimen.
Quickly melting, very heavy, black in fracture, and shining,
with a foul odor and black outside, is purified lead; otherwise it is impure.
<s>Sīsaka</s> is very hot, unctuous, bitter, and removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>.
It destroys urinary disease and disorders of water, stimulates digestion, and removes <s>āmavāta</s>.
One should add powders of <s>sinduvāra</s> root, <s>kauntī</s>, and turmeric.
Then, when <s>nāga</s> is melted, one should place it three times in the juice of <s>nirguṇḍī</s>.
Thus <s>nāga</s> becomes purified and does not produce fainting, eruptions, and the like.
In a crosswise-shaped stove one should set a pot with its mouth sideways.

children.text: taṃ ca vaktraṃ vinā sarvaṃ gopayedyatnato mṛdā ||
children.translated_text: Except for its mouth, one should carefully cover the whole of it with clay.
In that vessel called the roasting apparatus, one should place lead,
twenty palas of purified lead, and put a strong fire underneath.

children.text: drute nāge kṣipetsūtaṃ śuddhaṃ karṣamitaṃ śubham
children.translated_text: When the <s>nāga</s> is melted, one should add pure, good mercury measuring one <s>karṣa</s>.
After rubbing, one should add alkali, one pala of each.
Of <s>arjuna</s>, of the <s>akṣa</s> tree, and also of <s>mahārājagiri</s>,

children.text: dāḍimasya mayūrasya kṣiptvā kṣāraṃ pṛthak pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: and of pomegranate and peacock, one should add the alkali separately in each case.
In this way one should cook it for twenty nights with a strong fire,
stirring it firmly with both arms by means of an iron ladle, carefully.
That becomes a red <s>bhasma</s>, or else one with the color of a dove.
The <s>nāga</s>, freed from defects, becomes an exceedingly powerful <s>rasāyana</s>.
Lead that has been killed and revived becomes perfected after ten repetitions.
That dead lead, free from all defects, is a <s>rasāyana</s>.
Ashes of the bark of aśvattha and tamarind should be one fourth of the <s>nāga</s>.
One should add the <s>nāga</s>, cook it in a vessel, and stir it with an iron ladle.
After one <s>yāma</s>, having taken out that ash, with <s>manaḥśilā</s> equal in weight to the ash,

children.text: jambīrair āranālairvā piṣṭvā ruddhvā puṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: one should grind it with citron juice or with <s>āranāla</s>, seal it, and cook it in a <s>puṭa</s>.
When it has cooled on its own, one should grind it again, mixed with one-twentieth part <s>śilā</s>,
with a sour liquid alone for one <s>yāma</s>, and cook it in a <s>puṭa</s> as before.
Cooked in this way with sixty <s>puṭas</s>, <s>nāga</s> (lead) becomes well deprived of revival.
One should smear leaves of <s>nāga</s> with <s>śilā</s> and <s>ravidugdha</s> (arka latex),
and calcine it by the <s>puṭa</s> method; in that way it becomes non-revivable.
Thus, of the ash produced from <s>nāga</s>, one should add half as much ash of <s>tāpya</s>,

children.text: pādaṃ pādaṃ kṣipedbhasma śulbasya vimalasya ca ||
children.translated_text: and one quarter each of ash of <s>śulba</s> (copper) and of <s>vimala</s>,
and also, separately, of <s>kānta</s>, mica-essence, and <s>sphaṭika</s>.
Having powdered everything together, one should calcine it with water of <s>triphalā</s>.
With thirty <s>vanagiriṇḍas</s>, one should pulverize that thirty times,
and mix it with equal parts of powders of <s>vyoṣa</s> and <s>vellaka</s>.
Licked with honey and ghee in the measure of one <s>valla</s>, it destroys
the eighty diseases born from <s>vāta</s>, and especially <s>dhanurvāta</s>.
It also destroys all diseases of <s>kapha</s> without remainder, and all urinary diseases in every way,

children.text: śvāsaṃ kāsaṃ kṣayaṃ pāṇḍuṃ śvayathuṃ śītakajvaram ||
children.translated_text: dyspnea, cough, wasting, anemia, swelling, and fever caused by cold,
<s>grahaṇī</s>, the disorder of <s>āma</s>, and very hard-to-cure weakness of the digestive fire,
as well as all disorders of fluid, according to the appropriate vehicle for each disease.

children.text: rītikā kākatuṇḍī ca dvividhaṃ pittalaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rītikā</s> and <s>kākatuṇḍī</s>: <s>pittala</s> is of two kinds.

children.text: saṃtāpya kāṃjike kṣiptā tāmrābhā rītikā matā ||
children.translated_text: When heated and thrown into sour gruel, the copper-colored one is considered <s>rītikā</s>.

children.text: evaṃ yā jāyate kṛṣṇā kākatuṇḍīti sā matā ||
children.translated_text: That which becomes black in the same way is considered <s>kākatuṇḍī</s>.
<s>Rīti</s> is bitter in taste, dry, destructive of organisms, and removes bloody <s>pitta</s>.
In a proper formulation it removes anemia and skin disease; it is hot in potency and also cooling.
<s>Kākatuṇḍī</s> is devoid of unctuousness, bitter and hot, and removes <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
It removes liver and spleen disease, and is declared to be cooling in potency.

children.text: gurvī mṛdvī ca pītābhā sārāṅgī tāḍanakṣamā
children.translated_text: Heavy, soft, yellowish, substantial, capable of being hammered,
very unctuous and smooth-bodied: <s>rīti</s> of such a kind is good.
Pale-yellow, rough, dry, uneven, incapable of being hammered,
foul-smelling and light: such <s>rīti</s> is not desired in mercurial and similar preparations.
After heating it and quenching it in the juice of <s>nirguṇḍī</s> mixed with powder of <s>śyāmā</s>,
<s>rīti</s> certainly attains purification in five repetitions.
Coated with citron juice, <s>śilā</s>, and sulfur, and calcined eight times,
<s>rīti</s> attains the state of ash; then it should be applied as appropriate.
Having performed its calcination as in the case of copper, one should use it everywhere.
Calcined <s>ārakūṭa</s>, <s>kānta</s>, and calcined mica-essence,
these three in equal parts, with an equal amount of <s>vyoṣa</s> joined with <s>jantughna</s>,
combined with <s>brahmabīja</s>, <s>ajamodā</s>, <s>agni</s>, <s>bhallātaka</s>, and sesame,
when used in the measure of a <s>niṣka</s>, is indeed vermicidal and destroys skin disease.
It especially destroys white leprosy; it kindles digestion, promotes digestion, and is beneficial.
Powder of golden <s>rītikā</s>, after being eaten and again enveloped,
by a black-colored, rutting, young goat,

children.text: talliptaṃ kharpare dagdhaṃ drutiṃ muñcati śobhanām
children.translated_text: when smeared with that and burned in a potsherd, releases a fine liquefaction.
Its appearance is like gold of fourteen brilliant colors,
and, when applied in mercurial <s>rasāyana</s>, it is said to transform the body and metals.
With eight parts of copper and two parts of <s>khuraka</s>,
when melted, <s>kāṃsya</s> is produced; that which comes from <s>Saurāṣṭra</s> is good.
It has a sharp sound, is soft and unctuous, and is slightly dark and white,

children.text: nirmalaṃ dāharaktaṃ ca ṣoḍhā kāṃsyaṃ praśasyate ||
children.translated_text: clear and red when heated; in these six respects <s>kāṃsya</s> is praised.

children.text: tatpītaṃ dahane tāmraṃ kharaṃ rūkṣaṃ ghanāsaham
children.translated_text: That which is yellow, coppery in the fire, rough, dry, and unable to bear heavy blows,
with a dull sound and lost luster: <s>kāṃsya</s> with these seven defects should be rejected.

children.text: kāṃsyaṃ laghu ca tiktoṣṇaṃ lekhanaṃ dṛkprasādanam
children.translated_text: <s>Kāṃsya</s> is light, bitter, hot, scraping, and clears the eyesight.
It removes worms and skin disease, pacifies <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>, kindles digestion, and is beneficial.
Except for ghee alone, whatever else has been in <s>kāṃsya</s>, for people,
when eaten, gives health and comfort, is beneficial, and makes food wholesome by habituation.

children.text: taptaṃ kāṃsyaṃ gavāṃ mūtre vāpitaṃ pariśudhyati ||
children.translated_text: Heated <s>kāṃsya</s>, quenched in cow urine, is purified.
It is calcined with sulfur and <s>tāla</s>, and becomes non-revivable in five <s>puṭas</s>.
One should levigate the three alkalis and the five salts seven times with a sour liquid.
One should smear leaves of <s>kāṃsya</s> and <s>ārakūṭa</s> with that paste.
Sealed and cooked in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>, it attains the state of pure ash.
What is produced from <s>kāṃsya</s>, <s>arka</s>, <s>rīti</s>, iron, and <s>ahi</s> is <s>vartaloha</s>.
That very thing is called <s>pañcaloha</s> by those who know metals.
It is cold, sour, pungent, dry, and destroys <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>.

children.text: rucyaṃ tvacyaṃ kṛmighnaṃ ca netryaṃ malaviśodhanam ||
children.translated_text: It is appetizing, good for the skin, worm-killing, good for the eyes, and purifies the stool.
All rice, side dishes, and soups prepared in that vessel,
provided they are without sour ingredients, are very kindling, digestive, and beneficial.
Melted <s>vartaloha</s>, thrown into horse urine, is purified.
<s>Vartaloha</s> is calcined by being treated with sulfur and <s>tāla</s> in a <s>puṭa</s>.
In these various formulations here, it should be used according to rule.
Only with genuine substances, purified and properly prepared according to rule,
with <s>rasas</s>, <s>uparasas</s>, metals, and the like, does mercury succeed, and not otherwise.
Gems, metals, cowries, shells, stone-derived substances, hoof, horn, and bone,

children.text: mahārasādyeṣu kaṭhoradehaṃ bhasmīkṛtaṃ syāt khalu sūtayogyam ||
children.translated_text: and the hard-bodied substances among the great minerals and so on, when reduced to ash, are indeed suitable for mercury.
For the sake of melting diamonds, I shall describe the essence produced from <s>bhūnāga</s>.
That indeed is the supreme fiery potency for the king mercury and for diamonds.
What is produced from washed <s>bhūnāga</s> should be ground with liquids from <s>bhṛṅgaja</s>.
and separately for three days with lemon juices and with the fresh juices of <s>nirguṇḍī</s>.
That, joined with the <s>drāvaṇa-gaṇa</s> (group of solvents), should be ground and made into pellets.
After sealing it in a firm crucible, one should blow the fire strongly for two <s>daṇḍas</s>.
When it has cooled by itself, one should collect it and place it on a slab.
The small grains, equal to mustard seeds, are particles endowed with very great weight.
Having combined the grains with a twelfth part of <s>arka</s> and smelted them, one should remove the grains.
Quickly washing the grains, one should gather them carefully.
With that, one may carry out the melting of diamond and the like as desired.
This is called <s>khara-sattva</s>; it is an unsurpassed <s>rasāyana</s>.
In two or three crucibles, the essence of one crucible certainly comes into being.
Taking <s>bhujaṅgamas</s> measuring four <s>prasthas</s>,
earth-born ones arising from gold, silver, copper, iron, <s>kānta</s>, and <s>saṃbhūti</s>,
one should wash them with waters of turmeric and also with cool waters.

children.text: upoṣitaṃ mayūraṃ vā śūraṃ vā caraṇāyudham ||
children.translated_text: Then a fasting peacock, or else a strong cock whose feet are weapons,
should be fed with them in sequence, and its droppings should then be collected.

children.text: kṣārāmlaiḥ saha saṃpeṣya viśoṣya ca kharātape ||
children.translated_text: Grinding them with alkaline and sour substances, and drying them in fierce sunlight,

children.text: tataḥ kharparake kṣiptvā bharjayitvā maṣīṃ caret
children.translated_text: one should then put them into a potsherd, roast them, and make a black ash.
That ash, joined with the <s>drāvaṇa</s> group, should be well triturated.
After sealing it inside a furnace chamber, one should blow the fire for two <s>ghaṭikās</s>.
From the cooled crucible, one should take out the lump and grind it.
Washing the fine grains, one should collect them carefully.
Having smelted them in the manner used for gold, one should make grains and apply them.

children.text: bhūnāgodbhavasattvamuttamamidaṃ śrīsomadevoditaṃ dattaṃ pādamitaṃ dviśāṇakanakenaikaṃ gatenormikām
children.translated_text: This excellent essence produced from <s>bhūnāga</s>, taught by <s>Śrī Somadeva</s>, when given in a quarter-measure with two <s>śāṇas</s> of gold, one portion made into a ring,

children.text: taddhautāmbuvilepitaṃ sthiracarodbhūtaṃ viṣaṃ netraruk śūlaṃ mūlagadaṃ ca karṇajarujo hanyāt prasūtigraham ||
children.translated_text: and applied with the water in which it has been washed, destroys poison produced by stationary and moving beings, eye pain, colic, disease of the root, pains arising in the ear, and <s>prasūtigraha</s>.
Having crushed the roots of <s>uttaravāruṇī</s> in sour gruel,
one should add the crushed pulp of <s>aṅkolla</s> seeds.
Its oil, thick like ghee, should then be collected according to rule.
Then, after grinding the leaves of <s>uttaravāruṇī</s> and <s>peṭakārī</s>,
one should rub them with that paste, using sour gruel.
And the powder of <s>aṅkolla</s> seeds should be tied in a loosely woven cloth.
Hanging that in intense sunlight, one should place a cup beneath it.
The oil that falls into it should be taken; it destroys white leprosy.
Powder produced from <s>aṅkolla</s> seeds should be rubbed with sour gruel.
After it has stayed one night, it should then be made into a ball.
One should steam it in the ball-apparatus for two <s>ghaṭikās</s>.

children.text: tāṃ ca piṇḍīṃ dṛḍhe vastre baddhvā niṣpīḍya kāṣṭhataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then that lump should be tied in a strong cloth and pressed with a piece of wood.
The oil situated in the vessel below should be collected and applied.
In this way, by means of the ball-apparatus, all oils should be obtained.
There may also be oil of <s>aṅkola</s> from <s>kākatuṇḍī</s> together with its root.
And oil from <s>vākucī</s> and <s>devadālī</s> may be produced from the root of <s>karkoṭī</s>.
With a decoction of <s>apāmārga</s>, oil may be produced from <s>viṣamuṣṭi</s>.
With decoctions of the roots of <s>kumārī</s>, one should obtain oil born from <s>jaipāla</s>.
With decoctions of red <s>apāmārga</s>, one should obtain <s>vākucī</s> oil.
One should make powders of the seeds of black <s>kākatuṇḍī</s>,
and also powder of <s>kānta-pāṣāṇa</s>; having combined them, one should seal them up.
Afterwards, when it has been placed in a heap of grain, one should take it out and collect the oil.
Having examined all the <s>rasaśāstras</s> in due order,
this is now being made manifest for the benefit of practitioners.

children.text: na krameṇa vinā śāstraṃ na śāstreṇa vinā kramaḥ
children.translated_text: There is no śāstra without procedure, and no procedure without śāstra.

children.text: śāstraṃ kramayutaṃ jñātvā yaḥ karoti sa siddhibhāk ||
children.translated_text: The one who acts after knowing śāstra furnished with procedure becomes a possessor of success.
The teacher should be knowledgeable, skillful, and thoroughly versed in <s>rasaśāstra</s>,
perfected in mantras, very heroic, and steadily devoted to <s>Śiva</s>.
He should be a devotee of the Goddess, always steadfast, and devoted to worship of the deity.
He should know the particular teachings of all the transmissions and be skilled in operations with mercury.
One endowed with such characteristics should be the guru of <s>rasavidyā</s>.
Pupils should be devoted to the guru, of good conduct, truthful, and firm in their vows.
They should be free from laziness, know their own duty, and always obey commands.
They should be free from hypocrisy and jealousy, and initiated into the family traditions.
They should be exceedingly diligent, peaceful, and intent on the worship of mantras.
Endowed with these characteristics, pupils are fit for success with mercury.
There, assistants should be energetic, and even more so than the pupils.
They should be well-born and devoted to their master, and should be appointed in operations with mercury.
Those who are unbelievers, of bad conduct, grasping, or opposed to the guru,
and who desire to obtain the knowledge through theft, deceit, and base excitement,
for them nothing at all succeeds, whether gems, mantras, medicines, or the like.

children.text: kurvanti yadi mohena nāśayanti svakaṃ dhanam
children.translated_text: If they act out of delusion, they destroy their own wealth.

children.text: iha loke sukhaṃ nāsti paraloke tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: There is no happiness in this world, and likewise none in the next.
Therefore, when the guru is satisfied by the very strength of devotion,
then that knowledge is to be received by the pupil for self-success in <s>rasavidyā</s>.
Having obtained the boon through the joining of hand and head, he should practice it well.
In a land free from disease, in a delightful righteous kingdom,
in an auspicious prosperous city furnished with <s>Umā</s> and <s>Maheśvara</s>,
there the wise person should undertake the practice of <s>Rasarāja</s>.
In an exceedingly pleasant grove, adorned with four gates,
there a spacious and delightful hall should be built.
properly furnished with windows and ornamented with splendid pictures.
Near that, on level and shining ground, a <s>rasamaṇḍapa</s> (mercurial pavilion) should be made,
very secluded, very spacious, and beautified with door-panels and bolts.
It should be richly furnished with banners, parasols, and canopies, with flower-garlands hanging down,
and resounding with the sounds of kettledrums, trumpets, bells, horns, and the like.

children.text: bhūḥ samā tatra kartavyā sudṛḍhā darpaṇopamā
children.translated_text: There the ground should be made level, very firm, and like a mirror.
In its center a lovely altar, possessing the proper marks, should be made.
A gold leaf of three niṣkas and nine niṣkas of <s>rasendra</s> (mercury)

children.text: amlena mardayed yāmaṃ tena liṅgaṃ tu kārayet ||
children.translated_text: should be ground with an acid for one watch; with that one should make a liṅga.
In a swing-apparatus, with a pith-tube, it should be cooked for a day while placed in citron juice.
One should worship that liṅga there with very auspicious services.
The fruit that comes from properly worshipping a thousand crores of liṅgas,
that fruit, multiplied ten millionfold, arises from worshipping a <s>rasaliṅga</s> (mercury liṅga).
Thousands of killings of brahmins and indeed tens of thousands of killings of cows
go to destruction at that very moment by the sight of the <s>rasaliṅga</s>.
Liberation is obtained by touching it: this is true, spoken by <s>Śiva</s>.
In the southeast one should worship with the great king of mantras called <s>Śrīghora</s>.
One should contemplate the <s>rasaliṅga</s> as having eighteen arms, white, five-faced, three-eyed,
mounted on a corpse, and blue-throated.
In its lap one should visualize the great goddess, single-faced and four-armed,
holding a rosary and goad on the right, and a noose and the auspicious gesture of fearlessness on the left,
gleaming like heated gold and clothed in yellow garments.

children.text: vāṅmayī śrīḥ kāmarājaśaktibījaṃ rasāṅkuśāyai namo dvādaśārṇaiṣā jñeyā vidyā rasāṅkuśā ||
children.translated_text: The twelve-syllabled vidyā should be known as <s>Rasāṅkuśā</s>: speech, fortune, the <s>Kāmarāja</s> śakti-bīja, and 'namo rasāṅkuśāyai'.
With this one should worship the goddess with fragrances, flowers, unbroken grains, and so on.
One should worship <s>Nandī</s>, <s>Bhṛṅgī</s>, <s>Mahākāla</s>, and <s>Kulīra</s> in order from the eastern direction,
with name-mantras beginning with praṇava and ending in namaḥ.
Thus daily worship should be performed there for the sake of success with mercury.
The science of mercury was taught by <s>Śiva</s>; it should indeed be given to a practitioner
by the guru, with a delighted mind, according to the prescribed procedure.
At an excellent moment, under an excellent lunar mansion, when the moon and stars are strong,
one should set down a water-filled kalaśa, furnished with gold, jewels, and fruits,
in front of the <s>rasaliṅga</s>, wrapped in a splendid cloth.
One should worship it well with fragrances, flowers, unbroken grains, incenses, and food-offerings.
At the end of the worship one should perform an oblation in a well-marked womb-shaped fire-pit,
separately with sesame, ghee, milk-rice, flowers, dill, and the like.
With <s>Aghora</s> and with <s>Rasāṅkuśī</s>, at the end of the oblation, one should summon the disciple,
together with a <s>kālinī</s> śakti and devoted to success with mercury.

children.text: yasyāstu kuñcitāḥ keśāḥ śyāmā yā padmalocanā
children.translated_text: A woman whose hair is curly, who is dark, lotus-eyed,
beautiful, young, sexually opened, with broad hips, and auspicious,
whose chest is narrow and who bends under the weight of full breasts,
tender in kissing, embracing, and touch, and soft-spoken,
beautiful in the region of the yoni, which is like an aśvattha leaf,

children.text: kṛṣṇapakṣe puṣpavatī sā nārī kālinī smṛtā
children.translated_text: and menstruating in the dark fortnight: that woman is remembered as a <s>kālinī</s>.

children.text: rasabandhe prayoge ca uttamā sā rasāyane ||
children.translated_text: She is the best in binding mercury, in practical application, and in rasāyana.

children.text: tadabhāve surūpā tu yā kācit taruṇāṅganā
children.translated_text: In her absence, any beautiful young woman
should be given sulfur mixed with ghee for three weeks,
one karṣa each morning; she becomes equal to a <s>kālinī</s>.

children.text: evaṃ śaktiyuto yo 'sau dīkṣayet taṃ gurūttamaḥ
children.translated_text: The best guru should initiate the man who is thus joined with a śakti.
After he has bathed well, the guru should consecrate him with the waters of the kalaśa by means of the mantra.
The true guru should give the disciple the <s>Aghorāṅkuśī</s> vidyā.
A proper guru-gift should be given by the good disciple according to his ability.
Then, by the guru's command, he should recite the mantra, each one a hundred thousand times.

children.text: oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ adyoratara prasphuṭa 2 prakaṭa 2 oṃ hrīṃ hraiṃ hrauṃ hrūṃ aghorāya phaṭ imam aghoramantraṃ tu auṃ kāmarājaśaktibījarasāṅkuśāyai ājñayā vidyāṃ rasāṅkuśām
children.translated_text: Oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ adyoratara prasphuṭa prasphuṭa prakaṭa prakaṭa oṃ hrīṃ hraiṃ hrauṃ hrūṃ aghorāya phaṭ: this is the <s>Aghora</s> mantra; and, by the command, the vidyā <s>Rasāṅkuśā</s> is oṃ, with the <s>Kāmarāja</s> śakti-bīja, rasāṅkuśāyai.
With this one should worship the goddess, the śakti, by means of the goad-vidyā.
One should offer one tenth as oblation in a triangular fire-pit one hasta in measure,
using jasmine flowers smeared with the three sweets; at the completion, maidens are to be worshipped.
Then, having done this, he should enter a clean hall, smeared and provided with an altar.
There he should draw a six-cornered maṇḍala with vermilion, two hastas in size.
On the altar he should properly draw it, and outside it an eight-petaled
lotus, square and adorned with four gates.
In the pericarp he should place an iron mortar inscribed with gold.
In its center he should place <s>rasarāja</s> (king mercury), measuring one hundred palas,
or fifty or twenty-five, and worship it like the <s>rasaliṅga</s>.
Diamond, vaikrānta, vajrābhra, kāntapāṣāṇa, borax,
and earthworm: these śaktis should be worshipped in order in the six corners.
Sulfur, orpiment, green vitriol, realgar, kaṅkuṣṭha, bhūṣaṇa,

children.text: rājāvarto gairikaṃ ca khyātā uparasā amī
children.translated_text: lapis lazuli, and red ocher: these are known as the uparasas.
They should be worshipped on the eight petals, in order from the east to the northeast.

children.text: rasakaṃ vimalā tāpyaṃ capalā tuttham añjanam
children.translated_text: Rasaka, vimalā, tāpya, capalā, blue vitriol, and collyrium,

children.text: hiṅgulaṃ sasyakaṃ caiva khyātā ete mahārasāḥ
children.translated_text: cinnabar and sasyaka: these are known as the mahārasas.
They should be worshipped on the tips of the petals, from the east through the northeast.
At the eastern gate, gold and silver; at the southern, copper and lead;
at the western, tin and kānta; and at the northern, muṇḍa and tīkṣṇa iron.
All this should be worshipped with <s>Aghora</s>, accompanied by the goad.
Viḍa salts, sour-gruel apparatuses, alkalis, clay, salts, and
furnaces, crucibles, bent tubes, husk-charcoal, and forest dung-cakes;
bellows, many rods, stones, grinding mortars, and other mortars,
goldsmiths' equipment and all kinds of balances as well;
and various vessels made from clay, wood, copper, and iron,
the groups of divine herbs, and coloring and lubricating substances:
these should be worshipped outside the doorway with the root-mantra.

children.text: vāṅmāyā hrīṃ tataḥ kṣeṃ ca kṣmaśca pañcākṣaro manuḥ
children.translated_text: The mantra of five syllables is vāṅ, māyā, hrīṃ, then kṣeṃ and kṣmaṃ.
With this mantra one should worship <s>Bhairava</s> there.
Then one should recite the names of all the rasa-siddhas.
<s>Vyālācārya</s>, <s>Candrasena</s>, <s>Subuddhi</s>, <s>Naravāhana</s>,
<s>Nāgārjuna</s>, <s>Ratnaghoṣa</s>, <s>Surānanda</s>, <s>Yaśodhana</s>,
<s>Indra</s>, <s>Māṇḍavya</s>, <s>Carpaṭī</s>, and <s>Śūrasenaka</s>,

children.text: āgamo nāgabuddhiś ca khaṇḍaḥ kāpāliko mataḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Āgama</s>, <s>Nāgabuddhi</s>, and <s>Khaṇḍa Kāpālika</s> are recognized;
<s>Kāmāri</s>, <s>Tāntrika</s>, <s>Śambhu</s>, <s>Laṅkālampaṭa</s>, and <s>Śārada</s>,
<s>Bāṇāsura</s>, the best of sages, <s>Govinda</s>, <s>Kapila</s>, and <s>Bali</s>:

children.text: ete sarve tu sūtendrā rasasiddhā mahābalāḥ
children.translated_text: all these are lords of mercury, great and powerful rasa-siddhas.
They move through all the worlds, constantly intent on enjoyment.
Twenty-seven in number, they are givers of success in rasa.
Physicians should carefully worship them; after that one should perform the worship of rasa.
Gladdening brahmins and gods, one should satisfy one's chosen deities.
Maidens, yoginīs, lords of yoga, and practitioners of the ritual assembly
should be satisfied and worshipped with devotion, according to one's ability.
Thus one should perform the rasa festival furnished with all the required materials,
for the pacification of all obstacles and as a giver of every desired fruit.
But if some deluded man, without the procedure of mantra-initiation,
and without a guru, wishes to carry out the practice of <s>sūta</s> (mercury),
he does not attain success even by hundreds of crores of efforts.
Therefore, with every effort, one should have the rite performed as taught in scripture.

children.text: samyaksādhanasodyamā guruyutā rājājñayālaṃkṛtā nānākarmaparāṅmukhā rasaparāś cāḍhyā janaiścārthitāḥ
