children.translated_text: Those who are properly intent on practice, joined with a guru, authorized by royal command, turned away from various other occupations, devoted to rasa, wealthy, and sought out by people,

children.text: mātrāyantrasupākakarmakuśalāḥ sarvauṣadhe kovidāḥ teṣāṃ sidhyati nānyathā vidhibalācchrīpāradaḥ pāradaḥ ||
children.translated_text: skilled in measures, apparatuses, and well-cooked operations, and expert in all medicines: for them, by the force of rule, the blessed <s>Pārada</s> succeeds, and not otherwise.
The <s>rasaśāstra</s> should be given to brahmins for the sake of <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: rājñe vaiśyāya vṛddhyarthaṃ dāsyārtham itarasya ca ||
children.translated_text: to a king and to a vaiśya for prosperity, and to another for the sake of service.
When the guru is pleased, <s>Śiva</s> is pleased; when <s>Śiva</s> is pleased, so too is rasa.

children.text: rase tuṣṭe kriyāḥ sarvāḥ sidhyantyeva na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When rasa is pleased, all operations surely succeed; there is no doubt.
The science of rasa must be firmly guarded, surely like a mother's secret.

children.text: bhaved vīryavatī guptā nirvīryā ca prakāśanāt ||
children.translated_text: When kept secret it becomes potent; when revealed it loses its potency.
It should not be made known to a patient, nor should it be known by many.
A medicine that has become known among many patients becomes powerless.
One should construct a <s>rasaśālā</s> in a place free from every affliction,
in a pleasant region containing all herbs and furnished with a well.
It should be in a beautiful division of the quarters of <s>Yakṣa</s>, <s>Tryakṣa</s>, or <s>Sahasrākṣa</s>,
equipped with many implements and made handsome by an enclosing wall.
In the eastern part of the hall one should install <s>Rasabhairava</s>.
Fire-operations should be in the southeast, and stone-work in the south.
Operations with sharp instruments should be in the southwest, and washing and the like in the west.
Drying should be in the northwest, and piercing operations in the north.
The placement of perfected substances should be done in the northeast corner.
The collection of materials should be made for the purpose of accomplishing rasa.
One should gather a furnace for extracting essence and a beautiful dripping furnace,
a ground-furnace, a movable furnace, and many water troughs,
likewise a pair of bellows and tubes of bamboo and iron,
basins made of gold, iron, bell-metal, copper, stone, and also leather,
and various instruments and substances as well.
There should be pounding and grinding implements, small ones shaped like troughs and round ones,
iron heated mortars and pestles of the same kind,
and a sieve furnished with a thousand fine holes for the filtering of substances.

children.text: cālanī ca kaṭatrāṇi śalākā hi ca kuṇḍalī ||
children.translated_text: There should also be sieves, basket-guards, rods, and a ring.

children.text: cālanī trividhā proktā tatsvarūpaṃ ca kathyate
children.translated_text: A sieve is said to be of three kinds, and its form is now described.
The one made from bamboo rods and woven with cords

children.text: kīrtitā sā sadā sthūladravyāṇāṃ gālane hitā ||
children.translated_text: is said always to be useful for filtering coarse substances.
There is also another bamboo-made sieve for the purpose of sifting powder.
It is well made with fiber from karṇikāra, śālmalī, or harijāta,
and is furnished with a width of four fingers.
A ring, a cubit across, is wrapped with goat-skin.
Another sieve has its bottom bound with cloth made of horsehair.
With it one should perform sifting in order to retain very fine dust.
Clay for crucibles, husk, cotton, and powdered forest dung-cake,
and the threefold medicine made from mineral, animal, and root substances,

children.text: śikhitrā govaraṃ caiva śarkarā ca sitopalā ||
children.translated_text: <s>śikhitrā</s>, cow-dung, sugar, and white sugar-candy are to be gathered.
<s>Śikhitrās</s>, the leavings of fire, are coals known as <s>kokilā</s>.
<s>Kokilās</s> are kindled coals, extinguished without water.

children.text: piṣṭakaṃ chagaṇaṃ chāṇam upalaṃ cotpalaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Piṣṭaka</s>, <s>chagaṇa</s>, <s>chāṇa</s>, <s>upala</s>, and <s>utpala</s>,
<s>giriṇḍa</s>, <s>upala</s>, and <s>sāṭhī</s> are names for thoroughly dried dung.
There should be small bottles and cups made of glass, iron, clay, and cowrie-shell.

children.text: kūpikā kupikā siddhā golā caiva giriṇḍikā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kūpikā</s>, <s>kupikā</s>, <s>siddhā</s>, <s>golā</s>, and <s>giriṇḍikā</s>

children.text: caṣakaṃ ca kaṭorī ca vāṭikā khārikā tathā
children.translated_text: and <s>caṣaka</s>, <s>kaṭorī</s>, <s>vāṭikā</s>, and <s>khārikā</s> as well.
<s>Kañcolī</s> and <s>grāhikā</s>: these names indeed have one and the same meaning.
Winnowing baskets and other bamboo vessels, small śiprās and shell-like vessels,
razor-knives, and likewise cooking vessels, and whatever else is useful there,
pālikās, karṇikās, and little knives for cutting vegetables,
and whatever work is connected with sweeping the hall and the like up to the cooking of mercury,
and whatever else is useful there: all that, by means of the higher vidyā,
with the revered <s>Rasāṅkuśā</s>, should be consecrated with mantras and worshipped.
Otherwise the <s>Bhairavas</s> seize the fiery power that has entered it.
Physicians who think about mercury, those who know lexicons, and practical specialists,
and those who know the languages born in all regions, should also be gathered by the practitioners.
At the completion of the cooking of mercury one should always recite the <s>Aghora</s> mantra.
The attendants should be energetic, pure, brave, and strong.
A man who is highly righteous, truthful in speech, learned, a worshipper of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Keśava</s>,
compassionate, and lotus-handed should be appointed in the medical work of mercury.
He whose hand bears marks of a banner, water-pot, lotus, fish, and bow,
and a line-mark below the ring finger, is one who possesses an immortal hand.
A physician who is without initiation, devoid of compassion, greedy, and without a guru,
and whose hand has black lines, is called one with a burnt hand.
Those who know mantras of restraint should be appointed in the practice for obtaining treasure.
Those who are strong and truthful, red-eyed and dark-bodied,
and who know the lore for terrifying spirits, should be appointed in the rite of bali-offering.
Those who are free from greed, truthful speakers, worshippers of gods and brahmins,
self-controlled and eaters of wholesome food, should be appointed in rasāyana.
Those who are wealthy, generous, and furnished with all equipment,
and are always devoted to the guru's word, are auspicious in discourses on metals.
Those who know the names of each particular medicine, are pure, and are free from deception,
and who know the languages of many regions, are considered suitable for collecting medicines.
For those who are pure, truthful in speech, faithful, and resolute,
whose minds are free from doubt, mercury always succeeds.
That mercury, perfected by the eighteen operations, belongs to the foremost practitioner.

children.text: hā raso naṣṭamityuktvā sevetānyatra taṃ rasam ||
children.translated_text: Having said, 'Alas, the mercury is lost,' he should use that mercury elsewhere.

children.text: rasasiddho bhavenmartyo dātā bhoktā na yācakaḥ
children.translated_text: A mortal who has perfected mercury becomes a giver and enjoyer, not a beggar;
freed from old age, honored by the world, divinely radiant, and always happy.
For the awakening of deluded physicians, <s>Somadeva</s> explains
the terminology of <s>Rasendra</s>, as stated in the śāstras and by the perfected masters.

children.text: ardhaṃ siddharasasya tailaghṛtayorlehasya bhāgo'ṣṭamaḥ saṃsiddhākhilalohacūrṇavaṭakādīnāṃ tathā saptamaḥ
children.translated_text: Half of perfected mercury, an eighth share of oil, ghee, or electuary, and likewise a seventh of pills and the like made from fully perfected powders of all metals,

children.text: yo dīyeta bhiṣagvarāya gadibhirnirdiśya dhanvantarim sarvārogyasukhāptaye nigadito bhāgaḥ sa dhanvantareḥ ||
children.translated_text: which patients should give to the best physician, invoking <s>Dhanvantari</s> for the attainment of complete health and happiness, is declared to be the share of <s>Dhanvantari</s>.
Even of the material bought for medicine, the eleventh share

children.text: vaṇigbhyo gṛhyate vaidyai rudrabhāgaḥ sa ucyate ||
children.translated_text: which physicians take from merchants is called the share of <s>Rudra</s>.
A greedy-minded physician who, after taking more than the proper <s>Rudra</s>-share,
has an improper medicine administered, is a betrayer of trust.
Mercury ground with dry substances such as metals and sulfur,
very smooth and resembling lampblack, is called <s>kajjalī</s>.

children.text: sadravā marditā saiva rasapaṅka iti smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: That same mixture, when ground with liquid, is remembered as <s>rasapaṅka</s>.

children.text: arkāṃśatulyād rasato 'tha gandhān niṣkārdhatulyāt truṭiśo 'bhi khalle
children.translated_text: From mercury in the measure of an arka-share and then from sulfur equal to half a niṣka, placed little by little in a mortar,

children.text: arkātape tīvratare vimardyāt piṣṭī bhavet sā navanītarūpā ||
children.translated_text: when it is ground in very strong sunlight, it becomes a <s>piṣṭī</s> with the form of fresh butter.

children.text: khalle vimardya gandhena dugdhena saha pāradam
children.translated_text: Having ground mercury in a mortar with sulfur and milk,

children.text: peṣaṇāt piṣṭatāṃ yāti sā piṣṭīti matā paraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: through grinding it reaches the state of a paste; that is regarded by others as <s>piṣṭī</s>.
With gold as a fourth part, rubbed with mercury for sixty ghaṭikās,
it becomes that <s>pātanapiṣṭī</s>, giving the highest success of mercury.
Silver or gold, struck by mercury, sulfur, and the like,

children.text: samutthitaṃ ca bahuśaḥ sā kṛṣṭī hematārayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: and repeatedly brought up, is the <s>kṛṣṭī</s> of gold and silver.

children.text: piṣṭīṃ kṣipet suvarṇāntar na varṇo hīyate tayā ||
children.translated_text: One should cast <s>piṣṭī</s> into gold; by it the color is not diminished.
The seed made with gold-<s>kṛṣṭī</s> colors mercury.
Having melted copper joined with tīkṣṇa iron and thrown it in many times
into lakuca juice mixed with sulfur, an excellent metal comes forth.
Gold reddened with that is called <s>hemaraktī</s>.
When that is cast into molten gold, it produces an excellence of color;
it also colors silver and produces color in the bīja.
In exactly this way an attractive <s>tāraraktī</s> should be prepared,
which is indeed a colorant for silver and also a colorant for bījas.

children.text: mṛtena vā baddharasena vānyallohena vā sādhitamanyaloham
children.translated_text: Another metal prepared with killed mercury, with bound mercury, or with another metal,

children.text: sitaṃ ca pītatvamupāgataṃ taddalaṃ hi candrānalayoḥ prasiddham ||
children.translated_text: when white has become yellow, is known as <s>dala</s> in the case of silver and gold.
Or, joined with mercury that has been bound over the course of a month,

children.text: sādhitaṃ vānyalohena sitaṃ pītaṃ ca taddalam ||
children.translated_text: or prepared with another metal, that which is white and yellow is <s>dala</s>.
Copper killed with mākṣika and brought up ten times,
and, in the same way, thoroughly purified lead: this pair, four palas in quantity,
is again killed with blue collyrium and brought up seven times.
Thus, when it has been perfectly prepared, this is proclaimed to be <s>śulvanāga</s>.
The lord mercury prepared with that, when held in the mouth by men,
destroys the mass of urinary disorders, especially within a single month.
For one who eats wholesome food, within a year, along with gray hair and wrinkles,
there is vulture-like sight, shining robustness, and complete freedom from disease.

children.text: lohaṃ lohāntare kṣiptaṃ dhmātaṃ nirvāpitaṃ drave
children.translated_text: When one metal is cast into another metal, blown upon, and quenched in a liquid,
and becomes pale-yellow in luster, it is called <s>piñjarī</s>.

children.text: bhāgāḥ ṣoḍaśa tārasya tathā dvādaśa bhāsvataḥ
children.translated_text: Sixteen parts of silver, and likewise twelve parts of gold,
when melted together, are thereby called <s>candrārka</s>, 'moon-and-sun'.
If another metal is introduced through a bent tube into the metal being treated,
physicians call that quenching process <s>nirvāhaṇa</s> (carrying through).
One should put in a quenching substance equal in amount to the material to be carried through,

children.text: āvāhyaṃ vāpanīye ca bhāge dṛṣṭe ca dṛṣṭavat ||
children.translated_text: and, when the amount to be introduced into what is being infused has been observed, one should act according to what is seen.

children.text: mṛtaṃ tarati yattoye lohaṃ vāritaraṃ hi tat ||
children.translated_text: A calcined metal that floats on water is indeed called <s>vāritara</s> (water-floater).
That which, when rubbed between thumb and forefinger, enters into the lines of the skin,
is designated calcined metal, on account of the name <s>rekhāpūrṇa</s> (filling the lines).
When combined with jaggery, guñjā, sukhasparśa, honey, and ghee,
and it does not return to its original state through blowing, it is called <s>apunarbhava</s> (non-reversion).
Upon it one should place a heavy substance and also grain, without fail;
if it crosses the water like a goose, it is declared excellent.

children.text: raupyeṇa saha saṃyuktaṃ dhmātaṃ raupyeṇa cel laget
children.translated_text: If, when combined with silver and blown, it adheres to the silver,
then that metal is said to be <s>niruttha</s> (non-rising), and it is <s>apunarbhava</s>.
When, through a particular kind of quenching, it becomes each particular color,
being soft and suitable for varied processing, that is called <s>bīja</s> (seed).
This very process is indeed specified by physicians as <s>uttaraṇa</s> (removal):
the destruction of one of two metals that have come into contact.
When thoroughly blown through a bent tube, that is called <s>tāḍana</s> (striking).
Powdered mica, mixed with rice, tied in a cloth in sour gruel,
and forced out from the cloth by rubbing, is called <s>dhānyābhra</s> (grain-mica).
When something is blown in an ore-furnace together with alkaline, sour, and liquefying agents,
the essence that comes out from it is called <s>sattva</s> (metallic essence).
Through blowing with charcoal pieces filling the top of the furnace,
when they reach the neck of the crucible, it is considered <s>ekakolīsaka</s>.

children.text: drāvaṇe sattvapāte ca mādhukāḥ khādirāḥ śubhāḥ
children.translated_text: For melting and for precipitating <s>sattva</s>, liquorice and khadira woods are good;

children.text: durdrāve vaṃśajāste tu svedane bādarāḥ śubhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: for what is hard to melt, bamboo-born charcoal is good, while for steaming, jujube wood is good.
The mercury drawn off from cinnabar, rubbed with ginger juice,
from an apparatus called <s>Vidyādhara</s>, is called <s>hiṅgulākṛṣṭa</s> (extracted from cinnabar).
Bell-metal containing a little orpiment, struck through a bent tube,
becomes copper freed of tin; that is called <s>ghoṣākṛṣṭa</s>.
When tīkṣṇa iron, furnished with blue collyrium, is repeatedly blown firm,
soft, black, and quick to melt, it is called excellent lead.
The re-emergence of what has been calcined is described by the name <s>utthāpana</s> (raising up).
The casting of a melted substance into a liquid is regarded as <s>ḍhālana</s> (pouring).
Thirty palas of lead, rubbed with the milk of bhānu,
should be thoroughly ground and heated in a closed crucible until only a karṣa remains.
It never undergoes loss at all, even by a thousand such heatings;
this volatile substance, arising from lead, has been taught by the practical authorities.

children.text: itthaṃ hi capalaḥ kāryo vaṅgasyāpi na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this same way a volatile substance should also be made from tin; there is no doubt.
Mercury by itself is bound when touched by a hand that has touched that substance.

children.text: sa raso dhātuvādeṣu śasyate na rasāyane
children.translated_text: That mercury is commended in metallurgical operations, but not in rasāyana,
for this was taught by <s>Lokanātha</s>, called <s>Kharvaṇa</s>.
After washing with water containing the excrement of earth-snakes, the impurity is removed;
that black-colored substance is called <s>dhauta</s> (washed) by the mercury specialists.
The combining of two substances by rubbing and blowing is called <s>dvaṃdvāna</s>.
A later addition of more of a substance than one part, in colored gold,
or a consumption of fire by liquids, is regarded by the adepts as <s>bhañjanī</s>.

children.text: pataṅgīkalkato jātā lohe tāre ca hematā
children.translated_text: The gold-color that arises in iron and in silver from paste of <s>pataṅgī</s>,
after remaining for a few days, passes away; that is considered <s>cullakā</s>.
The exudation, from metal colored for a long time or by blowing for a long time,
is specified as that called <s>pataṅgīrāga</s> (pataṅgī-redness).

children.text: drute dravyāntarakṣepo lohādye kriyate hi yaḥ
children.translated_text: The addition of another substance to a melted material, such as metal,
is <s>āvāpa</s>, <s>pratīvāpa</s>; that same act is considered <s>ācchādana</s> (covering).
When, after stopping for eight instants while the melted metal stands in the fire,
water is thrown on, that is remembered as <s>abhiṣeka</s> (sprinkling).

children.text: taptasyāpsu vinikṣepo nirvāpaḥ snapanaṃ ca tat ||
children.translated_text: Casting a heated substance into water is <s>nirvāpa</s> (quenching), and that is also <s>snapana</s> (bathing).
Operations such as <s>pratīvāpa</s> should be performed on melted metal that is very pure.
When the fire has blazing flames and is accompanied by a white upsurge,

children.text: śuddhāvartas tadā jñeyaḥ sa kālaḥ sattvanirgame ||
children.translated_text: then it is to be known as the pure melting state; that is the time for the emergence of <s>sattva</s>.
When, during blowing, a flame resembling the substance to be melted is seen,
this is its readiness for melting; that is called <s>bījāvarta</s> (seed-melting).
What cools while still in the fire is called <s>svāṅgaśītala</s> (self-cooled).
What is cool after being drawn away from the fire is called <s>bahiḥśīta</s> (externally cooled).
Cooking in a swing-apparatus with alkalis, acids, or medicinal substances
is called <s>svedana</s> (steaming), producing looseness of impurity.
Grinding together with the stated medicines, with all sour liquids and with sour gruel,
is called <s>mardana</s> (trituration), destroying external impurity.
What, through rubbing with the prescribed medicines, causes the loss of the state of being pulverized,
is <s>mūrchana</s> (stupefaction); it destroys the skin of tin, lead, and bhujaka.
What, by means such as steaming and heating in the sun, brings about the restoration of the original form,
is called <s>utthāpana</s> (raising), destroying the disorder of <s>mūrchā</s>.

children.text: svarūpasya vināśena piṣṭatvād bandhanaṃ hi tat
children.translated_text: Through the loss of its own form and through becoming pulverized, that indeed is <s>bandhana</s> (binding).
Mercury that has been mastered by learned experts is called <s>naṣṭapiṣṭi</s>, 'that whose paste has disappeared.'
For mercury triturated with the stated medicines and placed in an apparatus, upward, downward, and sideways
expulsion is said to have the name <s>pātana</s>; it destroys the coating born from contact with tin and lead.
The keeping of mercury mixed with water and rock salt for three days
in an <s>āsthāpanī</s> jar is called <s>rodhana</s>.
For mercury that has gained potency from <s>rodhana</s>, steaming is performed

children.text: kriyate pārade svedaḥ proktaṃ niyamanaṃ hi tat ||
children.translated_text: to remove its volatility; that indeed is said to be <s>niyamana</s>.
Combined with metals, minerals, roots, and the like, and placed inside a jar,

children.text: grāsārthaṃ tridinaṃ svedo dīpanaṃ tanmataṃ budhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: steaming for three days for the sake of its <s>grāsa</s> (morsel to be consumed) is considered <s>dīpana</s> by the wise.
For mercury of this measure, the quantity consisting of edible material,
when it is stated as 'so much,' is called the measure of the <s>grāsa</s>.

children.text: grāsasya cāraṇaṃ garbhe drāvaṇaṃ jāraṇaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: The causing of the <s>grāsa</s> to circulate, its melting in the womb, and its digestion:
thus <s>jāraṇā</s> is described by the best authorities as having three forms.
<s>Grāsa</s>, <s>piṇḍa</s>, and <s>pariṇāma</s> are again three other names.

children.text: samukhā nirmukhā ceti jāraṇā dvividhā punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Jāraṇā</s> is also twofold: with a mouth and without a mouth.
The mouthless <s>jāraṇā</s> is said to occur by the addition of seed in portions.

children.text: śuddhaṃ svarṇaṃ ca rūpyaṃ ca bījam ityabhidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: Pure gold and silver are called <s>bīja</s> (seed).
An insertion of seed to the extent of one sixty-fourth part is called a mouth.

children.text: evaṃ kṛte raso grāsalolupo mukhavān bhavet
children.translated_text: When this has been done, the mercury becomes possessed of a mouth and eager for its <s>grāsa</s>;
it becomes capable of eating even hard metals.

children.text: iyaṃ hi samukhā proktā jāraṇā mṛgacāriṇā ||
children.translated_text: This is called mouth-possessing <s>jāraṇā</s> by <s>Mṛgacārin</s>.
When, through combination with divine medicines, it remains in open furnaces,
that one, having a demon's mouth, would consume all metals and the rest.
The exhaustion of the <s>grāsa</s> in the belly of mercury is regarded as <s>cāraṇā</s>.
The melting in the womb of what has been swallowed is called <s>garbhadruti</s>.
But when liquefaction of solid essence and the like is produced externally
for the digestion of <s>rasendra</s> (lord mercury), that is called external liquefaction.

children.text: nirlepatvaṃ drutatvaṃ ca tejastvaṃ laghutā tathā
children.translated_text: Non-adhesiveness, fluidity, fiery brilliance, and lightness,
together with non-combination with mercury: these are the five marks of liquefaction.
When, by the combination of medicines and furnace-blowing, metal, mineral substances, and the like
remain in liquid form, that is called <s>druti</s> (liquefaction).
The transformation of a liquefied <s>grāsa</s> by means of <s>viḍa</s>, apparatuses, and the like
is called <s>jāraṇā</s>; its varieties exist by the crore.
Alkalis, acids, sulfur and related substances, urines, and pungent materials
for the purpose of digesting mercury's <s>grāsa</s>: that is called <s>viḍa</s>.
The production of colors such as yellow in mercury
through the digestion of well-prepared seeds, metals, and the like is called <s>rañjana</s> (coloring).
The insertion of gold and the like into mercury placed in an apparatus with oil,
which causes a greater piercing effect in metal, is called <s>sāraṇā</s>.
Mercury furnished with penetrating medicines and cast into a substance

children.text: vedha ityucyate tajjñaiḥ sa cānekavidhaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: is called <s>vedha</s> by those who know; and it is remembered as being of many kinds.
They are <s>lepa</s>, <s>kṣepa</s>, <s>kunta</s>, the one called smoke, and the one designated sound.

children.text: lepanaṃ kurute lohaṃ svarṇaṃ vā rajataṃ tathā
children.translated_text: When it coats metal, or gold, or silver,

children.text: lepavedhaḥ sa vijñeyaḥ puṭamatra ca saurakam ||
children.translated_text: that should be known as <s>lepavedha</s>; here the heating is <s>sauraka</s>.
Insertion into melted metal is the <s>vedha</s> called <s>kṣepa</s>.
The drawing out of a melted substance by mercury held with tongs,
which produces the state of gold and the like, is called <s>kuntavedha</s>.
When fire is smoking, by the smoke of mercury thrown inside,
the production of gold and the like in metal is called <s>dhūmavedha</s>.
By blowing upon a small amount of metal with mercury kept in the mouth,
the production of the state of gold or silver is called <s>śabdavedha</s>.
The removal of discoloration and the like from a perfected substance by means of mercury,
and the revealing of its color, is called <s>udghāṭana</s>.
When a vessel is sealed very carefully together with alkalis, acids, and medicines,
and is carefully buried in the ground, that is called <s>svedana</s>.
For mercury mixed with medicines and sealed carefully in a vessel,
placing it inside a stove furnished with a gentle fire is called <s>saṃnyāsa</s>.
These two, <s>sveda</s> and <s>saṃnyāsa</s>, certainly belong to <s>rasarāja</s> (king mercury);
they generate qualities and powers and also cause rapid pervasion.
Having taken from every side, from the great ocean of mercury scripture, the jewels called very clear definitions,

children.text: vyaracayadatiyatnāttairimāṃ kaṇṭhamālāṃ kalayatu bhiṣagagryo maṇḍanārthaṃ sabhāyām ||
children.translated_text: <s>Somadeva</s> composed this necklace from them with great effort; let the foremost physician wear it in the assembly as an ornament.
When this chapter has been read repeatedly by practitioners of mercury doctrine,

children.text: rasakarmāṇi kurvāṇo na sa muhyati kutracit ||
children.translated_text: a person performing mercury operations is never confused anywhere.
Now all the apparatuses of the mercury system will be described
at present by <s>Somadeva</s>, after consideration, in concise form.
Because mercury is controlled with effort by the best authorities
in order to carry out operations beginning with steaming, therefore it is remembered as a <s>yantra</s> (apparatus).
After a vessel has been half-filled with a liquid substance or with water,
one should carefully make two openings on both sides of its mouth.
Into those one should insert a rod; in the middle of it one should tie a pouch of mercury,
and then steam it. This is remembered as the <s>dolāyantra</s> (swing apparatus).
One should place the material to be cooked on cloth tied over the mouth of a water-filled dish;
where it is cooked covered over, that is called the <s>svedanīyantra</s> (steaming apparatus).
With a circumference of eight <s>aṅgulas</s> and a height of ten <s>aṅgulas</s>...
The water-reservoir should rise four aṅgulas below the neck.
The mouth of that upper vessel should be inserted into the lower vessel,
into the opening of the top that is sixteen aṅgulas wide.
On the two sides, with buffalo milk, powder, iron-rust, and molasses,
one should smear and dry the joint, and put water into the water-reservoir.
One should set this on the stove; it is called the <s>pātana-yantra</s> (distillation apparatus).
Then, when the upper vessel has been smeared and set in water, the wise man,
with blazing cow-dung cakes, should carefully make the downward distillation.
Having placed a very broad potsherd in the middle of a vessel filled with water,

children.text: tadupari viḍamadhyagataḥ sthāpyaḥ sūtaḥ kṛtaḥ koṣṭhyām ||
children.translated_text: mercury, prepared in the furnace and placed amid <s>viḍa</s> (alkaline salt), should be set upon it.
It is covered with a small iron bowl whose joint has been coated with six layers of clay,
inside the aforesaid potsherd, with coals made from khadira and kola wood.
Through steaming and rubbing, <s>rasa</s> (mercury) placed in the <s>kacchapa-yantra</s> (tortoise apparatus) becomes digested.
Then, by the very force of the fire, all the metallic essences melt in the womb.
When mercury, placed in a lamp standing on an earthen seat inside the <s>kacchapa-yantra</s>, falls into it,
that is called the <s>dīpikā-yantra</s> (lamp apparatus).
Below the neck of the vessel, in a hole, one should insert a bamboo tube.
Having made two bronze vessels into a closed capsule filled with water,

children.text: nalikāsyaṃ tatra yojyaṃ dṛḍhaṃ taccāpi kārayet
children.translated_text: the mouth of the tube should be joined there, and that too should be made firm.
Mercury, first placed in that pot together with the appropriate substances,
when heated by fire, falls downward from the tube into that water.

children.text: yāvaduṣṇaṃ bhavet sarvaṃ bhājanaṃ tāvadeva hi
children.translated_text: For just as long as the whole vessel becomes hot,
the conjunction of mercury is produced; this is called the <s>ḍekī-yantra</s>.
Having made two iron crucibles, each measuring twelve aṅgulas,
one of them with a slight hole and joined with sulfur,
one should insert that one into the other crucible, which contains mercury.
Water should be below the mercury, and the kindling of fire above and below.
O good lady, garlic juice, carefully filtered through cloth,
should be poured in abundantly and carefully, so as to flood the mercury and sulfur.
Having covered it above with a pan, make another pan firm over it.
One should carefully smear the joint with clay and also with cloth.
In another pan one should apply the <s>puṭa</s> called kapota, always with a karṣa-fire.
Below the apparatus one should apply cow-dung fire, or else a very intense fire.

children.text: evaṃ tu tridinaṃ kuryāttato yantraṃ vimocayet
children.translated_text: Thus one should do it for three days; then one should open the apparatus.
With hot water and a hot stove one should not perform a cold operation.

children.text: na tatra kṣīyate sūto na ca gacchati kutracit
children.translated_text: There the mercury is not diminished, nor does it go anywhere.
By precisely this procedure one should carry out the digestion of sulfur.
The <s>vidyādhara-yantra</s> should be known as an enclosure made from two pans.
Having made a stove with four openings, one should place the vessel of the apparatus in it.
Having put the medicine there, one should close the mouth of the vessel.
The apparatus called <s>vidyādhara</s> is so proclaimed by those who know the tantras.
Fire is above, water below, and in the middle there is the collection of mercury.
This is called <s>somānala</s>; it digests mica and the like.
I shall explain the <s>garbha-yantra</s>, which makes ash from <s>piṣṭikā</s>.
It should be four aṅgulas long and three aṅgulas in breadth.
One should make a strong earthen crucible, with its mouth circular.
There should be twenty parts of salt and one part of guggulu.

children.text: suślakṣṇaṃ peṣayitvā tu vāraṃ vāraṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Having ground them very finely, again and again, repeatedly,
one should make a firm coating for the crucible with salt, half as much clay, and water.
The one who knows the measure should heat it gently in the ground with husk-fire.

children.text: ahorātraṃ trirātraṃ vā rasendro bhasmatāṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: In one day and night, or in three nights, lord mercury becomes ash.
Having filled a potsherd with sand, one should set it on top of that.

children.text: aparaṃ kharparaṃ tatra śanair mṛdvagninā pacet ||
children.translated_text: There one should place another potsherd and cook it slowly with gentle fire.

children.text: pañcakṣāraistathā mūtrair lavaṇaṃ ca viḍaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: With the five alkalis, and with urines, then salt and <s>viḍa</s>,
that apparatus is called <s>haṃsapāka</s> by the best of practitioners.
A glass bottle with its mouth hidden, covered to a finger's thickness with clay and cloth,
and dried, should be filled in three parts.
It should be well set in sand in a vessel a span deep.
That vessel should be filled with three parts and covered with other vessels.

children.text: bhāṇḍavaktraṃ maṇikayā saṃdhiṃ limpen mṛdā pacet
children.translated_text: One should cover the vessel's mouth with a lid, smear the joint with clay, and cook it.
In the stove, from the burning of grass lying on the back of the lid,
this is indeed the <s>vālukā-yantra</s> (sand apparatus), and that apparatus is based on salt.
Having carefully placed it in a vessel filled with five āḍhakas of sand,
a mercury ball and the like is cooked; this is called the <s>vālukā-yantra</s>.
Likewise, from the placing of salt, it is called the <s>lavaṇa-yantraka</s> (salt apparatus).
For the mouth of a copper vessel whose inside has been smeared with mercury paste,
one should smear the joint at the bottom of the vessel with clay and salt.
One should fill that vessel with salt, or with alkalis, and cook it as before.
Thus there is the <s>lavaṇa-yantra</s>, which is praised in operations with mercury.
Mercury placed in an iron tube, in a vessel filled with salt,
should be sealed and cooked as before; this is called the <s>nālikā-yantra</s> (tube apparatus).
A crucible containing mercury, its whole body hidden by sand, in a pit,
should be covered with blazing cow-dung cakes; that apparatus is called <s>bhūdhara</s>.
Placed inside a pair of saucers among cow-dung cakes, the one who knows the measure of fire...

children.text: paceccullyāṃ dviyāmaṃ vā rasaṃ tat puṭayantrakam ||
children.translated_text: One should cook the mercury in a stove for two yāmas; that is the <s>puṭayantra</s> apparatus.
Sixteen aṅgulas wide, one hasta in length, and level in form,
for the purpose of causing the metallic essence to fall, it is remembered as the <s>koṣṭhīyantra</s> apparatus.
Where, in an iron vessel, there are two rings on the two sides,
and a smaller vessel of that same kind is fitted through the rings, that is the chamber with inserted rings.
Having placed it above the former vessel, one should cast into the smaller vessel
the prepared mercury, while filling the large vessel with sour gruel.
One should steam it for two yāmas, for the sake of raising up the mercury.
This is the <s>valabhīyantra</s>, which brings about sixfold efficacy in mercury.
In a vessel made of fine <s>kānta</s> iron, the mercury becomes still more excellent in quality.
One should put mercury into a jar furnished with a long, bent, downward-facing tube.
That tube should indeed be inserted into the belly of another jar.
Then, after properly sealing the mouths of the two jars with clay,
one should kindle a fierce fire beneath the mercury jar.
Into the other jar one should pour sweet, cold water.
This is called <s>tiryakpātana</s>, horizontal distillation, by the technical authorities.
A round iron cup, with an upward rod whose tip is bent,
is the <s>pālikāyantra</s> apparatus, for the digestion of <s>bali</s>.
Holding four prasthas of water and having a mouth four aṅgulas wide,
this is called the <s>ghaṭayantra</s>; it is remembered as an apparatus for replenishment.

children.text: vidhāya vartulaṃ gartaṃ mallamatra nidhāya ca
children.translated_text: Having made a round pit and placed a shallow earthen bowl there,
one should set there a good brick that has a hollow in its middle.
Around the pit one should make a rim one aṅgula high.

children.text: garte sūtaṃ vinikṣipya gartāsye vasanaṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: After placing mercury in the pit, one should put cloth over the mouth of the pit.
One should put sulfur there, close the mouth with the earthen bowl,
and properly seal the space between the bowl and the rim with clay.

children.text: vanopalaiḥ puṭaṃ deyaṃ kapotākhyaṃ na cādhikam
children.translated_text: A <s>puṭa</s> with forest fuel-cakes, called <s>kapota</s>, should be given, and no more than that.

children.text: iṣṭikāyantram etat syād gandhakaṃ tena jārayet ||
children.translated_text: This is the <s>iṣṭikāyantra</s> apparatus; by means of it one should digest sulfur.

children.text: sthālikopari vinyasya sthālīṃ samyaṅ nirudhya ca
children.translated_text: Having placed one dish upon another and properly sealed it,

children.text: ūrdhvasthālyāṃ jalaṃ kṣiptvā vahniṃ prajvālayed adhaḥ
children.translated_text: one should put water into the upper dish and kindle fire below.
This is the <s>vidyādhara</s> apparatus, for extracting <s>hiṅgula</s>.
After setting an inverted dish above the apparatus-dish, one should seal it.
That apparatus is called <s>ḍamaruka</s> and is useful for making mercury ash.
In the middle of a shallow bowl one should make a pit; in it there should be mercury together with sulfur.
Around the pit one should construct a wall raised one aṅgula high.
Then one should cover it properly with a crucible shaped like a cow's udder,
and seal it well with water-clay, according to the formulation now being stated.
Fine powder of old slag, rubbed with a decoction of <s>babbūla</s> until it has the consistency of paste,
and combined with powdered jaggery,

children.text: iyaṃ hi jalamṛt proktā durbhedyā salilaiḥ khalu ||
children.translated_text: is called <s>jalamṛt</s>; it is indeed difficult for waters to pierce.
Chalk, salt, and slag, rubbed with buffalo milk,
become fire-clay, able to withstand the heat of a terrible fire.

children.text: etayā mṛtsnayā ruddho na gantuṃ kṣamate rasaḥ
children.translated_text: When sealed with this clay, mercury cannot go out,
like a man restrained by the mature love of a skilled woman.
<s>Nandī</s>, <s>Nāgārjuna</s>, <s>Brahmajyotis</s> the lord among sages,
and venerable <s>Somadeva</s> know this; no one else on earth does.
Then, after pouring in water, one should kindle fire below.
This is called the <s>nābhiyantra</s>, as taught by all-knowing <s>Nandī</s>.
By means of it mercury is digested by smokeless, purified sulfur.
A crucible inserted into the belly of another crucible, evenly round from beginning to end,

children.text: cipiṭāṃ ca tale proktaṃ grastayantraṃ manīṣibhiḥ
children.translated_text: and said to be flattened at the bottom, is called the <s>grastayantra</s> by the wise.
It has been taught by the knowers of mercury for cooking lord mercury.

children.text: sthālyāṃ tāmrādi nikṣipya mallenāsyaṃ nirudhya ca
children.translated_text: Having put copper and the like into a dish and closed the mouth with a shallow bowl,
it is cooked from beneath the dish; this is remembered as the <s>sthālīyantra</s>.
Having made an iron vessel eight aṅgulas wide and eight aṅgulas high,

children.text: kaṇṭhādho hy aṅgule deśe galādhāre hi tatra ca ||
children.translated_text: one should, at the neck-support there, in a place one aṅgula below the neck,
insert thin iron rods crosswise, laid across transversely.
Upon them one should place thin gold leaves.

children.text: pattrādho nikṣiped dhūmaṃ vakṣyamāṇam ihaiva hi
children.translated_text: Below the leaves one should place the fumigating substance that is to be described here itself.
That vessel should then be covered with another vessel placed upside down.

children.text: mṛdā vilipya saṃdhiṃ ca vahniṃ prajvālayed adhaḥ
children.translated_text: Having smeared the joint with clay, one should kindle fire below.
By that, all the leaves are killed according to the prescribed method.

children.text: rasaścarati vegena drutaṃ garbhe dravanti ca
children.translated_text: The mercury moves swiftly and they melt quickly in the womb of the apparatus.
The fumigation is with <s>kajjālī</s> made from sulfur, <s>ālaka</s>, and <s>śilā</s>, or with calcined <s>ahi</s>.
The fumigation of gold leaves has first been explained.
For silver, one should fumigate silver leaves with calcined tin.
And one should fumigate with other subsidiary minerals as is appropriate.
This is called the <s>dhūpayantra</s>, for preparing substances used in digestion.

children.text: sthūlasthālyāṃ jalaṃ kṣiptvā vāso baddhvā mukhe dṛḍham
children.translated_text: Having poured water into a large dish and tied cloth firmly over its mouth,

children.text: tatra svedyaṃ vinikṣipya tanmukhaṃ prapidhāya ca ||
children.translated_text: one should place on it the substance to be steamed and then cover its mouth.
One should kindle fire below; that apparatus is called <s>kanduka</s>.
Other wise men call this the steaming apparatus.

children.text: yadvā sthālyāṃ jalaṃ kṣiptvā tṛṇaṃ kṣiptvā mukhopari
children.translated_text: Or else, having poured water into a dish and placed grass over its mouth,
one should put the substance to be steamed on it and set on a lid,
then kindle fire below; that apparatus is remembered as <s>kanduka</s>.

children.text: khallayogyā śilā nīlā śyāmā snigdhā dṛḍhā guruḥ
children.translated_text: A stone suitable for a <s>khalla</s> (mortar) is blue-black, dark, smooth, firm, and heavy.
It is sixteen <s>aṅgulas</s> high and nine <s>aṅgulas</s> wide.
The grinding slab is twenty-four <s>aṅgulas</s> long and twelve <s>aṅgulas</s> wide.
Or it may be twenty <s>aṅgulas</s> long and ten <s>aṅgulas</s> high.
This should be understood as the measure of a <s>khalla</s>; it is best for operations with <s>rasa</s> (mercury).
The <s>khallayantra</s> (mortar apparatus) is said to be of three kinds for easy grinding of mercury and related substances.
They should be without projections, very smooth, and furnished with a pestle.

children.text: utsedhe sa daśāṅgulaḥ khalu kalātulyāṅgulāyāmavān vistāreṇa daśāṅgulo munimitairnimnas tayaivāṅgulaiḥ
children.translated_text: In height it is ten <s>aṅgulas</s>; in length it has an <s>aṅgula</s>-measure equal to the kalā; in breadth it is ten <s>aṅgulas</s>, and in depth measured by that same unit.

children.text: pālyāṃ dvyaṅgulivistaraśca masṛṇo 'tīvārdhacandropamo gharṣo dvādaśakāṅgulaśca tadayaṃ khallo mataḥ siddhaye ||
children.translated_text: At the rim it is two fingers wide, very smooth, shaped like a half-moon, and the grinder is twelve <s>aṅgulas</s> long; this <s>khalla</s> is approved for success.
In this, five <s>palas</s> of <s>sūta</s> (mercury) should be ground for purification.
According to the suitability of each case, one should apply it in other mortars as well.
A <s>khalla</s> twelve <s>aṅgulas</s> broad is made of very smooth stone.
It is four <s>aṅgulas</s> deep and made very smooth in the middle.
The pestle is flattened underneath and easy to grasp at the knob above.
This round <s>khalla</s> gives great ease in grinding.

children.text: lauho navāṅgulaḥ khallo nimnatve ca ṣaḍaṅgulaḥ
children.translated_text: An iron <s>khalla</s> is nine <s>aṅgulas</s> across and six <s>aṅgulas</s> in depth.
Its pestle is eight <s>aṅgulas</s> long; this too is called the heated <s>khalla</s>.
Having made a stove in the shape of a <s>khalla</s> and filled it with coals,

children.text: tasyāṃ niveśya taṃ khallaṃ pārśve bhastrikayā dhamet ||
children.translated_text: one should place that <s>khalla</s> in it and blow from the side with a bellows.
The paste ground inside it, combined with alkalis and acids,
flows very rapidly when heated; of this there is no doubt.

children.text: kṛtaḥ kāntāyasā so 'yaṃ bhavet koṭiguṇo rasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When made of magnetic iron, this <s>rasa</s> becomes endowed with ten millionfold efficacy.

children.text: mūṣā hi krauñcikā proktā kumudī karahāṭikā
children.translated_text: A crucible is called <s>krauñcikā</s>, <s>kumudī</s>, and <s>karahāṭikā</s>;
it is also termed <s>pācanī</s> and <s>vahnimitrā</s> by practitioners of <s>rasavāda</s> (alchemy).

children.text: muṣṇāti doṣān mūṣā yā sā mūṣeti nigadyate ||
children.translated_text: Because the crucible removes faults, it is called <s>mūṣā</s>.
Its material should be clay, and also iron.
Even a single <s>kākiṇī</s> coin that has come out of the mouth of a crucible is preferable;
fie on even a hundred thousand gained by honorable men through bowing down to a bad man.
In fastening the crucible and its lid, the fastening is the smearing of the joint.
Closing the opening and making an opening too are the joined sealing of the joint.
Clay that is pale, coarse, gravelly, and reddish-pale,
and that can endure long blowing, is especially praised for crucible work.

children.text: tadabhāve ca vālmīkī kaulālī vā samīryate ||
children.translated_text: In its absence, anthill clay or potter's clay is prescribed.

children.text: yā mṛttikā dugdhatuṣaiḥ śaṇena śikhitrakair vā hayaladdinā ca
children.translated_text: Clay that has been pounded with milk, husks, hemp, peacock-feather material, horse dung,

children.text: lauhena daṇḍena ca kuṭṭitā sā sādhāraṇā syāt khalu mūṣikārthe ||
children.translated_text: and an iron rod is indeed ordinary material for a small crucible.
White stones, husks, burnt peacock-feather material, hemp, potsherds,
dung, slag, and black clay should be combined in crucible clay.
For a <s>vajramūṣā</s> (diamond crucible), in the extraction of essence, one should use three parts clay, parts of hemp and dung,
one part of burnt husk, stone, and the like, and half a part of slag, after breaking them up.
Clay joined with burnt charcoal and husk, and anthill clay,
combined with the appropriate <s>viḍa</s> and smeared with that same <s>viḍa</s>,

children.text: tayā yā vihitā mūṣā yogamūṣeti kathyate
children.translated_text: forms a crucible made with that mixture, called a <s>yogamūṣā</s>.
Mercury prepared in this becomes richer in qualities.
With <s>gāra</s>, washed <s>bhūnāga</s>, hemp, and burnt husks,
the crucible clay, equal in amount to equal parts of those, is kneaded with buffalo's milk.
The <s>krauñcikā</s> has been described in many ways according to the particular apparatus.
A crucible fashioned with it is suitable for melting diamond.
A crucible furnished with six parts milk, eight parts <s>gāra</s>, slag, charcoal, and hemp,
and made with black clay is called a <s>gāramūṣā</s>.
It does not melt in the fire after blowing for a pair of <s>yāmas</s>.
Diamond, charcoal, and husks are equal; clay is four times that.

children.text: gārā ca mṛttikātulyā sarvair etair vinirmitā
children.translated_text: <s>Gāra</s> is equal to the clay; made from all these,
it is designated the excellent crucible, and it withstands fire for one <s>yāma</s>.
A red clay free from stones and processed with the red group,
made into a crucible from that clay and smeared with <s>kṣitikhecara</s>,
is called the color crucible and is employed for improving color.
A white clay free from stones and processed with the white group,
made into a crucible from that clay and smeared with <s>kṣitikhecara</s>,
is called the silver crucible and is employed for improving color.
Produced from the clay of each particular kind and smeared with the corresponding <s>viḍa</s>,
it is called the <s>viḍamūṣā</s>, for the purpose of operations on body and metal.
With <s>gāra</s>, washed <s>bhūnāga</s>, husk-cleansed hemp,
and crucible clay equal to equal parts of those, kneaded with buffalo's milk,
the <s>krauñcikā</s> has been described in many ways according to the apparatus.
A crucible fashioned with it is smeared with bedbug blood,
and with the roots of <s>bālā</s>, <s>abda</s>, and <s>dhvani</s>; this is the diamond-melting <s>krauñcikā</s>.
When perforated with liquid, it withstands fire for four <s>yāmas</s>.
At the time when melting begins in the molten material, through the application of blowing to the crucible,
the lifting of it for a moment is called <s>mūṣāpyāyana</s> (refreshing the crucible).
In an eggplant-shaped crucible, the tube is twelve <s>aṅgulas</s> long,
rising upward like a <s>dhattūra</s> flower, very firm, and like a closed blossom.

children.text: aṣṭāṅgulaṃ ca sacchidraṃ sā syād vṛntākamūṣikā
children.translated_text: It is eight <s>aṅgulas</s> long and has holes; that is the small eggplant crucible.
With this one should extract the essence of soft substances such as <s>kharpara</s>.
A crucible shaped like a cow's udder and having a peaked lid...

children.text: sattvānāṃ drāvaṇe śuddhau mūṣā sā gostanī bhavet ||
children.translated_text: For melting and purifying metallic essences, that <s>mūṣā</s> (crucible) is to be cow-udder-shaped, the <s>gostanī</s>.
The one prescribed as the <s>mallamūṣā</s>, made by closing together a pair of <s>malla</s> vessels,
is declared suitable for steaming <s>parpaṭī</s> and other mercurial preparations.
The crucible that has the form of a potter's vessel, is firm, and is fully fired,
is called the baked crucible, for cooking <s>poṭṭalī</s> and the like.
The mouthless, globular crucible, containing within it substances to be treated by <s>puṭa</s> heating,
is called the round crucible; it restrains the fluid of quick-yielding essences.
The one that is shaped like an elbow at the bottom and gradually widens above,
large like a stout eggplant with its stalk, is remembered as the great crucible.
It is used both for <s>puṭa</s> heating and for melting the essences of iron, mica, and the like.
The crucible that is frog-shaped, low in depth and not broad,
measuring six <s>aṅgulas</s>, is known as the frog crucible.
Having buried that crucible in the ground, one should then apply the <s>puṭa</s> heat above it.
The crucible that is flattened at the base, round, and eight <s>aṅgulas</s> high
is the crucible called <s>mūsala</s>; it is useful for mercury bound into a wheel.
For extracting essences and for purifying them once extracted,
there are furnaces of various forms; their characteristics are now stated.
It should be as high as a royal cubit, and half of that in length and breadth,

children.text: caturasrā ca kuḍyena veṣṭitā mṛnmayena ca ||
children.translated_text: square, and surrounded by a wall made of clay.
In one wall there should be a door furnished with an opening of a span,

children.text: dvāraṃ sārdhavitastyā ca saṃmitaṃ sudṛḍhaṃ śubham ||
children.translated_text: and the door, well made and firm, should measure one and a half spans.
Below the threshold an opening should be made for blowing, as appropriate.
Above it, the wall of the upper section should measure a <s>prādeśa</s>.
And above, another door should be made, indeed measuring a <s>prādeśa</s>.
Then, after closing it with bricks and plastering the joint of the door,
one should fill it with coals and blow it with two bellows.
The coals and the blowing material should be inserted through the upper door.
And balls for extracting essence should be added five at a time, again and again.
This is the charcoal furnace; it extracts the essences of hard substances.
On firm ground one should make a pit, well formed and measuring a span,
round; and then in its middle one should construct another pit,
endowed with a breadth and depth of four <s>aṅgulas</s>.
From the pit to the surface of the ground it should have a transverse channel,
slightly raised and sloping downward toward the outer pit.
One should place in the cavity of the inner pit a clay disk furnished with five holes.
After filling the furnace with coke, one should blow it with a single bellows.
This is the subterranean furnace; it extracts the essences of soft substances.
It was taught by <s>Nandin</s> for substances whose treatment is accomplished by blowing.
The one that is twelve <s>aṅgulas</s> deep and likewise measures a <s>prādeśa</s>,
and is furnished above, at four <s>aṅgulas</s>, with a rim,
one should place a disk with many holes upon the rim.
Putting coals there, one should blow it through a bent tube.
This is called the <s>gārakoṣṭhī</s>; it destroys refined metals.
A firm tube, measuring an <s>aratni</s>, should be made from crucible-clay.

children.text: adhomukhaṃ ca tadvaktre nālaṃ pañcāṅgulaṃ khalu
children.translated_text: It is turned downward, and at its mouth there is a tube of five <s>aṅgulas</s>.
This is called the bent tube, and is said to be for strong blowing.
A furnace is prescribed for preparing perfected mercury and the like.
It is twelve <s>aṅgulas</s> high and four <s>aṅgulas</s> at the base,
with its blowing-mouth set sideways; it purifies soft substances.
A <s>puṭa</s> is the means for knowing the proper measure of cooking for mercury and related substances.

children.text: neṣṭo nyūnādhikaḥ pākaḥ supākaṃ hitam auṣadham ||
children.translated_text: Cooking that is deficient or excessive is not desired; a well-cooked medicine is beneficial.
From the <s>puṭa</s> treatment come non-reversion of iron and the like, increase of qualities, and then superiority,
not sinking in water, and the ability to fill the lines.

children.text: puṭād grāvṇo laghutvaṃ ca śīghravyāptiśca dīpanam
children.translated_text: From <s>puṭa</s> there also come lightness of stone-like material, rapid pervasion, and stimulation of digestion.
The quality of metals is greater even than that produced from digested <s>sūtendra</s> (mercury).
Just as fire enters a stone through the use of external <s>puṭa</s> heating,
so, because of pulverization, the acquisition of qualities in metals is certain.
In a pit two cubits deep and broad, and square in shape,
filled with a thousand forest cow-dung cakes, the medicine to be heated by <s>puṭa</s>
should be carefully sealed in a <s>krauñcī</s> vessel and placed upon the prepared paste.
Half a thousand forest cow-dung cakes should be placed over the <s>krauñcikā</s> vessel.
One should kindle the fire there; this is remembered as the great <s>puṭa</s>.
A square pit of the measure of a royal cubit, and shallow,
should be filled up to the neck with pieces of cow-dung fuel and then arranged.
One should place there a <s>kumudī</s> vessel filled with the substance to be heated by <s>puṭa</s>.
One should put in half-filled round cakes made from complete cow-dung.
This is called the elephant <s>puṭa</s>, producing great efficacy.
In this way, when the pit measures an <s>aratni</s>, the <s>puṭa</s> is called the boar <s>puṭa</s>.
A <s>puṭa</s> on the surface of the ground, whose height is two spans in each case,
and whose breadth at the bottom is the same, is the chicken <s>puṭa</s>.
The <s>puṭa</s> that is applied on the ground with eight forest cow-dung cakes,
after sealing mercury or the ash of <s>arka</s>, is called the pigeon <s>puṭa</s>.
Cow-dung inside a cattle shed, crushed by cows' hooves, dried, and powdered,
is taught as <s>govara</s>; it is best in the preparation of mercury.
Wherever a <s>puṭa</s> is applied with <s>govara</s> or else with husks,
that is called the <s>govara-puṭa</s>, for accomplishing mercurial ash.
When cooking is performed by fire in a large vessel filled with husks,
with a crucible placed in the middle, that is called the vessel <s>puṭa</s>.
Below and above it is indeed covered with a <s>krauñcikā</s> vessel;
where this is done with heated sand, that is the <s>vālukāpuṭa</s> (sand heating).
One should properly bury the fire-friendly materials in the ground two fingers below;
where the heating is above, that heating is called <s>bhūdhara</s>.
Where heating is done above with sixteen measures of husks or with cow-dung cakes,
that is called <s>lāvaka</s>, for processing very soft substances.
When the measure of heating has not been stated, then according to the strength or weakness of the substance to be treated,
the heating should be determined and given by those skilled in inference and exclusion.

children.text: piṣṭakaṃ chagaṇaṃ chāṇam utpalaṃ copalaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Piṣṭaka</s>, <s>chagaṇa</s>, <s>chāṇa</s>, <s>utpala</s>, and likewise <s>upala</s>,
<s>giriṇḍa</s>, <s>upala-sāṭhī</s>, and <s>varāṭī</s> are names for <s>chagaṇa</s>.

children.text: suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ tāmraṃ trapu sīsakam āyasam
children.translated_text: Gold, silver, copper, tin, lead, and iron:
these six are the metals; bronze and brass are artificial.

children.text: lavaṇāni ṣaḍ ucyante sāmudraṃ saindhavaṃ viḍam
children.translated_text: Six salts are named: sea salt, rock salt, <s>viḍa</s> salt,
<s>sauvarcala</s>, <s>romaka</s>, and likewise <s>cūlikā</s> salt.
The triad of alkalis is declared to be <s>yava</s>, <s>sarjikā</s>, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>.
The alkalis of <s>palāśa</s> and <s>muṣkaka</s>, barley-alkali, and <s>suvarcikā</s>,
together with alkali produced from sesame stalks, form the set of five alkalis.

children.text: ghṛtaṃ guḍo mākṣikaṃ ca vijñeyaṃ madhuratrayam ||
children.translated_text: Ghee, jaggery, and honey should be known as the sweet triad.
From <s>kaṅguṇī</s>, <s>tumbinī</s>, <s>ghoṣā</s>, <s>karīra</s>, and <s>śrīphala</s>,
from bitter eggplant, mustard, <s>somarājī</s>, and <s>vibhītaka</s>,
from flax, <s>mahākālī</s>, neem, and sesame too,
from <s>apāmārga</s>, <s>devadālī</s>, <s>dantī</s>, and <s>tumburu</s>,
and likewise from <s>aṅkola</s>, thorn-apple, <s>bhallātaka</s>, and <s>palāśa</s>:
taking oil from these, one should apply it in mercury operations.
The fat of the jackal and frog, fat produced from the tortoise,
that of the crab, porpoise, cow, pig, and human being,
and the fat of goat, camel, donkey, sheep, and buffalo too are to be used.
The urines of elephant, camel, buffalo cow, donkey, and horse,

children.text: go'jāvīnāṃ striyaḥ puṃsāṃ puṣpaṃ bījaṃ tu yojayet ||
children.translated_text: of cow, goat, and sheep, female and male, as well as menstrual fluid and semen, should be applied.
Buffalo water, curd, milk, ghee, and dung-juice:
that should be known as the five buffalo products; the five goat products are similar.
<s>Amlavetasa</s>, citron, lime, and pomegranate,
<s>cāṅgerī</s>, sour chickpea preparation, tamarind, jujube, and pomegranate,
<s>ambaṣṭhā</s>, <s>tintiḍīka</s>, ginger, <s>rasapattrikā</s>,
<s>karavanda</s>, and other such things are proclaimed as the sour group.
Of all these, the sour chickpea preparation alone is praised,
or <s>amlavetasa</s> alone is the very best of all;
it is beneficial for the purification, liquefaction, and digestion of mercury and related substances.
The juices of jujube, pomegranate, tree-sour fruit, <s>cullikā</s>, and <s>cukrikā</s>
are called the five sours; that too is stated as the sour pentad.
Brick, red ochre, salt, ash, and ant-hill earth
are called the five earths by those skilled in mercury applications.
<s>Śṛṅgīka</s>, <s>kālakūṭa</s>, <s>vatsanābha</s>, artificial poison,

children.text: pittaṃ ca viṣavargo 'yaṃ sa varaḥ parikīrtitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and bile: this is the poison group, and it is proclaimed excellent.
This is recommended in mercury operations and also in the procedure for splitting it;
but if taken improperly, it certainly kills.
<s>Lāṅgalī</s>, poison-nut, oleander, <s>jayā</s>,
<s>nīlaka</s>, <s>kanaka</s>, and <s>arka</s>: this is the class consisting of lesser poisons.
Elephant cow, mare, woman, cow, female donkey, she-goat, ewe,
she-camel, fig tree, holy fig, <s>bhānu</s>, banyan, and <s>tilvaka</s>,
<s>dugdhikā</s>, <s>snuhī</s>, and likewise <s>uttamakaṇṭikā</s>:
their milks are specified as the milk group for mercury and related substances.
Of the pigeon, the blue jay, the dove, the peacock,
the vulture, and also the cock, the group of excrements is specified;
it is for purifying all metals, through heating and coating.
Safflower, catechu, lac, madder, red sandalwood,
<s>akṣī</s>, <s>bandhujīva</s>, and likewise the camphor-scented plant,
and <s>mākṣika</s>: this should be known as the red group, an excellent colorant.
<s>Kiṃśuka</s>, <s>karṇikāra</s>, and the two kinds of turmeric
are designated as the yellow group in the operations of <s>rasarāja</s> (king mercury).

children.text: tagaraḥ kuṭajaḥ kundo guñjā jīvantikā tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Tagara</s>, <s>kuṭaja</s>, jasmine, <s>guñjā</s>, and <s>jīvantikā</s>,
and the root of the white lotus are stated to be the white group.

children.text: kadalī kāravellī ca triphalā nīlikā nalaḥ
children.translated_text: Plantain, bitter gourd, <s>triphala</s>, indigo, reed,
mud, green vitriol, and unripe mango are stated to be the black group.
Whatever substance has the nature of digestion by means of the red group and the other groups
should be carefully impregnated with them in order to obtain the corresponding color.
The group is considered purifiable by glass, borax, and <s>śiprā</s>.
It destroys the impurities of essences, bound mercury, and metals;
the <s>kāpālī-kaṅguṇī-dhvaṃsī</s> group is so called by mercury experts.
Buffalo cow, sheep-horn, <s>kaliṅga</s>, and <s>dhava</s> seed,
together with hare bones: this compound destroys the hardness of iron.
With jaggery, guggul, <s>guñjā</s>, ghee, resins, and borax,
the group is considered useful for melting all metals and other substances that are hard to melt.

children.text: kṣārāḥ sarve malaṃ hanyur amlaṃ śodhanajāraṇam
children.translated_text: All alkalis destroy impurity; acid serves for purification and digestion.

children.text: māndyaṃ viṣāṇi nighnanti snaigdhyaṃ snehāḥ prakurvate ||
children.translated_text: Poisons remove sluggishness; oils produce unctuousness.

children.text: ṣaṭ truṭyaś caikalikṣā syāt ṣaḍ likṣā yūkam ucyate
children.translated_text: Six <s>truṭis</s> make one <s>likṣā</s>; six <s>likṣās</s> are called one <s>yūka</s>.
Six <s>yūkas</s> are said to be what is called a speck of dust, O fair-vowed one.

children.text: ṣaḍrajaḥ sarṣapaḥ sākṣātsiddhārthaḥ sa ca kīrtitaḥ
children.translated_text: Six specks of dust are directly a mustard seed; that is called <s>siddhārtha</s>.
O goddess, one <s>yava</s> is said to consist of six <s>siddhārthas</s>.
From six <s>yavas</s> there is one <s>guñjā</s>; three <s>guñjās</s> are called a <s>valla</s>.
And from six <s>guñjās</s> one <s>māṣa</s> is declared.

children.text: māṣā dvādaśa tolaḥ syādaṣṭau tolāḥ palaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Twelve <s>māṣas</s> make a <s>tola</s>, and eight <s>tolas</s> make a <s>pala</s>.
A <s>truṭi</s> is made of six atoms; from six of those a <s>likṣā</s> is taught.

children.text: tābhiḥ ṣaḍbhirbhaved yūkā ṣaḍyūkās tad rajaḥ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: From six of those there is a <s>yūkā</s>; six <s>yūkās</s> are remembered as a speck of dust.
Six specks of dust are said to be a mustard seed, and from six of those a <s>yava</s> is taught.
One <s>guñjā</s> is made from six <s>yavas</s>; a <s>niṣpāva</s> is two <s>guñjās</s>.

children.text: syādguñjātritayaṃ vallo dvau vallau māṣa ucyate
children.translated_text: A set of three <s>guñjās</s> is a <s>valla</s>; two <s>vallas</s> are called a <s>māṣa</s>.

children.text: dvau māṣau dharaṇaṃ te dve śāṇaniṣkakalāḥ smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Two <s>māṣas</s> are a <s>dharaṇa</s>; two of these are remembered as a <s>śāṇa</s>, <s>niṣka</s>, or <s>kalā</s>.

children.text: niṣkadvayaṃ tu vaṭakaḥ sa ca kola itīritaḥ
children.translated_text: Two <s>niṣkas</s> are a <s>vaṭaka</s>, and that is also called a <s>kola</s>.
Three <s>kolas</s> make a <s>tola</s>; a <s>karṣa</s> is four <s>niṣkas</s>.
<s>Udumbara</s>, <s>pāṇitala</s>, <s>suvarṇa</s>, and <s>kavalagraha</s> are terms for it.
So too are <s>akṣa</s>, <s>biḍālapadaka</s>, <s>śukti</s>, and a measure of two palms.
Some say that two <s>śuktis</s> make a <s>pala</s>; others know it as three <s>śuktis</s>.
The same is also called <s>muṣṭi</s>, <s>prakuñca</s>, and <s>bilva</s>.
Two <s>palas</s> are a <s>prasṛta</s>; twice that is a <s>kuḍava</s> or <s>añjali</s>.

children.text: kuḍavau mānikā tau syātprastho dve mānike smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Two <s>kuḍavas</s> are a <s>mānikā</s>; two <s>mānikās</s> are remembered as a <s>prastha</s>.

children.text: prasthadvayaṃ śubhaṃ tau dvau pātrakaṃ dvayamāḍhakam
children.translated_text: Two <s>prasthas</s> are a <s>śubha</s>; two of those are a <s>pātraka</s>, and two <s>pātrakas</s> are an <s>āḍhaka</s>.
With four of these, <s>ghaṭa</s>, <s>unmāna</s>, <s>nalvana</s>, <s>ārmaṇa</s>, and <s>śūrpaka</s>

children.text: droṇasya śabdāḥ paryāyāḥ palānāṃ śatakaṃ tulā
children.translated_text: are equivalent names for a <s>droṇa</s>; one hundred <s>palas</s> make a <s>tulā</s>.
A <s>bhāra</s> is declared to be forty <s>tulās</s>, each of one hundred <s>palas</s>.
Having examined treatises such as the <s>Rasārṇava</s>, I have stated this.
Whatever is useful for <s>rasa</s> has been shown merely in outline.
Now we shall explain the processes for the king of <s>rasa</s>, mercury.

children.text: syātsvedanaṃ tadanu mardanamūrchane ca utthāpanaṃ patanarodhaniyāmanāni
children.translated_text: There is steaming, then rubbing, mūrchana, raising, distillation, restraining, and regulating,

children.text: saṃdīpanaṃ gaganabhakṣaṇamānamatra saṃcāraṇā tadanu garbhagatā drutiśca ||
children.translated_text: kindling, feeding on mica, measuring, moving, and then internal liquefaction.

children.text: bāhyā drutiḥ sūtakajāraṇā syād grāsastathā sāraṇakarma paścāt
children.translated_text: There is external liquefaction, digestion of mercury, ingestion, and afterward the operation of <s>sāraṇa</s>.

children.text: saṃkrāmaṇaṃ vedhavidhiḥ śarīre yogas tathāṣṭādaśadhātra karma ||
children.translated_text: Then there are transference, the method of piercing, and bodily application: thus the mercury operation is eighteenfold.

children.text: na yojyo marmaṇi chinne na ca kṣārāgnidagdhayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: It should not be applied where a vital spot is cut, nor where there are burns from alkali or fire.
When purified it endures a gentle fire; when mūrchita, it destroys disease.
When killed, free from quivering motion under intense fire, it gives long life and health.
Poison, fire, and impurity are the three innate defects.
In mercury they are respectively the causes of killing, burning distress, and stupor.
Lead and tin are two acquired defects; they produce dullness, bloating, and skin disease.
Again, other adventitious defects are named as the seven coverings.

children.text: bhūmijā girijā vārjās te ca dve nāgavaṅgajau ||
children.translated_text: They are earth-born, mountain-born, and water-born, and the two that arise from lead and tin.
These twelve defects in mercury have been taught by experts in <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: parpaṭī pāṭanī bhedī drāvī malakarī tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Parpaṭī</s>, <s>pāṭanī</s>, <s>bhedī</s>, <s>drāvī</s>, <s>malakarī</s>,

children.text: andhakārī tathā dhvāṅkṣī vijñeyāḥ sapta kañcukāḥ ||
children.translated_text: as well as <s>andhakārī</s> and <s>dhvāṅkṣī</s>, should be known as the seven coverings.

children.text: bhūmijāḥ kurvate kuṣṭhaṃ girijā jāḍyameva ca
children.translated_text: The earth-born defects cause skin disease, while the mountain-born cause only dullness.
The water-born defects cause obstruction of wind; the defects of lead and tin are full of faults.
Therefore, for the sake of procedures involving mercury, one should be joined by skilled assistants.
Having gathered all the equipment, one should begin the mercury operation.

children.text: dve sahasre palānāṃ tu sahasraṃ śatameva vā
children.translated_text: The processing of mercury may be done with two thousand <s>palas</s>, or one thousand, or one hundred,
or just twenty-eight <s>palas</s>, ten, five, or one.
The processing of mercury may even be performed with half a <s>pala</s>.
On a good day, under an auspicious lunar mansion, one should begin the purification of mercury.
One should add the three pungents, salt, <s>āsurī</s>, <s>citraka</s>, ginger, and radish root.

children.text: kṣiptvā sūto muhuḥ svedyaḥ kāñjikena dinatrayam ||
children.translated_text: The mercury should be steamed repeatedly with sour gruel for three days.
House soot, powdered brick, curd mixed with jaggery,
and salt together with <s>āsurī</s> should be added, and the mercury should be rubbed.

children.text: ṣoḍaśāṃśaṃ tu tad dravyaṃ sūtamānān niyojayet
children.translated_text: That substance should be used in the amount of one sixteenth of the measure of mercury.

children.text: sūtaṃ kṣiptvā samaṃ tena dināni trīṇi mardayet ||
children.translated_text: Having placed the mercury together with that, one should rub it for three days.

children.text: jīrṇābhrakaṃ tathā bījaṃ jīrṇasūtaṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: Digested mica, seed material, and likewise digested mercury

children.text: nairmalyārthaṃ hi sūtasya khalle dhṛtvā vimardayet ||
children.translated_text: should be placed in a mortar and rubbed for the sake of the mercury's purity.

children.text: gṛhṇāti nirmalo rāgān grāse grāse vimarditaḥ
children.translated_text: When rubbed, the purified mercury takes on colors with each morsel it consumes.
The operation called rubbing is what produces the qualities of mercury.
<s>Gṛhakanyā</s> removes impurity; <s>triphalā</s> destroys fire.

children.text: citramūlaṃ viṣaṃ hanti tasmād ebhiḥ prayatnataḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Citramūla</s> destroys poison; therefore, with these, carefully,
mercury mixed with the substances should be mūrchita seven times.
Mercury mūrchita in this way becomes free from defects.
Purified by this purgation, mercury should then be distilled.
It is drawn out from a decoction of sour gruel in order to remove the defect of foul odor.
Making a paste with copper, one should distill it in an upward vessel.
Leaving behind tin and lead, the mercury becomes purified.

children.text: śulvena pātayet piṣṭīṃ tridhordhvaṃ saptadhā tv adhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With copper one should distill the paste three times upward and seven times downward.
With <s>triphalā</s>, <s>śigru</s>, <s>śikhi</s>, and salt together with <s>āsurī</s>,
one should make the mercury into a vanished paste and smear it on the upper vessel.
Then one should carry out downward distillation there with blazing fuel cakes.
With turmeric, <s>aṅkola</s>, <s>śampāka</s>, <s>kumārī</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, and <s>agni</s>,
with <s>taṇḍulīyaka</s>, <s>varṣābhū</s>, asafoetida, rock salt, and <s>mākṣika</s>,
or with mercury ground with salts and with <s>sarpākṣī</s> and the like...
Or, O <s>Devī</s>, he should distill it; with <s>yakṣalocana</s> it becomes a healer of wounds.

children.text: itthaṃ hy adhaūrdhvapātena pātito 'sau yadā bhavet
children.translated_text: When it has thus been distilled by downward and upward distillation,
then, according to the particular substance, it becomes suitable for <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative alchemy).
Or, when made to descend in the <s>dīpaka</s> apparatus, it is freed from all defects.
But <s>sūtarāja</s> (king mercury), made to descend by the method of transverse distillation,
together with finely powdered mica flakes, <s>rasendra</s> (mercury), and <s>aranāla</s>,

children.text: khalle dattvā mṛditaṃ yāvat tan naṣṭapiṣṭatām eti
children.translated_text: should be placed in a mortar and triturated until it reaches the state in which the paste has disappeared.
One should process the mercury distilled by transverse distillation with gradually intensified fire.

children.text: saṃsvedyaḥ pātyo 'sau na patati yāvad dṛḍhaś cāgnau
children.translated_text: It should be steamed and distilled until it no longer falls and is firm in the fire.
Then that mercury is purified and certainly becomes capable of effective operations.

children.text: mardanair mūrchanaiḥ pātair mandaḥ śānto bhaved rasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Through grindings, stupefactions, and distillations, dull mercury becomes pacified.
Then, by restraint with <s>sṛṣṭyambuja</s>, the mercury becomes able to take a mouth.
Under the influence of steaming and the other procedures, mercury obtains unsurpassed potency.
It should then be properly restrained so that its fickleness ceases.
With <s>karkoṭī</s>, <s>phaṇinetra</s>, <s>vṛścikāmbuja</s>, and <s>mārkava</s>,
made equal and mixed with <s>aranāla</s>, one should steam it for three days.
With peppers joined with <s>bhūkhaga</s>, and with salt, <s>asurī</s>, <s>śigru</s>, and borax,
mixed with sour gruel, it becomes eager for morsels after three days of steaming.
With the three alkalis, rock salt, <s>khaga</s>, <s>bhūśikhī</s>, <s>śigru</s>, <s>rājī</s>, pungent substances, and <s>amlavetasa</s>, with salty, hot, and sour substances,
and with Nepalese copper leaf dried in <s>āranāla</s> and poulticed with sour wine and acids, that is the kindling of mercury.
One should steam it with sour wine for the increase of potency and brilliance.

children.text: yathopayogaṃ svedyaḥ syān mūlikānāṃ raseṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: According to the intended use, it should also be steamed in the juices of herbs.
<s>Sarpākṣī</s>, <s>kṣīriṇī</s>, <s>vandhyā</s>, <s>matsyākṣī</s>, and <s>śaṅkhapuṣpikā</s>,
<s>kākajaṅghā</s>, <s>śikhiśikhā</s>, <s>brahmadaṇḍī</s>, and <s>ākhukarṇikā</s>,
<s>varṣābhū</s>, <s>kambukī</s>, <s>dūrvā</s>, <s>sairyaka</s>, blue lotus, and <s>śimbikā</s>,
<s>śatāvarī</s>, <s>vajralatā</s>, <s>vajrakandā</s>, and <s>agnikarṇikā</s>,
white <s>arka</s>, <s>śigru</s>, <s>dhattūra</s>, <s>mṛgadūrvā</s>, and <s>rasāṅkuśā</s>,
plantain, red <s>ābhā</s>, <s>nirguṇḍī</s>, <s>lajjālu</s>, and <s>suradālikā</s>,
<s>maṇḍūkaparṇī</s>, <s>pātālī</s>, <s>citraka</s>, and <s>grīṣmasundarā</s>,
<s>kākamācī</s>, <s>mahārāṣṭrī</s>, turmeric, and <s>tilaparṇikā</s>,
<s>jātī</s>, <s>jayantī</s>, <s>śrīdevī</s>, <s>bhūkadamba</s>, and safflower,
<s>kośātakī</s>, water, <s>kaṇā</s>, <s>lāṅgalī</s>, and bitter gourd,
<s>cakramarda</s>, <s>amṛtā</s>, bulbous roots, and <s>puṅkhikā</s> among the sun-turning plants,
<s>vārāhī</s> and <s>hastiśuṇḍī</s>: these are, for the most part, the herbs for mercury.

children.text: rasasya bhāvane svede mūṣālepe ca pūjitāḥ
children.translated_text: They are esteemed for impregnating mercury, for steaming it, and for coating crucibles.
Thus the eight mercury saṃskāras, equal in the substance used for <s>rasāyana</s>,
should be performed first; the remaining ones, useful for particular substances, have not been stated.
We shall now describe the mercury bindings, twenty-five in number.

children.text: yena yena hi cāñcalyaṃ durgrahatvaṃ ca naśyati
children.translated_text: By whatever means the restlessness and the difficult-to-grasp nature
of the king mercury disappear, that has been declared by the specialists to be the purpose of binding.
<s>Haṭha</s>, <s>āroṭa</s>, then <s>ābhāsa</s>, <s>kriyāhīna</s>, and <s>piṣṭikā</s>,
<s>kṣāra</s>, <s>khoṭa</s>, <s>poṭa</s>, <s>kalkabandha</s>, and <s>kajjalī</s>,
<s>sajīva</s>, <s>nirjīva</s>, <s>nirbīja</s>, and <s>sabījaka</s>,
<s>śṛṅkhalābandha</s>, <s>drutibandha</s>, <s>bālaka</s>, and <s>kumāraka</s>,

children.text: taruṇaś ca tathā vṛddho mūrtibaddhas tathāparaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>taruṇa</s>, likewise <s>vṛddha</s>, and another called <s>mūrtibaddha</s>,
<s>jalabandha</s>, <s>agnibandha</s>, and the one named <s>susaṃskṛtakṛt</s>,
and that called <s>mahābandha</s>: these are said to be the twenty-five.
Some say there is a twenty-sixth, called <s>jalūkābandha</s>.
It is not so much approved for the body, but in the liquefaction procedure for women it is highly praised.

children.text: haṭho rasaḥ sa vijñeyaḥ samyak śuddhivivarjitaḥ
children.translated_text: Mercury known as <s>haṭha</s> should be understood as lacking proper purification.

children.text: sa sevito nṛṇāṃ kuryān mṛtyuṃ vā vyādhimuddhatam ||
children.translated_text: When consumed, it may cause death or a severe disease in men.
Properly and thoroughly purified mercury is called <s>āroṭa</s>.
It is best for preparing the body as a field and gradually destroys disease.

children.text: puṭito yo raso yāti yogaṃ muktvā svabhāvatām
children.translated_text: Mercury that, when baked in a covered heating, leaves its compound and returns to its natural state,
though impregnated with metals, roots, and the like, is <s>ābhāsa</s>, because of alteration in its qualities.
The excellent mercury that has been prepared with unpurified metals and similar substances
should be known as <s>kriyāhīna</s>; through improper regimen it undergoes harmful alteration.
Through fierce sunlight and very strong trituration, a <s>piṣṭī</s> is formed, having the appearance of fresh butter.
That mercury is <s>piṣṭikābandha</s>; it is an especially strong kindler and digester.
The mercury that has been prepared with conch shell, oyster shell, cowries, and the like
is <s>kṣārabandha</s>; it greatly produces digestive fire and nourishment and destroys colic.

children.text: bandho yaḥ khoṭatāṃ yāti dhmāto dhmātaḥ kṣayaṃ vrajet
children.translated_text: A binding that becomes a lump and, when repeatedly blown in the furnace, goes to destruction
should be known as <s>khoṭabandha</s>; it quickly removes all diseases.
Liquefied <s>kajjalikā</s>, flattened in a plantain leaf,
is <s>poṭa</s>, the same as <s>parpaṭī</s>; it removes all diseases beginning with those of children.
Mercury prepared by steaming and the like, and brought to the condition of mud,
should be known as <s>kalkabaddha</s>; it gives the result stated for its formulation.
<s>Kajjalī</s>, arising from mercury and sulfur, very smooth and like lamp-black,
when combined with the respective formulations, is called <s>kajjalībandha</s>.

children.text: bhasmīkṛto gacchati vahniyogād rasaḥ sajīvaḥ sa khalu pradiṣṭaḥ
children.translated_text: Mercury that is reduced to ash through application of fire is indeed prescribed as <s>sajīva</s>.

children.text: saṃsevito'sau na karoti bhasmakāryaṃ javād rogavināśanaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: When consumed, it does not produce a <s>bhasmaka</s>-like condition and it rapidly destroys disease.
When it has digested mica, or thoroughly digested sulfur, and has been reduced to ash with the chief of all metals,

children.text: nirjīvanāmā hi sa bhasmasūto niḥśeṣarogān vinihanti sadyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that ash-mercury is named <s>nirjīva</s>; it immediately destroys diseases without remainder.
Mercury, digested with gold to the amount of a quarter part and triturated with the addition of sulfur,
when calcined successively with equal parts of sulfur, is called seedless and destroys every disease.
That mercury which has been triturated and digested with mica-essence, gold, silver, copper, and magnetite,
and then killed with six times as much sulfur, is bound with seed and has great power.
Mercury killed by diamond and the like is one kind; killed mercury as such is another, equivalent kind.
But chain-bound mercury is effective for operations on the body and on metals,
and only <s>Śaṃkara</s> knows its wondrous, swift power of pervasion.

children.text: yukto'pi bāhyadrutibhiśca sūto bandhaṃgato vā bhasitasvarūpaḥ
children.translated_text: Even when joined with external liquefactions, mercury that has entered bondage or has the form of ash,
in a dose of a quarter mustard seed, destroys hard-to-cure diseases; it is called bound by liquefaction.

children.text: samābhrajīrṇaḥ śivajastu bālaḥ saṃsevito yogayuto javena
children.translated_text: Young <s>Śivaja</s> (mercury), digested with an equal amount of mica and used together with a proper formulation, swiftly
acts as a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenant), removes future diseases, and destroys dangerous diseases with complications.

children.text: harodbhavo yo dviguṇābhrajīrṇaḥ sa syātkumāro mitataṇḍulo'sau
children.translated_text: That <s>Harodbhava</s> (mercury) which is digested with twice as much mica is called the prince; its measured dose is a rice grain.

children.text: triḥ saptarātraiḥ khalu pāparogasaṃghātaghātī ca rasāyanaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: In three periods of seven nights it strikes down masses of evil diseases, and it is also a <s>rasāyana</s>.
That which has taken four times its quantity of mica as food is foremost among <s>rasāyanas</s> and is called youthful.
Within seven nights it destroys all diseases; it is a <s>rasāyana</s>, giving virility and strength.

children.text: yasyābhrakaḥ ṣaḍguṇito hi jīrṇaḥ prāptāgnisakhyaḥ sa hi vṛddhanāmā
children.translated_text: That in which sixfold mica has indeed been digested, and which has attained friendship with fire, is called old.

children.text: dehe ca lohe ca niyojanīyaḥ śivādṛte ko 'sya guṇān pravakti ||
children.translated_text: It is to be applied in the body and in metals; who apart from <s>Śiva</s> could proclaim its qualities?
Mercury made with divine herbs and able to withstand excessive fire,
