without digestion with mica, becomes an embodied binding, a great <s>rasa</s> (mercurial preparation).

children.text: ayaṃ hi jāryamāṇastu nāgninā kṣīyate rasaḥ
children.translated_text: This mercury, while it is being digested, is not diminished by fire.
Applied in all formulations, it grants incomparable results.
Bound by waters such as stone-water and similar liquids, this is the one possessing water-bondage.
It destroys old age, disease, and death, and grants the fruit stated in the ritual procedure.
Alone or joined with a formulation, when blown in the fire it becomes pill-shaped.
Undiminished and bound by fire, it produces sky-going and similar powers.
With <s>viṣṇukrāntā</s>, <s>śaśilatā</s>, <s>kumbhī</s>, and <s>kanakamūlaka</s>,
with <s>viśālā</s>, <s>nāginīkanda</s>, <s>vyāghrapādī</s>, and <s>kuruṇṭaka</s>,
with <s>vṛścikālī</s> and <s>ibhaśuṇḍī</s>, and with <s>haṃsapādā</s> together with <s>āsurī</s>,

children.text: aprasūtagavāṃ mūtraiḥ piṣṭaṃ vā kulake pacet ||
children.translated_text: one should grind it with the urine of cows that have not calved, or cook it in a sealed vessel.
When thus cooked, the mercury should be triturated with dead metals and cooked again.
This, in brief, is the procedure for the mūrchā (stupefying fixation) of mercury in apparatuses.

children.text: hemnā vā rajatena vā sahacaro dhmāto vrajatyekatām akṣīṇo nibiḍo guruśca guṭikākāro 'tidīrghojjvalaḥ
children.translated_text: Blown in the fire with gold or with silver as a companion, it attains unity; undiminished, compact, heavy, pill-shaped, and very brightly shining for a long time,

children.text: cūrṇatvaṃ paṭuvat prayāti nihato ghṛṣṭo na muñcenmalaṃ nirgandho dravati kṣaṇāt sa hi mahābandhābhidhāno rasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: when killed it becomes powder like cloth; when rubbed it does not release impurity, and, odorless, it melts in a moment: that mercury is called the great binding.
When half as much gold has been placed in the womb of mercury, or else a quarter part of lead, together with five-fingered <s>śālmalī</s> made rutting and with <s>śleṣmātaka</s> seeds,

children.text: tadvat tejinīkolakākhyaphalajaiś cūrṇaṃ tilaṃ pattrakaṃ tapte khallatale nidhāya mṛdite jātā jalūkā varā ||
children.translated_text: and likewise with powders from fruits called <s>tejinī</s> and <s>kolaka</s>, with sesame and leaf, placed on the surface of a hot mortar and rubbed, an excellent <s>jalūkā</s> is produced.

children.text: saiṣā syātkapikacchūromapaṭale candrāvatītailake candre ṭaṅkaṇakāmapippalījale svinnā bhavet tejinī
children.translated_text: This same, on a sheet of <s>kapikacchū</s> hairs, in <s>candrāvatī</s> oil, and boiled with <s>candra</s> in water of borax and <s>kāmapippalī</s>, becomes <s>tejinī</s>.

children.text: tapte khallatale vimardya vidhivadyatnādvaṭī yā kṛtā sā strīṇāṃ madadarpanāśanakarī khyātā jalūkā varā ||
children.translated_text: The pill carefully made by proper rubbing on the surface of a hot mortar is the famous excellent <s>jalūkā</s>, which destroys the pride of intoxication in women.

children.text: bālye cāṣṭāṅgulā yojyā yauvane ca daśāṅgulā
children.translated_text: In girlhood one measuring eight <s>aṅgulas</s> is to be used; in youth, one measuring ten <s>aṅgulas</s>.
For mature women, one of exactly twelve is prescribed; <s>jalaukā</s> is considered threefold.
Holding a vessel at the mouth of the mercury, one should supply sheep's milk.
One should set it in strong sunlight for twenty-one days.

children.text: dvitīyātra mayā proktā jalaukā drāvaṇe hitā
children.translated_text: Here I have taught a second <s>jalaukā</s>, beneficial for liquefaction.
Placed on the head of the penis for men, it liquefies semen in a wondrous way.
The juice of <s>munipattrā</s>, the water from the stalk of <s>śālmalī</s>,
the water of jasmine root, together with <s>śiṃśapā</s> water,
the fruit of <s>śleṣmātaka</s>, and also <s>triphala</s> powder,

children.text: kokilākṣasya cūrṇaṃ ca pāradaṃ mardayed budhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the powder of <s>kokilākṣa</s>: the wise person should triturate mercury with these.
A divine <s>jalūkā</s> is produced, charming to women.

children.text: sā yojyā kāmakāle tu kāmayetkāminī svayam ||
children.translated_text: It is to be used at the time of lovemaking; then the desirous woman desires of her own accord.
Lead dipped seven times in <s>triphala</s>, <s>bhṛṅga</s>, <s>mahauṣadha</s>, honey, ghee, goat's milk, and cow urine,
and digested with an equal amount of mercury, becomes a <s>jalūkā</s>.
Taking mercury in a measure counted by the suns, vowels, and days, and taking a dīnāra weight,
one should perform purification with the juices of <s>aṅkola</s>, <s>rājavṛkṣaka</s>, and <s>kanyā</s>.
With powders of <s>śaśirekhā</s>, <s>varavarṇinī</s>, <s>kokilākṣā</s>, <s>apāmārga</s>, and <s>kanaka</s>,
one should rub it thoroughly for twenty-one days.

children.text: niśāyāḥ kāñjikaṃ yūṣaṃ dattvā yonau praveśayet
children.translated_text: Having added sour gruel and pulse-broth of <s>niśā</s>, one should introduce it into the vagina.
It should be used among young, middle-aged, and mature women after discerning the proper order.
Even for passionless men, a woman becomes eager for union.

children.text: rasabhāgaṃ catuṣkaṃ ca vaṅgabhāgaṃ ca pañcamam
children.translated_text: There should be four parts of mercury and a fifth part of tin,
mixed with an equal amount of <s>surasāra</s> and combined with borax.

children.text: tridinaṃ mardayitvā ca golakaṃ taṃ rasodbhavam
children.translated_text: After triturating it for three days, that ball born from mercury
placed on the tip of the penis and inserted into the vagina, makes her obedient for life.

children.text: karpūrasūraṇasubhṛṅgasumeghanādair nāgaṃ niṣicya tu mitho valayed rasena
children.translated_text: After quenching lead with camphor, <s>sūraṇa</s>, <s>subhṛṅga</s>, and <s>meghanāda</s>, one should wind it together with mercury.

children.text: liṅgasthitena valayena nitambinīnāṃ svāmī bhavatyanudinaṃ sa tu jīvahetuḥ ||
children.translated_text: By means of the ring placed on the penis, he becomes master of shapely women every day; it is a cause of vitality.
With borax, <s>pippalī</s>, elephant-foot yam, camphor, and citron juices,
one should make a paste for his own <s>liṅga</s>; it causes the <s>yoni</s> of women to become moist.
Into lead that has been turned about in the fire one should put twice as much <s>harabīja</s>.
Then, with <s>muni</s>, gold, lead, serpent-material, and <s>dantī</s>, he should sprinkle its middle.
After grinding it with buttermilk, he should make the <s>madana-valaya</s> (love-ring) with the group of ingredients.
At the time of intercourse it destroys the erotic pride of women.
The juice of the fruits of <s>vyāghrī</s> and <s>bṛhatī</s>, elephant-foot yam tuber, and sour chickpea-leaf preparation,
with powders of <s>kapikacchu</s>, <s>vajravallī</s>, <s>pippalī</s>, and tamarind,
should be ground nine times with lead that has been turned in the fire and with cooling substances.
When this <s>smara-valaya</s> (love-ring) has been made, it causes women to become moist.
Mercury together with <s>palāśa</s> seed, ground with the sour juice of red citron,

children.text: sajīvaṃ marditaṃ yantre pācitaṃ mriyate dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: and cooked alive in an apparatus, is certainly killed.
With well-powdered <s>kharamañjarī</s> seeds and <s>puṣkara</s> seeds one should make a paste.
He should roast mercury in a strong crucible; it becomes <s>bhasma</s> (ash).
Asafoetida, well impregnated with the milk of <s>kākodumbarikā</s>,
through the procedure of grinding and roasting, indeed turns mercury into ash.
One should grind <s>devadālī</s> and <s>harikrāntā</s> with sour gruel.
With their liquids, mercury ground seven times should be made stupefied.

children.text: tatsūtaṃ kharpare dadyāddattvā dattvā tu taddravam
children.translated_text: One should place that mercury on a potsherd, repeatedly adding that liquid.
He should cook it over the hearth for a day; it becomes ash resembling salt.
One should powder the seeds of <s>apāmārga</s> and likewise of castor.
That powder should be put with mercury in a crucible, below and above.

children.text: ruddhvā laghupuṭaiḥ pacyāc caturbhir bhasmatāṃ nayet ||
children.translated_text: After sealing it, he should cook it with four light roastings and bring it to the state of ash.
In the tuber produced from bitter bottle-gourd, placed inside and soaked in woman's milk,
mercury, steamed seven times, is killed by a cow-dung fire.
He should grind the root of <s>aṅkola</s> with water and triturate it in a mortar.
At day's end he should confine mercury combined with sulfur.

children.text: puṭayedbhūdhare yantre dinānte sa mṛto bhavet ||
children.translated_text: He should roast it in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus; by day's end it is killed.
He should grind mercury and mica with banyan latex for three watches.
He should cook it with that wood; that <s>rasa</s> becomes ash.
Then the patient should regard the <s>rasācārya</s> (mercury-teacher) as the god <s>Maheśvara</s> in person,
and the prepared <s>rasa</s>, kept in containers of horn, tooth, bamboo, and the like.
After worshiping him according to his ability, and also the gods, cows, and brahmins,
he should eat the mercury placed on a piece of leaf, with the proper after-drink.
Food prepared with ghee, rock salt, coriander, cumin, and fresh ginger,
<s>taṇḍulīyaka</s>, coriander, <s>paṭola</s>, <s>ālambuṣā</s>, and the like,
aged Śāli rice, cow's milk, ghee, and curd,
<s>haṃsodaka</s> water and mung-bean soup: this, in brief, is the class of wholesome things.
One should avoid <s>bṛhatī</s>, bilva, pumpkin, reed-shoot, and bitter gourd,

children.text: māṣaṃ masūraṃ niṣpāvaṃ kulatthaṃ sarṣapaṃ tilam ||
children.translated_text: black gram, lentils, broad beans, horse gram, mustard, and sesame,
fasting, rubbing the body, bathing, copper, liquor, and fermented drinks,
marshland meat, sour grain-gruel, eating on a banana leaf,

children.text: kāṃsye ca guruviṣṭambhi tīkṣṇoṣṇaṃ ca bhṛśaṃ tyajet ||
children.translated_text: and in bronze vessels, as well as food that is heavy, obstructive, excessively sharp, and hot.

children.text: kaṇṭārīphalakāñjikaṃ ca kamaṭhas tailaṃ tathā rājikām
children.translated_text: <s>kaṇṭārī</s> fruit, sour gruel, tortoise, oil, and likewise mustard,
lemon, <s>kataka</s>, <s>kaliṅgaka</s> fruit, pumpkin, and cucumber,
<s>kārī</s>, cock, bitter-gourd fruit, and the fruit of <s>karkoṭikā</s>,

children.text: vṛntākaṃ ca kapitthakaṃ khalu gaṇaḥ proktaḥ kakārādikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: eggplant and wood-apple: this is indeed the group called the one beginning with ka.
This group beginning with ka, taught in the <s>Devīśāstra</s>, is accepted.
Another form, specified in another treatise, is now stated.
<s>kaṅgu</s>, <s>kanduka</s>, jujube, cock, <s>kalaka</s>, boar, and horse gram,
<s>kaṇṭārī</s>, pungent oil, <s>kṛṣṇagalaka</s>, tortoise, pea, and <s>kaṇā</s>,

children.text: karkāruśca kaṭhillakaṃ ca katakaṃ karkoṭakaṃ karkaṭī kālī kāñjikameṣakādikagaṇaḥ śrīkṛṣṇadevoditaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>karkāru</s>, <s>kaṭhillaka</s>, <s>kataka</s>, <s>karkoṭaka</s>, cucumber, <s>kālī</s>, sour gruel, and the group beginning with sheep and the like: this was taught by <s>Śrīkṛṣṇadeva</s>.
In whatever <s>rasa</s> preparation the group beginning with ka is expressly forbidden,
there, in each case, that very group should be prohibited, according to its suitability and otherwise.
When belching occurs, one should take curd-rice with black fish and cumin.
When wind is disturbed, there should be oil massage with oils such as <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> oil.
When there is distaste, cold water should be poured over the head.
When there is thirst, one should take coconut water and mung beans with sugar.
One should resort to the fruits of grapes, pomegranate, dates, and plantain.
For increasing the potency of the <s>rasa</s>, curd, milk, sugarcane juice, and sugar are used,
and other cooling treatment as well, and again in the procedure for discontinuing the <s>rasa</s>.
One may eat <s>bṛhatī</s> and bilva once; this is a common rule.
For fever, bleeding disorders, cough, dyspnea, and hiccup,
for loss of voice, wasting disease, and also loss of appetite and salivation,
for vomiting and heart disease, and for thirst, disorders arising from liquor, and piles,
for upward movement of wind, diarrhea, intestinal pain, and dysentery,
for cholera-like disease, weak digestive fire, dysuria, and urinary stones,
for urinary disease, <s>somaroga</s>, pustules, and abscess,
for enlargement, abdominal tumors and related diseases, colics, and abdominal disease,
for anemia, swelling, erysipelas, skin disease, leucoderma, and disorders of wind,
for gout and obstructed conditions, for barren women and pains of pregnant women,
for diseases of women in childbirth and of children, and also in insanity and epilepsy,
for diseases of the eye, ear, nose, and mouth,
for diseases arising in the head, for wounds, fractures, and fistula-in-ano,
for glandular swellings and other minor diseases, for diseases of the genitals, and for poisons.
for old age, and for childless women, for the purpose of nourishing the seed.
By this procedure, indeed, the treatment of all diseases
with preparations of mercury, metals, and poisons will be taught here according to tradition.
Horripilation and trembling, sweetness in the mouth, yawning, piercing pain in the head, and burning

children.text: vātajvarasyoktam idaṃ hi lakṣma bhuktottaraṃ syādyadi śaśvadeva ||
children.translated_text: are declared to be this sign of vāta-fever, if they occur continually after eating.
Purgation, wasting, bitterness in the mouth, intense heat, delirious speech, dizziness, and fainting:
these are the signs of pitta-fever, together with vomiting, thirst, and burning in the limbs.
Cough and dyspnea, dullness in the mouth, sweetness, much sleep,
sweating, and slight burning are the signs of kapha-born fever.

children.text: miśritaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ yattu dvayos triṣu bhavecca tat ||
children.translated_text: But when the symptoms are mixed, that fever is produced from two doṣas or from all three.

children.text: vimarditābhyāṃ rasagandhakābhyāṃ nīreṇa kuryādiha golakaṃ tam
children.translated_text: With mercury and sulfur well triturated together with water, one should make that pellet here.
After placing it in a new vessel, a copper vessel should be set over that pellet.

children.text: sārdhaṃ muhūrtaṃ vinirudhya dhīmān uddīpayed dīptakṛśānunāsya
children.translated_text: The wise physician, having sealed it for one and a half muhūrtas, should heat it with a blazing fire below.
From beneath, this <s>parpaṭī</s> is perfected, a cloud of fire against the forest of new fever.

children.text: vilipya pūrvaṃ rasanāṃ ca tāludeśaṃ ca sindhūdbhavajīrakārdraiḥ
children.translated_text: First anointing the tongue and the region of the palate with sea-salt, cumin, and fresh ginger,

children.text: vallonmitāṃ cārdrakatoyamiśrām enāṃ niyojya sthagayet paṭena ||
children.translated_text: one should administer this, one <s>valla</s> in measure and mixed with ginger juice, and cover it with a cloth.

children.text: gharmodgamo yāvadataḥ paraṃ ca takraudanaṃ pathyamiha prayojyam
children.translated_text: Until sweat breaks out, and afterward, buttermilk-rice is to be used here as the wholesome diet.

children.text: kuryāddinānāṃ tritayaṃ yadītthaṃ jvarasya śaṅkāpi tadā bhavetkim ||
children.translated_text: If one does this for three days, how could even any suspicion of fever then remain?
Equal parts of <s>sūta</s> (mercury), <s>arka</s>, sulfur, <s>capalā</s>, <s>jayapāla</s>, bitter <s>pathyā</s>, <s>trivṛt</s>, and poison-nut
should be impregnated with <s>vajrī</s> milk; three <s>vallas</s> with honey make <s>Trailokyaḍambara-rasa</s>, which destroys fresh fever.
With one-quarter part of <s>sāraravi</s> and an equal part of sulfur, cooked and ground in its own decoction,
the preparation called <s>Meghanāda</s>, taken successively in a dose of one <s>māṣa</s>, is for fevers beginning with vāta.

children.text: daradajaladayuktaṃ śuddhasūtaṃ ca gandhaṃ praharamatha supiṣṭaṃ vallayugmaṃ ca dadyāt
children.translated_text: Pure mercury joined with <s>darada</s> and <s>jalada</s>, and sulfur, should then be very finely ground for a prahara; two <s>vallas</s> should be given.
The preparation named <s>Jvaragajahari</s> is taken with ginger water; if it first produces burning, it should be eaten with milk-rice.
A portion of heated lead, mercury, sulfur, and long pepper
should be combined separately there in equal portions according to rule.
All of it should be triturated in citron juice for three days,
and also for three days in the juices of <s>Meghanāda</s> and aloe.
For two days in goat urine and for three days in cow urine,
one should impregnate it as appropriate; into that these should be added:
rock salt, one part of <s>citraka</s>, and likewise <s>sauvarcala</s> salt.

children.text: tena sammelanaṃ kṛtvā bhāvayecca punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having made the mixture with that, one should impregnate it again and again.

children.text: anena vidhinā samyak siddho bhavati tadrasaḥ
children.translated_text: By this method that <s>rasa</s> becomes properly perfected.
Joined with sugar and ghee, three <s>vallas</s> of the preparation should be given.
Wheat-rice is the wholesome diet, along with black gram soup and <s>vāstuka</s>,
mixed with emblic myrobalan fruit; it destroys every fever.
This is called <s>Dīpikārasa</s> by those who know the tantra.
Mercury, calamine, orpiment, blue vitriol, sulfur, and borax:
all these, purified and in equal quantity, should be triturated for a day with the juices of bitter gourd.
With that paste one should smear the inside of a copper vessel,
to a thickness of half of half a finger, and cook it in the apparatus called the sand-bath.
When grains of rice burst on the back of it in this way,
then the physician should take the well-cooled substance from inside the copper vessel.
The preparation called <s>Śītabhañjī-rasa</s> should be powdered with an equal amount of black pepper.
One should eat one <s>māṣa</s> with a piece of leaf; it destroys fever,
within three days even if irregular, severe, and recurring every one, two, three, or four days.
Equal parts of mercury, orpiment, and realgar should be triturated in cucumber juice.
Having placed that paste, made into a black collyrium-like mass, in a copper vessel,
one should cook it in a sand apparatus according to the prescribed method.
Then the excellent physician should give a dose of one <s>māṣa</s> with powdered black pepper.
In cold fever, one should drink a handful of hot water.
This is <s>Śītabhañjī-rasa</s>, a remover of cold fever.

children.text: kūṣmāṇḍacūrṇatilajaiḥ praviśuddhatālaṃ gāḍhaṃ vimardya suṣavīsalilena tulyam
children.translated_text: Purified orpiment should be strongly triturated with powder of ash gourd and sesame products, together with an equal amount of <s>suṣavī</s> water,

children.text: sūtena hiṅgulabhuvā sikatākhyayantre golaṃ vidhāya parivṛttakapālamadhye ||
children.translated_text: and with mercury born from cinnabar; having made a pellet in the apparatus called the sand-bath, inside two inverted pots,

children.text: pattreṇa taṃ dinapateśca pidhāya ruddhvā saṃdhiṃ tayorguḍasudhākhaṭikāśivābhiḥ
children.translated_text: one should cover it with a leaf of the sun-plant and seal the joint of the two with jaggery, lime, chalk, and <s>śivā</s>.

children.text: vahnau pacenmṛduni pātraśiraḥsthaśālīvaivarṇyamātram avadhiṃ pravidhāya dhīmān ||
children.translated_text: The wise physician should cook it over a gentle fire, setting as the limit only the discoloration of rice placed on the head of the vessel.

children.text: vallaṃ tataḥ surasamiśramamuṣya dadyāt sarpiḥ sitākaṇapayomadhu cānupeyam
children.translated_text: Then one should give one <s>valla</s> of this mixed with <s>surasā</s>; ghee, sugar, long pepper, milk, and honey are the after-drink.

children.text: jetuṃ jvarān praviṣamān iha vāntiśāntyai maulau suśītalajalasya dadīta dhārām ||
children.translated_text: To conquer very irregular fevers here, and for the calming of vomiting, one should pour a stream of very cool water on the head.
Now there is the preparation called <s>Mṛtajīvana</s>, the crest-jewel adorning the head of <s>Rasarāja</s>,

children.text: sudhāraseneva rasena yena saṃjīvanaṃ syāt sahasāturāṇām ||
children.translated_text: by whose nectar-like juice there would be sudden revival for the sick.
Mercury, cinnabar, and <s>jepāla</s>, increased successively and triturated with the juice of <s>dantī</s>,
destroys fever in half a day, in a dose of one <s>guñjā</s> together with sugar.

children.text: śuddhaṃ sūtaṃ viṣaṃ gandhaṃ dhūrtabījaṃ tribhiḥ samam
children.translated_text: Purified mercury, poison, sulfur, and <s>dhūrtā</s> seed, equal to three parts,
and the three pungents equal to four parts should be powdered and stored.

children.text: dantabhāṇḍe 'tha vā śārṅge kāṣṭhe naiva kadācana
children.translated_text: It should never be kept in an ivory vessel, nor in a horn vessel, nor in wood.
It is to be given in fever caused by <s>vāta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s>, or in a dual fever, or in one arising from all three <s>doṣas</s>.
With the juice of fresh ginger, or again with the juice of citron,
two <s>guñjās</s> should be administered; when this has been digested, curd-rice should be used.
It will destroy fevers in one, two, or three days, according to the sequence of the <s>doṣas</s>.
This <s>rasa</s>, named <s>Mahājvarāṅkuśa</s>, was taught by <s>Śambhu</s>.

children.text: tālaṃ tāmrarajo rasaśca gaganaṃ gandhaśca nepālakaṃ dīnārapramitaṃ tadardhamuditaṃ ṭaṅkaṃ śilāmākṣikam
children.translated_text: <s>Tāla</s>, copper powder, mercury, mica, sulfur, and <s>nepālaka</s> are in the measure of a <s>dīnāra</s>; half that amount is prescribed for borax and <s>śilāmākṣika</s>.

children.text: dīnāradvitayaṃ viṣasya śikhinaḥ piṣṭvā rasaiḥ pācito yaścintāmaṇivajjvaraughavijayī nāmnā tu mṛtyuṃjayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Two <s>dīnāras</s> of poison and <s>śikhin</s>, ground with juices and cooked, conquers hosts of fevers like a wish-fulfilling jewel; it is called <s>Mṛtyuṃjaya</s>.

children.text: tālaṃ tāmram ayorajaśca capalā tutthābhrakaṃ kāntakaṃ nāgaṃ syācca samāṃśakaṃ sumṛditaṃ mūlaṃ ca paunarnavam
children.translated_text: <s>Tāla</s>, copper, iron powder, <s>capalā</s>, blue vitriol, mica, <s>kāntaka</s>, and lead should be in equal parts, well triturated with the root of <s>punarnavā</s>.
This paste, made with the juices from leaves of <s>bhṛṅgī</s>, <s>kāsaharī</s>, <s>punarnavā</s>, and great <s>mandāra</s>, and cooked in a sand apparatus, brings every fever to an end.

children.text: tutthena tulyaḥ śivajaśca gandho jambīranīreṇa vimardanīyaḥ
children.translated_text: Blue vitriol, an equal amount of <s>śivaja</s>, and sulfur should be triturated with citron water.

children.text: dinatrayaṃ melaya tena tulyaṃ vyoṣaṃ tataḥ sidhyati candrasūryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For three days one should mix it; then add an equal amount of <s>vyoṣa</s>, and the preparation <s>Candrasūrya</s> is perfected.

children.text: vallo vijetuṃ viṣamāvalambi dalena deyo bhujagākhyavallyāḥ
children.translated_text: One <s>valla</s>, to conquer a persistent irregular fever, should be given with a leaf of the creeper called <s>bhujaga</s>.

children.text: dugdhaṃ hitaṃ syādiha śṛṅgaverarasena śaityeṣu niṣevaṇīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Milk is beneficial here; in cold conditions it should be taken with ginger juice.
For fever with pregnancy and for pain, buttermilk is used; with raisin-water, the regimen stated immediately afterward is wholesome.

children.text: rodhaṃ varāyāḥ salilena śūlaṃ jambīranīreṇa varājalena ||
children.translated_text: For obstruction, it is given with water of <s>varā</s>; for pain, with citron water and water of <s>varā</s>.
In loss of consciousness it should be employed here as an anointing, together with <s>bimba</s> and milk-derived substances.

children.text: ghṛtaudanaṃ syādiha bhojanāya jambīranīreṇa nihanti gulmam ||
children.translated_text: Ghee-rice should be the food here; with citron water it destroys <s>gulma</s>.
It should be given with the juice of asafoetida, sour gruel, and citron; in splenic abdominal disease, buttermilk-rice is used here.

children.text: stambhārthamasminsasitaṃ payaḥ syād guḍo niyojyo vamanapraśāntyai ||
children.translated_text: For checking it, milk with sugar is used in this case; jaggery should be prescribed for calming vomiting.

children.text: aśītir yasya varṣāṇi vasuvarṣāṇi yasya vā
children.translated_text: For one who is eighty years old, or for one who is eight years old,

children.text: viṣaṃ tasya na dātavyaṃ dattaṃ ced doṣakārakam ||
children.translated_text: poison must not be given; if it is given, it causes disorder.
<s>Megha</s>, mercury, sulfur, stone, poison, the three pungents, and the salts,
and the two kinds of cumin: these should be prepared in equal parts.
It should be triturated with the juice of <s>sinduvāra</s> and also with garlic juice,
and with the juice of <s>apāmārga</s>, for seven nights.
When it has been cooked in a sand apparatus, one should administer a dose the size of a <s>guñjā</s>.
It is given with betel and black pepper; after that one should make the patient drink cold water.
The <s>rasa</s> named <s>Umāprasādana</s> removes cold fever.
It destroys quartan fever, or one recurring over three nights; how much more the other kinds.
Borax, mercury, and sulfur should be arranged in equal parts.
After adding twice as much <s>nepāla</s>, one should triturate it in the mortar.
One should triturate it slowly until it reaches smoothness.
Rock salt, black pepper, conch, tamarind alkali, and <s>mākṣika</s> are added.
Having made this equal to that, one should triturate it with lemon water.
For three days one should eat pills the size of a chickpea.

children.text: aikāhikaṃ dvyāhikaṃ ca tryāhikaṃ ca caturthakam
children.translated_text: For one-day, two-day, three-day, and four-day fevers,
it is remembered as <s>Jvarāṅkuśa</s>, for the destruction of every fever.
Mica, sulfur, and mercury are to be taken separately, one <s>tola</s> each.
One should take half a <s>tola</s> of poison and half a <s>tola</s> of tamarind fruit.
Having combined all this, one should triturate it in the mortar.
One should keep triturating it slowly until it becomes smooth.

children.text: vistāre pariṇāhe ca gartāṃ kṛtvā ṣaḍaṅgulām
children.translated_text: Having made a pit six fingers in breadth and circumference,
one should place leaves of the betel creeper inside the pit.

children.text: parṇeṣu sūtakalkaṃ taṃ gartāyāṃ sthāpayed dṛḍham
children.translated_text: On the leaves one should firmly place that mercury paste in the pit.
Above the paste, one should fill the mouth of the pit with those leaves.
Then a heating should be applied in the pit with forest fuel-cakes.
When it is known to have cooled of itself, one should afterward draw it out completely.
Together with the leaves smeared with mercury, one should triturate the paste in a mortar.
After adding half a <s>tola</s> of <s>amṛta</s> and half a <s>tola</s> of tamarind fruit,
one should keep the triturated paste and apply it in a dose the size of a <s>guñjā</s>.
It should be joined with ginger water, <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, <s>citraka</s>, and rock salt.
It is to be given in <s>saṃnipāta</s>, in <s>vāta</s> disorder, in the three-<s>doṣa</s> condition, and in irregular fever,
as well as in weak digestion, in <s>grahaṇī</s>, and in a patient with diarrhea.
Curd-rice should be used as the food in connection with this <s>rasa</s>.
One should act according to the disease and related factors, and then pour on water.
This splendid, excellent formula gives life to living beings.
It is known as <s>Cintāmaṇi-rasa</s>, complete and beautiful in every respect.

children.text: sūtendraṃ parimardya pañcapaṭubhiḥ kṣārais tribhis taṃ tataḥ piṇḍe hiṅgumahauṣadhāsurīmaye saṃsvedya dhānyodake
children.translated_text: Having triturated lord mercury with the five salts and then the three alkalis, one should steam it in rice-water inside a lump made of asafoetida, <s>mahauṣadha</s>, and <s>asurī</s>.

It is then treated with waters produced from <s>nirguṇḍī</s>, <s>hutāśamantha</s>, sesame leaves, <s>unmattā</s>, <s>bhṛṅga</s>, fresh ginger, <s>kāmātā</s>, mountain <s>karṇikā</s>, <s>plava</s> leaves, and <s>pañcāṅgula</s>.

children.text: sūtendreṇa samair vimardya sahajaiḥ pittaistato bhāvayed daṃṣṭricchāgalulāyamatsyaśikhināṃ sā saṃnipātāñjayet
children.translated_text: After triturating it with an equal amount of mercury and then impregnating it with the natural biles of boar, goat, buffalo, fish, and peacock, that pill conquers <s>saṃnipāta</s>.

children.text: vikhyātā bhuvi lokanāthaguṭikā mārīcamātrā hitā syādasyāḥ sahitaṃ dadhīkṣuśakalaṃ vīryaṃ bhavecchītalam ||
children.translated_text: Famous on earth as <s>Lokanātha-guṭikā</s>, it is beneficial in a dose the size of a black pepper; accompanied by curd and a piece of sugarcane, its potency is cooling.
The ashes of <s>vajra</s> and <s>vaikrānta</s> should each be one <s>niṣka</s> in measure,
with two <s>niṣkas</s> of <s>śṛṅgīviṣa</s> and three <s>niṣkas</s> of <s>cūlikāpaṭu</s>.
There should also be five <s>niṣkas</s> of <s>agnijāra</s>; all of this should be combined in one place.
One should triturate it with mercury, in an amount equal to the ash, for three days.
It should be impregnated with the alkaline water of the <s>śārṅgaṣṭādi</s> group,
twenty-three times, grinding and drying it each time.
Then, after grinding it for a day, one should place it in an ivory casket.
This <s>rasa</s> is called <s>Mṛtasaṃjīvana</s>, the needle-applied preparation.
For a man about to die from severe <s>saṃnipāta</s>, even one who has been placed in the ground,
one should make an incision in the palate and then insert this <s>rasa</s> there.
With an extremely fine needle, moistened with water, and with the greatest care,
then one should smear him with oil and place him where there is no wind.
If, after more than half a <s>prahara</s>, he has passed urine and feces,
has regained consciousness, is full of heat, and repeatedly tosses his head,
one should know that he will live; otherwise, indeed, the opposite is the case.
After that one should place him in a cauldron filled with cold water.
There, when the water has become hot, one should remove it and add other water.

children.text: yācamānam amuṃ paścāt pāyayet sasitaṃ payaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When afterward he asks for it, one should give him milk with sugar to drink.
Likewise one should give curds mixed with sugar, coconut water,
and plantain fruits; otherwise, indeed, he dies.
When he has regained consciousness, is speaking, and asks for fruit and the like,
one should draw him out from there, anointed with oil, and remove the oil by rubbing it away.
One should smear him with sandal and camphor from the soles of the feet to the head,
and should tend him for seven nights with such cooling substances.
At the ears, eyes, nose, and mouth one should repeatedly apply pads or supports.
When the eighth day has arrived, the juice produced from the root of <s>dardurī</s>,
together with sugar, should be given to drink in order to bring down the force of the <s>rasa</s>.
After the <s>rasa</s> has been brought down, one may give food and curds as desired.
If he is furnished with inhalation and exhalation and with other signs of life restored,
one should place him in a cauldron filled with water so that he may regain awareness.
After he has regained awareness, one should draw him out and tend him as before.
Having lived out the measure of his lifespan, he then dies thereafter.
One who rescues a man sinking in the ocean of death
in a most terrible <s>saṃnipāta</s>: even <s>Brahmā</s> does not find the end of his merit.
A man freed from the great fear of death by <s>saṃnipāta</s>
should worship the life-saving physician even by giving all his property.
Otherwise he remains in hell for as long as the succession of aeons lasts.
This should be known as the command of <s>Śaṅkara</s>, proclaimed by <s>Śambhu</s>.
The root used for bringing down the <s>rasa</s> should not be made public.
Foolish men, out of desire for wealth, give it without the teaching of the śāstra.
Having obtained the favor of the guru, it should be employed in <s>saṃnipāta</s>.

children.text: śārṅgaṣṭā ca tathā vyāghrī karīras tilaparṇikā
children.translated_text: <s>Śārṅgaṣṭā</s>, likewise <s>vyāghrī</s>, <s>karīra</s>, <s>tilaparṇikā</s>,
<s>indravāruṇikā</s>, <s>mustā</s>, turmeric, and the root of <s>aṅkola</s>,

children.text: apāmārgaḥ kaṇā svarṇaṃ kaṭutumbī ca tintiḍī
children.translated_text: <s>apāmārga</s>, <s>kaṇā</s>, <s>svarṇa</s>, bitter gourd, and tamarind:
this is the group beginning with <s>śārṅgaṣṭā</s>, the supreme remover of <s>saṃnipāta</s>.

children.text: sūtaṃ gandhakatālakaṃ maṇiśilāṃ tāpyaṃ lavaṃ tutthakaṃ jepālaṃ viṣaṭaṅkaṇaṃ madhuphalaṃ kṛtvā samāṃśaṃ dṛḍham
children.translated_text: Mercury, sulfur, orpiment, realgar, <s>tāpya</s>, salt, blue vitriol, <s>jepāla</s>, poison, borax, and <s>madhuphala</s> should be made firm in equal parts.

children.text: kṛtvā kajjalikāṃ viṣolbaṇaphaṇeḥ pittaiśca saṃbhāvayet kṣiptvā sīsakakūpike rasavaraṃ sūcīmukhaṃ nāmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having made a black collyrium-like mass, one should impregnate it with the bile of a fiercely poisonous snake, and, placing the excellent <s>rasa</s> in a leaden bottle, it is called <s>Sūcīmukha</s>.

children.text: brahmadvāri vikīrṇalohitalave guñjaikamātraṃ daded dattvā sampuṭabaddhatandrikadhanurvāte saśākhāhime
children.translated_text: At the <s>brahmadvāra</s>, where a small drop of blood has been scattered, one should give a single <s>guñjā</s> measure; having given it for closed-jaw stupor and bow-like tetanus with chills in the limbs,

children.text: kāsaṃ śvāsamarocakaṃ pralapanaṃ kampaṃ ca hikkāturaṃ mūkatvaṃ badhiratvam unmadam apasmāraṃ jayet tatkṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: it immediately conquers cough, dyspnea, loss of appetite, delirious speech, tremor, distress with hiccup, muteness, deafness, insanity, and epilepsy.
Mercury, sulfur, copper, mica, <s>lāṅgalī</s>, <s>vahni</s>, and <s>rāmaṭha</s>,
<s>vandhyā</s>, <s>paṭola</s>, <s>nirguṇḍī</s>, fragrant substances, and shoots of neem,
<s>pāṭhā</s>, the three alkalis, <s>kṣveḍa</s>, <s>bola</s>, and seeds of thorn-apple,
together with <s>śṛṅgī</s> and the essence of <s>madhuka</s>, should be triturated with sour citron juice.
One should make a pill in the measure of a <s>niṣka</s>; that restrains
<s>saṃnipāta</s> with sweating, burning, and delirium, and is the elephant-goad for <s>saṃnipāta</s>.

children.text: sasārā vaiṣṇavī senā acalā kādi kaṅkaṇā
children.translated_text: The <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s> army moved, immovable, with a bracelet beginning with <s>ka</s>,
endowed with redness and a <s>Rudra</s>-like form, mature, and bearing a head.

children.text: tribhāgaṃ tālakaṃ vidyād ekabhāgaṃ tu pāradam
children.translated_text: One should know three parts to be orpiment, but one part mercury;

children.text: tadardhaṃ gandhakaṃ caiva tadardhaṃ tu manaḥśilā ||
children.translated_text: half of that should be sulfur, and half of that again realgar.
One should triturate it with juices of bitter-gourd leaves for three <s>praharas</s>.
Cooked in a sand apparatus, this <s>rasa</s> removes quartan fever.
There should be sulfur, pleasing in appearance, joined with mercury;
it is tripled with <s>hiyāvallī</s> and triturated with the juice of <s>nirguṇḍī</s>.
It should be applied seven times with fresh ginger juice.
<s>Cāturthikagajāṅkuśa</s> destroys continuous fever and related fevers.
<s>Tāpya</s>, orpiment, <s>jepāla</s>, <s>vatsanābha</s>, and realgar,
together with copper, sulfur, and mercury, are triturated with <s>musalī</s> juice.
Cooked by the <s>kukkuṭīpuṭa</s> method, it is known as <s>Mṛtyuñjaya</s>.
One should administer two <s>vallas</s>; food with curds may be given as desired.
This great <s>rasa</s> destroys new fever and <s>saṃnipāta</s>.

children.text: śuddhaṃ sūtaṃ viṣaṃ gandhaṃ maricaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ kaṇām
children.translated_text: Purified mercury, poison, sulfur, black pepper, borax, and <s>kaṇā</s>

children.text: mardayed dhūrtajadrāvair dinam ekaṃ tu śoṣayet ||
children.translated_text: should be triturated for one day with liquids from thorn-apple and then dried.
The <s>rasa</s> named <s>Pañcavaktra</s>, in a dose of two <s>guñjās</s>, conquers <s>saṃnipāta</s>.
One should also administer a decoction of <s>arka</s> root, together with the three pungents, as the after-drink.

children.text: dadhyodanaṃ hitaṃ tatra jalayogaṃ ca kārayet ||
children.translated_text: Yogurt-rice is wholesome in that case, and one should also apply the water regimen.
Equal parts of <s>rasa</s> (mercury) and sulfur should be combined with liquids produced from <s>dhattūra</s> fruit,

children.text: mardayed dinamekaṃ tu tattulyaṃ trikaṭu kṣipet
children.translated_text: and triturated for one day; then one should add an equal amount of <s>trikaṭu</s> (the three pungents).
This <s>rasa</s>, called <s>Unmattākhya</s> by name, when used as a nasal medicine, conquers <s>saṃnipāta</s>.
One should powder ten <s>niṣkas</s> of seeds born from <s>jepāla</s>, with the husk removed,
and mix in black pepper, long pepper, and <s>sūta</s> (mercury), one <s>niṣka</s> each.
It should be carefully impregnated with liquids from citron for seven days.

children.text: saṃnipātaṃ nihantyāśu añjane yaḥ śivaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When applied as a collyrium, this preparation, remembered as <s>Śiva</s>, quickly destroys <s>saṃnipāta</s>.
Madanaphala, viḍa salt, and mustard seeds, two <s>niṣkas</s> each,
should be powdered; one should drink them with a decoction of <s>triphala</s>, together with borax.

children.text: kuṣṭhe jvare kāmalāyāṃ kaṇṭharoge hy ajīrṇake
children.translated_text: In skin disease, fever, jaundice, throat disease, and indigestion,
and for nasal use, one seed produced from <s>girikarṇī</s> should be taken with cold water.

children.text: pratyekaṃ rasagandhayor dvipalayoḥ kṛtvā maṣīṃ śuddhayor ramyāṃ mlecchalulāyalocanamanodhātrīprakuñcatrayam
children.translated_text: Taking two <s>palas</s> each of purified <s>rasa</s> and sulfur and making a fine black powder, one should add the pleasing set of three <s>prakuñcas</s> called mleccha, lulāya-locana, and manodhātrī.

children.text: pathyāyā badaratrikaṃ trikaṭu ṣaṭśāṇaṃ vacā dharmiṇī vellāmbhodharapattrakadviradakiñjalkāśvagandhāhvayam ||
children.translated_text: There should also be <s>pathyā</s>, three badaras in measure, six <s>śāṇas</s> of <s>trikaṭu</s>, and the ingredients called vacā, dharmiṇī, vellā, ambhodhara, pattraka, dvirada-kiñjalka, and aśvagandhā.

children.text: piṣṭvaitat samasāram akhilaṃ karṣonmitaṃ nyasya tat pronmardyārdhakarañjakāmṛtayutaṃ sāgastikatryūṣaṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: Having ground all this to an even essence, measured by <s>karṣas</s>, and placed it aside, one should thoroughly triturate it with half-measures of karañja and amṛta, together with āgastika and the three pungents.

children.text: bhūdhātrīvijayāsaritpatiphalaṃ jvālāmukhīmārkavaiḥ pratyekaṃ vidadhīta niścalamatiḥ sapta kramād bhāvanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: With bhūdhātrī, vijayā, the fruit of saritpati, jvālāmukhī, and arka, one should perform seven successive impregnations with each, keeping the mind steady.

children.text: pittairatho pañca vidhāya pañcabhiḥ karañjapattrāmṛtadhūpanaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: Then, after making five treatments with the five biles, one should fumigate it with karañja leaves and amṛta.
After giving it ginger juice, the best physician should make a pill in the shape of a grain of rice.

children.text: deyaikā saṃnipāte pratihataviṣaye mohanetraprasuptyoḥ syādgulme sājamodā pavanavikṛtiṣu tryūṣaṇena grahaṇyām
children.translated_text: One pill should be given in <s>saṃnipāta</s>, in loss of response to objects, in delusion, eye disorders, and stupor; with ajamodā it is for abdominal tumors, and with the three pungents for disorders of wind and for <s>grahaṇī</s>.

children.text: dātavyā jīrakeṇa dvipaturaganṛṇāṃ prāṇasaṃrakṣaṇāya kāyāmbhodhir etaṃ rasakasamarasaṃ vaidyanātho'bhyadhatta ||
children.translated_text: It should be given with cumin for the protection of the lives of elephants, horses, and men; <s>Vaidyanātha</s> taught this ocean for the body, a <s>rasa</s> equal in efficacy to rasaka.
Mercury equal to sulfur and mica, triturated with the juice of <s>vārāhī</s>,
should be cooked in a sand-bath apparatus with <s>triphala</s>, <s>vyoṣa</s>, and <s>citraka</s>.
It should be joined with the three alkalis, the five salts, asafoetida, guggulu, and dīpyaka,
together with cumin and indrayava, each mixed separately with an equal amount of its juice.
A dose the size of a <s>māṣa</s> is to be taken with an after-drink of two <s>palas</s> of hot water.
For those suffering from <s>abhinyāsa</s>, loss of digestive fire, <s>grahaṇī</s>, anemia, and abdominal tumors,
it protects life; therefore it is remembered as <s>Prāṇeśvara</s>.
When the disease has increased, this application may be made twice, as approved by physicians.
One should take mercury, iron, <s>vyoṣa</s>, <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, <s>śilā</s>, <s>tāla</s>, mica, and cinnabar,
as well as kumbhī, agni, bhṛṅga, mārī, taṇḍulīyaka, and mākṣika.
These, together with hastiśuṇḍī, are to be in equal parts, while <s>śivā</s> and sulfur are to be half as much.
Having ground them for three days with fresh ginger water, one should place them in a flask and heat them with sand-fire.
One should add the waters or juices of jayā, citron, nirguṇḍī, and cāṅgerī,
cook the preparation for fourteen days, then grind it with ginger juice and dry it.
This <s>rasa</s>, called <s>Mṛtasaṃjīvana</s>, is eaten in a dose of one <s>valla</s>.
The medicine quickly conquers <s>saṃnipāta</s> and all other diseases.
There should be one part of mercury, and sulfur is held to be twice as much.
Poison, orpiment, <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, <s>śilā</s>, cinnabar, and iron,
agni, <s>trikaṭu</s>, the substance called bhṛṅga, gold pyrites, and mica,
hastiśuṇḍī, poison, kumbhī, taṇḍulīyaka, and copper:
taking one part each of these, one should powder them.
One should triturate them for three days with the liquid of ginger.
Citron juice should be taken in the tested measure of three <s>palas</s>,
and of <s>triphala</s> and nirguṇḍī, three <s>palas</s> each.
The juice of cāṅgerī is declared to be in the measure of one <s>pala</s>.
The careful practitioner should place it in a glass flask and set it in the apparatus.
After removing it, one should triturate it with ginger extracts and dry it.
This <s>rasa</s>, known on earth, is named <s>Mṛtasaṃjīvana</s>.
One should give two <s>guñjās</s> of it for the removal of <s>saṃnipāta</s>.

children.text: vaṅgaṃ nāgaṃ ca sūtaṃ ca nepālaṃ gandhakaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Tin, lead, mercury, nepāla, and sulfur,
together with copper and poison in equal parts, should be triturated with fresh juice.
Then it should be triturated again, worked with the juices of nirguṇḍī and cāṅgerī.
Used in a dose of one <s>valla</s>, this <s>rasa</s> removes <s>saṃnipāta</s>.

children.text: gandhakaṃ ca rasaṃ śuddhaṃ pratyekaṃ karṣasammitam
children.translated_text: Sulfur and purified mercury, each measured by one <s>karṣa</s>,

children.text: ekatra kajjalīṃ kṛtvā tataḥ kurvīta golakam ||
children.translated_text: should be made together into a black <s>kajjalī</s>; then one should form a ball.
Putting it into a new vessel, one should cover it with a copper vessel,
seal that vessel firmly, and then set it on the fire.
After no more time than it takes rice grains to crack, one should remove it when it has cooled by itself.
In fresh fever one should use the <s>rasa</s> called <s>Parpaṭikā</s>.
With ginger juice, the physician should administer three <s>vallas</s> for three days,
and cover the fevered patient tightly until sweat arises.
For the person freed from fever, buttermilk-rice is the wholesome diet.
This <s>rasa</s> is called <s>Navajvarāri</s>, the enemy of fresh fever, and is exceedingly rare.
It is considered a general <s>rasa</s>, especially in fever caused by wind.
Borax, mercury, sulfur, and black peppers should be in equal parts.
One should triturate the whole with citron water for three days.
After drying it and mixing it with sugar, one should impregnate it with fish bile.
That <s>rasa</s>, when impregnated for three days with fresh ginger juice, is perfected.

children.text: vallaṃ vāratrayaṃ deyaṃ pānārthaṃ vāri śītalam
children.translated_text: One <s>valla</s> should be given three times; cold water is for drinking.
Buttermilk-rice should be the wholesome diet, together with eggplant fruit.
This <s>Jalamañjarī-rasa</s> destroys all fresh fevers.
One should make ash from vessels of <s>kānta</s> that have apertures at the neck.
Mercury, sulfur, and borax, equal to that, are to be mixed with neem water.
Then, having ground that paste, one should again triturate it for three days.
One should impregnate it with fish bile equal in amount to the mercury.
This <s>Kāntarasa</s>, when perfected, is to be prescribed for a recent fever
by the best physicians, with a dose accompanied by ginger.
Mercury and sulfur, and likewise tin and mica, in equal parts,
should be combined; then mercury equal to the tin should be thoroughly triturated with it.
After uniting the sulfur and mica there, it should be ground with citron water.

children.text: sāmānyaṃ puṭam ādadyāt saptadhā sādhitaṃ rasam ||
children.translated_text: One should apply an ordinary heating; the <s>rasa</s>, processed seven times, is perfected.
Then, having impregnated it seven times with aloe and also with <s>citraka</s>,
one should prescribe it, with jaggery and cumin, in chronic fever.
In cough and dyspnea it is used with aloe and a decoction of <s>triphalā</s>.
It treats madness and <s>dhanurvāta</s> when used with a decoction of <s>amṛtā</s>.
Thus the <s>rasa</s> named <s>Candrodaya</s> removes the heat of diseases.

children.text: nāgaṃ vaṅgaṃ rasaṃ tāmraṃ gandhakaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Lead, tin, mercury, copper, sulfur, and borax,

children.text: viṣaṃ ca nepālaṃ haritālaṃ samaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: and poison, <s>nepāla</s>, and orpiment, likewise in equal quantity,
should all be triturated with the milk of the banyan tree and made into a ball.
That ball should be cooked inside a vessel over a lamp-flame fire.

children.text: taṃ golaṃ śītalaṃ kṛtvā bhṛṅgarājena mardayet
children.translated_text: Having cooled that ball, one should triturate it with <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>.
It should also be triturated again and again with fresh ginger juice.
One should administer pills the size of chickpeas with the juice of fresh ginger.
This, in a dose of two <s>guñjās</s>, removes chronic fever.

children.text: haraśca gandhakaṃ caiva kunaṭī ca samaṃ samam
children.translated_text: <s>Hara</s>, sulfur, and <s>kunaṭī</s> are to be taken in equal quantities.
They should be triturated with the juice of <s>karkoṭikā</s> and prescribed.
It is <s>Navajvaramurāri</s>; one <s>valla</s> is taken with sugar.
The after-drink is the juice of <s>taṇḍulīya</s>, or else with sugar.
In a dose of two <s>guñjās</s>, it forcibly destroys fresh fevers.

children.text: kaṭvamlatīkṣṇalavaṇoṣṇavidāhirūkṣaiḥ pittaṃ praduṣṭam aśanair atisevitais taiḥ
children.translated_text: Pitta, vitiated by excessive, gradual use of pungent, sour, sharp, salty, hot, burning, and dry substances,
corrupts the blood; then, moving through both channels, the blood issues in excess from the sites of the liver and spleen.
Mercury and cinnabar should be combined by means of an upward apparatus.
One part of hen's egg fluid and borax alkali as well,
and likewise one part of sulfur, should be thoroughly triturated with ghee.
Taking the perfected <s>rasa</s>, one should administer it with cumin water.
For three days, in a dose of one <s>māṣa</s>, it conquers <s>grahaṇī</s> and disorders of the blood.
It also destroys fever and burning, and removes <s>raktapitta</s>.
Mercury and copper ash, each in the measure of a <s>tola</s>,

children.text: dināni trīṇi guṭikāṃ kṛtvā cāgnau vinikṣipet ||
children.translated_text: should be made into a pill over three days and placed in the fire.

children.text: tataḥ śuṣkaṃ samādāya punareva ca mardayet
children.translated_text: Then, taking it when dry, one should again triturate it.

children.text: samastaiḥ samagandhaiśca kṛtvā kajjalikāṃ ca taiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Together with all of them and equal sulfur, one should make a black collyrium-like mass from them.
With <s>mustā</s>, pomegranate, <s>dūrvā</s>, <s>ketakī</s>, and breast-water,
with the waters of <s>sahadevī</s>, aloe, and also <s>parpaṭa</s>,
with the waters of <s>rāmaśītalikā</s> and with the juice of <s>śatāvarī</s>,
one should carefully impregnate it separately, day by day.
Bitter <s>guḍūcī</s> starch, <s>parpaṭī</s>, <s>uśīra</s>, and <s>māgadhī</s>,
<s>śṛṅgāṭa</s> and <s>sārivā</s>: an equal, fine powder of these
should be impregnated seven times with a decoction beginning with raisins.
Then, placing it on cloth, one should make pills like chickpeas.
This <s>rasendra</s> is proclaimed under the name <s>Candrakalā</s>.
It destroys all pitta disorders and removes vāta-pitta diseases.
It has great power to destroy severe internal and external burning.
It is especially praised in the summer season and in the autumn season.
It does not cause weakness of digestion, and it removes fever with great heat.
It quickly removes fatigue, fainting, and the heavy bleeding of women.
It also removes upward and downward <s>raktapitta</s>, especially vomiting of blood,
and destroys all difficulties in urination; there is no doubt about this.
Powder of <s>paṭola</s> and iron, with excellent mercury in equal proportion,
rubbed with the group hostile to iron, is the supreme remover of <s>raktapitta</s>.
A man who licks in the morning a <s>karṣa</s> of the fresh juice of <s>vṛṣa</s> leaves, mixed with one <s>guñjā</s> of <s>rasendra</s>, honey, and sugar,
destroys painful, terrible <s>raktapitta</s>.
Together with <s>paṭola</s> and cinnabar, and with honey, it removes <s>raktapitta</s>.

children.text: navanītaṃ sitā lājā drākṣayā saha bhakṣayet ||
children.translated_text: One should eat fresh butter, sugar, parched grain, and raisins together.
And one should apply ghee to the head; it is the supreme remover of <s>raktapitta</s>.
One should drink a decoction combined with raisins and <s>vāsā</s>, impregnated with sugar.
Or the juice of <s>vāsā</s> with sugar and honey, or parched grains with an equal amount of sugar:
by eating these, one afflicted with <s>raktapitta</s> conquers thirst, burning, and fever.
One should eat powder of emblic myrobalan mixed with sugar; it removes <s>raktapitta</s>.

children.text: doṣāḥ śoṣamano'bhitāpakupitāḥ kurvanti kāsaṃ tataḥ pītaṃ pūtikaphaṃ pratīpanayanaḥ pūyopamaṃ ṣṭhīvati
children.translated_text: The doṣas, aggravated by wasting and mental distress, then produce cough; he spits yellow, foul-smelling phlegm, moving in the opposite direction and resembling pus.

children.text: śītoṣṇecchur akāraṇena bahubhuk snigdhaprasannānanaḥ pārśvārtyalpabalakṣayākṛtir api prādurbhavatyanyathā ||
children.translated_text: Desiring cold and heat without cause, eating much, with an unctuous and clear face, and also with pain in the side, little strength, and an appearance of emaciation, it manifests otherwise.
<s>Abhraka</s> with alkali and iron, triturated with the excellent juices of <s>agastya</s>, <s>kāsamarda</s>, and <s>varā</s>,
and worked with sour <s>vetasa</s>, then made into a lump, is a destroyer of cough.
Having put powdered realgar into silver, and four times as much orpiment,
one should triturate it for two praharas with the extracts of <s>vāsā</s> and <s>gokṣura</s>.
When it has been steamed in a sand apparatus, in a dose measuring two <s>guñjās</s>,
it removes cough when joined with powders of <s>trikaṭu</s> and the root of <s>nirguṇḍī</s>.
The essences of earthworm and <s>abhraka</s>, magnetic iron, gold, <s>abhraka</s>, silver,
pearls, gems, <s>tāpya</s>, and also <s>vaikrānta</s>:
all this, reduced to ash separately, is considered to be one <s>māṣa</s> in measure for each,
and likewise pure powder of <s>rājāvarta</s> measuring one <s>niṣka</s>.
Combining all this in equal amount and triturating it with sour <s>vetasa</s>,
one should seal it in the belly of a crucible and blow it in a furnace until an opening appears.
In this way one should blow it a hundred times, after triturating it with sour <s>vetasa</s>.
Then, when this has been powdered, two <s>śāṇas</s> of pearl-ash

children.text: maricaṃ pañca śāṇeyaṃ kṣiptvā saṃmardya yatnataḥ
children.translated_text: and five <s>śāṇas</s> of black pepper should be added, and it should be carefully triturated.
Putting it in an attractive small casket, one should store it thereafter.

children.text: so 'yaṃ ratnakaraṇḍako rasavaro madhvājyasaṃkrāmaṇo hanyācchvāsagadaṃ jvaraṃ grahaṇikāṃ kāsaṃ ca hidhmāmayam
children.translated_text: This excellent <s>rasa</s>, called <s>Ratnakaraṇḍaka</s>, taken with honey and ghee, destroys the disease asthma, fever, <s>grahaṇikā</s>, cough, and hiccup disease.

children.text: śūlaṃ śoṣamahodaraṃ bahuvidhaṃ kuṣṭhaṃ ca hanyād gadān balyo vṛṣyakaraḥ pradīpanatamaḥ svasthocito vegavān ||
children.translated_text: It destroys colic, consumption, ascites, many kinds of skin disease, and other diseases; it is strengthening, aphrodisiac, extremely kindling, fit for the healthy, and swift-acting.
One part of purified <s>sūta</s> (mercury), one part of purified sulfur,
three parts of incinerated copper, and five parts of black pepper,
four parts of incinerated <s>abhraka</s>, and one part of poison should be added,
together with one part of <s>bhūtāṅkuśa</s>; all of it should be triturated with a sour liquid.
For one <s>yāma</s>: this preparation, named <s>Bhūtāṅkuśa</s>, in a dose of one <s>māṣa</s>, conquers vāta-type cough.
As the after-drink, one should lick the rind of the <s>vibhītaka</s> fruit with honey.
It destroys pitta-type cough, anorexia, asthma, and wasting cough.

children.text: rasabhasma viṣaṃ tulyaṃ gandhakaṃ dviguṇaṃ matam
children.translated_text: Ash of <s>rasa</s> and poison are equal; sulfur is considered double.
<s>Bola</s>, orpiment, <s>vāhlīka</s>, <s>karkoṭī</s>, <s>mākṣika</s>, and turmeric,
<s>kaṇṭakārī</s>, barley-alkali, <s>lāṅgalī</s> alkali, and rock salt,
and extract of licorice should be powdered and mixed for seven days with ginger juices.
For removing phlegmatic cough, one should eat a pill the size of a jujube fruit.
This <s>rasa</s>, bound with <s>bola</s>, conquers asthma and pallor.
<s>Rasa</s>, sulfur, long pepper, <s>harītakī</s>, <s>akṣa</s>, and <s>vāsaka</s>,
made into powder in six-plus-increasing proportions and impregnated with a decoction of <s>babbula</s>,
should be dried and powdered after twenty-one treatments.

children.text: bhakṣayenmadhunā hanti kāsam agniraso hy ayam ||
children.translated_text: One should eat it with honey; this is indeed <s>Agnirasa</s>, and it destroys cough.
<s>Trikaṭu</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, cardamom, nutmeg, and cloves:
of these, in equal parts, the preceding <s>rasa</s> should be present in an equal amount.
One should fill and stir it in honey; it is to be eaten two <s>niṣkas</s> at a time.
Named <s>Svayamagnirasa</s>, it cuts off wasting cough.
The leaves of <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>, powdered with honey,
should be held as a ball in the mouth for calming obstruction caused by cough.

children.text: arkairaṇḍasya pattrāṇāṃ rasaṃ pītvā ca kāsajit ||
children.translated_text: By drinking the juice of the leaves of <s>arka</s> and castor, one conquers cough.

children.text: dantīmūlasya dhūmaṃ vā nirguṇḍyā vā pibejjayet ||
children.translated_text: Or one should inhale the smoke of <s>dantī</s> root, or of <s>nirguṇḍī</s>; he will conquer it.
One afflicted by wasting cough should eat the root of <s>indravāruṇikā</s>
together with <s>bhṛṅgī</s> and black sesame, in a dose of one <s>niṣka</s>, for relief.

children.text: śleṣmoparuddhamanaḥ pavano 'tiduṣṭaḥ saṃdūṣayannanu jalānnavahāś ca nāḍīḥ
children.translated_text: The wind, obstructed by phlegm and extremely vitiated, corrupts in turn the channels that carry water and food.

children.text: āmāśayodbhavam imaṃ vidadhāty urasthaḥ śvāsaṃ ca vakragamano hi śarīrabhājām ||
children.translated_text: Situated in the chest, moving crookedly, it produces this asthma, arising from the stomach, in embodied beings.
Root of <s>indravāruṇikā</s>, <s>devadāru</s>, and the three pungents,
mixed with sugar, should be eaten for the calming of upward asthma.
Half a part of <s>sūta</s> and sulfur should be triturated for one <s>yāma</s> with aloe juices.
A copper sheet equal to the two should be combined with the preceding paste.
Having cooked it for one day in a pot apparatus, one should take it out and powder it.

children.text: sūryāvartaraso hy eṣa dviguñjaḥ śvāsajit bhavet ||
children.translated_text: This is <s>Sūryāvartarasa</s>; two <s>guñjās</s> of it conquers asthma.

children.text: sūtaḥ ṣoḍaśa tatsamo dinakarastasyārdhabhāgo baliḥ sindhustasya samaḥ susūkṣmamṛditaḥ ṣaṭ pippalī cūrṇitaḥ
children.translated_text: Mercury is sixteen parts; <s>dinakara</s> is equal to that; <s>bali</s> is half of that, and <s>sindhu</s> is equal to it, all rubbed very fine, with six powdered long peppers.

children.text: jambīrasvarasena marditam idaṃ taptaṃ supakvaṃ bhavet kāsaśvāsasagulmaśūlajaṭharaṃ pāṇḍuṃ lihannāśayet ||
children.translated_text: Triturated with citron juice and heated until well cooked, this, when licked, destroys cough, asthma, abdominal tumor, colic, abdominal swelling, and pallor.

children.text: sādhāraṇaṃ tu vaṭakaṃ vakṣyāmi śṛṇu tattvataḥ
children.translated_text: Now I shall tell the general pill; listen according to the truth.

children.text: pāradaṃ gandhakaṃ caiva palamekaṃ pṛthak pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: Mercury and sulfur, one <s>pala</s> each, separately,
three <s>palas</s> of <s>trikaṭu</s>, and one <s>pala</s> of tin should be added.

children.text: sarvam ekatra saṃyojya dināni trīṇi mardayet ||
children.translated_text: Combining everything together, one should triturate it for three days.
Then for three days one should triturate it with cow urine.
One should make pills of <s>akṣa</s> measure and dry them in the shade.

children.text: nityamekaṃ tu vaṭakaṃ dināni triṃśadeva ca
children.translated_text: One pill should be taken daily for thirty days exactly.
It removes asthma, cough, and fever, and drives away weak digestion and anorexia.
There should be one part of <s>rasa</s>; sulfur is considered twice as much.
Long pepper should be taken in three parts, and <s>harītakī</s> in four parts.
<s>Vibhītaka</s> is five parts, while <s>vāsā</s> should be sixfold.
<s>Bhārṅgī</s> should be taken sevenfold; all of it should be prepared as a powder.
Taking a decoction of <s>babbula</s>, one should impregnate it twenty-one times.
With honey, one should form a pill in the measure of a <s>vibhītaka</s> fruit.
One should eat one each morning; the pill is called <s>Saptāmṛtā</s>.
This remedy would destroy disease such as dyspnea and cough at once.

children.text: sūtaṃ śulbaṃ sulohaṃ balim amṛtayutaṃ tritrikaṃ reṇukābdaṃ gaṇḍīraṃ kesarāgniṃ dviguṇaguḍayutaṃ mardayitvā samastam
children.translated_text: Mercury, copper, good iron, sulfur joined with <s>amṛtā</s>, <s>tritrika</s>, <s>reṇukā</s> and <s>abda</s>, <s>gaṇḍīra</s>, saffron and <s>agni</s>, all mixed with twice as much jaggery, should be triturated together.

children.text: kuryāt kolāsthimātrān suruciravaṭakān bhakṣayet prāgdinādau pathyāsīsarvarogān harati ca nitarāṃ nīlakaṇṭhābhidhānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One should make attractive pills the size of a kola-stone and eat them early at the beginning of the day while taking wholesome food; the preparation called <s>Nīlakaṇṭha</s> thoroughly removes all diseases.
A paste of silver, copper, and mercury, together with realgar, sulfur, and orpiment in equal shares, is to be worked with juices.
Triturate it with juices produced from <s>āṭarūṣa</s>, <s>surasā</s>, and fresh substances, and then make a pellet.

children.text: mṛtsnayā ca pariveṣṭya golakaṃ yāmayugmam atha bhūdhare pacet
children.translated_text: Having enclosed the pellet with clay, one should cook it for two yāmas in a <s>bhūdhara</s> furnace.

children.text: gandhakena kuru tatsamaṃ tataś cāṭarūṣakaṭukair vibhāvayet ||
children.translated_text: Then make it equal with sulfur and afterward impregnate it with <s>āṭarūṣa</s> and pungent substances.
The wise man should take the <s>rasa</s> called <s>Karikesarī</s> for dyspnea and cough, in a <s>valla</s> measure.
Mercury, sulfur, copper, mica, <s>kaṇā</s>, dry ginger, and black pepper are taken in equal parts.

children.text: bhūtam ekaṃ viṣaṃ caikaṃ sūryaḥ kāsādināśanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With one part of <s>bhūta</s> and one part of poison, the preparation called <s>Sūrya</s> destroys cough and related conditions.
One should drink sulfur and black pepper with ghee; it removes dyspnea and kapha.

children.text: śilā hiṅgu viḍaṅgaṃ ca maricaṃ kuṣṭhasaindhavam
children.translated_text: Realgar, asafoetida, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, black pepper, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, and rock salt
should be licked in a karṣa dose with honey and ghee; it removes dyspnea, cough, and kapha.
By foods that are burning, heavy, obstructive, dry, and clogging,
by cold drinks, foods, and places, and by dust, smoke, heat, and wind,
by exercise, labor, carrying loads, travel, suppression of urges, and undernourishment,
hiccup, dyspnea, and cough arise among people.
Mercury, sulfur, <s>dhānya</s>, mica, orpiment, <s>tāpya</s>, and <s>opala</s>, successively,
are increased by parts and combined with <s>vacā</s>, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, turmeric, alkali, and <s>citraka</s>.
Together with <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>lāṅgalī</s>, <s>vyoṣa</s>, rock salt, <s>akṣa</s>, and poison in equal amounts,
when impregnated with the juice of <s>bhṛṅga</s>, it removes hiccup, hoarseness, and cough.

children.text: pakvatāmre rasaḥ piṣṭo balinā hidhmināṃ hitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Mercury ground with cooked copper and sulfur is beneficial for those suffering from hiccup.
Having placed the powder of <s>pāṭhā</s> and <s>indravāruṇī</s> in a vessel, then <s>kunaṭī</s>
and purified mercury should be put on its surface, along with a share of <s>kunaṭī</s>.
The powder of <s>kunaṭī</s> should be half the mercury, and the powder of the preceding roots half of that.
After putting in the powder, one should cook it on a stove for eight yāmas with a gentle fire.

children.text: śilāpūto raso nāma hanti hikkāṃ triguñjakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>rasa</s> named <s>Śilāpūta</s>, in a three-guñjā dose, destroys hiccup.
Calcined mercury, calcined copper, asafoetida, and <s>puṣkara</s>-root,

children.text: saindhavaṃ gandhakaṃ tālaṃ kaṭukaṃ cūrṇayet samān ||
children.translated_text: rock salt, sulfur, orpiment, and <s>kaṭuka</s> should be powdered in equal parts.
With the liquids of <s>devadālī</s> and <s>punarnavā</s>, of <s>nirguṇḍī</s> and <s>meghanāda</s>,
and with the juices of bitter <s>koṣātakī</s>, one should triturate it firmly for one day.
One should lick the <s>rasa</s> called <s>Manthānabhairava</s>, in a māṣa measure, with honey.
Afterward, for the calming of kapha diseases, one should drink a decoction of neem.

children.text: viśvāditrikanirgatadravaniśā kīrapriyotthaṃ dalaṃ nīlagrīvagalālayaṃ surapates tārtīyanetrābhidham
children.translated_text: The liquid extracted from the triad beginning with <s>viśvā</s>, turmeric, the leaf produced by <s>kīrapriya</s>, that which dwells in the throat of the blue-necked one, and the substance called the third eye of the lord of the gods,

children.text: vidvatpuñjavatī kṛmipratibhaṭaṃ nirguṇḍikāvāriṇā tulyāṃśāś caṇakapramāṇavaṭikāḥ saśvāsakāsaghnikāḥ ||
children.translated_text: together with <s>vidvatpuñjavatī</s>, the foe of worms, and <s>nirguṇḍī</s> water, all in equal portions, makes chickpea-sized pills that destroy dyspnea and cough.
One should give a decoction of <s>rāsnā</s>, <s>bṛhatī</s>, <s>agni</s>, <s>balā</s>, and milk to drink.
One should make a hiccuping patient inhale smoke from leaves produced by <s>śikhinī</s>.

children.text: karṣaikaṃ gandhakaṃ śuddhaṃ ghṛtaiś coṣṇodakaiḥ pibet
children.translated_text: One karṣa of purified sulfur should be drunk with ghee and hot water.

children.text: kaphaṃ hantyatha vā kṣaudraiḥ pañcavaktrarasaḥ khalu ||
children.translated_text: It destroys kapha; alternatively, <s>Pañcavaktra-rasa</s> should indeed be taken with honey.
Through very loud speaking, poison, excessive recitation, injury, and corrupting causes, vāta and the other doṣas become aggravated.

children.text: srotaḥsu te svaravaheṣu gatāḥ pratiṣṭhāṃ hanyuḥ svaraṃ bhavati cāpi hi ṣaḍvidhaḥ saḥ ||
children.translated_text: When they have gone and become established in the channels that carry the voice, they destroy the voice; that condition is also sixfold.
Having triturated mercury with twice as much sulfur, together with <s>bhṛṅga</s>,
and melted it in an iron vessel smeared with ghee by a jujube-wood fire,

children.text: ūrdhvādho gomayaṃ dattvā kadalyāḥ komale dale
children.translated_text: placing cow-dung fuel above and below, on a tender leaf of plantain,
one should bring it, with a greased iron ladle, to the form of a flaky <s>parpaṭa</s>.
Placed in an iron vessel, it becomes <s>Lohaparpaṭikā</s>.
Placed in a copper vessel, it becomes <s>Tāmraparpaṭikā</s>.
One should add a quarter-part of poison in the diseases that are treatable by it,
with the liquids of <s>surasā</s> and <s>jayantī</s>, and of <s>kanyakā</s> and <s>āṭarūṣaka</s>,
of <s>triphala</s>, <s>muni</s>, <s>bhārṅgī</s>, <s>muṇḍī</s>, <s>trikaṭu</s>, and <s>citraka</s>,
and of <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> and <s>vahni</s>; it is impregnated with liquid day by day.
Again one should impregnate it seven times with ginger juice.
One should warm the excellent <s>parpaṭa-rasa</s> slightly over coals.
One should give eight guñjās of it into the mouth, joined with betel leaf,
and afterward give a decoction of ten <s>pippalīs</s> and <s>nirguṇḍī</s> to drink.

children.text: svarabhaṅge kaphe śvāse prayojyaḥ sarvadā rasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This <s>rasa</s> is always to be used in loss of voice, kapha, and dyspnea.
One should crush the roots of <s>trikaṇṭaka</s> and dry ginger and place them
in goat's milk together with half as much water, and boil until only the milk remains.
That milk should be given to drink at night, with <s>kaṇā</s>, and also at meal-time.
One should avoid pumpkin, tamarind, eggplant, and cucumber,

children.text: āranālaṃ ca tailaṃ ca saṃsargaṃ ca vivarjayet
children.translated_text: as well as sour gruel, oil, and sexual intercourse.
One should follow this for three months for the cessation of cough and dyspnea.
With cumin, asafoetida, and <s>vyoṣa</s>, the <s>rasa</s> calms <s>grahaṇī</s>.
With water of <s>daśamūla</s> it calms vāta fever, and with <s>trikaṭu</s> it calms kapha fever.
It calms fever with the essence of <s>madhuka</s>, and fever arising from all doṣas with <s>pañcakola</s>.
It calms consumption with honey and <s>pippalī</s>, and rectal sprouts with cow urine.
It calms colic with castor oil, and pallor and swelling when accompanied by <s>guggulu</s>.
[It treats] skin diseases with <s>bhṛṅga</s>, <s>bhallātaka</s>, <s>vākucī</s>, and the five kinds of neem.
Through combination with seeds of <s>dhattūra</s>, it destroys urinary disease and insanity.
It quickly destroys epilepsy when used together with <s>vyoṣa</s> and neem leaves.
This <s>rasa</s> is especially beneficial for suckling infants.
According to the use of powders such as <s>pathyā</s> and <s>akṣa</s>, it also overcomes other very difficult diseases.
One should administer <s>Parpaṭīrasa</s> with nutmeg and cold water.
In indigestion arising from pitta, his head should also be sprinkled with cold water.
For a patient with kapha, one should use nasal medication, expectoration, pungent fumigation, vomiting, and purgation.
The food should be dry, scanty, sharp, hot, pungent, bitter, and astringent.
For a kapha patient, one should also prescribe wine that has stood for a long time.
Weak digestive fire, fever, chilliness, and vomiting of blood and pus,
together with loss of vitality and weakness, are the symptoms of <s>rājaroga</s>.
One should prepare gold ash in a quantity equal to that of the <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: tālakaṃ gandhakaṃ tutthaṃ mākṣikaṃ rasakaṃ śilām ||
children.translated_text: Orpiment, sulfur, blue vitriol, pyrites, zinc ore, and realgar,
should be added in equality with the <s>rasa</s>; the blue vitriol should be put in after being calcined.
Thus calcined in fire, it is the excellent blue-vitriol preparation called <s>Mayūrakatuttha</s>.

children.text: kiṃciṭ ṭaṅkaṇakaṃ dattvā mārjārasya viśā yutam
children.translated_text: After adding a little borax, together with the poison of a cat,

children.text: prathamaṃ puṭayed dadhnā dvitīyaṃ madhunā saha ||
children.translated_text: one should give the first heating with curds and the second together with honey.
First one should purify the orpiment by cooking it in alkali of white gourd.

children.text: taile pacettataḥ samyak cūrṇe vā pariśodhayet ||
children.translated_text: Then it should be cooked thoroughly in oil, or else purified in powdered form.
One should purify sulfur in milk, and zinc ore with human urine.
Pyrites, mixed with salt, should be cooked in citron juice.
The realgar, ground with the liquid of <s>jayantī</s>, should be cooked there as well.
After combining everything, one should triturate it with the latex of <s>arka</s>.
With <s>jayantī</s>, <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>, <s>vāsā</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>kṛśānu</s>,
and also with <s>agasti</s> and <s>lāṅgalī</s>, one by one, for a day each, slowly.
Then, having bound it into a ball, one should cook it in the manner previously taught.
After that, having powdered it well, one should impregnate it with ginger water.
Seven times with extracts of <s>vyoṣa</s>: this <s>rasa</s> is <s>Kanakasundara</s>.
A dose of two or three <s>guñjās</s> of it is for removing <s>rājayakṣmā</s>.
With honey and long peppers, or with black peppers mixed with ghee,
the physician, knowing the distinctions of strength and condition, should have the patient lick it.
Or, with powders of <s>jayapāla</s> and with dry ginger anointed with cow ghee,

children.text: dadīta śūline prājño gulmine ca viśeṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: the wise physician should give it to one suffering from colic, and especially to one with an abdominal tumor.

children.text: kādivarjyaṃ caretpathyaṃ hṛdyaṃ balyaṃ ca pūrvavat
children.translated_text: Avoiding the unsuitable items beginning with the ka-class, he should follow a wholesome, agreeable, and strengthening regimen, as before.
In <s>saṃnipāta</s>, one should give this medicine mixed with ginger juice.
Excellent <s>guggulu</s>, processed with decoctions of <s>guḍūcī</s> and <s>triphalā</s>,
three parts of calcined <s>rasa</s> and one part of gold ash,
one part of dead copper, and purified realgar, sulfur, and orpiment,
two parts each: having combined them, one should powder them finely.
One should fill cowries with that; borax should be ground with goat's milk.

children.text: piṣṭvā tena mukhaṃ ruddhvā mṛdbhāṇḍe tannirodhayet
children.translated_text: After sealing the mouth with that, one should enclose it in an earthen vessel.
It should be cooked, purified, in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>; when cooled by itself, it should be powdered.
This <s>rasa</s>, called <s>Rājamṛgāṅka</s>, in a dose of four <s>guñjās</s>, removes wasting disease.
With ten long peppers, honey, and nineteen black peppers,
together with ghee, the physician should administer it to pacify the king of diseases.
One <s>niṣka</s> of conch-shell rings and four <s>niṣkas</s> of cowries,
half a <s>niṣka</s> of blue vitriol, and sulfur equal to all of them,

children.text: gandhatulyaṃ mṛtaṃ nāgaṃ nāgatulyaṃ mṛtaṃ rasam
children.translated_text: dead lead equal to the sulfur, and dead mercury equal to the lead,
with borax equal to the mercury, should be triturated and cooked like <s>Mṛgāṅka</s>.
This remover of <s>rājayakṣmā</s> is known by the name <s>Śaṅkheśvara</s>.
One should grind sixteen <s>niṣkas</s> of conch navel with cow's milk.
A crucible should be made from that; in its middle, calcined mercury
and three parts of sulfur, reduced to powder, should be placed, half a <s>niṣka</s> in measure.
After sealing it, one should wrap it in cloth and smear clay on the outside.
It should be dried, cooked in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>, and powdered together with the crucible.
With a dose of one <s>guñjā</s> and the proper vehicle, it destroys wasting disease like <s>Mṛgāṅka</s>.
Two <s>niṣkas</s> of the ash of mercury, one <s>niṣka</s> of gold ash,
and two <s>niṣkas</s> of purified sulfur should be powdered with juices of <s>citraka</s>.
After two <s>yāmas</s>, when it has dried, cowries should then be filled with it.
The cowries should be sealed in an earthen vessel and cooked in a <s>gajapuṭa</s>.
When cooled by itself, it should then be pulverized as a pouch containing gold.
Eaten like <s>Mṛgāṅka</s> in a dose of four <s>guñjās</s>, it removes <s>rājayakṣman</s>.
One should take three <s>niṣkas</s> of <s>Svayamagnirasa</s>; it removes <s>rājayakṣman</s>.
The ashes of mercury, mica, and iron, together with equal parts of <s>śilājatu</s> and poison,
and likewise <s>guggulu</s> processed with decoctions of <s>guḍūcī</s> and <s>triphalā</s>,
and dead Nepalese copper should be used in place of mercury.
Having combined that, one should take two <s>guñjās</s>; it removes <s>rājayakṣman</s>.
It is called <s>Pañcāmṛtarasa</s>, and its vehicle is as stated before.
With <s>kṣīrā</s> and <s>ajagandhā</s>, or with <s>jayantī</s>, it removes wasting disease.

children.text: tulyaṃ pāradagandhakaṃ trikaṭukaṃ tābhyāṃ rajaḥ kambujaṃ taistulyaṃ ca bhavetkapardabhasitaṃ syātpāradāṭṭaṅkaṇam
children.translated_text: Mercury, sulfur, and <s>trikaṭu</s> should be equal; shell powder should equal those, and cowrie ash should equal them, with borax measured from the mercury.

children.text: pādāṃśaṃ sakalaiḥ samānamaricaṃ lihyātkramātsājyakaṃ yāvanniṣkamitaṃ bhavetpratidinaṃ māsātkṣayaḥ śāmyati ||
children.translated_text: Black pepper, a quarter part and equal to the whole mixture, should be licked gradually with ghee until the daily dose reaches a <s>niṣka</s>; within a month, wasting disease subsides.
With the ash of the <s>rasa</s>, one should prepare gold in a quarter portion.
Having added twice as much sulfur, one should triturate it with the liquid of <s>citraka</s>.
After filling it into the mouth of a <s>carācara</s> vessel, and closing it with borax,
one should place it in a vessel smeared with powder, and then seal it with clay.
After drying it, one should heat it in a pit a ratni deep in the afternoon.
When it has cooled of itself, one should take it out, powder it, and then set it aside.
This is named <s>Lokeśvara</s>; it increases nourishment and virility.
A dose of four <s>guñjās</s>, with ghee and combined with peppers,
should be eaten with supreme devotion to <s>Lokeśa</s>, O all-seeing one.
In emaciation of the limbs and weak digestion, this <s>rasa</s> is for cough and hiccup.
It should be administered for three days with peppers joined with ghee.
There one should avoid salt; the food should be with ghee and with curds.
For twenty-one days one should drink pepper together with ghee.
The prescribed diet should be given as in the case of <s>Mṛgāṅka</s>; one should lie with the feet extended upward.
But when vomiting has begun, one should bring the liquid of <s>guḍūcī</s>.
One should make him drink it together with honey, and should feed him roasted eggplant.
He should bathe with cool water, and a stream should be poured on the head.
But when a disorder of phlegm has arisen, one should bring banana fruit.
Having fried it together with peppers, one should feed it to him for the removal of phlegm.
Or ginger mixed with honey, or else ginger with jaggery, may be given.
Having fried coriander and hulled black gram, one should then powder them.
Mixed with sugar and ghee, they should be given for the calming of anorexia.

children.text: bhṛṣṭvā kustumbarīṃ samyag ghṛte śarkarayā pibet
children.translated_text: Having fried coriander properly in ghee, one should drink it with sugar,
together with cardamom and pepper, until the vomiting subsides.

children.text: ajamodaṃ viḍaṅgaṃ ca piṣṭvā takreṇa pāyayet
children.translated_text: One should grind <s>ajamodā</s> and <s>viḍaṅga</s> and make him drink them with buttermilk,
for the calming of an aggravation of worms, or else a decoction of <s>vātaghna</s> and <s>musta</s>.

children.text: saṃskṛtya dugdhikāṃ vahnau vireke ca prayojayet
children.translated_text: After preparing <s>dugdhikā</s> over the fire, one should employ it when there is purgation.
Slightly roasting the powder of <s>jayā</s>, one should make him eat it with honey at night.
When there is piercing pain in the limbs, the physician should rub the limbs with ghee and, with warm water,
bathe the patient, while recollecting the <s>Lokanātha</s> <s>rasa</s>.
One <s>niṣka</s> of a conch bangle, four <s>niṣkas</s> of cowries,
one <s>karṣa</s> each of blue vitriol, orpiment, sulfur-stone, and borax,
and half as much blue vitriol and <s>nāgarasa</s>, each in <s>niṣka</s> measure, should be heated as before.
The cowrie powder should be cooked in a coating prepared with <s>maṇḍūra</s>.
Half a <s>māṣa</s> of this, half a <s>māṣa</s> of pepper, and material impregnated with the juice of betel vine,
smeared on that leaf, should be licked with honey, or with fresh butter, or with ghee.

children.text: nāḍīmārge nirgate cālpamalpaṃ pathyaṃ bhojyaṃ lokanāthopadiṣṭam
children.translated_text: When it has passed out through the channel little by little, wholesome food prescribed for <s>Lokanātha</s> should be eaten.

children.text: yāme yāme caivam ā maṇḍalāntāt siddhaṃ sadyaḥ śoṣajidvaidyanāthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this way at every <s>yāma</s> until the end of the <s>maṇḍala</s>, <s>Vaidyanātha</s>, successful at once, conquers wasting disease.
The portions of <s>rasa</s> and blue vitriol are one and a half <s>niṣkas</s> each, separately, with a <s>karṣa</s> each of sulfur and borax.

children.text: śaṃkhasya karṣaṃ mṛtatāmrato dvau varāṭikānāṃ nava sampuṭasthān ||
children.translated_text: There is a <s>karṣa</s> of conch, two from incinerated copper, and nine cowries placed in a covered crucible.
Having cooked them, one should cook them again, moistened with the juice of <s>arka</s> leaves, with half a portion of dung-cakes.

children.text: asyārdhapādaṃ maricārdhabhāgaṃ gandhāśmaniṣkaṃ ca ghṛtena lihyāt ||
children.translated_text: One should lick half a quarter of this, half a portion of pepper, and one <s>niṣka</s> of sulfur-stone with ghee.
One should eat the prescribed diet as before for twenty-one days.
Named <s>Lokanātharasa</s>, it cuts down the king of diseases.
Iron powder measuring twenty <s>niṣkas</s>, impregnated with an <s>āḍhaka</s> of <s>bhṛṅga</s> juice,
moistened with the juices of <s>dhattūra</s>, <s>bhārṅgī</s>, and <s>triphalā</s>, with an equal part of <s>tāpya</s>, should be well cooked in heating pits.
