children.text: sūtaṃ ca niṣkaṃ samabhāgatutthaṃ gandhopalau dvau caturo varāṭān
children.translated_text: One <s>niṣka</s> of mercury, an equal amount of blue vitriol, two of sulfur-stone, and four cowries,
should be cooked in a heating fire together with the iron powder, and then cooked mixed with the previous juices.
In this powder there should be seven peppers and ten each of blue vitriol and borax.
One should combine these, each in separate <s>niṣkas</s>; it is taught as the preparation called <s>Prāṇanātha</s>.
Half a quarter of the <s>rasa</s> should be eaten by those suffering specifically from royal consumption,
and by those afflicted with wasting disease, abdominal disease, piles, <s>grahaṇī</s>, fever, abdominal tumors, and the like.
A <s>karṣa</s> of the essence of <s>kharpara</s>, after six months, in melted gold,
and six <s>niṣkas</s> of mercury inserted into eight <s>niṣkas</s> of sulfur-stone,
together with powder of coral and pearls in equal parts with gold,
and, in order, two, three, and four <s>niṣkas</s> of incinerated iron, lead, and <s>bhāskara</s>,
should be triturated for three <s>yāmas</s> with the sour juice of <s>cāṅgerī</s> and powdered separately.
Two <s>niṣkas</s> each should be taken from <s>nīlavaṭaka</s>, <s>vyoma</s>, lodestone, and orpiment,
and four each from <s>aṅkolla</s> seed, <s>kaṅguṇī</s> seed, and blue vitriol,
as well as eight from borax-alkali and twenty from cowries.
One should grind it with two <s>prasthas</s> of the juice of great citron.
This, placed in eight earthen dishes, is to be purified with a <s>khārī</s> of husk,
and cooked in a load of dung-cakes; then two <s>māṣas</s> of it,
with a quarter as much sulfur and also an equal amount of impregnated pepper,
should be stirred with honey and licked, smeared on a betel leaf.
When one <s>ghaṭikā</s> has passed after it, he should eat wholesome food at every <s>yāma</s>.
Otherwise, the digestive fire, once kindled, digests the bodily constituents in a moment.
Having taken this for one day, one should abandon the prohibited things throughout a <s>maṇḍala</s>.

children.text: tataḥ paraṃ yatheṣṭāśī dvādaśābdaṃ sukhī bhavet
children.translated_text: After that, eating as one wishes, one will be happy for twelve years.

children.text: ekamekaṃ dinaṃ bhuktvā varṣe varṣe mahārasam ||
children.translated_text: Having taken the great <s>rasa</s> for one day each year,

children.text: varṣādau ca tyajettyājyaṃ dvādaśābdaṃ jarāṃ jayet
children.translated_text: and having abandoned the prohibited things at the beginning of the year, one conquers old age for twelve years.
This is named <s>Vajrarasa</s>; it splits the mountain of wasting disease.

children.text: niṣkau dvau tutthabhāgasya rasād ekaṃ susaṃskṛtāt
children.translated_text: Two <s>niṣkas</s> of the portion of blue vitriol, and one of well-prepared <s>rasa</s>,
Two <s>niṣkas</s> of poison, one <s>karṣa</s> portion of sharp iron, and sulfur and pearl should be taken.
With the juices of <s>agniparṇī</s>, <s>harilatā</s>, <s>bhṛṅga</s>, fresh ginger, and <s>surasā</s>,
it should be triturated and cooked in a sealed crucible smeared with the bulb of <s>lāṅgalī</s>.

children.text: ardhapādaṃ ca poṭalyāḥ kākinyau dve viṣasya ca
children.translated_text: One half-quarter of the packet, and two <s>kākinīs</s> of poison,
should be licked with powdered pepper and honey, in the same amount as the packet.
For those suffering from consumption, <s>grahaṇī</s>, diarrhea, weakness of digestive fire, cough,
pallor, and abdominal tumors, this excellent beneficial <s>rasa</s> is called <s>Mahāvīra</s>.
In one who is excessively obese, or who has pus, blood, or phlegm not vomited out, or in wasting,
one should not prescribe milk and meat soups, because they are contrary in procedure and principle.
The roots of citron, powdered parched grain, and rock salt,
mixed with long pepper and honey, should be eaten for calming vomiting.
Turmeric, conch-shell, and betel-nut, one <s>niṣka</s> each, remove vomiting.
Or one should drink half a <s>niṣka</s> of borax with the juices of <s>kākamācī</s>.
Or one should drink or eat <s>sugandhā</s>, for the calming of every kind of vomiting.
The juice of lac with honey is supreme for removing vomiting of blood.
Orpiment, pyrite, and <s>svarṇamākṣika</s>, combined with a paste of sulfur,
and properly brought to the state of ash, prevents thirst and vomiting.
<s>Rājāvarta</s>, <s>rasa</s>, copper, and pyrite, cooked in ghee,
mixed with honey, ghee, and sugar, destroys all disorders from intoxication.
<s>Rājāvarta</s>, <s>rasa</s>, and copper, placed within mercury,
rubbed with the juices of licorice and cooked in ghee,
mixed with honey, ghee, and sugar, destroys all disorders from intoxication.
Gold, silver, copper, essence of mica, and magnetic iron,
all these in successively increasing quantities, and lead and tin, each in a <s>śāṇa</s> measure,
should all be melted together; after causing them to flow, one should then proceed.
One <s>pala</s> each of sulfur and realgar should be set apart.
Putting everything into a mortar, one should triturate it with the sour group.

children.text: tāpyaṃ nīlāñjanaṃ tālaṃ śilāgandhaṃ ca cūrṇitam ||
children.translated_text: Heated pyrite, blue vitriol, orpiment, realgar, and sulfur should be powdered.
Adding them again and again, one should heat it in a closed firing until twenty times have been completed.
With mercury twice the quantity of the metal, and then with sulfur twice that amount,

children.text: vidhāya kajjalīṃ ślakṣṇāṃ kṣiptvā tāṃ lohapātrake
children.translated_text: one should make a smooth black sulfide paste, put it into an iron vessel,
and melt it with gentle jujube-charcoal embers; then one should add
the ash of the five metals beginning with gold, and stir it around.
Then he should place that on a plantain leaf set on cow dung.
Covering it with another leaf, he should carefully make it into a thin parpaṭī cake.
Immediately he should put only a little cow dung over it.

children.text: svataḥ śītaṃ samāhṛtya paṭacūrṇaṃ vidhāya ca
children.translated_text: When it has cooled by itself, he should collect it and make it into cloth-filtered powder.
After that he should put it into a small ladle with its handle turned upward.
As before, he should melt it slowly with gentle jujube-charcoal embers.
An equal amount of orpiment, realgar, and sulfur, half a <s>pala</s>, impregnated with poison,
should be made equal to the previous parpaṭī, and from it a little should be added again and again.
He should digest it in the ladle in such a way that the parpaṭī is not burnt.
The <s>palikā</s> is defined as a small apparatus for adding oily substances.
When the powders such as orpiment have been digested, cloth-filtered powder should be made.
With the roots of <s>pūtīkarañja</s>, <s>ṣaṭkola</s>, <s>vyāghrī</s>, and <s>saubhāñjana</s>,
a decoction should be made from five <s>palas</s> of these, reduced until one sixteenth remains.

children.text: tena kvāthena saṃsvedya śoṣayetsaptadhā hi tām
children.translated_text: With that decoction one should steam it and dry it seven times.
With juices produced from the fruits of <s>viṣatindu</s> and with juices of <s>nirguṇḍikā</s>,
after impregnating it, putting it into the ladle, and using a jujube fire,
one should make it sweat slightly and set it aside with very great care.
This, taught by <s>Bhairavanātha</s>, is <s>Pañcāmṛtaparpaṭī</s>.
Licked with the three pungents and ghee, in a dose equal to a <s>guñjā</s> seed,
it destroys the disease of consumption, even when complete with all its symptoms.
It destroys asthma, cough, cholera, diabetes, and abdominal disease,
anorexia that is hard to cure, salivation, and vomiting arising from the heart,
all anal diseases of every origin, and colic and skin diseases without remainder,
vāta fever, constipation, <s>grahaṇī</s>, and diseases born of phlegm,
and other great diseases arising from one doṣa, two doṣas together, or all three doṣas.
This parpaṭī certainly destroys especially weakness of digestion.
Thus it should be combined and administered in diseases by the best physicians,
with the appropriate disease-destroying combinations and with the appropriate after-drinks for each disease.
<s>Pañcāmṛtaparpaṭī</s> becomes destructive of all diseases beginning with consumption.
One should avoid sesame, mustard, bilva, sour substances, bitter gourd, and safflower,
as well as pigeon meat, eggplant, and chicken.
Skin-tags arise outside or inside the anus.
They produce all diseases in men and are known as <s>arśas</s>.
Among them, those that discharge blood are declared to be pitta-born.
Those born of vāta arise with helplessness and produce upward movement of wind.
Those born of phlegm cause swelling, while those born of all three doṣas produce all symptoms.
One <s>pala</s> of purified mercury and two <s>palas</s> of purified sulfur,

children.text: mṛtaṃ tāmraṃ mṛtaṃ lohaṃ pratyekaṃ tu palatrayam ||
children.translated_text: dead copper and dead iron, three <s>palas</s> each,

children.text: tryūṣaṇaṃ lāṅgalī dantī pirukaṃ citrakaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: the three pungents, <s>lāṅgalī</s>, <s>dantī</s>, <s>piruka</s>, and <s>citraka</s>,

children.text: pratyekaṃ dvipalaṃ yojyaṃ yavakṣāraṃ ca ṭaṅkaṇam ||
children.translated_text: two <s>palas</s> each should be added, along with barley-alkali and borax.
Both of these should be added in five-<s>pala</s> amounts, and five <s>palas</s> of rock salt.
Thirty-two <s>palas</s> of cow urine, and the same amount of <s>snuhī</s> latex,
should all be cooked in an earthen pot over a gentle fire until it becomes a good bolus.
One should always eat two <s>māṣas</s>; this <s>rasa</s> is an axe against hemorrhoids.
That should be taken with buttermilk, with pomegranate water, or else with cooked tuber.
Incinerated <s>sūta</s>, <s>arka</s>, gold, <s>abhraka</s>, <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, and <s>muṇḍa</s>, together with sulfur,
<s>maṇḍūra</s> and <s>mākṣika</s>, in equal amounts, should be triturated for a day with the juices of <s>kanyā</s>.
Placed in a blind crucible, it should be cooked for three days with a fire of chaff.
Powdered, one should eat one <s>māṣa</s> of it with sugar; it conquers hemorrhoids caused by pitta.

children.text: śuddhaṃ sūtaṃ palaṃ gandhaṃ gandhārdhaṃ tālatāpyakam
children.translated_text: Purified <s>sūta</s>, one <s>pala</s>; sulfur, half as much as the sulfur, orpiment, <s>tāpyaka</s>,
<s>amṛta</s> and <s>rasaka</s>, each in a half-share relative to the orpiment:

children.text: eteṣāṃ kajjalīṃ kuryād dṛḍhaṃ saṃmardya vāsaram
children.translated_text: one should make a <s>kajjalī</s> of these, after firmly triturating them for a day.
Then one should triturate it for three days, having added citron water indeed.
Having made pills and dried them, one should place them in a glass bottle.
One should carefully cover its mouth with an <s>arka</s> leaf equal to one <s>niṣka</s>.
And one should smear it with clay to a height measuring one and a half fingers.
Then, in the third part of a vessel filled with sand,
having placed it on the sand, one should fill over it with sand.
Having sealed its mouth, one should kindle fire beneath it for a day and a half.
When it has cooled by itself, one should draw that <s>rasa</s> out from the glass jar.
Then, making a cloth-filtered powder, one should add two <s>palas</s> each of copper and <s>abhraka</s>,
also half a <s>pala</s> of <s>amṛta</s>, and four <s>palas</s> of black pepper.
Combining everything together, one should place it in a coconut shell.

children.text: sājyo guñjādvimāno harati rasavaraḥ sarvalokāśrayo'yaṃ vātaśleṣmottharogāngudajanitagadaṃ śoṣapāṇḍvāmayaṃ ca
children.translated_text: This excellent <s>rasa</s>, taken with ghee in a dose of two <s>guñjās</s>, relied upon by all people, removes diseases arisen from vāta and phlegm, disease produced in the rectum, wasting, and pallor.

children.text: yakṣmāṇaṃ vātaśūlaṃ jvaramapi nikhilaṃ vahnimāndyaṃ ca gulmaṃ tattadrogaghnayogaiḥ sakalagadacayaṃ dīpanaṃ tatkṣaṇena ||
children.translated_text: It also removes consumption, vāta colic, every kind of fever, weak digestive fire, and abdominal tumors; when joined with disease-specific remedies, it kindles digestion and instantly removes the whole mass of diseases.

children.text: arśoghnaṃ vaṭakaṃ vakṣye putrakaṃ śṛṇu bhadraka
children.translated_text: I shall teach a pill that destroys hemorrhoids; listen, dear son, fortunate one.
Long pepper, root of long pepper, wild elephant-foot yam, and <s>citraka</s>,
black pepper, <s>kaṇṭakārī</s>, and <s>raktapuṣpī</s>, in equal parts:

children.text: palamekaṃ pṛthak sarvaṃ ślakṣṇaṃ dṛṣadi peṣayet ||
children.translated_text: one <s>pala</s> of each separately should all be ground finely on a stone slab.
One should place it in a clean vessel in the urine of elephants, goats, and cattle.
One should cook the whole with a gentle fire until it is reduced to powder.

children.text: loṇatrayaṃ ca tatraiva palamekaṃ tu nikṣipet
children.translated_text: And one should add there one <s>pala</s> of the three salts.
In this way one should make separate pills of <s>akṣa</s> measure.
For thirty days the wise man should use this hemorrhoid-destroying, supreme digestive stimulant.
Food mixed with ghee and buttermilk should be prescribed.

children.text: gandhakaṃ tāratāmraṃ ca kṛtvā caikatra piṣṭikām
children.translated_text: Sulfur, silver, and copper should be made together into one paste.
Equal to that should be <s>abhraka</s> and <s>tīkṣṇa</s>; poison should be one-fifth of the sulfur.

children.text: viṣaṃ ca ṣoḍaśāṃśena dvau bhāgau sūtakasya ca
children.translated_text: And poison should be one-sixteenth, and there should be two parts of <s>sūtaka</s>.
Combining them carefully, it is to be triturated with citron juice.
Having placed it in an earthen vessel, one should impregnate it with a decoction of <s>varā</s>.
Then it should be cooked successively in decoctions of <s>daśamūla</s> and <s>śatāvarī</s>.
Afterwards, having carefully taken it out, the learned man should make pills.
In a dose of three <s>guñjās</s>, it removes colic and rectal sprouts.

children.text: varanāgaṃ tathā vyomasattvaṃ śulbaṃ ca tīkṣṇakam
children.translated_text: Superior lead, likewise essence of <s>vyoma</s>, copper, and <s>tīkṣṇaka</s>:
having melted everything together and added a little each time,
one should stir continually until there is certainly three times as much orpiment.
Then, having triturated with that, one should make a paste with <s>rasa</s>.
Thereafter one should dig a hole within the root of a <s>bhallātakī</s> tree and put that paste there.
After a month, having drawn out that paste, one should put it into cow's milk.
Then, taking <s>bhallātakī</s> oil by means of an underground apparatus,

children.text: āyase bhājane snigdhe piṣṭikāṃ tāṃ niveśya ca ||
children.translated_text: and placing that paste in a greased iron vessel,
one should very carefully digest into it a <s>prastha</s> measure of that oil.
With fragrances impregnated with that oil, after being calcined in a sealed heating, it becomes ash.
Then, with juices from the leaves of <s>koraṇṭa</s> produced in the month of <s>Kārttika</s>,

children.text: rasaṃ saṃmardya saṃmardya gharme saṃsthāpya mārayet ||
children.translated_text: one should triturate the <s>rasa</s> again and again and, having placed it in the heat, kill it.
One should mix that ash with the former ash in equal parts.
Wild elephant-foot yam, <s>nirguṇḍī</s>, <s>mahārāṣṭrī</s>, and <s>bhakaṇṭikā</s>,

children.text: vajravallī śikhī caiṣāṃ rasaiḥ piṣṭvā viśoṣayet
children.translated_text: <s>vajravallī</s> and <s>śikhī</s>: having ground it with the juices of these, one should dry it.
Three times one should liquefy it with juices of <s>mārkava</s> and dry it.
Having carefully powdered it, one should put it in a glass container.

children.text: so'yaṃ mūlakuṭhārako rasavaro dīpyāgnivellottamāsaṃyuktaḥ saghṛtaśca vallatulitaḥ saṃsevito nāśayet
children.translated_text: This excellent <s>rasa</s> called <s>Mūlakuṭhāraka</s>, joined with excellent blazing <s>agnivella</s>, and taken with ghee in a <s>valla</s> measure, destroys

children.text: arśāṃsy ānananāsikākṣigudajāny atyugrapīḍāni ca plīhānaṃ grahaṇīṃ ca gulmayakṛtau māndyaṃ ca kuṣṭhāmayān ||
children.translated_text: hemorrhoids born in the mouth, nose, eyes, and rectum, even when exceedingly painful, as well as enlargement of the spleen, <s>grahaṇī</s>, abdominal tumor, disorders of the liver, sluggishness, and skin diseases.
Three <s>palas</s> of sulfur swallowed and emitted by <s>rasa</s>,
and one <s>karṣa</s> each, separately, of incinerated <s>sūta</s>, <s>abhraka</s>, copper, and iron;
one <s>pala</s> of powdered cinnabar, and three <s>palas</s> of <s>mākṣika</s>,
also one <s>pala</s> of <s>kampillaka</s>, and half a <s>pala</s> of poison likewise:
one should triturate all this for seven days, repeatedly adding powder-water.
Then, having made it into a ball, one should place it in the sun for seven days.
One should smear it, to the thickness of a finger, with powdered jaggery and powdered stone.

children.text: tripalaṃ gandhakaṃ dattvā krauñcyām atha ca golakam ||
children.translated_text: Having put three <s>palas</s> of sulfur into a <s>krauñcī</s> vessel, then the ball should be placed there.
And over the top of the ball one should put three <s>palas</s> of orpiment.
Having sealed it with great care, one should indeed apply a <s>gajapuṭa</s> heating.
When it has cooled by itself, one should take out the ball together with the coatings.
Having powdered it, seven times with substances produced from the fruit of <s>viṣatindu</s>...
with liquids; then, when it has dried in the sun, one should put it into a fine container.
One should add into it <s>vaikrānta-bhasma</s> in the proportion of one-thirtieth.

children.text: ayaṃ hi nandīśvarasampradiṣṭo raso viśiṣṭaḥ khalu rogahantā
children.translated_text: This excellent <s>rasa</s>, taught by <s>Nandīśvara</s>, is indeed a destroyer of diseases,
unimpaired in its power against all diseases, and named <s>Mahodayapratyayasāra</s>.

children.text: hanyātsarvagudāmayānkṣayagadaṃ kuṣṭhaṃ ca mandāgnitāṃ śūlādhmānagadaṃ kaphaṃ śvasanatām unmādakāpasmṛtī
children.translated_text: It destroys all diseases of the anus, wasting disease, skin disease, weak digestive fire, colic and distension, kapha, difficulty in breathing, insanity, and epilepsy;

children.text: sarvā vātarujo mahājvaragadān nānāprakārāṃstathā vātaśleṣmabhavaṃ mahāmayacayaṃ duṣṭagrahaṇyāmayam ||
children.translated_text: also all pains of vāta, great fevers of many kinds, the great mass of diseases born of vāta and śleṣman, and disease of a corrupted <s>grahaṇī</s>.
Let there be <s>rasa</s>, washed <s>mākṣīka</s>, magnetic <s>abhraka</s>, lead, and gold,
equal with <s>pṛthvībhaṭa</s>, and sulfur equal to all of them.
Having placed them in a <s>Vidyādhara</s> apparatus, one should heat them with forest cow-dung cakes.
When it has cooled by itself, one should take it out and mix it with <s>tryūṣaṇa</s>.
One should use it in hemorrhoidal disease, in pain of the waist, and in severe eye pain,

children.text: sannipāte kṣaye kāse śvāse mandānale jvare ||
children.translated_text: in <s>sannipāta</s>, wasting, cough, dyspnea, weak digestive fire, and fever;
one should apply it in ear pain, headache, and toothache,

children.text: pīnase plīhni hṛcchūle granthivāte ca dāruṇe ||
children.translated_text: in nasal catarrh, spleen disease, heart pain, and severe <s>granthi-vāta</s>;

children.text: ekāṅge vā dhanurvāte kampavāte ca mūrchite
children.translated_text: in hemiplegia, tetanic vāta, tremor from vāta, and fainting;
and it destroys all intermittent fevers and diseases in many forms.
The <s>rasa</s> called <s>Kanakasundara</s>, used with an appropriate regimen,
should be given in a dose the size of a <s>guñjā</s>, with a suitable accompanying drink.

children.text: ghṛtena saṃyuto vāte madhunā paittike jvare
children.translated_text: Joined with ghee it is for vāta; with honey, for pitta fever.
It should be given with long pepper in a śleṣman disorder, and, when born of pitta, together with sandalwood.
With buttermilk it is for śleṣman and vāta together; in vāta and pitta it is accompanied by ghee.
In śleṣman and pitta it is given with fresh ginger, and in a <s>sānnipātika</s> condition with <s>nirguṇḍī</s>.
In colics, and also in intermittent fevers, it should be given with the three fruits.
Or one may give it with fresh ginger, especially in weakness of the digestive fire.
In ocular inflammation and headache it is joined with <s>gāyatrī</s> and <s>bola</s>.
In kapha-vāta and in fainting it is combined with the meat of birds.

children.text: ekāṅge ca dhanurvāte kṣīrayuktaṃ ca pīnase
children.translated_text: In hemiplegia and tetanic vāta it is joined with milk, and also in nasal catarrh.
In anemia, wasting, and cough it is used; in jaundice, with black pepper and ghee.
With <s>ajamodā</s> and <s>viḍaṅga</s>, it conquers navel pain and weak digestion.
In dry fever and loss of appetite it should be given with banana fruit.
With <s>bola</s> it is for pain in one side of the waist, as stated by <s>Nāgabodhin</s>.

children.text: nāgaṃ pāradagandhakaṃ trilavaṇaṃ vāyarkajaṃ melayed ekaikaṃ ca palaṃ palaṃ trayamataḥ pañca kramānmardayet
children.translated_text: One should combine lead, mercury, sulfur, the three salts, and the product of <s>arka</s>, one <s>pala</s> of each; then one should triturate them in five successive stages.

children.text: sarvaṃ taddivasatrayaṃ tadanu taddattvā puṭaṃ bhāvanāḥ kuryātsatriphalāgnivetasarasaiḥ pañcādhikā viṃśatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: All that is treated for three days; afterwards, having given it a <s>puṭa</s> heating, one should make twenty-five further impregnations with juices of <s>triphalā</s> and <s>agnivetasa</s>.

children.text: pañcaitat kramaśastato guḍabhavair datto'sya vallo jalair hantyarśāṃsyakhilāni sūraṇaghṛtaistasyānnam asminhitam
children.translated_text: After this has been done five times in order, a <s>valla</s> of it, given with waters derived from jaggery, destroys all hemorrhoids; food with elephant-foot yam and ghee is beneficial for him in this treatment.

children.text: arkeśaḥ parivarjyatāmiti muniḥ śrīvāsudevo'vadat kūṣmāṇḍīphalamāṣapāyasam ativyāyāmam arkātapam ||
children.translated_text: The sage <s>Śrīvāsudeva</s> said that one should avoid <s>arka</s>, pumpkin fruit, black gram, milk-rice, excessive exertion, and the heat of the sun.
Mercury, gold, <s>arka</s>, <s>biḍāla</s>, <s>gola</s>, <s>surāyasa</s>, iron-slag, mica, sulfur,

children.text: tāpyaṃ ca kanyārasamardito'yaṃ pakvaḥ puṭe tīkṣṇamukho'rśasāṃ syāt ||
children.translated_text: and <s>tāpya</s>: this, triturated with the juice of <s>kanyā</s> and cooked in a <s>puṭa</s>, becomes a sharp-mouthed remedy for hemorrhoids.

children.text: śreṣṭhā dantyagniyugmatrikaṭukahalinīpīlukumbhaṃ vipakvaṃ prasthe mūtrasya sasnukpayasi rasapalaṃ dve pale gandhakasya
children.translated_text: The best <s>dantī</s>, two <s>agnis</s>, the three pungents, <s>halinī</s>, <s>pīlu</s>, and <s>kumbha</s>, cooked in a <s>prastha</s> of urine together with the milk of <s>snuk</s>, with one <s>pala</s> of <s>rasa</s> and two <s>palas</s> of sulfur,

children.text: lohasya trīṇi tāmrātkuḍavamatha rajaḥkṣārayoścāpi pañca kṣiptvā sthālyāṃ pacettu jvalati dahanataścūrṇam arśaḥkuṭhāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: three of iron, then a <s>kuḍava</s> of copper, and five each of <s>rajas</s> and alkali: having put these in a pot, one should cook them over a blazing fire; the powder is <s>Arśaḥkuṭhāra</s>, the axe against hemorrhoids.
The essence produced from diamond and black mica, purified glass, and borax,
having liquefied it, reduced it to powder, and fried it with ghee,
one should heat it three times in a <s>puṭa</s>, furnished with one-eighth part of <s>sasyaka</s>.
Then three times with <s>nṛpavarta</s> joined with citron juice,
and four times with the juices of <s>varṣābhū</s>, <s>vāsā</s>, and <s>matsyākṣikā</s>,
and thirty times, carefully, with decoctions of <s>guggulu</s> and <s>triphalā</s>.
With one-eighth part of <s>kajjalī</s> made from equal parts <s>rasa</s> and sulfur,
one should give it fifty <s>puṭa</s> heatings and triturate it at each heating.
Purified and liquefied essence of magnetic iron, triturated with ghee,
one should heat in a <s>puṭa</s> together with one-eighth part of cinnabar and water of <s>lakuca</s>.

children.text: daśavāraṃ tathā samyak tāraṃ śuddhaṃ manohvayā
children.translated_text: So, properly, ten times; likewise purified silver with <s>manohvā</s>,
twenty times in the same way with the juices of <s>balinī</s> and <s>mīnadṛk</s>.
Ten times with <s>tāpya</s> joined with the ghee of a black cow;
those two, in equal parts, should be heated with the juices of <s>nirguṇḍikā</s>.
Again one should heat it ten times with <s>kajjalī</s> produced from <s>rasa</s> and sulfur.
Into that one should put <s>vaikrānta-bhasma</s> in the proportion of one-eighth.
With <s>rājāvarta</s> in a sixteenth part and <s>parpaṭī</s> in an equal part,
having triturated all that and then impregnated it with ginger water,
also with the expressed juice of <s>guḍūcī</s> or with the juice of <s>bhūkadamba</s>,
and also with the juice of <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> and the juice of <s>citramūla</s>,
with <s>vyoṣa</s>, <s>gañjā</s>, and <s>kinī</s> tubers, and again with a moist liquid,
then, having made a cloth-filtered powder, one should put it into a clean container.
This is the celebrated <s>Trailokyatilaka</s>, the best of all <s>rasas</s>,
auspicious and remover of every disease, proclaimed by <s>Śambhu</s>.

children.text: udāvartaṃ ca viḍbandhaṃ vyathāṃ ca jaṭharodbhavām
children.translated_text: It removes upward-moving wind, constipation, and pain arising in the abdomen,
excessive salivation, dullness of intellect, colic, and also infertility;
all puerperal diseases without remainder, and various kinds of colic as well.
And it breaks up the severe colic called <s>pariṇāma-śūla</s>.

children.text: raktagulmaṃ ca nārīṇāṃ rajaḥśūlaṃ ca duḥsaham
children.translated_text: It also breaks up bloody abdominal tumors in women and the unbearable pain of menstruation.
The vehicle and the regimen should be according to each particular disease.
<s>Vacā</s>, <s>hiṅgu</s>, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, rock salt, and old dry ginger,
black pepper, long pepper, <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>pathyā</s>, <s>vahni</s>, and <s>ajamodaka</s>:
these are to be powdered in successively increasing quantities, with jaggery twice the quantity of all of them.
One should drink a <s>karṣa</s> of it with hot water for the conquest of vāta-type hemorrhoids.
Incinerated iron, <s>indrayava</s>, dry ginger, <s>bhallātaka</s>, and <s>citraka</s>,
pulp of bilva, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, and <s>pathyā</s> should be powdered in equal measure.

children.text: sarvatulyaṃ guḍaṃ yojyaṃ karṣaṃ bhuktvārśasāṃ jayet
children.translated_text: Jaggery equal to the whole should be added; having eaten a <s>karṣa</s>, one conquers hemorrhoids.
For the pacification of kapha-type hemorrhoids, <s>Ānandabhairava</s> should be given.

children.text: mṛtatāmreṇa santulyaṃ deyaṃ guñjātrayaṃ hi tat ||
children.translated_text: That should indeed be given in a dose of three <s>guñjās</s>, together with an equal amount of incinerated copper.
The tender leaves of safflower should be cooked simply with sour gruel.
One should eat them daily like greens, for the pacification of hemorrhoidal disease.
The seeds of <s>devadālī</s>, finely powdered with rock salt,
make this paste with sour rice-water, which cuts down the root-disease.
Powdered flowers of <s>kāñcanī</s>, powdered conch-shell, and realgar,
made into a paste with water of <s>gajapippalī</s>, are indeed an axe against hemorrhoids.
One should perform cleansing with a decoction of <s>devadālī</s>, which destroys hemorrhoids.
Even prolapse of the rectum comes to relief by this, and not otherwise.
A bitter gourd with its seeds, ground with sour rice-water,
and mixed with jaggery, destroys the ill-named hemorrhoids completely from the root when applied as a paste.
A suppository smeared with <s>pīlu</s> oil and placed inside the anus
quickly destroys hemorrhoids, and all the pain as well.
The latex of <s>arka</s>, the stem of <s>snuhī</s>, the leaf of bitter gourd,
and <s>karañja</s>, with goat urine, make a paste beneficial for discharging hemorrhoids.
An application made from <s>śigru</s> root and leaves born from <s>arka</s> is beneficial for hemorrhoids.

children.text: rūkṣaiḥ kodravajīrṇamudgacaṇakaiḥ kruddho'nilo'dho vahan ruddhvā vartma malaṃ viśoṣya kurute viṇmūtrasaṃgaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: Aggravated by dry foods such as <s>kodrava</s>, old mung beans, and chickpeas, the wind, moving downward, blocks the channel, dries up the feces, and then causes retention of feces and urine.

children.text: hṛtpṛṣṭhodaravastimastakarujaḥ saśvāsakāsaṃ jvaraṃ gacchannūrdhvamasau hi nūnam aniśaṃ kopādudāvartayet ||
children.translated_text: As it moves upward, it produces pain in the heart, back, abdomen, bladder, and head, along with dyspnea, cough, and fever; from its aggravation it certainly causes <s>udāvarta</s> continually.
<s>Kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, <s>hiṅgu</s>, rock salt, <s>trivṛt</s>, <s>dantī</s>, <s>vacā</s>, and <s>abhayā</s>,

children.text: citrakasya tu mūlaṃ ca kalkīkṛtya paced ghṛtam ||
children.translated_text: and also the root of <s>citraka</s>: having made them into a paste, one should cook ghee.
It should be joined with four times as much cow's milk and with a measured amount of <s>snuhī</s> latex.
When drunk regularly, it destroys <s>udāvarta</s> and abdominal diseases.
Through excessive drinking of water, sesame paste, sprouted grains, dry and dried meat, overeating, constipation, and the like,

children.text: kruddho'nilo 'tisaraṇāya ca kalpate'gniṃ hatvā malaṃ śithilayannapi toyadhātūn ||
children.translated_text: the aggravated wind becomes capable of producing diarrhea, after destroying the digestive fire and loosening the feces as well as the watery elements.
A very fine, sharp powder, in equal part with <s>rasendra</s> (mercury),
rubbed with juices of <s>kāñcanāra</s>, destroys every kind of diarrhea.
This mercury, ground with an equal amount of <s>tīkṣṇa</s> and triturated with water of <s>kāñcanāra</s>,
then cooked in a sealed heating, destroys diarrhea and is called <s>Dardura</s>.

children.text: hiṃgulaṃ vatsanābhaṃ ca maricaṃ ṭaṃkaṇaṃ kaṇā
children.translated_text: Cinnabar, <s>vatsanābha</s>, black pepper, borax, and <s>kaṇā</s>
should be triturated in equal parts; this medicine is <s>Ānandabhairava rasa</s>.

children.text: guṃjaikāṃ vārdhaguñjāṃ vā balaṃ jñātvā pradāpayet
children.translated_text: One should administer one <s>guñjā</s>, or half a <s>guñjā</s>, after considering the patient's strength.
It should be licked with honey, followed by the fruit and bark of <s>kuṭaja</s>,
powdered, in a dose of a <s>karṣa</s>; it conquers diarrhea arising from the three doṣas.
Curd-rice should be prescribed as the wholesome diet, or cow's ghee, or buttermilk.

children.text: pipāsāyāṃ jalaṃ śītaṃ vijayā ca hitā niśi ||
children.translated_text: For thirst, cold water is beneficial, and <s>vijayā</s> is beneficial at night.
One <s>pala</s> each of sulfur-stone and mercury should be made into black sulfide paste.
Having liquefied it, one should add one <s>pala</s> of mica whose luster has departed.
Stirring all of it with a wooden stick, one should place it on <s>kuṭaja</s> leaves.
Then, after powdering it again with care, one should impregnate it repeatedly.
This is done with juices of young <s>tindu</s> fruits and with milks of <s>audumbara</s>,
and also with juices of <s>aralu</s> bark and with the fresh juice of <s>dugdhinī</s>.
It is also done with the fine juices of young pomegranate fruit cooked in a sealed heating,
with juices of the root of <s>kṛṣṇakāmbojikā</s>, and with those produced from the bark of <s>kuṭaja</s>.
One should add two <s>palas</s> of powder of <s>viśva</s> and <s>gāndhārī</s> in equal portions,
with <s>mustā</s>, <s>vatsaka</s>, <s>dīpyāgni</s>, <s>mocasāra</s>, and cumin.

children.text: vatsanābhaṃ ca karṣāṃśaṃ pratyekaṃ tatra nikṣipet
children.translated_text: One should also add <s>vatsanābha</s>, one <s>karṣa</s> for each ingredient there.
After powdering it, one should again impregnate it seven times with a decoction of dry ginger.

children.text: itthaṃ siddho rasaḥ piṣṭaḥ karaṇḍe viniveśayet
children.translated_text: When this medicine has been prepared and ground in this way, it should be placed in a casket.
It is known as <s>Sudhāsāra</s>, with a radiance equal to the essence of nectar.
It kindles appetite, digests, checks looseness, is pleasant to the heart, and improves taste.
It immediately checks diarrhea caused by all three doṣas, even when difficult to conquer by other medicines,

children.text: āmaṃ caivamāraktaṃ ca jvarātīsāram eva ca
children.translated_text: and also diarrhea with undigested matter, bloody diarrhea, and fever-diarrhea,
as well as <s>viṣūcī</s> accompanied by diarrhea.
It checks them at once, just as a violation of due honor toward the honorable obstructs the arising of the fruit of merit.
Having made small cakes with a paste of powdered <s>viśvābda</s>,
one should place them in a steaming apparatus and cook them for half a <s>ghaṭikā</s>.
Drawing them out, one should triturate them with those very waters and extract the juice.
Into that one should put <s>Sudhāsāra rasa</s>, in a quantity equal to coriander seed.
The excellent physician should prescribe it for the diseases stated above.

children.text: gotakreṇātha dadhnā vā pathyaṃ deyaṃ hitaṃ mitam ||
children.translated_text: With cow's buttermilk or with curds, a wholesome and moderate diet should be given.
Young plantain fruit, <s>gurvī</s> fruit, bilva fruit as well,

children.text: āmrapeśī ca madhukaṃ vṛntākaṃ ca praśasyate ||
children.translated_text: mango kernel, <s>madhuka</s>, and eggplant are recommended.

children.text: sarvātisāraṃ grahaṇīṃ ca hikkāṃ mandāgnim ānāhamarocakaṃ ca
children.translated_text: It destroys every kind of diarrhea, <s>grahaṇī</s> disease, hiccup, weak digestive fire, abdominal distension, and loss of appetite,
and this excellent <s>rasa</s>, when administered in indigestion, does so at once in two or three applications.
After placing the material to be cooked in a pot with water, with its mouth covered by a cloth,
the apparatus in which it is covered and cooked is called a steaming apparatus.
One should combine two parts of sulfur with eight parts of powdered conch shell,
and one single part of mercury should be triturated with the latex of <s>arka</s>.
After drying it again and again in this same way with the juice of <s>citraka</s>,
then, having made it one with the mercury, one should add half as much alkali.
With the latex of <s>arka</s> one should make balls and then dry them.
After sealing them in a vessel smeared with powder, one should then give them a sealed heating.
This is indeed <s>Lokeśvararasa</s>, a cutter-down of <s>grahaṇī</s> disease.
Four <s>guñjās</s> of it, together with black pepper and ghee,

children.text: dadīta dadhibhaktaṃ ca pathyaṃ lokeśvare tathā ||
children.translated_text: should be given; curd-rice is the prescribed diet for <s>Lokeśvara</s> as well.
One part of incinerated mercury and four parts of purified sulfur

children.text: yāmaṃ ca mardayetkhalle tena pūrvā varāṭakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: should be triturated for a <s>yāma</s> in a mortar; with that, the cowries described before are treated.

children.text: ṭaṅkaṇaṃ tu gavāṃ kṣīraiḥ piṣṭvā tena mukhaṃ lipet
children.translated_text: Borax should be ground with cow's milk, and with it one should smear the mouths

children.text: varāṭānāṃ prayatnena ruddhvā bhāṇḍe puṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: of the cowries; having carefully sealed them in a vessel, one should cook them in a sealed heating.
When cooled by themselves, the cowries should be taken out and then powdered.
The preparation is named <s>Lokanātharasa</s>; four <s>guñjās</s> are to be taken with honey.
It should be accompanied by a decoction containing dry ginger, <s>ativiṣā</s>, <s>mustā</s>, <s>devadāru</s>, and <s>vacā</s>;
it destroys diarrhea caused by vāta.
With ash of lead, mercury, mica, and sulfur, each measured at half a <s>pala</s>,
one should make a smooth black sulfide paste; immediately after that it should be put
into two <s>palas</s> of melted resin and thoroughly mixed.
With fried <s>yakṣākṣa</s>, rock salt, <s>vacā</s>, the three pungents, and the two cumin seeds,
and with <s>pathyā</s>, <s>vijayā</s>, and <s>dīpyaka</s>, all powdered in equal parts,
one should combine the former paste and then impregnate it.
With the essences of the bark of great neem, with liquids from the root of <s>kāmbojī</s>,
and with the juices of <s>nāgabalā</s> and <s>guḍūcī</s>, it should be treated three times with each.
Then pills should be made, the size of a jujube stone.
<s>Nāgasundararasa</s>, taken in a <s>valla</s> measure, indeed destroys
many kinds of diarrhea, prolapse of the rectum, and <s>biṃbiśī</s>.
Six <s>niṣkas</s> of sesame oil and one <s>niṣka</s> of citron juice,

children.text: lavaṇaṃ pañcaguñjaṃ ca aṃgulyā mardayed dṛḍham
children.translated_text: together with five <s>guñjās</s> of salt, should be rubbed firmly with the finger.
It should be licked; it destroys diarrhea attended by <s>āmavāta</s>, and the prescribed diet is as before.
It repeatedly gathers the stool and at times causes purging;
loss of appetite, swelling, and sluggishness are symptoms of <s>grahaṇī</s> disease.
Incinerated mercury and mica, sulfur, barley-alkali together with borax,

children.text: vacā jayā samaṃ sarvaṃ jayantī bhṛṃgajadravaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>vacā</s> and <s>jayā</s>, all in equal measure, should be triturated with the juices of <s>jayantī</s> and <s>bhṛṅgaja</s>,
together with citron, for three days; that ball should then be dried.
It should be steamed slowly over a weak fire in an iron vessel for half a <s>yāma</s>.
When it is equal to the <s>rasa</s>, <s>mocarasa</s> should also be added every night.
It should be impregnated with the juices of <s>vijayā</s>, dried, and ground seven times.
This <s>rasa</s> called <s>Vajrakapāṭa</s> should be licked with honey in a dose of half a <s>niṣka</s>.

children.text: dagdhāṃ kapardikāṃ piṣṭvā tryūṣaṇaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ viṣam
children.translated_text: Having ground burnt cowrie shell, the three pungents, borax, poison,

children.text: gandhakaṃ śuddhasūtaṃ ca tulyaṃ jambīrajair dravaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: sulfur, and purified mercury in equal parts with citron liquids,
one should eat a <s>māṣa</s> measure and afterwards lick black pepper with ghee.
It destroys <s>grahaṇī</s> disease; buttermilk-rice is the beneficial prescribed diet.

children.text: hiṅgulaṃ maricaṃ gandhaṃ pippalī ṭaṅkaṇaṃ viṣam
children.translated_text: Cinnabar, black pepper, sulfur, long pepper, borax, poison,
and the seeds of <s>kanaka</s>, in equal parts, should be triturated with the juices of <s>vijayā</s>.
It should be triturated for the length of one <s>yāma</s> and made into a pill the size of a chickpea.
One should eat it; the <s>rasa</s> called <s>Kanakasundara</s> destroys <s>grahaṇī</s>.
It removes weak digestion, intense fever, and diarrhea.
Curd-rice should be prescribed as the diet, or buttermilk made from cow's or goat's milk.
Mercury, mica, and sulfur, in successively increasing parts, should be triturated with the juice of <s>jayā</s> for three days.

children.text: gadyāṇakārdhaṃ madhunā sametaṃ dadīta pathyaṃ dadhibhaktakaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: Half a <s>gadyāṇaka</s>, together with honey, should be given; the prescribed diet is curd-rice.
The seed of <s>Maheśvara</s> situated in cinnabar should be extracted by the method of the descending apparatus.
Then it should be triturated in an iron mortar with sulfur, borax, incinerated mica in equal quantity, and <s>kokilākṣa</s>.
It is to be ground in a state of continued pouring, placed over a smokeless fire,
until it becomes capable of drying up water; a <s>valla</s> dose is taken with cumin and fresh ginger.

children.text: saṃgrahajvaram atisrutigulmān arśasāṃ ca vinihanti samūham
children.translated_text: It destroys <s>saṃgraha</s> fever, excessive discharge, abdominal tumors, and the whole group of hemorrhoids.
This king of <s>rasas</s>, taught by <s>Vāsudeva</s>, is the sole bolt against the disease of violent <s>saṃgraha</s>.
Equal parts of purified mercury, sulfur, mica, and cinnabar
should be placed in an iron mortar and combined with cow's ghee.
One should carefully set the mortar in a trough-stove supplied with embers,
and grind it with an iron pestle for two days.
Thus perfected, this lord of <s>rasa</s> is considered <s>Laghusiddhābhraka</s>.
A dose equal to a <s>valla</s>, together with cumin-water, in the morning,
when drunk, swiftly removes very obstinate <s>grahaṇī</s>,
very terrible diarrhea and fever accompanied by diarrhea.
It is digestive, kindles appetite, is pleasing to the heart, and produces lightness of the limbs.
It was taught by <s>Nāgārjuna</s> and produces immediate confidence from experience.
One <s>pala</s> measure of mercury is combined with an equal amount of purified lead.
Having melted it in an iron vessel, one should place it, with oil, in the earth.

children.text: tato drute vinikṣipya gaṃdhake tad viloḍya ca
children.translated_text: Then, when it has melted, one should add sulfur to it and stir it,
and again, after putting it into an iron vessel, melt it thoroughly and set it down.
One should digest into it an equal quantity of orpiment; then, having powdered it again as before,
one should properly digest into it an equal quantity of purified <s>kunaṭī</s>.
When that has been powdered, one should add an equal quantity of lead that has become incapable of rising up.
Likewise the same amount of calcined <s>tāpya</s>, and every other ingredient should be equal to that.

children.text: tīkṣṇāyaḥ kharparaṃ vyoma hiṃgulaṃ ca śilājatu
children.translated_text: Steel, <s>kharpara</s>, mica, cinnabar, and mineral pitch,
each in the measure of one <s>karṣa</s>, together with the six pungents, <s>kaṭphala</s>, and <s>miśī</s>,
<s>dīpyaka</s>, the four aromatics, <s>reṇukā</s>, <s>uśīra</s>, and <s>ellaka</s>,
<s>tuṃburu</s>, <s>bhārṅgikā</s>, <s>rāsnā</s>, <s>kaṅkola</s>, <s>cora</s>, and <s>puṣkara</s>,
<s>riṅgiṇī</s>, <s>ciratikta</s>, and the seeds of <s>unmattaka</s>,
as well as two <s>palas</s> of <s>lāṅgalī</s>; of all these the twelfth part should be used.

children.text: vatsanābhaṃ sitaṃ bhūri vinikṣipya tataḥ param
children.translated_text: Afterwards one should add plenty of white <s>vatsanābha</s>.
Then, after that, with a decoction of <s>triphala</s> and <s>daśamūla</s>,
and also with the juices of <s>jayantī</s>, fresh ginger, <s>vāsā</s>, and <s>mārkava</s>,
having impregnated it, one should make pills the size of chickpeas.
One pill at a time should be used; it produces a very intense appetite.

children.text: viṣūcīmaratiṃ hikkāṃ sevyaṃ svādu ca śītalam ||
children.translated_text: For cholera-like disorder, restlessness, and hiccup, sweet and cooling food should be taken.

children.text: sāmāṃ ca grahaṇīṃ sadāṅgatudanaṃ śoṣotkaṭaṃ pāṇḍutām ārtiṃ vātakaphatridoṣajanitāṃ śūlaṃ ca gulmāmayam
children.translated_text: For <s>grahaṇī</s> accompanied by undigested matter, pain in all the limbs, severe wasting, pallor, distress arising from vāta, kapha, or all three doṣas, colic, and abdominal tumor disease,

children.text: hikkādhmānaviṣūcikāṃ ca kasanaṃ śvāsārśasāṃ vidradhiṃ sarvāropyavaṭī kṣaṇādvijayate rogāṃstathānyānapi ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Sarvāropyavaṭī</s> conquers at once hiccup, distension, cholera-like disorder, cough, asthma, hemorrhoids, abscess, and all other diseases as well.
Having made a black sulphide paste of equal parts mercury and sulfur,
one should melt it in an iron vessel and add an amount equal to the mercury:
ash produced from living and nonliving sources, especially that arising from <s>mākṣika</s>,
together with sulfur-stone; one should place it in an iron vessel.
Then, after stirring it with a stick, one should put it on a banana leaf.
Thereafter, covering it, powdering it, and placing it in an iron vessel,
one should add an <s>akṣa</s> measure of ash produced from <s>mākṣika</s>.
Mica ash, brought properly to a state without metallic shine, should be one <s>pala</s> in measure.

children.text: viṣaṃ viṣāṃ ca gandhārīṃ mocasāraṃ sajīrakam
children.translated_text: Poison, <s>viṣā</s>, <s>gandhārī</s>, <s>mocasāra</s>, and cumin,

children.text: sarvaṃ samāṃśikaṃ kṛtvā rase cārdhāṃśikaṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: all made in equal portions, should be added to the mercury in half portions.
Having triturated all this, one should impregnate it with very great care
with <s>jayantī</s>, <s>mahārāṣṭrī</s>, <s>gañjākinī</s>, and <s>aśvagandhā</s>,
and with decoctions of the five pungents; then one should make it into a powder.
This <s>rasa</s>, prepared in this way, is the lion against the elephant of <s>grahaṇī</s>.
By name it is declared by <s>Nandin</s> to be <s>Grahaṇīgajakesarī</s>, and by action a treasure of nectar.
This <s>rasa</s>, measured by a <s>valla</s>, should be used with dry ginger smeared with ghee.

children.text: sevito grahaṇīṃ hanti satsaṅga iva vigraham
children.translated_text: It destroys <s>grahaṇī</s>, as good company destroys conflict.
In this case the prescribed diet should be given with a little ghee and with curd and buttermilk.

children.text: hitaṃ mitaṃ ca viśadaṃ laghu grāhi rucipradam
children.translated_text: It should be wholesome, moderate, clear, light, constipating, and appetite-producing.
It is digestive, very strongly kindles the digestive fire, removes undigested matter, and promotes relish.
When combined with the appropriate medicinal formulation, it destroys every kind of diarrhea.

children.text: badhnannapi malaṃ śīghraṃ nādhmānaṃ kurute nṛṇām ||
children.translated_text: Even while quickly binding the stool, it does not produce abdominal distension in people.

children.text: pāradaṃ gandhakaṃ vyoma tīkṣṇaṃ tālaṃ manaḥśilā
children.translated_text: Mercury, sulfur, mica, steel, orpiment, and realgar,
purified collyrium of <s>sauvīra</s> and <s>vimala</s>, in equal parts:
having made a black paste from these, one should fry it with a little oil.

children.text: granthikaṃ jīrakaṃ citraṃ dīpyakaṃ mustakaṃ viṣam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Granthika</s>, cumin, <s>citra</s>, <s>dīpyaka</s>, <s>mustaka</s>, and poison,
young mango, young bilva, and <s>mocasāra</s>, in equal parts:
having powdered them, one should add half as much paste as before.
One should again triturate it carefully until it becomes uniform.
One should impregnate it seven times with a decoction of the five pungents.
It should also be impregnated ten times with the juice of <s>aralu</s> bark.
By the stated sequence of procedures this <s>rasa</s> is produced.

children.text: jagdho viśvaghanāmbunā sa hi rasaḥ śīghraprabhāvābhidho niṣkārdhapramito mahāgrahaṇikāroge'tisārāmaye
children.translated_text: This <s>rasa</s>, called <s>Śīghraprabhāva</s>, eaten with water of dry ginger and <s>viśva</s>, in a measure of half a <s>niṣka</s>, acts powerfully in the great disease of <s>grahaṇī</s> and in diarrhea,

children.text: ādhmāne grahaṇībhave rucihate vāte ca mandānale mukte cāpi male punaścalamalāśaṅkāsu hikkāsu ca ||
children.translated_text: in abdominal distension, in conditions arising from <s>grahaṇī</s>, loss of taste, vāta disorder, weak digestive fire, loosened stool, recurrent fear of moving bowels, and hiccup.

children.text: kapardatulyaṃ rasagandhakalkaṃ lohaṃ mṛtaṃ ṭaṅkaṇakaṃ ca tulyam
children.translated_text: A paste of mercury and sulfur equal to a cowrie shell, calcined iron, and borax in equal quantity

children.text: jayārasenaikadinaṃ vimardya cūrṇena sampiṣya puṭettu bhāṇḍe ||
children.translated_text: should be triturated for one day with the juice of <s>jayā</s>, ground together with powder, and cooked in a sealed vessel.
One should give that packet for the removal of <s>grahaṇī</s> in which the three doṣas are predominant.
Mercury and sulfur, each four <s>māṣas</s>, should be reduced to an amalgam-like paste.
Mica, in a measure of one <s>māṣa</s>, should be triturated with the sour juice of citron.

children.text: śodhitaṃ saptadhā caiva dvimāṣaṃ tryūṣaṇaṃ pṛthak
children.translated_text: Having been purified seven times, and with two <s>māṣas</s> each of the three pungents,
<s>triśūlī</s>, <s>bhṛṅga</s>, <s>cāṅgerī</s>, <s>sātalā</s>, and <s>tīkṣṇaparṇikā</s>,
white <s>aparājitā</s>, <s>kanyā</s>, <s>matsyākṣī</s>, and <s>grīṣmasundarā</s>,
<s>kariṇī</s>, <s>karṇamoṭī</s>, and <s>rudaṃtī</s>, together with <s>citraka</s> and fresh ginger,
with the separate juices of <s>dhustūra</s>, <s>kākamācī</s>, and <s>musalī</s>,
it should be triturated with two <s>palas</s> of each, and pills of one <s>māṣa</s> measure should be made.
For <s>grahaṇī</s>, taken with a piece of leaf and mixed with the three pungents,
the pill pacifies loss of appetite, royal consumption, weak digestive fire, and puerperal diseases.
It is celebrated by the name <s>Vahnijvālā</s>.
Mercury, sulfur, copper, mica, the three alkalis, <s>varuṇa</s>, and <s>vṛṣa</s>,
and the alkali of <s>apāmārga</s> and salt, each two <s>māṣas</s> in measure,
Ground with the juices of <s>cāṅgerī</s> and <s>hastiśuṇḍī</s>, it should be cooked in a <s>puṭa</s> heating.

children.text: bhakṣayitvā tato guñjāṃ grahaṇyāṃ kāṃjikaṃ pibet ||
children.translated_text: Then, after eating a <s>guñjā</s> of it, one should drink <s>kāñjika</s> for <s>grahaṇī</s>.

children.text: paktiśūle ca kāse ca mandāgnāv ārdrakadravam
children.translated_text: For colic from indigestion, for cough, and for weak digestive fire, one should take fresh ginger juice.

children.text: amlapitte ca dhāroṣṇaṃ kṣīraṃ vajradharo hyayam ||
children.translated_text: And in acid dyspepsia, one should take milk warm straight from the cow; this indeed is <s>Vajradhara</s>.
<s>Rasendra</s>, sulfur, <s>ativiṣā</s>, <s>abhayā</s>, <s>abhra</s>, the two alkalis, <s>mocarasa</s>, and <s>vacā</s>,

children.text: jayā ca jaṃbīrarasena piṣṭaṃ piṇḍīkṛtaṃ syādgrahaṇīkapāṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: together with <s>jayā</s>, ground with citron juice and made into lumps: this is <s>Grahaṇīkapāṭa</s>.
In the morning one should lick half a <s>māṣa</s> of it with honey, and also conch ash, ghee, and honey.
At the beginning one should give <s>sakṣīriṇī</s>, cumin, <s>māṇimantha</s>, sharp substances, and food with curds.
<s>Sauvarcala</s> salt, the two cumins, coriander, <s>jayā</s>, <s>yavānī</s>, long pepper, and dry ginger:

children.text: kapitthasāreṇa samaṃ pragṛhya dadīta cūrṇaṃ niśi tīvrapittaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: taking these in equal measure with the pith of wood-apple, one should give the powder at night to those with severe pitta.
A <s>gadyāṇa</s> measure, mixed with sugar-candy and combined with buttermilk, is for quickly calming loss of appetite.

children.text: vātapradhāne ca kaphapradhāne rātrau kaṣāyaṃ kuṭajasya dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: And when vāta predominates or kapha predominates, one should give a decoction of <s>kuṭaja</s> at night.
<s>Mustā</s>, <s>vatsaka</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>agni</s>, the three pungents, <s>prativiṣā</s>, and poison,
with <s>dhātakī</s>, exudate of <s>moca</s>, and mango stone, remove <s>grahaṇī</s>.
One should grind equal parts of <s>vahni</s>, dry ginger, <s>biḍa</s> salt, <s>bilva</s>, and salt.
Drinking it afterward with hot water, one conquers <s>grahaṇī</s> arising from vāta.
Burnt conch and salt from the Sindhu, in equal measure, should be made into a linctus with honey.
One <s>niṣka</s> of each quickly destroys a violent disease of <s>grahaṇī</s>.
<s>Kṛśānu</s>, the two kinds of cumin, mixed with honey and also with the three pungents, not hot,
together with <s>cāṅgerikā</s>, the two cumins, and coriander, should be given with curds for the milk-and-greens regimen.

children.text: vireko jaṭhare śūlaṃ vamanaṃ ca muhurmuhuḥ
children.translated_text: Purging, pain in the belly, and repeated vomiting,
together with contraction of the hands, feet, and so on, are the symptoms of complete indigestion.
Purified <s>sūta</s>, poison, and sulfur, in equal parts, should all be powdered finely.
Black pepper, in an amount equal to the whole, is added with the fruit juices of <s>kaṇṭakārī</s>.
One should triturate and impregnate the whole mixture twenty-one times.
One should eat a pill of three <s>guñjās</s> for the calming of complete indigestion.
This <s>rasa</s>, called <s>Ajīrṇakaṇṭaka</s>, destroys <s>viṣūcikā</s>.
Afterward one should drink the root of <s>tilaparṇī</s>, ground with water.
Having triturated sulfur, stone, and borax, and then having impregnated it seven times with the waters of <s>jātī</s> fruits,

children.text: toyaiḥ phalānāmatha siddhasūto vidhvaṃsanāmā śamano viṣūcyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the prepared mercury called <s>Vidhvaṃsana</s> becomes a pacifier of <s>viṣūcī</s>.

children.text: amuṣya guñjā nava dāpanīyā hantuṃ viṣūcīṃ sitayā sametāḥ
children.translated_text: Nine <s>guñjās</s> of this should be administered with sugar to destroy <s>viṣūcī</s>.

children.text: takraudanaṃ syādiha bhojanāya pathyaṃ ca śākaṃ kila vāstukasya ||
children.translated_text: Here food should be rice with buttermilk, and the wholesome vegetable is said to be <s>vāstuka</s> greens.
Mercury, sulfur, and calcined borax, in equal parts, should be thoroughly triturated and impregnated seven times with nutmeg.
Used with sugar in a measure of nine <s>raktikās</s>, while one eats churned buttermilk-rice, it conquers <s>viṣūcikā</s>.
A <s>pala</s> of mercury and sulfur, prepared with the juices of <s>haṃsapādī</s>,
and a <s>kola</s> of powdered poison are to be cooked in a sand-bath apparatus.
One should mix in a <s>śāṇa</s> of poison and half a <s>pala</s> of black pepper.
This <s>Agnikumāra</s> is a digestive stimulant, especially in <s>grahaṇī</s>.
It draws off diseases born of vāta and phlegm in a moment.
It destroys fever from combined humors, dyspnea, wasting, and cough.

children.text: ṭaṃkaṇaṃ maricaṃ tutthaṃ pṛthak karṣatrayaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: Borax, black pepper, and blue vitriol should each be three <s>karṣas</s>.
<s>Sundara</s> should be twelve <s>niṣkas</s>, and iron slag thirty <s>niṣkas</s>.
Combining these powders, one should keep them in a clean vessel.
A man whose body has been purified should drink this after a meal.
Then he should eat a little wholesome food, and afterwards take betel.
The digestive fire in that man's belly becomes equal to the submarine fire.
What more need be said here? This is a <s>rasāyana</s> for men.
<s>Kānta</s>, rubbed in lotus juice, should be cooked in a <s>puṭa</s> with the juice of <s>varā</s>.
Iron slag should be rubbed seven times with the fresh juice of <s>mārkava</s>.

children.text: śuddhau sūtabalī carācararajaḥ karṣāṃśataḥ kajjalīm kṛtvā gopayasā vimardya divasaṃ ruddhvā ca mūṣodare
children.translated_text: When purification has been done, one should make a black paste from purified <s>sūta</s>, <s>balī</s>, and <s>carācararajas</s>, each by the <s>karṣa</s>; after triturating it for a day with cow's milk, one seals it inside a crucible.

children.text: siddhaṃ kumbhapuṭe svataśca śiśirā piṣṭā karaṇḍe sthitā syād vaiśvānarapoṭalīti kathitā tīvrāgnidīptipradā ||
children.translated_text: Perfected in a <s>kumbhapuṭa</s>, cooled by itself, ground, and kept in a box, it is called <s>Vaiśvānarapoṭalī</s>, giver of intense kindling of the digestive fire.
This should be given with powders of nineteen black peppers mixed with ghee,
in a <s>valla</s> measure, after considering age and strength.
One should swallow it for purification of the throat; curd-rice is excellent.
In the amount of three mouthfuls, it calms foul-smelling belching.
Then at midday food should be taken with ghee and buttermilk as accompaniments.

children.text: rātrau ca payasā sārdhaṃ yadvā rogānusārataḥ ||
children.translated_text: At night it should be taken together with milk, or else according to the disease.
One should avoid heating foods, pulses, excessive salt, and things cooked in oil,

children.text: bilvaṃ ca kāravellaṃ ca vṛṃtākaṃ kāṃjikaṃ tyajet ||
children.translated_text: as well as <s>bilva</s>, bitter gourd, eggplant, and <s>kāñjika</s>.

children.text: iyaṃ hi poṭalī proktā siṅghaṇena mahībhṛtā
children.translated_text: This <s>poṭalī</s> was taught by King <s>Siṅghaṇa</s>.
It destroys the entire mass of diseases produced by weak digestive fire.
It was prescribed for <s>Siṅghaṇa</s> by <s>Bhairavānandayogin</s>.
The procedures for the <s>poṭalī</s> taught by <s>Lokanātha</s> are remembered here.

children.text: poṭalyo dīpanāḥ snigdhā maṃdāgnau nitarāṃ hitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Poṭalīs</s> are digestive stimulants, unctuous, and exceedingly beneficial when digestion is weak.
Yellow in color, heavy and unctuous, knotted on the back, and stainless,

children.text: carācareti sā proktā varāṭī naṃdinā khalu ||
children.translated_text: that is called <s>Carācara</s>, a <s>varāṭī</s>, according to <s>Nandin</s>.
The best one measures one and a half <s>niṣkas</s>; the middling one measures one <s>niṣka</s>.
And the inferior <s>varāṭikā</s> here measures a quarter less than a <s>niṣka</s>.
Those smaller than that are fruitless, and male <s>varāṭas</s> are pitta-producing.

children.text: dattvā dattvā guṇānbhūyo vikārānkurvate hi te ||
children.translated_text: For, after repeatedly imparting their qualities, they also produce further pathological changes.
With ashes of copper and iron, <s>vella</s>, <s>halinī</s>, the three pungents, water, neem leaves, and with turmeric, together with salt, white <s>amṛtā</s>,

children.text: bhṛṅgāmbhoviṣatindukārdrakarasaiḥ sampiṣya guṃjāmitā saṃśuṣkā vaḍavāmukhīti guṭikā nāmnoditā tārayā ||
children.translated_text: and with juices of <s>bhṛṅga</s>, water, poison, and fresh <s>tinduka</s>, one should grind them into a pill of <s>guñjā</s> measure and dry it; this pill is taught under the name <s>Vaḍavāmukhī</s>.

children.text: kṣipraṃ kṣutparibodhinī khalu matā sarvāmayadhvaṃsinī śleṣmavyādhividhūnanī kasanahṛcchvāsāpahā śūlanut kṣudvaiṣamyaharā ca gulmaśamanī mūlārtimūlaṃkaṣā śophavyādhiharātra kiṃ bahugirā sarvāmayotsādinī ||
children.translated_text: It is considered quick to awaken hunger, destructive of all diseases, dispelling diseases of phlegm, removing cough and breathlessness, relieving colic, correcting irregular hunger, pacifying abdominal tumors, cutting at the root of piles, and removing swelling disorders; in short, it eradicates all ailments.
Having melted two <s>palas</s> of purified sulfur, one should add
mercury in the measure of one <s>pala</s>, and again calcined copper and iron.
After adding them in the measure of one <s>tola</s>, one should place the mixture on a leaf of the five-finger plant.
Then, carefully powdering it, one should put it in an iron vessel.
Setting it carefully on the stove, one should heat it with a gentle fire.
One should thoroughly digest it with just enough lemon juice to fill the vessel.
After powdering it, with decoctions made from the five pungents together with sour <s>vetasa</s>,
fifty measured impregnations should then be performed.
One should mix it with an equal amount of powder of roasted borax.
Half of that should be black salt, and pepper should be equal to the whole.
Afterwards one should impregnate it seven times with water of chickpea alkali.
Then, drying and grinding it, one should place it in the belly of a glass bottle.
After eating very heavy meats and many kinds of heavy foods,
and after eating up to the throat, one should take this <s>rasa</s> in a measure of four <s>vallas</s>.
It should be drunk with pungent, sour buttermilk as the accompanying drink.

children.text: kṣipraṃ tajjīryate bhuktaṃ jāyate dīpanaṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What has been eaten is quickly digested by it, and again stimulation of the digestive fire arises.
This <s>rasa</s>, named <s>Kravyāda</s>, was taught by the <s>Manthānabhairavas</s>.
It was prescribed for <s>Siṅghaṇa</s>, the lord of the earth, who was very fond of abundant meat,
by the yogin <s>Bhairavānanda</s> when he reached the village.

children.text: kuryāddīpanamuddhataṃ ca pacanaṃ duṣṭāmasaṃśoṣaṇaṃ tundasthaulyanibarhaṇaṃ garaharaṃ mūlārtiśūlāpaham
children.translated_text: The <s>Kravyāda</s> <s>rasa</s> produces powerful stimulation of digestion and cooking of food, dries up corrupted undigested matter, removes corpulence of the belly, removes poison, and takes away the pain and colic of piles.

children.text: gulmaplīhavināśanaṃ grahaṇikāvidhvaṃsanaṃ sraṃsanaṃ vātagranthimahodarāpaharaṇaṃ kravyādanāmā rasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It destroys abdominal tumors and spleen disease, abolishes <s>grahaṇī</s>, causes downward evacuation, and removes vāta-knots and great abdominal enlargement.
One part of calcined mercury, and two parts of <s>vatsanābha</s>,
<s>śivā</s> powder equal to the mercury, and likewise sulfur and the three pungents:
having powdered them with the greatest care, one should impregnate them for seven days
with water from betel leaves and with juices born from golden <s>dhustūra</s>.
After grinding, one should make pills of <s>caṇa</s> measure and dry them in the shade.
The <s>Rājaśekhara</s> pill, taken with hot water, destroys weak digestive fire, pacifies pains from many forms of severe fever, and removes piles completely.

children.text: pāṇḍuvyādhimahodarārtiśamanī śūlāntakṛt pācinī śophaghnī pavanārtināśanapaṭuḥ śleṣmāmayadhvaṃsinī ||
children.translated_text: It pacifies anemia and the pain of great abdominal enlargement, ends colic, cooks the food, destroys swelling, is skilled in removing pain from wind, and destroys diseases of phlegm.

children.text: śuddhaṃ sūtaṃ viṣaṃ gaṃdhaṃ dvikṣāraṃ paṭupañcakam
children.translated_text: Purified mercury, poison, sulfur, the two alkalis, and the group of five salts,
together with ten equal parts of fresh roasted <s>vijayā</s>,
and half as much moringa root as that quantity:
all that should be rubbed with juices of <s>vijayā</s>, moringa, <s>citraka</s>, and <s>bhṛṅga</s>.

children.text: drāvair dinatrayaṃ mardyaṃ ruddhvā bhāṇḍe pacellaghu
children.translated_text: It should be triturated for three days with those juices, sealed in a vessel, and cooked lightly.
With a lamp-flame for one watch, one should remove it when it has become dry.
The physician should impregnate it seven times with ginger juice and then powder it.
This appetizer is <s>Agnikumāra</s>; one should lick one <s>niṣka</s> with honey.

children.text: pratikarṣaṃ guḍaṃ śuṃṭhī hyanupānaṃ ca dīpanam ||
children.translated_text: Jaggery and dry ginger, in the measure of a <s>karṣa</s> each, are the accompanying digestive adjuvant.
With equal parts of <s>kuṣṭha</s>, sulfur, poison, mica, <s>triphala</s>, and mercury,
rubbed with <s>mṛgāmbu</s>, the auspicious <s>Amṛtavaṭī</s> should be made in the measure of a mung bean.
It destroys indigestion, phlegm, and wind, stimulates digestion, and increases relish.

children.text: tāmraṃ pāradagaṃdhakau trikaṭukaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ ca sauvarcalaṃ khalle mardya dṛḍhaṃ vidhāya sikatākumbhe'ṣṭayāmaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: Copper, mercury, sulfur, the three pungents, iron, and <s>sauvarcala</s> salt should be firmly rubbed in a mortar, placed in a sand-filled pot, and cooked for eight watches.

children.text: svinnaṃ tasya ca raktaśākinibhavaṃ kṣāraṃ samaṃ melayet sarvaṃ bhāvitamātuluṃgajarasairnāmnā raso rākṣasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After it has been steamed, one should mix in an equal amount of alkali produced from red greens; the whole, impregnated with citron juices, is a <s>rasa</s> named <s>Rākṣasa</s>.

children.text: mandāgnau satataṃ dadīta munaye prātaḥ purā śaṃkaraḥ sakhya asmai cyavanāya maṃdahutabhugvaryāya naṣṭaujase
children.translated_text: Of old, <s>Śaṅkara</s> gave it constantly at dawn to the sage <s>Cyavana</s>, his friend, whose digestive fire was weak and whose vigor had been lost.

children.text: tenādāya samastalokagurave sūryāya tasmai namo martyānāmapi cāsya dānasamaye guṃjāṣṭakaṃ varjayet ||
children.translated_text: Having taken it, he gave homage to that <s>Sūrya</s>, the teacher of all worlds; when administering it even to mortals, one should avoid a dose of eight <s>guñjās</s>.
Mercury and sulfur, rock salt, <s>kaṇā</s>, borax, <s>abhayā</s>, <s>agni</s>, <s>hiyāvalī</s>, and the fruit of <s>kataka</s>,
each successively greater than the previous one, should be powdered and impregnated with the juice of <s>bṛhatī</s>.
Then, in sequence, it should be impregnated with the juices of ginger, asafoetida, <s>punarnavā</s>, <s>pūtika</s>, and <s>chinna</s>.

children.text: tatra kalāṃśaviśaṃ ca vimiśraṃ tadrasamānaṃ mānavidhayā ||
children.translated_text: Into that, poison in a fractional portion should be mixed, and by rule it should be equal in measure to that <s>rasa</s>.
This <s>Rasendra</s> called <s>Dīpanajīvana</s> destroys all indigestion, phlegm, wind, anemia, swelling, <s>halīmaka</s>, jaundice, and colic.
It kindles the abdominal digestive fire and gives life.

children.text: śulbaṃ tālakagandhakau jalanidheḥ pheno 'gnigarbhāśayaḥ kāntāyo lavaṇāni hemapavayo nīlāṃjanaṃ tutthakam
children.translated_text: Copper, orpiment, sulfur, sea-foam, <s>agnigarbha</s>, magnetic iron, salts, <s>hemapavaya</s>, blue collyrium, and blue vitriol,

children.text: bhāgo dvādaśako rasasya tu dinaṃ vallyaṃbughṛṣṭaṃ śanaiḥ siddho'yaṃ vaḍavānalo gajapuṭe rogānaśeṣāñjayet ||
children.translated_text: with twelve parts of mercury, should be slowly rubbed for a day with creeper-water; this prepared <s>Vaḍavānala</s>, cooked in an elephant-pit firing, conquers all diseases without remainder.
Equal parts of <s>kaṇā</s>, dry ginger, sulfur, mercury, poison, and black pepper,
made with the juices of <s>lakuca</s> into pills the size of a chickpea, quickly produces the digestive fire.
Purified mercury, poison, sulfur, <s>ajamodā</s>, the three fruits,
<s>sarjīkṣāra</s>, <s>yavakṣāra</s>, <s>vahni</s>, rock salt, and cumin,
<s>sauvarcala</s> salt, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, sea salt, and the three pungents, all in equal measure,
with <s>viṣamuṣṭi</s> equal to all the rest, should be triturated with the sour juice of citron.
One should eat a pill the size of a black pepper to quiet weakness of the digestive fire.

children.text: pathyā śuṇṭhī guḍaṃ cānu palārdhaṃ bhakṣayetsadā ||
children.translated_text: Afterwards one should always eat half a <s>pala</s> of <s>pathyā</s>, dry ginger, and jaggery.
This pill, famed for weak digestion, is the destroyer of every family of diseases.
Calcined copper, equal in amount to <s>kaṇā</s>, should be mixed as a powder with honey.
One should eat half a <s>niṣka</s> of it daily to kindle a lost digestive fire.
Afterwards one should drink a <s>pala</s> measure of fresh ginger juice with honey.
Eating ghee and meat as desired, the digestive fire becomes strong.

children.text: kaṭau kukṣipradeśe ca śūlaṃ prathamato bhavet
children.translated_text: At first there is pain in the region of the lower back and belly,
then obstruction and burning urination: these are the symptoms of urinary-stone disease.
Having carefully triturated mercury with twice as much sulfur,

children.text: vasuḥ punarnavā vāsā śvetā grāhyā prayatnataḥ ||
children.translated_text: one should carefully take <s>vasu</s>, <s>punarnavā</s>, <s>vāsā</s>, and white <s>aparājitā</s>.
With their juices one should impregnate this mercury, each one for three days.
When it has been cooked in a crucible and dried, one should heat it by means of a water apparatus.
This is called <s>Pāṣāṇabhedī</s>; one should administer it in a <s>valla</s> dose.
The milk of <s>gopālakarkaṭī</s> and the root of <s>bhūmyāmalaka</s>,
ground with water from a decoction of horse gram, should be given as the vehicle for it.
With the juice of white <s>varṣābhū</s>, mercury and twice as much sulfur

children.text: ghṛṣṭaṃ pacecca mūṣāyāṃ dvau māṣau tasya bhakṣayet ||
children.translated_text: should be rubbed together and cooked in a crucible; two <s>māṣas</s> of it should be eaten.
Afterwards one should drink the root of <s>pātālakarkaṭī</s> with horse-gram water.
At night one should drink a decoction of the roots of <s>gokaṇṭaka</s> and <s>sadābhadrā</s>.
This <s>rasa</s>, named <s>Pāṣāṇabhinna</s>, breaks urinary stones.
Powder made from <s>gokṣura</s> seeds, combined with sheep's milk,
and mixed with the excellent <s>rasa</s>, when drunk, causes the stone to crumble and fall out.
Calcined copper should be cooked with goat's milk in an equal amount until the liquid is gone.

children.text: tattāmraṃ śuddhasūtaṃ ca gaṃdhakaṃ ca samaṃ samam ||
children.translated_text: That copper, purified mercury, and sulfur should each be taken in equal portions.
It should be triturated for a day with juices arising from <s>nirguṇḍī</s>; that ball should be sealed up.
It should be cooked for one <s>yāma</s> in a sand apparatus and administered in a dose of two <s>guñjās</s>.
The moist root of <s>bījapūra</s> should be given afterwards as the vehicle.
The <s>rasa</s> named <s>Trivikrama</s> drives out urinary stones within one month.
Sesame stalks, stalks of <s>apāmārga</s>, those of bitter gourd and of barley,
together with <s>palāśa</s> wood, all in equal amounts, should be burned in a closed heating.
From one <s>niṣka</s> of that, with goat's urine, one should make the pill called <s>Ānandabhairavī</s>.
One should give it to drink; it destroys urinary stones in seven days, of this there is no doubt.
The pale root of <s>phalikā</s>, taken with water alone, removes urinary stones.

children.text: madhunā ca yavakṣāraṃ līḍhaṃ syād aśmarīharam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Yavakṣāra</s> licked with honey is also a remover of urinary stones.
Or one should drink one <s>karṣa</s> of turmeric and jaggery with <s>āranāla</s>.
Having eaten the tuber of <s>vandhyākarkoṭakī</s>, together with honey and sugar,

children.text: aśmarīṃ hanti no citraṃ karṣamātraṃ śivoditam ||
children.translated_text: one destroys urinary stones; it is no marvel. A <s>karṣa</s> measure is taught by <s>Śiva</s>.
Wasting, heat, emaciation of the limbs, and excessive urination,
together with malaise in all the limbs, are the symptoms of <s>mūtrameha</s> urinary disease.
One should take powder of <s>mārkaṇḍī</s> and eat it with jaggery at night.
One part of calcined mercury and four parts of purified sulfur

children.text: piṣṭvā varāṭakaṃ tena rasapādaṃ ca ṭaṃkaṇam ||
children.translated_text: should be ground; with it, cowries, borax equal to a quarter of the mercury,
should be ground with milk, their mouths closed, and the cowries sealed and calcined.
When self-cooled, it should then be powdered: this is <s>Laghu Lokeśvara Rasa</s>.
Of this <s>rasa</s> the dose is four <s>guñjās</s>, with nineteen black peppers.
One <s>pala</s> of <s>jāti</s> root should be ground with goat's milk,
then drunk after being treated with sugar; it is supreme for removing dysuria.
The divisions of barren women are indeed declared to be ninefold.
Among them, primary barrenness is the first, produced by bad karma.

children.text: raktena ca pṛthagdoṣaiḥ samastaiḥ pañcadhā bhavet
children.translated_text: Because of blood, and because of the doṣas separately and collectively, it becomes fivefold.
Through spirits, gods, and sorcery, three further barren conditions are taught.
A man too may be barren because these doṣas affect the semen.
The woman who miscarries is remembered first, and the woman whose children die is second.
The third is the woman who bears only daughters; the <s>kākavandhyā</s> is one who has borne once.

children.text: suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ tāmraṃ tāpyasattvaṃ ca vaikṛtam
children.translated_text: Gold, silver, copper, the essence of <s>tāpya</s>, and modified metal,
each in a <s>niṣka</s> measure, should be thoroughly purified and calcined.
Mercury four times the amount of these, and sulfur twice the amount of the mercury,
should be triturated with water of <s>lakṣmaṇā</s> and also with juice of <s>bandhujīva</s>.

children.text: kācakūpyāṃ tataḥ kṣiptvā tāmrapātraṃ mukhe nyaset
children.translated_text: Then, after placing it in a glass bottle, one should set a copper vessel at the mouth.
One should coat the bottle all around with clay raised to a finger's thickness.

children.text: viśoṣya ca puṭaṃ dadyādbhūmau nikṣipya kūpikām
children.translated_text: After drying it, one should give a heating, placing the bottle in the ground.
The heating known as <s>gajapuṭa</s> is sufficient, with fuel cakes measured by <s>śāṇa</s> and <s>karṣa</s>.
When self-cooled, it should then be powdered and impregnated with juices of <s>lakṣmaṇā</s>.
After drying it seven times, one should place it inside a casket.
This excellent <s>rasa</s>, joined with powder of <s>aśvagandhā</s> and combined with red cow's milk,

children.text: sevito guñjayā tulyaḥ sitayā ca rasottamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: is to be used in a dose equal to one <s>guñjā</s>, and with sugar.
By using it for three months, a barren woman becomes the mother of a son.
For a woman who has sons and has been purified by bathing, the two eyes of an old <s>kauśika</s> owl,

children.text: gavyājyena ca saṃsādhya tattadānīṃ hi bhojayet
children.translated_text: cooked with cow's ghee, should indeed be fed to her at that time.
This should be given at each menstrual season until three months have passed.
This <s>rasendra</s> has been taught by the dwellers in <s>Campakāraṇya</s>,
by the foremost yogins called <s>Pūrṇāmṛta</s>, under the name <s>Jayasundara</s>.
When this <s>rasa</s> is used by women, no puerperal disease arises,
and a son is born who is long-lived, learned, and adorned with good fortune.

children.text: vajraṃ marakataṃ padmarāgaṃ puṣpaṃ ca nīlakam
children.translated_text: Diamond, emerald, <s>padmarāga</s>, <s>puṣpa</s>, and blue sapphire,

children.text: vaidūryaṃ cātha gomedaṃ mauktikaṃ vidrumaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: as well as <s>vaidūrya</s>, <s>gomeda</s>, pearl, and coral,
each jewel measured at five <s>guñjās</s>, the best being successively increased by portions,
should be carefully reduced to ash according to the procedure taught in its tantra.
Ash produced from <s>vaikrānta</s> should be eight times as much as all of them,
and ash born from <s>tāpya</s> should be equal to that, and likewise ash of <s>vimala</s>.
A black paste of mercury and sulfur, equal to three times the whole,
should be mixed all together and triturated for two days with goat's milk.
After carefully making it into <s>parpaṭī</s> flakes, one should carefully pulverize it,
and triturate it with a decoction of the leaves of <s>vandhyākarkoṭakī</s>.
One should heat it in a <s>puṭa</s> sixteen times with twenty <s>kānanotpala</s> flowers.
Thus the prepared <s>rasa</s> is obtained, called <s>Ratnabhāgottara</s>.
It gives offspring to all barren women, beginning with those who are greatly barren,
and, as specified in the <s>Devīśāstra</s>, it removes the disease of infertility in men.

children.text: so'yaṃ pācanadīpano rucikaro vṛṣyastathā garbhiṇīsarvavyādhivināśano ratikaraḥ pāṇḍupracaṇḍārtinut
children.translated_text: This is digestive, kindles appetite, improves taste, is aphrodisiac, destroys all diseases of pregnant women, gives sexual pleasure, and removes the severe distress of pallor-disease.

children.text: dhanyo buddhikaraśca putrajananaḥ saubhāgyakṛdyoṣitāṃ nirdoṣaḥ smaramandirāmayaharo yogādaśeṣārtinut ||
children.translated_text: It is auspicious, produces intelligence, causes the birth of sons, creates good fortune for women, is faultless, removes diseases of the house of love, and, through its preparation, removes every pain.
There should be one <s>pala</s> of sulfur, and separately one <s>akṣa</s> each of <s>śilā</s> and <s>lākṣā</s>.
After triturating them for three days, one should then make a fine black paste.
One should then put the black paste into a horn-shaped crucible,

children.text: dvipalasya ca tāmrasya tanmukhe cakrikāṃ nyaset ||
children.translated_text: and place at its mouth a small disc made from two <s>palas</s> of copper.
Having sealed it with the greatest care, when the joint-seal has dried,
one should then properly carry out the cooking with half a <s>karipuṭa</s>.
When it has cooled by itself, one should take out the small disc and pulverize it,
and put it into a small bottle after filtering it through cloth.
This <s>rasa</s>, called <s>Cakrikābandha</s>, with medicines that remove the respective diseases,
should be given in cases of colic, piles, abdominal tumors, and fistula-in-ano,
in <s>grahaṇī</s>, weak digestive fire, abscess, and abdominal disease,
and likewise in <s>nāgodara</s>, <s>upaviṣṭaka</s>, and <s>jalakūrmaka</s>.
By <s>Skanda</s>, out of great compassion, for the sake of protecting the three worlds,
